Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Abhidhammapiṭake

In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka

Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā

The Commentary on the Five Treatises

Dhātukathā-aṭṭhakathā

Commentary on the Discourse on Elements

Aṭṭhārasahi [P 0.0114][M 0.0001][V 0.0001] bhedehi, vibhaṅgaṃ mārabhañjano;

Desayitvā mahāvīro, yaṃ tasseva anantaraṃ.

The Great Hero, the destroyer of Māra, having expounded the Analysis in eighteen ways, immediately thereafter...

Adesayi dhātukathaṃ, dhātubhedappakāsano;

Tassatthaṃ dīpayissāmi, taṃ suṇātha samāhitāti.

He taught the Discourse on Elements, revealing the distinctions of elements; I will explain its meaning, listen with collected minds.

1. Mātikāvaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Mātikā

1. Nayamātikāvaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Naya Mātikā

1. Saṅgaho [V 0.0002] asaṅgahotiādīnañhi vasena idaṃ pakaraṇaṃ cuddasavidhena vibhattanti vuttaṃ. Taṃ sabbampi uddesaniddesato dvidhā ṭhitaṃ. Tattha mātikā uddeso. Sā pañcavidhā – nayamātikā, abbhantaramātikā, nayamukhamātikā, lakkhaṇamātikā, bāhiramātikāti. Tattha saṅgaho asaṅgaho…pe… vippayuttena saṅgahitaṃ asaṅgahitanti – ayaṃ cuddasahi padehi nikkhittā nayamātikā nāma. Ayañhi iminā saṅgahādikena nayena dhātukathā dhammā vibhattāti dassetuṃ ṭhapitattā nayamātikāti vuccati. Etesaṃ padānaṃ mūlabhūtattā mūlamātikātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati.

1. Indeed, it has been said that this treatise is classified in fourteen ways in terms of inclusion, non-inclusion, and so forth. All of that stands in two ways: as summary and detailed explanation. Therein, the mātikā is the summary. It is fivefold: the mātikā of methods, the internal mātikā, the mātikā of method entrances, the mātikā of characteristics, and the external mātikā. Therein, 'inclusion, non-inclusion... included by the dissociated and not included'—this, laid down in fourteen terms, is called the mātikā of methods. For this is called the mātikā of methods because it is established to show that the phenomena of the Dhātukathā are classified by this method beginning with inclusion. Since these terms are fundamental, it is also proper to call it the root mātikā.

2. Abbhantaramātikāvaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Internal Mātikā

2. Pañcakkhandhā [M 0.0002] …pe… manasikāroti ayaṃ pañcavīsādhikena padasatena nikkhittā abbhantaramātikā nāma. Ayañhi “sabbāpi dhammasaṅgaṇī dhātukathāya mātikā”ti evaṃ avatvā saṅgahādinā nayena vibhajitabbe khandhādidhamme sarūpato dassetvā dhātukathāya abbhantareyeva ṭhapitattā abbhantaramātikāti vuccati. Khandhādipadānaṃ dhammasaṅgaṇīmātikāya [P 0.0115] asaṅgahitattā pakiṇṇakamātikātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati.

2. ‘The five aggregates …pe… attention’—this, set forth in one hundred and twenty-five terms, is called the internal mātikā. For this is called the internal mātikā because, without saying, “the entire Dhammasaṅgaṇī is the mātikā for the Dhātukathā,” it shows the aggregates and other phenomena that are to be analyzed by the method of inclusion and so on in their own nature, and because it is placed within the Dhātukathā itself. Since the terms for the aggregates and so on are not included in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī mātikā, it is also fitting to call it the miscellaneous mātikā.

3. Nayamukhamātikāvaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Mātikā of Method Entrances

3. Tīhi saṅgaho, tīhi asaṅgaho; catūhi sampayogo, catūhi vippayogoti ayaṃ catūhi padehi nikkhittā nayamukhamātikā nāma. Ayañhi sabbesupi pañcakkhandhādīsu ceva kusalattikādīsu ca mātikādhammesu, tīhi khandhāyatanadhātupadeheva saṅgaho ca asaṅgaho ca yojetabbo. Tathā catūhi arūpakkhandhehi sampayogo ca vippayogo ca. Etāni imesaṃ saṅgahāsaṅgahādīnaṃ nayānaṃ mukhānīti dassetuṃ ṭhapitattā nayamukhamātikāti vuccati.

3. ‘Inclusion by three, non-inclusion by three; association by four, dissociation by four’—this, laid out in four terms, is called the mātikā of method entrances. For in all mātikā phenomena—such as the five aggregates and so forth, and the wholesome triad and so forth—inclusion and non-inclusion should be connected precisely by means of the three terms of aggregates, sense bases, and elements. Similarly, association and dissociation by means of the four immaterial aggregates. Because these are established to show the entrances to these methods of inclusion, non-inclusion, and so on, it is called the mātikā of method entrances.

4. Lakkhaṇamātikāvaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Mātikā of Characteristics

4. Sabhāgo[V 0.0003], visabhāgoti ayaṃ dvīhi padehi nikkhittā lakkhaṇamātikā nāma. Ayañhi sabhāgalakkhaṇehi dhammehi saṅgahanayo, visabhāgalakkhaṇehi asaṅgahanayo, tathā sampayogavippayoganayo yojetabboti sabhāgavisabhāgalakkhaṇavasena saṅgahādilakkhaṇaṃ dassetuṃ ṭhapitattā lakkhaṇamātikāti vuccati.

4. ‘Similar, dissimilar’—this, set forth in two terms, is called the mātikā of characteristics. For the method of inclusion is to be applied through phenomena with similar characteristics, the method of non-inclusion through phenomena with dissimilar characteristics, and likewise the method of association and dissociation. Because it is established to show the characteristics of inclusion and so forth by way of the characteristics of similarity and dissimilarity, it is called the mātikā of characteristics.

5. Bāhiramātikāvaṇṇanā

5. Explanation of the External Mātikā

5. Sabbāpi dhammasaṅgaṇī dhātukathāya mātikāti ayaṃ chasaṭṭhi tikapadāni, dve ca dukapadasatāni saṅkhipitvā nikkhittā bāhiramātikā nāma. Ayañhi “pañcakkhandhā…pe… manasikāro”ti evaṃ dhātukathāya abbhantare avatvā “sabbāpi dhammasaṅgaṇī”ti evaṃ dhātukathāya mātikato bahi ṭhapitattā bāhiramātikāti vuccati.

5. ‘The entire Dhammasaṅgaṇī is the mātikā of the Dhātukathā’—this, summarizing sixty-six triad terms and two hundred dyad terms, is set forth as what is called the external mātikā. For, not stating internally in the Dhātukathā, ‘the five aggregates...attention,’ but stating, ‘the entire Dhammasaṅgaṇī,’ it is called the external mātikā because it is placed outside the mātikā of the Dhātukathā.

Evaṃ [M 0.0003] mātikāya pañcadhā ṭhitabhāvaṃ viditvā idāni ‘saṅgaho asaṅgaho’tiādīsu saṅgaho tāva jātisañjātikiriyāgaṇanavasena catubbidho. Tattha – “sabbe khattiyā āgacchantu, sabbe brāhmaṇā, sabbe vessā, sabbe suddā āgacchantu”, “yā cāvuso visākha, sammāvācā, yo ca sammākammanto, yo ca sammāājīvo, ime dhammā sīlakkhandhe saṅgahitā”ti ayaṃ jātisaṅgaho nāma. “Ekajātikā āgacchantū”ti vuttaṭṭhāne viya hi idha sabbepi jātiyā ekasaṅgahaṃ gatā. “Sabbe kosalakā āgacchantu, sabbe māgadhakā, sabbe bhārukacchakā āgacchantu”, “yo cāvuso visākha, sammāvāyāmo; yā ca sammāsati, yo ca sammāsamādhi, ime dhammā [P 0.0116] samādhikkhandhe saṅgahitā”ti (ma. ni. 1.462) ayaṃ sañjātisaṅgaho nāma. “Ekaṭṭhāne jātā saṃvaḍḍhā āgacchantū”ti vuttaṭṭhāne viya hi idha sabbepi sañjātiṭhānena nivutthokāsena ekasaṅgahaṃ gatā. “Sabbe hatthārohā āgacchantu, sabbe assārohā, sabbe rathikā āgacchantu”, “yā cāvuso visākha, sammādiṭṭhi, yo ca sammāsaṅkappo, ime dhammā paññākkhandhe saṅgahitā”ti (ma. ni. 1.462) ayaṃ kiriyāsaṅgaho nāma. Sabbeva hete attano kiriyākaraṇena ekasaṅgahaṃ gatā. “Cakkhāyatanaṃ katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti? Rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatī”ti. Hañci cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – ‘cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhena saṅgahita”nti (kathā. 471), ayaṃ [V 0.0004] gaṇanasaṅgaho nāma. Ayamidha adhippeto. Tappaṭipakkhena asaṅgaho veditabbo. Tesaṃ vikappato saṅgahitena asaṅgahitādīni. Ekuppādekanirodhaekavatthukaekārammaṇatāvasena sampayogo, tappaṭipakkhato vippayogo. Tesaṃ vikappato sampayuttena vippayuttādīni. Tadubhayasaṃsaggavikappato saṅgahitena sampayuttaṃ vippayuttantiādīni. Pañcakkhandhātiādīni pana khandhavibhaṅgādīsu vuttanayeneva veditabbāni. Phassādayo panettha sanniṭṭhānavasena vuttasabbacittuppādasādhāraṇato vuttāti.

Having thus understood the fivefold nature of the matrix, now, regarding ‘inclusion, exclusion,’ and so on, inclusion is, in the first place, of four kinds: by way of birth, origin, action, and enumeration. Herein: “Let all Khattiyas come, all Brāhmaṇas, all Vessas, all Suddas come,” and “Friend Visākha, right speech, right action, and right livelihood—these states are included in the aggregate of virtue”—this is called inclusion by birth. For here, all are included as one by birth, just as in the case where it is said, ‘Let those of one birth come.’ “Let all Kosalans come, all Magadhans, all Bhārukacchakas come,” and “Friend Visākha, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration—these states are included in the aggregate of concentration”—this is called inclusion by origin. For here, all are included as one by way of their place of origin and place of residence, just as in the case where it is said, ‘Let those born and raised in one place come.’ “Let all elephant-riders come, all horse-riders, all charioteers come,” and “Friend Visākha, right view and right intention—these states are included in the aggregate of wisdom”—this is called inclusion by action. For all these are included as one by their own actions. “To which aggregate-count does the eye-base belong? It belongs to the aggregate-count of form.” “If the eye-base belongs to the aggregate-count of form, then it must be said, ‘The eye-base is included with the aggregate of form’”—this is called inclusion by enumeration. This is what is intended here. By its opposite, exclusion is to be understood. From the alternatives of these, there are [pairs such as] included with excluded, and so on. Association is by way of arising together, ceasing together, having one basis, and having one object; by its opposite, dissociation. From the alternatives of these, there are [pairs such as] associated with dissociated, and so on. From the alternatives of the combination of both, there are [triplets such as] included with associated, included with dissociated, and so on. As for the five aggregates, and so on, they should be understood in the very way stated in the Analysis of the Aggregates, and so on. Here, contact and so on are stated by way of conclusion because they are common to all the stated arisings of consciousness.

Mātikāvaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Matrix.

2. Niddesavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Exposition

1. Paṭhamanayo saṅgahāsaṅgahapadavaṇṇanā

1. First Method: Explanation of the Terms of Inclusion and Non-inclusion

1. Khandhapadavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Term 'Aggregates'

6. Idāni [M 0.0004] pañcakkhandhādivasena nikkhittamātikaṃ ‘saṅgaho asaṅgaho’tiādīhi nayamātikāpadehi saddhiṃ yojetvā dassetuṃ rūpakkhandho katihi khandhehītiādinā [P 0.0117] nayena niddesavāro āraddho. Tattha yasmā “saṅgaho asaṅgahotiādikāya nayamātikāya “tīhi saṅgaho, tīhi asaṅgaho”ti nayamukhamātikā ṭhapitā, tasmā rūpakkhandhādīnaṃ saṅgahaṃ dassetuṃ katihi khandhehi katihāyatanehi katihi dhātūhīti tīṇi khandhāyatanadhātupadāneva uddhaṭāni. ‘Cattāri saccānī’tiādīsu ekampi na parāmaṭṭhaṃ. Yasmā ca “sabhāgo visabhāgo”ti evaṃ lakkhaṇamātikā ṭhapitā, tasmā imassa pañhassa vissajjane rūpakkhandho ekena khandhenātiādi vuttaṃ. Sabhāgā hi tassa ete khandhādayoti. Tattha ekena khandhenāti rūpakkhandheneva. Yañhi kiñci rūpaṃ rūpakkhandhasabhāgattā rūpakkhandhotveva saṅgahaṃ gacchatīti rūpakkhandheneva gaṇitaṃ, taṃ rūpakkhandheneva paricchinnaṃ. Ekādasahāyatanehīti manāyatanavajjehi. Sabbopi hi rūpakkhandho dasāyatanāni dhammāyatanekadeso ca hoti, tasmā ekādasahāyatanehi gaṇito[V 0.0005], paricchinno. Ekādasahi dhātūhīti sattaviññāṇadhātuvajjāhi ekādasahi etāsu hi apariyāpannaṃ rūpaṃ nāma natthi.

6. Now, the section of exposition has begun with the method of 'the form aggregate, by how many aggregates,' and so on, in order to show the matrix, which was laid out in terms of the five aggregates and so on, by connecting it with the methodical matrix terms such as 'inclusion and non-inclusion.' Herein, because the methodical opening matrix, 'threefold inclusion, threefold non-inclusion,' has been established by the methodical matrix beginning with 'inclusion and non-inclusion,' therefore, to show the inclusion of the form aggregate and so on, only three terms—aggregates, bases, and elements—have been taken up. Not even one term in 'the four truths,' and so on, has been touched upon. And because the characteristic matrix has been established as 'similar and dissimilar,' therefore, in answering this question, it is said, 'the form aggregate by one aggregate,' and so on. For these aggregates, and so on, are similar to it. Herein, 'by one aggregate' means by the form aggregate itself. For whatever form there is, because it is of the same nature as the form aggregate, it is included only as the form aggregate; thus, it is reckoned only by the form aggregate and is defined only by the form aggregate. 'By eleven bases' means excluding the mind base. For the entire form aggregate consists of the ten bases and a part of the mental-object base; therefore, it is reckoned and defined by eleven bases. 'By eleven elements' means excluding the seven consciousness elements, for there is no form that is not included in these.

Asaṅgahanayaniddese katihi asaṅgahitoti saṅkhepeneva pucchā katā. Vissajjane panassa yasmā rūpakkhandhassa visabhāgā cattāro arūpakkhandhā, ekaṃ manāyatanaṃ, satta viññāṇadhātuyo; tasmā catūhi khandhehītiādi vuttaṃ. Iminā nayena sabbapadesu saṅgahāsaṅgaho veditabbo. Imasmiṃ pana khandhaniddese – “rūpakkhandho katihi khandhehī”tiādimhi tāva ekamūlake saṅgahanaye sarūpeneva dassitā pañca pucchā, pañca vissajjanāni. Asaṅgahanaye saṅkhepena dassitā pañca pucchā, pañca vissajjanāni. Iminā upāyena dukamūlakādīsupi pucchāvissajjanāni [P 0.0118] veditabbāni. Rūpakkhandhamūlakāyeva cettha dukatikacatukkā dassitā. Pañcake pana “rūpakkhandho [M 0.0005] ca…pe… viññāṇakkhandho cā”ti evaṃ bhedato ca, “pañcakkhandhā katihi khandhehī”ti evaṃ abhedato cāti dvidhā pucchāvissajjanāni katāni. Evaṃ pāḷinayo veditabboti.

In the exposition of the method of non-inclusion, the question "by how many is it not included?" is asked concisely. But in answering, because the four immaterial aggregates, one mind base, and seven consciousness elements are dissimilar to the form aggregate, therefore, it is said, "by four aggregates," and so on. By this method, inclusion and non-inclusion should be understood in all instances. However, in this exposition of the aggregates—"the form aggregate, by how many aggregates," and so on—first, in the method of inclusion based on a single root, five questions and five answers are shown explicitly. In the method of non-inclusion, five questions and five answers are shown concisely. By this approach, the questions and answers based on two roots, and so on, should also be understood. Herein, only the dyads, triads, and tetrads based on the form aggregate are shown. But in the pentad, the questions and answers are made in two ways: both divided, as "the form aggregate and... the consciousness aggregate," and so on, and undivided, as "the five aggregates, by how many aggregates," and so on. Thus, the method of the Pāḷi should be understood.

2. Āyatanapadādivaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Terms 'Bases', and so on

22. Āyatanapadaniddesādīsu āyatanapadaniddese tāva cakkhāyatanaṃ ekena khandhenāti ekena rūpakkhandheneva, ekena cakkhāyataneneva ekāya cakkhudhātuyāva saṅgahitanti veditabbaṃ. Sotāyatanādīsupi imināva nayena saṅgahāsaṅgaho veditabbo. Asaṅkhataṃ khandhato ṭhapetvāti ettha pana yasmā asaṅkhataṃ dhammāyatanaṃ nāma nibbānaṃ, tañca khandhasaṅgahaṃ na gacchati; tasmā ‘khandhato ṭhapetvā’ti vuttaṃ. Catūhi khandhehīti rūpavedanāsaññāsaṅkhārakkhandhehi. Nibbānavajjañhi dhammāyatanaṃ etehi saṅgahitaṃ. Viññāṇakkhandhena pana ṭhapetvā dhammāyatanadhammadhātuyo sesāyatanadhātūhi ca taṃ na saṅgayhati. Tena vuttaṃ – “ekena khandhena, ekādasahāyatanehi, sattarasahi dhātūhi asaṅgahita”nti. Yathā ca te heṭṭhā rūpakkhandhamūlakā, evamidhāpi cakkhāyatanamūlakāva nayā veditabbā. Dukamattameva pana pāḷiyaṃ dassetvā “dvādasāyatanānī”ti abhedatova pucchāvissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Dhātuniddesepi eseva nayo.

22. In the exposition of the sense-base terms and so on, first, regarding the exposition of the sense-base terms, the eye-base is to be understood as included in one aggregate, namely the form aggregate alone; in one sense-base, the eye-base itself; and in one element, the eye-element alone. The ear-base and others should be understood in the same way regarding inclusion and exclusion. As for 'the unconditioned is excluded from the aggregates,' here, because the unconditioned, namely Nibbāna, is the mental-object base, and it is not included in the aggregates, therefore it is said 'excluded from the aggregates.' By four aggregates—that is, by the form, feeling, perception, and mental-formations aggregates—the mental-object base, except for Nibbāna, is included. By the consciousness aggregate, however, it is not included; nor is it included by the remaining sense-bases and elements, excepting the mental-object base and mental-object element. Hence it is said: 'Not included by one aggregate, eleven sense-bases, and seventeen elements.' Just as those below are rooted in the form aggregate, so here too the methods should be understood as rooted in the eye-base. But in the Pāli text, only a pair is shown, and the question and answer are given without distinction as 'twelve sense-bases.' The same method applies in the exposition of the elements.

40. Saccaniddese [V 0.0006] – sabbepi dukatikacatukkā pāḷiyaṃ dassitā. Yasmā ca dukatikesu samudayasaccasadisameva maggasaccepi vissajjanaṃ, tasmā taṃ samudayānantaraṃ vuttaṃ.

40. In the exposition of the Truths, all the dyads, triads, and tetrads are shown in the Pāli. And since in the dyads and triads, the explanation of the Path Truth is similar to that of the Origin Truth, it is therefore stated immediately after the Origin.

50. Indriyaniddese – jīvitindriyaṃ dvīhi khandhehīti rūpajīvitindriyaṃ rūpakkhandhena, arūpajīvitindriyaṃ [P 0.0119] saṅkhārakkhandhena saṅgahitaṃ. Sesaṃ vuttanayānusāreneva veditabbaṃ. Pāḷivavatthānaṃ panettha āyatanadhātuniddesasadisameva.

50. In the exposition of the faculties, the life faculty is included in two aggregates: the material life faculty is included in the aggregate of form, and the immaterial life faculty is included in the aggregate of mental formations. The rest should be understood just as previously explained. Here, the Pāli classification is similar to that in the exposition of the sense-bases and elements.

6. Paṭiccasamuppādavaṇṇanā

6. The Elucidation of Dependent Origination

61. Paṭiccasamuppādaniddese – “avijjā katihi khandhehī”ti pucchaṃ anārabhitvā avijjā ekena khandhenāti evaṃ vissajjanameva dassitaṃ. Tattha saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇanti paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca sabbampi vipākaviññāṇaṃ. Tenevāha [M 0.0006] – “sattahi dhātūhi saṅgahita”nti. Nāmarūpampi paṭisandhipavattivaseneva veditabbaṃ. Tenevettha saddāyatanampi saṅgahetvā ekādasahāyatanehi saṅgaho dassito. Phassādīsu khandhabhedo veditabbo. Aññeneva hi ekena khandhena phasso saṅgahito, aññena vedanā, taṇhāupādānakammabhavā pana saṅkhārakkhandheneva saṅgahitā. Bhavapadañcettha kammabhavādīnaṃ vasena ekādasadhā vibhattaṃ. Tattha kammabhavo phassādīhi sadisavisajjanattā tehi saddhiṃ ekato dassito. Upapattibhavakāmabhavasaññābhavapañcavokārabhavā aññamaññasadisavissajjanattā ekato dassitā. Yasmā cete upādinnakadhammāva tasmā “ekādasahāyatanehi sattarasahi dhātūhī”ti vuttaṃ. Saddāyatanañhi anupādinnaṃ, taṃ ettha na gahitaṃ.

61. In the exposition of dependent origination—without raising the question, "By how many aggregates is ignorance included?"—the answer alone is shown: that ignorance is included in one aggregate. There, "consciousness conditioned by volitional formations" refers to all resultant consciousness, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence. Hence it is said: "Included by seven elements." Name-and-form should also be understood in terms of rebirth-linking and the course of existence. Therefore, here the inclusion is shown by eleven bases, having also included the sound-base. Regarding contact and so on, the division of aggregates should be understood. For contact is included by one aggregate and feeling by another, while craving, clinging, and kamma-existence are included only in the aggregate of volitional formations. Here, the term "existence" is analyzed in eleven ways, based on kamma-existence and so on. Among these, kamma-existence is shown together with contact and so on, because they share similar explanations. The types of existence—rebirth existence, sensual existence, perception existence, and five-aggregate existence—are shown together because they share similar explanations. Since these are all clung-to phenomena, it is said: "By eleven bases and seventeen elements." The sound-base, however, is not clung-to and thus is not included here.

68. Rūpabhavaniddese – pañcahāyatanehīti cakkhusotamanarūpadhammāyatanehi. Aṭṭhahi dhātūhīti cakkhusotacakkhuviññāṇasotaviññāṇarūpadhammamanodhātumanoviññāṇadhātūhi. Arūpabhavādayopi tayo sadisavissajjanattāva ekato dassitā. Tathā asaññābhavaekavokārabhavā. Tattha dvīhāyatanehīti rūpāyatanadhammāyatanehi. Dhātūsupi eseva nayo. Ekatalavāsikānañhi sesabrahmānaṃ cakkhusabbhāvato tassārammaṇattā tattha rūpāyatanaṃ uddhaṭaṃ.

68. In the exposition of the form-realm—by five bases: the eye, ear, mind, form, and mental-phenomena bases. By eight elements: the eye, ear, eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, form, mental-phenomena, mind-element, and mind-consciousness element. The three types of existence beginning with the formless realm are also shown together because they share similar explanations. Similarly, the non-percipient existence and the one-constituent existence. There, by two bases: the form-base and the mental-phenomena base. The same method applies to the elements. Indeed, the form-base is mentioned there because for the other Brahmās dwelling on the same plane, the eye exists, and that form serves as its object.

71. Jāti dvīhi khandhehīti rūpajāti rūpakkhandhena, arūpajāti saṅkhārakkhandhena. Jarāmaraṇesupi [V 0.0007] eseva nayo. Sokādīsupi [P 0.0120] ekena khandhenāti sokadukkhadomanassāni vedanākkhandhena, paridevo rūpakkhandhena, upāyāsādayo saṅkhārakkhandhenāti evaṃ khandhaviseso veditabbo.

71. Birth by two aggregates: material birth by the form aggregate, immaterial birth by the formations aggregate. The same principle applies to aging and death. In sorrow and the like, by one aggregate: sorrow, suffering, and displeasure belong to the feeling aggregate; lamentation to the form aggregate; despair and the like to the formations aggregate. Thus, the distinction among aggregates should be understood.

73. Iddhipādo dvīhīti saṅkhāraviññāṇakkhandhehi, manāyatanadhammāyatanehi, dhammadhātumanoviññāṇadhātūhi ca. Jhānaṃ dvīhīti vedanākkhandhasaṅkhārakkhandhehi. Appamaññādayo sadisavissajjanattā ekato niddiṭṭhā. Cittaṃ pana cetanānantaraṃ nikkhittampi asadisavissajjanattā pacchā gahitaṃ. Tattha appamaññādīsu ekena khandhenāti vedanā vedanākkhandhena, saññā saññākkhandhena, sesā saṅkhārakkhandhena saṅgahitāti evaṃ khandhaviseso veditabbo.

73. The basis of psychic power by two: the formations and consciousness aggregates; the mind-base and mental-phenomena base; and the mental-phenomena element and mind-consciousness element. Jhāna by two: the feeling and formations aggregates. The immeasurables and others are shown together because they share similar explanations. But the mind, although placed immediately after volition, is taken up later because its explanation is dissimilar. There, among the immeasurables and others, "by one aggregate" means: feeling is included in the feeling aggregate, perception in the perception aggregate, and the rest are included in the formations aggregate. Thus, the distinction among aggregates should be understood.

7. Tikapadavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Triad-Terms

77. Evaṃ [M 0.0007] abbhantaramātikāya saṅgahaṃ dassetvā idāni bāhiramātikāya saṅgahaṃ dassetuṃ kusalā dhammātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha vedanāttike tīhi dhātūhīti kāyaviññāṇamanoviññāṇadhammadhātūhi. Sattahi dhātūhīti cakkhusotaghānajivhāviññāṇadhātūhi ceva manodhātudhammadhātumanoviññāṇadhātūhi ca. Vipākattike aṭṭhahi dhātūhīti kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā saddhiṃ tāhiyeva. Vipākadhammadhammā pana saṃkiliṭṭhasaṃkilesikehi saddhiṃ sadisavissajjanattā ekato gahitā. Yathā cete, evaṃ sabbatikadukapadesu yaṃ yaṃ padaṃ yena yena padena saddhiṃ sadisavissajjanaṃ hoti, taṃ taṃ uppaṭipāṭiyāpi tena tena saddhiṃ gahetvā vissajjitaṃ. Tattha vuttānusāreneva saṅgahāsaṅgahanayo veditabboti.

77. Having thus shown the summary of the internal matrix, now, to present the summary of the external matrix, the section beginning with "Wholesome phenomena, etc." is commenced. There, in the feeling triad, by three elements: the body-consciousness, mind-consciousness, and mental-phenomena elements. By seven elements: the eye-, ear-, nose-, and tongue-consciousness elements, as well as the mind-element, mental-phenomena element, and mind-consciousness element. In the resultant triad, by eight elements: those very seven elements together with the body-consciousness element. But 'resultant-dhammas that are dhammas' are taken together with 'the defiled and defiling' due to their similar exposition. And just as these, so in all triad and dyad sections, whatever term has a similar exposition to another term, that is taken together with it and expounded, even out of sequence. There, the method of inclusion and exclusion should be understood according to what has been stated.

Saṅgahāsaṅgahapadavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Terms of Inclusion and Non-inclusion.

2. Dutiyanayo saṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā

2. The Second Method: Explanation of the Terms Not Included by the Included.

171. Idāni [P 0.0121] saṅgahitena asaṅgahitapadaṃ bhājetuṃ cakkhāyatanenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tatridaṃ [V 0.0008] lakkhaṇaṃ – imasmiñhi vāre yaṃ khandhapadena saṅgahitaṃ hutvā āyatanadhātupadehi asaṅgahitaṃ, khandhāyatanapadehi vā saṅgahitaṃ hutvā dhātupadena asaṅgahitaṃ, tassa khandhādīhi asaṅgahaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Taṃ pana rūpakkhandhādīsu na yujjati. Rūpakkhandhena hi rūpakkhandhova saṅgahito. So ca aḍḍhekādasahi āyatanadhātūhi asaṅgahito nāma natthi. Vedanākkhandhena ca vedanākkhandhova saṅgahito. Sopi dhammāyatanadhammadhātūhi asaṅgahito nāma natthi. Evaṃ asaṅgahitatāya abhāvato etāni aññāni ca evarūpāni manāyatanadhammāyatanādīni padāni imasmiṃ vāre na gahitāni. Yāni pana padāni rūpekadesaṃ arūpena asammissaṃ, viññāṇekadesañca aññena asammissaṃ dīpenti, tāni idha gahitāni. Pariyosāne ca –

171. Now, to analyze the terms not included by what is included, the section beginning 'by the eye-base,' etc., is commenced. Herein is the characteristic: in this section, that which, having been included by the aggregate-term, is not included by the sense-base and element terms; or that which, having been included by the aggregate and sense-base terms, is not included by the element-term—its non-inclusion by the aggregates, etc., is questioned and an explanation is given. This, however, does not apply to the form aggregate and so on. For by the form aggregate, only the form aggregate is included. And it is not the case that this is not included by the ten and a half sense-bases and elements. And by the feeling aggregate, only the feeling aggregate is included. And it is not the case that this is not included by the mind-object base and mind-object element. Thus, due to the absence of non-inclusion, these and other such terms—like the mind-base, mind-object base, etc.—are not taken up in this section. But those terms which indicate a portion of form unmixed with the formless, and a portion of consciousness unmixed with another—these are taken up here. And at the conclusion—

“Dasāyatanā [M 0.0008] sattarasa dhātuyo,

Sattindriyā asaññābhavo ekavokārabhavo;

Paridevo sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ,

Anidassanaṃ punadeva sappaṭighaṃ upādā”ti.

The ten sense-bases, the seventeen elements, the seven faculties, the realm of non-perception, the realm of one constituent; lamentation, the visible and resistant, the unseen and also resistant, and clinging.

Evaṃ uddānagāthāya dassitāneva. Tasmā tesaṃ vaseneva saṅgahāsaṅgaho veditabbo. Pañhavasena hi imasmiṃ vāre āyatanadhātuvaseneva sadisavissajjane vīsati dhamme samodhānetvā eko pañho kato, satta viññāṇadhātuyo samodhānetvā eko, sattindriyāni samodhānetvā eko, dve bhave samodhānetvā eko, paridevena ca sanidassanasappaṭighehi ca eko, anidassanasappaṭighehi eko, sanidassanehi eko, sappaṭighehi ca upādādhammehi ca ekoti aṭṭha pañhā katā. Tesu khandhādivibhāgo [P 0.0122] evaṃ veditabbo seyyathidaṃ – paṭhamapañhe tāva catūhi khandhehīti arūpakkhandhehi, dvīhāyatanehīti cakkhāyatanādīsu ekekena saddhiṃ manāyatanena, aṭṭhahi dhātūhīti cakkhudhātuādīsu ekekāya saddhiṃ sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi.

Thus, they are shown by the summary verse. Therefore, their inclusion and non-inclusion should be understood by means of them. Indeed, in this section, by way of questions, one question was made by combining twenty phenomena which have similar answers regarding the sense-bases and elements; one by combining the seven consciousness elements; one by combining the seven faculties; one by combining the two existences; one by combining lamentation with the visible and resistant phenomena; one by combining the invisible and resistant phenomena; one by combining the visible phenomena; and one by combining the resistant and the clinging phenomena—thus, eight questions were made. Among them, the division of aggregates and so on should be understood as follows: in the first question, 'by four aggregates' means the formless aggregates; 'by two sense-bases' means each of the eye sense-base and so on, together with the mind-base; and 'by eight elements' means each of the eye element and so on, together with the seven consciousness elements.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – cakkhāyatanena hi khandhasaṅgahena rūpakkhandho saṅgahito. Tasmiṃ saṅgahite rūpakkhandhe āyatanasaṅgahena cakkhāyatanamevekaṃ saṅgahitaṃ. Sesāni dasa āyatanāni asaṅgahitāni. Dhātusaṅgahenapi tena cakkhudhātuyevekā saṅgahitā. Sesā dasa dhātuyo asaṅgahitā. Iti yāni tena asaṅgahitāni dasāyatanāni, tāni cakkhāyatanamanāyatanehi dvīhi [V 0.0009] asaṅgahitāni. Yāpi tena asaṅgahitā dasa dhātuyo, tā cakkhudhātuyā ceva sattahi ca viññāṇadhātūhi asaṅgahitāti. Rūpāyatanādīsupi eseva nayo.

Herein is the method: By the eye sense-base, the form aggregate is included by way of aggregate inclusion. When that form aggregate is included, only the eye sense-base is included by way of sense-base inclusion. The remaining ten sense-bases are not included. And by way of element inclusion, only the eye element is included by that. The remaining ten elements are not included. Thus, those ten sense-bases not included by that are also not included by the two sense-bases, namely the eye sense-base and the mind sense-base. And those ten elements not included by that are also not included by the eye element and the seven consciousness elements. The same method applies to the form sense-base and so on.

172. Dutiyapañhe – yasmā yāya kāyaci viññāṇadhātuyā saṅgahito viññāṇakkhandho manāyatanena asaṅgahito nāma natthi, tasmā āyatanasaṅgahena saṅgahitāti vuttaṃ. Ettha pana catūhi khandhehīti rūpādīhi catūhi. Ekādasahāyatanehīti manāyatanavajjehi. Dvādasahi dhātūhīti yathānurūpā cha viññāṇadhātuyo apanetvā sesāhi dvādasahi. Cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā hi cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyeva saṅgahitā, itarā asaṅgahitā. Sotaviññāṇadhātuādīsupi eseva nayo.

172. In the second question, since the consciousness aggregate, when included by any consciousness element whatsoever, is never not included by the mind-base, it is therefore said to be 'included by way of sense-base inclusion.' Here, however, 'by the four aggregates' means by the four, beginning with form. 'By the eleven sense-bases' means excluding the mind-base. 'By the twelve elements' means by the remaining twelve, after removing the six corresponding consciousness elements. For by the eye-consciousness element, only the eye-consciousness element itself is included; the others are not included. The same method applies in the case of the ear-consciousness element, and so on.

173. Tatiyapañhe [M 0.0009] – cakkhundriyādīnaṃ vissajjanaṃ cakkhāyatanādisadisameva. Itthindriyapurisindriyesu pana dhammāyatanena saddhiṃ dve āyatanāni, dhammadhātuyā ca saddhiṃ aṭṭha dhātuyo veditabbā.

173. In the third question, the explanation for the eye faculty, etc., is similar to that for the eye-base, etc. However, in the case of the female faculty and male faculty, two sense-bases, together with the mind-object base, and eight elements, together with the mind-object element, should be understood.

174. Catutthapañhe – tīhāyatanehīti rūpāyatanadhammāyatanamanāyatanehi. Tesu hi bhavesu rūpāyatanadhammāyatanavasena dveva āyatanāni tehi saṅgahitāni[P 0.0123]. Sesāni nava rūpāyatanāni teheva ca dvīhi, manāyatanena cāti tīhi asaṅgahitāni nāma honti. Navahi dhātūhīti rūpadhātudhammadhātūhi saddhiṃ sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi.

174. In the fourth question, 'by three sense-bases' means by the form sense-base, the mind-object sense-base, and the mind sense-base. For in those existences, only two sense-bases are included by them, namely the form sense-base and the mind-object sense-base. The remaining nine physical sense-bases are not included by those very two, and also by the mind sense-base; thus they are not included by these three. 'By nine elements' means by the form element and the mind-object element, together with the seven consciousness elements.

175. Pañcamapañhe – dvīhāyatanehīti paṭhamapadaṃ sandhāya saddāyatanamanāyatanehi. Dutiyapadaṃ sandhāya rūpāyatanamanāyatanehi. Dhātuyopi tesaṃyeva ekekena saddhiṃ satta viññāṇadhātuyo veditabbā.

175. In the fifth question, 'by two sense-bases' means, with reference to the first term, by the sound sense-base and the mind-base. With reference to the second term, it means by the form sense-base and the mind-base. The elements, too, should be understood as the seven consciousness elements together with each of those.

176. Chaṭṭhapañhe – dasahāyatanehīti rūpāyatanadhammāyatanavajjehi. Soḷasahi dhātūhīti rūpadhātudhammadhātuvajjeheva. Kathaṃ? Anidassanasappaṭighā hi dhammā nāma nava oḷārikāyatanāni. Tehi khandhasaṅgahena saṅgahite rūpakkhandhe, āyatanasaṅgahena tāneva navāyatanāni saṅgahitāni. Rūpāyatanadhammāyatanāni asaṅgahitāni. Dhātusaṅgahenapi tā eva nava dhātuyo saṅgahitā. Rūpadhātudhammadhātuyo asaṅgahitā. Iti yāni tehi asaṅgahitāni dve āyatanāni[V 0.0010], tāni rūpāyatanavajjehi navahi oḷārikāyatanehi, manāyatanena cāti dasahi asaṅgahitāni. Yāpi tehi asaṅgahitā dve dhātuyo, tā rūpadhātuvajjāhi navahi oḷārikadhātūhi, sattahi ca viññāṇadhātūhīti soḷasahi asaṅgahitāti veditabbā.

176. In the sixth question, 'by ten sense-bases' means those excluding the form sense-base and the mind-object sense-base. 'By sixteen elements' means those excluding the form element and the mind-object element. How so? For the unseen and resistant phenomena are the nine gross sense-bases. When the form aggregate is included by them by way of aggregate inclusion, then by way of sense-base inclusion, those very nine sense-bases are included. The form sense-base and the mind-object sense-base are not included. And by way of element inclusion, those same nine elements are included. The form element and the mind-object element are not included. Thus, the two sense-bases not included by them are not included by the nine gross sense-bases which exclude the form sense-base, and by the mind sense-base—thus by ten. And the two elements not included by them are to be understood as not included by the nine gross elements which exclude the form element, and by the seven consciousness elements—thus by sixteen.

177. Sattamapañhe – dvīhāyatanehīti rūpāyatanamanāyatanehi. Aṭṭhahi dhātūhīti rūpadhātuyā saddhiṃ sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi.

177. In the seventh question – "by two sense-bases" means by the form sense-base and the mind sense-base. "By eight elements" means by the form element together with the seven consciousness elements.

178. Aṭṭhamapañhe – ekādasahāyatanehīti sappaṭighadhamme sandhāya dhammāyatanavajjehi, upādādhamme sandhāya phoṭṭhabbāyatanavajjehi. Dhātūsupi eseva nayo. Atthayojanā panettha heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbāti.

178. In the eighth question – "by eleven sense-bases" means referring to phenomena with impact, excluding the mental-object sense-base; referring to clung-to phenomena, excluding the tangible sense-base. The same principle applies to the elements. The meaning here should be understood according to the method stated below.

Saṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Section on 'Not Included by the Included'.

3. Tatiyanayo asaṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā

3. The Third Method: Explanation of the Section on 'Included by the Unincluded'.

179. Idāni [M 0.0010][P 0.0124] asaṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadaṃ bhājetuṃ vedanākkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tatridaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ – imasmiñhi vāre yaṃ khandhapadena asaṅgahitaṃ hutvā āyatanadhātupadehi saṅgahitaṃ, tassa khandhādīhi saṅgahaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Taṃ pana rūpakkhandhaviññāṇakkhandhacakkhāyatanādīsu na yujjati. Rūpakkhandhena hi cattāro khandhā khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā. Tesu tena ekadhammopi āyatanadhātusaṅgahena saṅgahito nāma natthi. Nanu ca vedanādayo dhammāyatanena saṅgahitāti? Saṅgahitā. Na pana rūpakkhandhova dhammāyatanaṃ, rūpakkhandhato hi sukhumarūpamattaṃ dhammāyatanaṃ bhajati. Tasmā ye dhammāyatanena saṅgahitā, na te rūpakkhandhena saṅgahitā nāma. Viññāṇakkhandhenapi itare cattāro khandhā asaṅgahitā. Tesu tena ekopi āyatanadhātusaṅgahena saṅgahito nāma natthi. Evaṃ saṅgahitatāya abhāvato etāni aññāni ca evarūpāni cakkhāyatanādīni padāni imasmiṃ vāre na gahitāni. Yāni pana padāni [V 0.0011] viññāṇena vā oḷārikarūpena vā asammissaṃ dhammāyatanekadesaṃ dīpenti, tāni idha gahitāni. Tesaṃ idamuddānaṃ –

179. Now begins the explanation of the section on 'Included by the Unincluded', starting with "by the aggregate of feeling," etc. Herein is the characteristic: In this section, that which is not included by the term 'aggregate' but is included by the terms 'sense-base' and 'element,' has been questioned and answered regarding its inclusion by aggregates, etc. However, this does not apply to the aggregate of form, the aggregate of consciousness, the eye-base, etc. For, by the aggregate of form, the other four aggregates are not included by way of aggregate-inclusion. Among them, not even a single phenomenon is included by way of sense-base or element-inclusion. But are not feeling, etc., included by the mind-object base? They are included. Yet, the aggregate of form is not the mind-object base, for only subtle form from the aggregate of form belongs to the mind-object base. Therefore, what is included by the mind-object base is not included by the aggregate of form. Similarly, the other four aggregates are not included by the aggregate of consciousness. Among them, not even one is included by way of sense-base or element-inclusion. Thus, due to the absence of such inclusion, these and other similar terms—such as the eye-base, etc.—are not taken up in this section. However, those terms that indicate a part of the mind-object base without being mixed with consciousness or gross form are included here. This is the summary of them—

“Tayo khandhā tathā saccā, indriyāni ca soḷasa;

Padāni paccayākāre, cuddasūpari cuddasa.

Three aggregates, likewise the truths, and sixteen faculties; Terms in the mode of conditionality, fourteen upon fourteen.

“Samatiṃsa padā honti, gocchakesu dasasvatha;

Duve cūḷantaradukā, aṭṭha honti mahantarā”ti.

There are thirty-two terms, and ten in the clusters; Two are minor internal dyads, eight are major internal ones.

Etesu pana padesu sadisavissajjanāni padāni ekato katvā sabbepi dvādasa pañhā vuttā. Tesu evaṃ khandhavibhāgo veditabbo. Āyatanadhātūsu pana bhedo natthi. Tattha paṭhamapañhe tāva – tīhi khandhehīti rūpasaññāsaṅkhārakkhandhehi. Āyatanadhātuyo pana dhammāyatanadhammadhātuvasena veditabbā.

Among these terms, grouping together those that have similar explanations, all twelve questions have been stated. Among them, the division by aggregates should be understood thus. However, there is no distinction in the sense-bases and elements. There, in the first question, "by three aggregates" refers to the aggregates of form, perception, and mental formations. The sense-bases and elements, however, should be understood as the mind-object base and the mind-object element.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – vedanākkhandhena hi nibbānañca sukhumarūpasaññāsaṅkhārā [P 0.0125] ca khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā hutvā āyatanadhātusaṅgahena saṅgahitā. Tesu nibbānaṃ khandhasaṅgahaṃ na gacchati, sesā rūpasaññāsaṅkhārakkhandhehi saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Āyatanadhātusaṅgahaṃ pana nibbānampi gacchateva. Tena vuttaṃ [M 0.0011] – “asaṅkhataṃ khandhato ṭhapetvā tīhi khandhehi, ekenāyatanena, ekāya dhātuyā saṅgahitā”ti. Saññākkhandhapakkhe panettha saññaṃ apanetvā vedanāya saddhiṃ tayo khandhā saṅkhārādīsu saṅkhārakkhandhaṃ apanetvā rūpavedanāsaññāvasena tayo khandhā veditabbā.

Herein is the method: By the feeling aggregate, Nibbāna and subtle form, perception, and mental formations, though not included by way of aggregate-inclusion, are included by way of sense-base and element-inclusion. Among these, Nibbāna is not included by aggregates, while the remaining—subtle form, perception, and mental formations—are included by the aggregates of form, perception, and mental formations. However, Nibbāna is indeed included by way of sense-bases and elements. Therefore, it is said: "Having excluded the unconditioned from the aggregates, it is included by three aggregates, one sense-base, and one element." And here, in the case of the perception aggregate, having excluded perception, the three aggregates should be understood as form, feeling, and mental formations; and in cases such as the mental formation aggregate, having excluded the mental formation aggregate, the three aggregates should be understood as form, feeling, and perception.

180. Dutiye – catūhi khandhehīti viññāṇavajjehi. Te hi nirodhena khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā hutvā āyatanadhātusaṅgahena saṅgahitā.

180. In the second, "by four aggregates" refers to those excluding consciousness. For they, by way of cessation, though not included by way of aggregate-inclusion, are included by way of sense-base and element-inclusion.

181. Tatiye – dvīhīti vedanāsaññākkhandhehi. Rūpārūpajīvitindriyena hi vedanāsaññāviññāṇakkhandhā ca khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā. Tesu pana vedanāsaññāva āyatanadhātusaṅgahena saṅgahitā. Tena vuttaṃ – “vedanāsaññākkhandhehī”ti. Iminā upāyena sabbattha khandhabhedo veditabbo. Ito parañhi khandhānaṃ nāmamattameva vakkhāma.

181. Thirdly – by two, meaning by the aggregates of feeling and perception. For, by the life faculty, the aggregates of feeling, perception, and consciousness are not included by way of aggregate-inclusion. Among these, however, feeling and perception alone are included by way of sense-base and element-inclusion. Therefore, it is said: "by the aggregates of feeling and perception." By this method, the distinction of aggregates should be understood everywhere. For from here onwards, we will speak only of the mere names of the aggregates.

182. Catutthe [V 0.0012] – tīhi khandhehīti itthindriyapurisindriyesu vedanāsaññāsaṅkhārehi, vedanāpañcake rūpasaññāsaṅkhārehi; saddhindriyādīsu phassapariyosānesu rūpavedanāsaññākkhandhehi. Vedanāya vedanākkhandhasadisova taṇhupādānakammabhavesu saṅkhārakkhandhasadisova vinicchayo.

182. In the fourth—by three aggregates: in the faculties of femininity and masculinity, by feeling, perception, and formations; in the fivefold feeling, by form, perception, and formations; in the faculties of faith, etc., ending with contact, by the aggregates of form, feeling, and perception. As for feeling, the determination is similar to that of the feeling aggregate; and in the case of craving, clinging, and kamma-becoming, the determination is similar to that of the mental formation aggregate.

183. Pañcame – jātijarāmaraṇesu jīvitindriyasadisova. Jhānena pana nibbānaṃ sukhumarūpaṃ saññā ca khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā hutvā āyatanadhātusaṅgahena saṅgahitā. Tasmā taṃ sandhāya rūpakkhandhasaññākkhandhānaṃ vasena dve khandhā veditabbā.

183. In the fifth—in the case of birth, aging, and death, it is similar to the life faculty. However, with regard to jhāna, Nibbāna, subtle form, and perception, though not included by way of aggregate-inclusion, are included by way of sense-base and element-inclusion. Therefore, with reference to that, two aggregates should be understood by way of the aggregate of form and the aggregate of perception.

184. Chaṭṭhe – sokādittaye vedanāya sadiso. Upāyāsādīsu saṅkhārasadiso. Puna vedanāya vedanākkhandhasadiso, saññāya saññākkhandhasadiso, cetanādīsu saṅkhārakkhandhasadiso [P 0.0126] vinicchayo. Iminā upāyena sattamapañhādīsupi saṅgahāsaṅgaho veditabboti.

184. In the sixth—in the triad beginning with sorrow, it is similar to feeling. In despair, etc., it is similar to formations. Further, the determination for feeling is similar to that of the feeling aggregate; for perception, it is similar to that of the perception aggregate; and in the case of volition, etc., it is similar to that of the formation aggregate. By this method, inclusion and non-inclusion should also be understood in the seventh question, etc.

Asaṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Section on 'Included by the Unincluded'.

4. Catutthanayo saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā

4. The Fourth Method: Explanation of the Section on 'Included by the Included'.

191. Idāni [M 0.0012] saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadaṃ bhājetuṃ samudayasaccenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yaṃ khandhādīhi saṅgahitena khandhādivasena saṅgahitaṃ, puna tasseva khandhādīhi saṅgahaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Taṃ khandhāyatanadhātūsu ekampi sakalakoṭṭhāsaṃ gahetvā ṭhitapadesu na yujjati. Sakalena hi khandhādipadena aññaṃ khandhādivasena saṅgahitaṃ nāma natthi, yaṃ attano saṅgāhakaṃ saṅgaṇhitvā puna teneva saṅgahaṃ gaccheyya. Tasmā tathārūpāni padāni imasmiṃ vāre na gahitāni. Yāni pana padāni saṅkhārekadesaṃ vā aññena asammissaṃ dīpenti – vedanekadesaṃ vā sukhumarūpaṃ vā saddekadesaṃ vā, tāni idha gahitāni. Tesaṃ idamuddānaṃ –

191. Now, to analyze the term 'included by the included,' the section beginning with 'by the truth of origin' and so forth is undertaken. Herein, that which is included by the aggregates and so forth, is included in terms of the aggregates and so forth; then, having been questioned again about its inclusion by those same aggregates and so forth, a reply is given. This does not apply to terms that stand for even a single complete portion of the aggregates, sense bases, or elements. For by a complete term for aggregates and so forth, there is nothing else included in terms of aggregates and so forth, which, having included its own includer, would again be included by that same one. Therefore, such terms are not taken in this section. But those terms that indicate a part of formations, or—unmixed with anything else—a part of feeling, or subtle form, or a part of sound, are taken here. Their summary is as follows:

“Dve saccā pannarasindriyā, ekādasa paṭiccapadā;

Uddhaṃ puna ekādasa, gocchakapadamettha tiṃsavidha”nti.

“Two truths, fifteen faculties, eleven factors of dependent origination; further, again eleven; here the collective term is thirtyfold.”

Pañhā [V 0.0013] panettha dveyeva honti. Tattha yaṃ pucchāya uddhaṭaṃ padaṃ, tadeva yehi dhammehi khandhādivasena saṅgahitaṃ, te dhamme sandhāya sabbattha ekena khandhenātiādi vuttaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ nayo – samudayasaccena hi taṇhāvajjā sesā saṅkhārā khandhādisaṅgahena saṅgahitā. Puna tehi taṇhāva saṅgahitā. Sā [P 0.0127] taṇhā puna saṅkhāreheva khandhādisaṅgahena saṅgahitāti. Eseva nayo sabbattha. Arūpadhammapucchāsu panettha saṅkhārakkhandho vā vedanākkhandho vā eko khandho nāma. Rūpadhammapucchāsu rūpakkhandho. Paridevapucchāya saddāyatanaṃ ekaṃ āyatanaṃ nāma. Saddadhātu ekā dhātu nāma, sesaṭṭhānesu dhammāyatanadhammadhātuvaseneva attho veditabboti.

Here, there are only two questions. Herein, with reference to those phenomena by which the term extracted in the question is included in terms of aggregates and so forth, it is said everywhere, 'by one aggregate,' and so on. Herein, this is the method: by the truth of origin, the remaining formations, excluding craving, are included by the inclusion of aggregates and so forth. Again, by them, craving is included. That craving is again included by those very formations through the inclusion of aggregates and so forth. This is the method everywhere. In questions about immaterial phenomena, the aggregate of formations or the aggregate of feeling is called 'one aggregate.' In questions about material phenomena, the aggregate of form. In the question about lamentation, the sound base is called 'one sense base.' The sound element is 'one element.' In the remaining instances, the meaning should be understood by way of the mind-object base and the mind-object element.

Saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Term 'Included by the Included'.

5. Pañcamanayo asaṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā

5. The Fifth Method: The Explanation of the Term 'Unincluded by the Unincluded'.

193. Idāni asaṅgahitena asaṅgahitapadaṃ bhājetuṃ rūpakkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yaṃ khandhādīhi asaṅgahitena khandhādivasena asaṅgahitaṃ, puna tasseva khandhādīhi asaṅgahaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Taṃ pañcakkhandhaggāhakesu dukkhasaccādīsu [M 0.0013] viññāṇena saddhiṃ sukhumarūpaggāhakesu anidassanaappaṭighādīsu ca padesu na yujjati. Tādisena hi padena nibbānaṃ khandhasaṅgahamattaṃ na gaccheyya. Sesā khandhādīhi asaṅgahitadhammā nāma natthi. Tasmā tathārūpāni padāni imasmiṃ vāre na gahitāni. Yāni pana pañcakkhandhe viññāṇañca sukhumarūpena saddhiṃ ekato na dīpenti, tāni idha gahitāni. Tesaṃ idamuddānaṃ –

193. Now, to analyze the term 'unincluded by the unincluded,' the section beginning with 'by the aggregate of form' and so forth is undertaken. Herein, that which is unincluded by the aggregates and so forth, is unincluded in terms of the aggregates and so forth; then, when questioned again regarding its non-inclusion by those same aggregates and so forth, a reply is given. This does not apply to terms that grasp the five aggregates, such as the truth of suffering and so forth, nor to terms that grasp subtle form together with consciousness, such as the invisible and non-resistant and so forth. For by such a term, Nibbāna would not be merely included among the aggregates. There are no other phenomena that are unincluded by the aggregates and so forth. Therefore, such terms are not taken in this section. But those terms which do not indicate the five aggregates and consciousness together with subtle form as one, are taken here. Their summary is as follows:

“Sabbe khandhā tathāyatanadhātuyo saccato tayo;

Indriyānipi sabbāni, tevīsati paṭiccato.

“All aggregates, likewise sense bases and elements; three by way of truths; all faculties too; twenty-three by way of dependent origination.”

“Parato soḷasa padā, tecattālīsakaṃ tike;

Gocchake sattati dve ca, satta cūḷantare padā.

“Sixteen terms from the other section, forty-three in the triads; seventy-two in the groups, and seven terms in the minor intermediate sections.”

“Mahantare [V 0.0014] padā vuttā, aṭṭhārasa tato paraṃ;

Aṭṭhāraseva ñātabbā, sesā idha na bhāsitā”ti.

“In the major intermediate sections, eighteen terms are stated; beyond that, eighteen alone should be known, the rest are not spoken of here.”

Pañhā panettha sadisavissajjanānaṃ vasena samodhānetvā katihi saddhiṃ sabbepi catuttiṃsa honti. Tattha yaṃ [P 0.0128] pucchāya uddhaṭaṃ padaṃ, tadeva yehi khandhādīhi asaṅgahitaṃ, te dhamme sandhāya ekena khandhenātiādi vuttaṃ.

Here, the questions, when harmonized by way of their similar answers, amount to thirty-four in all. Herein, with reference to those phenomena by which the term extracted in the question is unincluded by the aggregates and so forth, it is said, 'by one aggregate,' and so on.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – rūpakkhandhena hi cattāro khandhā nibbānañca khandhasaṅgahena asaṅgahitā. Āyatanadhātusaṅgahena pana ṭhapetvā viññāṇaṃ avasesā saṅgahitāti viññāṇameva tīhipi khandhasaṅgahādīhi asaṅgahitaṃ nāma. Puna tena viññāṇena saddhiṃ nibbānena cattāro khandhā khandhādisaṅgahena asaṅgahitā. Te sabbepi puna viññāṇeneva khandhādisaṅgahena asaṅgahitāti ekena khandhena, ekenāyatanena, sattahi dhātūhi asaṅgahitā nāma honti. Atha vā – yadetaṃ rūpakkhandhena viññāṇameva tīhi khandhādisaṅgahehi asaṅgahitaṃ, tehipi viññāṇadhammehi te rūpadhammāva tīhi saṅgahehi asaṅgahitā. Puna te rūpadhammā viññāṇeneva tīhi saṅgahehi asaṅgahitā. Viññāṇañca khandhato eko viññāṇakkhandho hoti, āyatanato ekaṃ manāyatanaṃ, dhātuto satta viññāṇadhātuyo. Tasmā “ekena khandhenā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Iminā upāyena sabbattha yaṃ pucchāya uddhaṭaṃ padaṃ, tadeva yehi dhammehi khandhādivasena asaṅgahitaṃ, tesaṃ dhammānaṃ vasena khandhādayo veditabbā. Tattha dutiyapañhe tāva – rūpaviññāṇānaṃ vasena [M 0.0014] veditabbā. Vedanādayo hi rūpaviññāṇeheva khandhādisaṅgahena asaṅgahitā. Te ca dve khandhā ekādasāyatanāni sattarasa dhātuyo honti.

Herein, this is the method: By the aggregate of form, the four aggregates and Nibbāna are unincluded by the inclusion of aggregates. However, by the inclusion of sense bases and elements, setting aside consciousness, the remainder are included; thus, consciousness alone is what is called 'unincluded' by the three—the inclusion of aggregates and so forth. Again, together with that consciousness and Nibbāna, the four aggregates are unincluded by the inclusion of aggregates and so forth. All of them, again, are unincluded by the inclusion of aggregates and so forth through consciousness alone. Thus, they are said to be unincluded by one aggregate, one sense base, and seven elements. Alternatively, just as by the aggregate of form, consciousness alone is unincluded by the three inclusions of aggregates and so forth, so too by those consciousness-phenomena, those very form-phenomena are unincluded by the three inclusions. Again, those form-phenomena are unincluded by the three inclusions through consciousness alone. And consciousness, from the perspective of aggregates, is the one aggregate of consciousness; from the perspective of sense bases, it is the one mind base; and from the perspective of elements, it is the seven consciousness elements. Therefore, it is said, 'by one aggregate,' and so on. By this method, in all cases, the aggregates and so forth should be understood in terms of those phenomena by which the very term extracted in the question is unincluded. Therein, in the second question, for instance, they should be understood in terms of form and consciousness. For feeling and the rest are unincluded by the inclusion of aggregates and so forth through form and consciousness alone. And these are two aggregates, eleven sense bases, and seventeen elements.

195. Tatiyapañhe – viññāṇaṃ rūpādīhi catūhi asaṅgahitanti tesaṃ vasena khandhādayo veditabbā.

195. In the third question, consciousness is unincluded by the four beginning with form; in terms of these, the aggregates and so forth should be understood.

196. Catutthapañhe – cakkhāyatanaṃ vedanādīhi catūhīti iminā nayena sabbattha khandhādayo veditabbā. Pariyosāne – rūpañca dhammāyatananti uddānagāthāya dassitadhammāyeva aññenākārena saṅkhipitvā dassitāti.

196. In the fourth question—the eye-base is unincluded by the four beginning with feeling—by this method the aggregates and so forth should be understood everywhere. At the conclusion—'and form and the mind-object base'—the very phenomena shown in the summary verse are presented concisely in another manner.

Asaṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Term 'Unincluded by the Unincluded'.

6. Chaṭṭhanayo sampayogavippayogapadavaṇṇanā

6. The Sixth Method: The Explanation of the Terms 'Association' and 'Dissociation'.

228. Idāni [P 0.0129][V 0.0015] sampayogavippayogapadaṃ bhājetuṃ rūpakkhandhotiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yaṃ labbhati yañca na labbhati taṃ sabbaṃ pucchāya gahitaṃ. Vissajjane pana yaṃ na labbhati, taṃ natthīti paṭikkhittaṃ. Catūhi sampayogo, catūhi vippayogo; sabhāgo visabhāgoti hi vacanato catūhi arūpakkhandheheva sabhāgānaṃ ekasantānasmiṃ ekakkhaṇe uppannānaṃ arūpakkhandhānaṃyeva aññamaññaṃ sampayogo labbhati. Rūpadhammānaṃ pana rūpena nibbānena vā, nibbānassa ca rūpena saddhiṃ sampayogo nāma natthi. Tathā rūpanibbānānaṃ arūpakkhandhehi, visabhāgā hi te tesaṃ. Yathā ca arūpakkhandhānaṃ rūpanibbānehi, evaṃ bhinnasantānehi nānākkhaṇikehi arūpadhammehipi saddhiṃ natthiyeva. Tepi hi tesaṃ santānakkhaṇavisabhāgatāya visabhāgāyeva. Ayaṃ pana visabhāgatā saṅgahaṭṭhena virujjhanato saṅgahanaye natthi. Gaṇanūpagamattañhi saṅgahaṭṭho. Sampayoganaye pana atthi, ekuppādatādilakkhaṇañhi sampayogaṭṭhoti. Evamettha yassa ekadhammenapi sampayogalakkhaṇaṃ na yujjhati, tassa pucchāya saṅgahaṃ katvāpi natthīti paṭikkhepo kato. Yassa vippayogalakkhaṇaṃ yujjati, tassa vippayogo dassito. Yāni pana padāni sattasu viññāṇadhātūsu ekāyapi avippayutte rūpena nibbānena vā missakadhamme dīpenti, tāni sabbathāpi idha na yujjantīti na gahitāni. Tesaṃ idamuddānaṃ –

228. Now, in order to analyze the terms 'association' and 'dissociation', the section beginning with 'the form aggregate', etc., has been commenced. Herein, whatever is obtainable and whatever is not obtainable—all that is included in the question. But in the answer, whatever is not obtainable is rejected as 'it does not exist'. Association is with four, dissociation is with four. For, according to the statement 'homogeneous and heterogeneous', association is obtained only among the four immaterial aggregates themselves, which are homogeneous, having arisen in a single moment within a single continuum. However, there is no such thing as association of material phenomena with matter or Nibbāna, nor of Nibbāna with matter. Similarly, there is no association of matter and Nibbāna with the immaterial aggregates, for they are heterogeneous to them. Just as the immaterial aggregates do not associate with matter or Nibbāna, so too they do not associate with immaterial phenomena from different continuums or arising in different moments. These too are heterogeneous to them due to the difference in their continuum and moment. But this heterogeneity is not relevant in the method of inclusion because it conflicts with the meaning of inclusion. For the meaning of inclusion is merely being subject to counting. In the method of association, however, it is relevant, because the meaning of association is characterized by having a single arising, etc. Thus, here, in respect of whatever does not fit the characteristic of association even with a single phenomenon, although it is included in the question, its existence is rejected. Whatever fits the characteristic of dissociation is shown as dissociated. But the terms that indicate phenomena mixed with matter or Nibbāna, which are not dissociated from even one of the seven consciousness elements, are entirely unsuitable here and thus are not included. Their summary is as follows:

“Dhammāyatanaṃ [M 0.0015] dhammadhātu, dukkhasaccañca jīvitaṃ;

Saḷāyatanaṃ nāmarūpaṃ, cattāro ca mahābhavā.

The mental-objects base, the mental-objects element, the truth of suffering, and life; the six sense bases, name-and-form, and the four great primary elements.

“Jātijarā ca maraṇaṃ, tikesvekūnavīsati;

Gocchakesu ca paññāsa, aṭṭha cūḷantare padā.

Birth, aging, and death; nineteen in the triads; fifty in the groups; and eight terms in the minor section.

“Mahantare pannarasa, aṭṭhārasa tato pare;

Tevīsa padasataṃ etaṃ, sampayoge na labbhatī”ti.

Fifteen in the great section, eighteen thereafter; these one hundred and twenty-three terms are not obtainable in association.

Dhammāyatanañhi [P 0.0130] rūpanibbānamissakattā tasmiṃ apariyāpannena viññāṇenapi na sakkā sampayuttanti [V 0.0016] vattuṃ. Yasmā panettha vedanādayo viññāṇena sampayuttā, tasmā vippayuttantipi na sakkā vattuṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Evaṃ sabbatthāpi etāni na yujjantīti idha na gahitāni. Sesāni khandhādīni yujjantīti tāni gahetvā ekekavasena ca samodhānena ca pañhavissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Tesu pañhesu, paṭhame – ekenāyatanenāti manāyatanena. Kehicīti dhammāyatanadhammadhātupariyāpannehi vedanāsaññāsaṅkhārehi.

For the mental-objects base, owing to its being mixed with matter and Nibbāna, it cannot be said to be associated even with consciousness not included within it. But since here feeling, etc., are associated with consciousness, they cannot be said to be dissociated either. The same method applies to the rest. Thus, these are entirely unsuitable everywhere and are not included here. The remaining aggregates, etc., are suitable, so they are included, and the answers to the questions are given individually and collectively. Among these questions, in the first—'with one base'—means with the mind base. 'With some' means with feeling, perception, and formations included in the mental-objects base and the mental-objects element.

229. Dutiye – tīhīti pucchitaṃ pucchitaṃ ṭhapetvā sesehi. Kehici sampayuttoti vedanākkhandho saññāsaṅkhārehi. Itarepi attānaṃ ṭhapetvā itarehi. Kehici vippayuttoti rūpanibbānehi. Evaṃ sabbattha rūpassa vippayoge dhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu arūpaṃ, arūpassa vippayoge rūpaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tatiyapañho uttānatthova.

229. In the second [question]—'with three' means with the remaining items, after excluding the one asked about. 'Associated with some' means the feeling aggregate is associated with perception and formations. The others also, excluding themselves, are associated with the others. 'Dissociated with some' means with matter and Nibbāna. Thus, everywhere, in the dissociation of matter, the immaterial part of the mental-objects base and mental-objects element should be understood; in the dissociation of the immaterial, matter should be understood. The meaning of the third question is straightforward.

231. Catutthe – ‘katihi khandhehī’tiādiṃ avatvā sampayuttanti natthīti vuttaṃ. Taṃ pana khandhādīnaṃyeva vasena veditabbaṃ. Paratopi evarūpesu pañhesu eseva nayo. Ādipañhasmiñhi sarūpato dassetvā parato pāḷi saṃkhittā. Iminā nayena sabbattha atthayojanā veditabbā. Yattha pana nātipākaṭā bhavissati, tattha naṃ pākaṭaṃ katvāva gamissāma.

231. In the fourth [question]—without stating 'with how many aggregates?' and so forth, it is stated, 'there is no association.' However, this is to be understood in terms of the aggregates, etc., themselves. This same method applies to similar questions thereafter. For in the first question the meaning is shown in its own form, but subsequently the Pāli is abbreviated. By this method, the application of the meaning should be understood everywhere. But where it is not very clear, we shall proceed only after making it manifest.

234. Soḷasahi dhātūhīti cakkhuviññāṇadhātu tāva attānaṃ ṭhapetvā chahi viññāṇadhātūhi, dasahi ca rūpadhātūhi. Sesāsupi eseva nayo.

234. 'With sixteen elements' means: the eye-consciousness element, excluding itself, is dissociated from the six other consciousness elements and the ten material elements. The same method applies to the rest.

235. Tīhi [M 0.0016] khandhehīti saṅkhārakkhandhaṃ ṭhapetvā sesehi. Ekāya dhātuyāti manoviññāṇadhātuyā. Samudayamaggānañhi aññāya dhātuyā sampayogo natthi. Ekena khandhenāti saṅkhārakkhandhena. Ekenāyatanenāti dhammāyatanena. Ekāya [P 0.0131] dhātuyāti dhammadhātuyā. Etesu hi taṃ saccadvayaṃ kehici sampayuttaṃ.

235. 'With three aggregates' means with the remaining [aggregates], excluding the formations aggregate. 'With one element' means with the mind-consciousness element. For there is no association of the truths of origin and path with any other element. 'With one aggregate' means with the formations aggregate. 'With one base' means with the mental-objects base. 'With one element' means with the mental-objects element. For in these, those two truths are associated with some [of their components].

238. Sukhindriyādipañhe – tīhīti saññāsaṅkhāraviññāṇehi. Ekāya dhātuyāti kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā, manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca. Chahi dhātūhīti kāyaviññāṇadhātuvajjāhi.

238. In the question on the faculty of pleasure, etc.—'with three' means with perception, formations, and consciousness. 'With one element' means with the body-consciousness element and the mind-consciousness element. 'With six elements' means with those excluding the body-consciousness element.

245. Rūpabhavapañhe – sabbesampi arūpakkhandhānaṃ arūpāyatanānañca atthitāya na kehicīti [V 0.0017] vuttaṃ. Ghānajivhākāyaviññāṇadhātūnaṃ pana natthitāya tīhi dhātūhi vippayuttoti vuttaṃ.

245. In the question on the form realm—since all immaterial aggregates and immaterial bases exist, it is said that they are not associated 'with any'. However, because the nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, and body-consciousness elements do not exist [there], it is said that they are 'dissociated from three elements'.

256. Adhimokkhapañhe – dvīhi dhātūhīti manodhātumanoviññāṇadhātūhi. Pannarasahīti sesāhi dasahi rūpadhātūhi, pañcahi ca cakkhuviññāṇādīhi.

256. In the question on resolution—'with two elements' means with the mind element and the mind-consciousness element. 'With fifteen' means with the ten material elements and the five [sense] consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness.

257. Kusalapañhe – kusalehi catunnampi khandhānaṃ gahitattā sampayogo paṭikkhitto.

257. In the question on the wholesome, association is rejected because all four [immaterial] aggregates are included in the wholesome.

258. Vedanāttikapañhe – ekena khandhenāti vedanākkhandheneva. Pannarasahīti cakkhusotaghānajivhāviññāṇadhātumanodhātūhi ceva rūpadhātūhi ca. Ekādasahīti kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā saddhiṃ rūpadhātūhi.

258. In the question on the triad of feeling—'with one aggregate' means only with the feeling aggregate. 'With fifteen' means with the eye-, ear-, nose-, and tongue-consciousness elements, the mind element, and the ten material elements. 'With eleven' means with the body-consciousness element together with the ten material elements.

262. Nevavipākanavipākadhammadhammapañhe – pañcahīti cakkhuviññāṇādīhi. Anupādinnaanupādāniyapañhe – chahīti manoviññāṇadhātuvajjāhi. Savitakkasavicārapañhe – pannarasahīti pañcahi viññāṇehi saddhiṃ rūpadhātūhi. Avitakkavicāramattapañhe – ekena khandhenātiādi saṅkhārakkhandhavaseneva veditabbaṃ. Dutiyajjhānavicārañhi ṭhapetvā sesā avitakkavicāramattā nāma. Pītiṃ ṭhapetvā sesā pītisahagatā. Tattha vicāro vicārena, pīti ca pītiyā na sampayuttāti saṅkhārakkhandhadhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu kehici sampayuttā nāma. Soḷasahīti dhammadhātumanoviññāṇadhātuvajjāheva. Avitakkaavicārapañhe [P 0.0132][M 0.0017] – ekāya dhātuyāti manodhātuyā. Sukhasahagatā upekkhāsahagatā ca vedanāttike vuttāva. Dassanenapahātabbādayo kusalasadisāva.

262. In the questions concerning phenomena that are neither resultant nor productive of result—'five' means the eye-consciousness, etc. In the questions concerning the non-grasped and not to be grasped—'six' means those excluding the mind-consciousness element. In the questions concerning the states with initial and sustained thought—'fifteen' means the five consciousnesses together with the form elements. In the questions concerning the states without initial thought but with only sustained thought—'with one aggregate', etc., should be understood in terms of the formations aggregate. For, excepting the sustained thought of the second jhāna, the remaining are designated as 'without initial thought but with only sustained thought'. Excluding joy, the remaining are accompanied by joy. There, sustained thought is not associated with sustained thought, and joy is not associated with joy; thus, they are associated with some in the formations aggregate, the mental-objects base, and the mental-objects element. 'Sixteen' means those excluding the mental-objects element and the mind-consciousness element. In the questions concerning the states without initial and without sustained thought—'one element' means the mind element. States accompanied by pleasure and by equanimity are as stated in the triad on feelings. Those to be abandoned by vision, and so forth, are similar to the wholesome.

271. Parittārammaṇaṃ vipākadhammasadisaṃ. Ekāya dhātuyāti dhammadhātuyā. Kehicīti ye tattha parittārammaṇā na honti, tehi. Dhammadhātu pana parittārammaṇānaṃ channaṃ cittuppādānaṃ vasena catūhi khandhehi saṅgahitattā paṭhamapaṭikkhepameva bhajati. Mahaggatārammaṇādayo kusalasadisāva.

271. The question on limited objects is similar to that on resultant phenomena. 'With one element' means with the mental-objects element. 'With some' means with those that do not have a limited object. The mental-objects element, however, being included by four aggregates in respect of the six arisings of consciousness with limited objects, partakes of the first negation. The questions on exalted objects, etc., are just like those on the wholesome.

273. Anuppannesu – pañcahi dhātūhīti cakkhuviññāṇādīhi. Tāni hi ekantena uppādidhammabhūtāneva, uppannakoṭṭhāsampi pana bhajanti. Paccuppannārammaṇādayo parittārammaṇasadisāva[V 0.0018]. Hetuādayo samudayasadisāva. Sahetukā ceva na ca hetūpi pītisahagatasadisāva. Tathā parāmāsasampayuttā. Anupādinnā anuppannasadisāva. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

273. In the question on the unarisen—'by five elements' means eye-consciousness and so forth. These are indeed entirely phenomena whose nature is to arise, yet they also partake of the arisen portion. The questions on present objects, and so forth, are similar to those on limited objects. The questions on conditions, and so forth, are similar to those on origination. States that are with a root condition and yet are not themselves root conditions are similar to those accompanied by joy. Similarly, those associated with clinging. The ungrasped are similar to the unarisen. The remainder is clear in meaning everywhere.

Sampayogavippayogapadavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Terms 'Conjoined' and 'Disjoined'.

7. Sattamanayo sampayuttenavippayuttapadavaṇṇanā

7. The Seventh Method: Explanation of the Term 'Disjoined from the Conjoined'.

306. Idāni sampayuttenavippayuttapadaṃ bhājetuṃ vedanākkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tatridaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ – imasmiñhi vāre pucchāya uddhaṭapadena ye dhammā sampayuttā, tehi ye dhammā vippayuttā, tesaṃ khandhādīhi vippayogaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Taṃ pana rūpakkhandhādīsu na yujjati. Rūpakkhandhena hi sampayuttā nāma natthi. Tasmā tañca aññāni ca evarūpāni padāni imasmiṃ vāre na gahitāni. Yāni pana padāni dhammadhātuyā [P 0.0133] sampayutte dhamme viññāṇañca aññena asammissaṃ dīpenti, tāni idha gahitāni. Tesaṃ idamuddānaṃ –

306. Now, in order to analyze the term 'disjoined from the conjoined,' the exposition beginning 'by the feeling aggregate,' etc., is undertaken. Here is the characteristic: in this section, concerning the term extracted for the question, an answer is given about the disjunction from aggregates, etc., of those phenomena that are disjoined from the phenomena conjoined with that term. This, however, does not apply in the case of the form aggregate, and so forth. For indeed, there are no phenomena conjoined with the form aggregate. Therefore, that and other such terms are not included in this section. But those terms are included here which indicate phenomena conjoined with the phenomena-element, and consciousness unmixed with anything else. Their summary is as follows:

“Cattāro [M 0.0018] khandhāyatanañca ekaṃ,

Dve indriyā dhātupadāni satta;

Tayo paṭiccā atha phassasattakaṃ,

Tike tayo satta mahantare ca.

Four aggregates, and one base; Two faculties, seven element-terms; Three [factors of] dependent origination, then the heptad of contact; Three triads, and seven great pairs.

“Ekaṃ savitakkaṃ, savicāramekaṃ;

Yuttaṃ upekkhāya ca ekamevā”ti.

One with initial thought; one with sustained thought; and one conjoined with equanimity, just one.

Pariyosāne – khandhā caturotiādināpi ayamevattho saṅgahito. Tattha yāni padāni sadisavissajjanāni, tāni uppaṭipāṭiyāpi samodhānetvā tattha vedanākkhandhādikā pañhā katā. Tesu evaṃ khandhādivibhāgo veditabbo. Vedanākkhandhādipañhe tāva – ekenāti manāyatanena. Sattahīti viññāṇadhātūhi. Kehicīti dhammāyatane vedanādīhi. Viññāṇadhātupañhe [V 0.0019] – te dhammā na kehicīti te pucchāya uddhaṭapadaṃ viññāṇadhātuṃ ṭhapetvā sesā cha viññāṇadhātudhammā, rūpaṃ, nibbānañca. Tehi sabbesaṃ khandhāyatanānaṃ saṅgahitattā na kehici khandhehi āyatanehi vā vippayuttā. Ekāya dhātuyāti yā yā pucchāya uddhaṭā hoti tāya tāya.

At the conclusion, this same meaning is encompassed by the phrase 'the four aggregates,' and so forth. Herein, terms that have similar answers are to be coordinated, even in reverse order, and in that way questions concerning the feeling aggregate, and so forth, are formulated. Among these, the division of aggregates, and so forth, should be understood thus. In the question on the feeling aggregate, and so forth: 'by one' means by the mind-base; 'by seven' means by the consciousness-elements; 'by some' means by feeling, etc., within the phenomena-base. In the question on the consciousness-element, regarding the answer 'those phenomena are not disjoined from any': 'those phenomena' refers to the remaining six consciousness-elements, form, and Nibbāna, after setting aside the consciousness-element extracted for the question. Since all aggregates and bases are included by these, they are not disjoined from any aggregates or bases. 'By one element' refers to whichever element has been extracted for the question.

309. Upekkhindriyapañhe – pañcahīti upekkhāsampayuttāhi cakkhuviññāṇadhātuādīhi. Iminā nayena sabbattha pucchāya uddhaṭapadeneva saddhiṃ vippayuttānaṃ vasena attho veditabboti.

309. In the question on the equanimity faculty, 'by five' means by the five [consciousness-elements] associated with equanimity, namely the eye-consciousness element, and so forth. By this method, the meaning should be understood everywhere in terms of the phenomena that are disjoined from the very term extracted for the question.

Sampayuttenavippayuttapadavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Term 'Disjoined from the Conjoined'.

8. Aṭṭhamanayo vippayuttenasampayuttapadavaṇṇanā

8. The Eighth Method: Explanation of the Term 'Conjoined with the Disjoined'.

317. Idāni vippayuttenasampayuttapadaṃ bhājetuṃ rūpakkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha sabbāpi pucchā moghapucchāva[P 0.0134]. Rūpakkhandhena hi vippayuttā nāma cattāro khandhā, tesaṃ aññehi sampayogo natthi. Vedanākkhandhena vippayuttaṃ rūpaṃ nibbānañca, tassa ca kenaci sampayogo natthi. Evaṃ sabbapadesu. Vippayuttānaṃ pana sampayogābhāvo veditabbo. Iti pucchāya moghattā sabbavissajjanesu natthi natthiicceva vuttanti.

317. Now, to analyze the term 'conjoined with the disjoined,' the exposition beginning 'by the form aggregate,' etc., is undertaken. Herein, every question is a futile question. For the four [mental] aggregates are what is disjoined from the form aggregate, and they have no conjunction with others. What is disjoined from the feeling aggregate is form and Nibbāna, and that has no conjunction with anything. Thus it is in all cases. The absence of conjunction for what is disjoined should be understood. Therefore, because the questions are futile, in all the answers it is said, 'There is not, there is not.'

Vippayuttenasampayuttapadavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Term 'Conjoined with the Disjoined'.

9. Navamanayo sampayuttenasampayuttapadavaṇṇanā

9. The Ninth Method: Explanation of the Term 'Conjoined with the Conjoined'.

319. Idāni [M 0.0019] sampayuttenasampayuttapadaṃ bhājetuṃ vedanākkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yaṃ [V 0.0020] khandhādivasena sampayuttaṃ, puna tasseva khandhādīhi sampayogaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Taṃ rūpena vā rūpamissakehi vā sabbarūpakkhandhasaṅgāhakehi vā padehi saddhiṃ na yujjati. Rūpena hi rūpamissakena vā aññesaṃ sampayogo natthi. Sabbarūpakkhandhasaṅgāhakehi sabbesaṃ sampayogārahānaṃ khandhādīnaṃ gahitattā aññaṃyeva natthi, yaṃ tena saha sampayogaṃ gaccheyya. Tasmā tathārūpāni padāni idha na gahitāni. Yāni pana padāni rūpena asammissaṃ arūpekadesaṃ dīpenti, tāni idha gahitāni. Tesaṃ idamuddānaṃ –

319. Now, to analyze the term 'associated by the associated,' the exposition beginning with 'with the aggregate of feeling,' etc., has been commenced. Herein, concerning that which is associated by way of the aggregates, etc., after inquiring again about its association with those very aggregates, etc., a reply has been given. That does not accord with terms related to form, or mixed with form, or inclusive of the entire aggregate of form. For there is no association of others with form or with what is mixed with form. Since by the terms inclusive of the entire aggregate of form all the aggregates, etc., suitable for association have been included, there is nothing else which could enter into association with it. Therefore, such terms have not been taken up here. But those terms that indicate a portion of the immaterial, unmixed with form, have been taken up here. This is their summary:

“Arūpakkhandhā cattāro, manāyatanameva ca;

Viññāṇadhātuyo satta, dve saccā cuddasindriyā.

The four immaterial aggregates, and the mind-base alone; Seven consciousness-elements, two truths, and fourteen faculties.

“Paccaye dvādasa padā, tato upari soḷasa;

Tikesu aṭṭha gocchake, tecattālīsameva ca.

Twelve terms in the Conditions, and sixteen thereafter; In the Triads, eight clusters, and forty-three as well.

“Mahantaraduke satta, padā piṭṭhidukesu cha;

Navamassa padassete, niddese saṅgahaṃ gatā”ti.

Seven terms in the Great Dyads; six in the Subsidiary Dyads. These terms are included in the exposition of the ninth term.

Sabbapañhesu pana ye dhammā pucchāya uddhaṭā, te yehi sampayuttā honti, tesaṃ vasena khandhādibhedo veditabbo[P 0.0135]. Vedanākkhandhena hi itare tayo khandhā sampayuttā, puna tehi vedanākkhandho sampayutto. So tehi saññādīhi tīhi khandhehi, ekena manāyatanena, sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi, ekasmiṃ dhammāyatane, dhammadhātuyā ca, kehici saññāsaṅkhāreheva sampayutto. Eseva nayo sabbatthāti.

Now, in all questions, the division into aggregates, etc., of the phenomena raised in the inquiry should be understood according to those with which they are associated. For the other three aggregates are associated with the aggregate of feeling, and in turn, the aggregate of feeling is associated with them. It is associated with those three aggregates beginning with perception, with one mind-base, with seven consciousness-elements, and, within the one mind-object base and mind-object element, with certain perceptions and formations only. This same method applies in all cases.

Sampayuttenasampayuttapadavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Term 'Associated by the Associated'.

10. Dasamanayo vippayuttenavippayuttapadavaṇṇanā

10. The Tenth Method: The Explanation of the Term 'Dissociated by the Dissociated'.

353. Idāni [V 0.0021] vippayuttenavippayuttapadaṃ bhājetuṃ rūpakkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha ye sampayogavippayogapadaniddese rūpakkhandhādayo dhammā uddhaṭā, sabbapucchāsu teyeva uddhaṭā. Sadisavissajjanānaṃ pana ekato gahitattā [M 0.0020] padāni aññāya paṭipāṭiyā āgatāni. Tattha yaṃ padaṃ pucchāya uddhaṭaṃ, taṃ yehi dhammehi vippayuttaṃ, tesaṃ vasena khandhādivibhāgo veditabbo. Rūpakkhandhena hi vedanādayo vippayuttā, tehi ca rūpakkhandho vippayutto. Nibbānaṃ pana sukhumarūpagatikameva. So rūpakkhandho catūhi khandhehi, ekena manāyatanena sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi, dhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu, kehici vedanādīhi dhammeheva vippayutto. Eseva nayo sabbatthāti.

353. Now, to analyze the term 'dissociated by the dissociated,' the exposition beginning with 'with the aggregate of form,' etc., has been commenced.
