Herein, the phenomena such as the aggregate of form, etc., which were raised in the exposition of the terms of association and dissociation, are the very same ones raised in all the questions. However, as similar answers are taken together, the terms appear in a different order. Herein, whichever term is raised in the question, the classification into aggregates, etc., should be understood according to those phenomena with which it is dissociated. For the aggregates of feeling, etc., are dissociated from the aggregate of form, and the aggregate of form is dissociated from them. Nibbāna, however, is only of a subtle nature. That aggregate of form is dissociated from the four aggregates, one mind-base, seven consciousness-elements, and, within the mind-object base and mind-object element, from certain phenomena such as feeling, etc., only. This same method applies everywhere.

Vippayuttenavippayuttapadavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Term 'Dissociated by the Dissociated'.

11. Ekādasamanayo saṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapadavaṇṇanā

11. The Eleventh Method: The Explanation of the Term 'Associated and Dissociated by What Is Included'.

409. Idāni saṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapadaṃ bhājetuṃ samudayasaccenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha ye saṅgahitenasaṅgahitapadaniddese samudayasaccādayova dhammā uddhaṭā, sabbapucchāsu teyeva uddhaṭā. Sadisavissajjanānaṃ pana ekato gahitattā padāni aññāya paṭipāṭiyā āgatāni. Tattha ye dhammā pucchāya uddhaṭapadena khandhādisaṅgahena saṅgahitā, tesaṃ yehi sampayogo vā vippayogo vā hoti, tesaṃ vasena [P 0.0136] khandhādivibhāgo veditabbo.

409. Now, to analyze the term 'associated and dissociated by what is included,' the section beginning with 'with the truth of origination,' etc., is commenced. Here, in the exposition of the term 'included by what is included,' the very phenomena such as the truth of origination, etc., are raised, and these same ones are raised in all the questions. However, because similar answers are taken together, the terms have come in a different order. Here, for those phenomena that are included by way of inclusion as aggregates, etc., by the term raised in the question, the division into aggregates, etc., should be understood according to those with which they are associated or dissociated.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – samudayasaccena tāva saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā dhammā khandhādisaṅgahena saṅgahitā. Te ca sesehi tīhi khandhehi, ekena manāyatanena, sattahi viññāṇadhātūhi, saṅkhārakkhandhe dhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu ca ṭhapetvā taṇhaṃ sesehi sampayuttattā kehici sampayuttā nāma. Ekena pana rūpakkhandhena, dasahi rūpāyatanehi, rūpadhātūhi ca vippayuttā, ekasmiṃ dhammāyatane [V 0.0022] dhammadhātuyā ca, rūpanibbānehi vippayuttattā kehici vippayuttā nāma. Iminā upāyena sabbattha attho veditabboti.

Here is the method: First, by the truth of origination, phenomena comprised within the aggregate of formations are included by way of inclusion as aggregates, etc. And these, because they are associated with the remaining three aggregates, the one mind-base, the seven consciousness-elements, and with the remaining phenomena (excepting craving) within the aggregate of formations in the mind-object base and mind-object element, are called ‘associated with some’. However, because they are dissociated from the one aggregate of form, the ten form bases, and the ten form elements, and from form and Nibbāna within the one mind-object base and mind-object element, they are called ‘dissociated with some’. By this method, the meaning should be understood everywhere.

Saṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapadavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Term 'Associated and Dissociated by What Is Included'.

12. Dvādasamanayo sampayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā

12. The Twelfth Method: The Explanation of the Term 'Included and Not Included by What Is Associated'.

417. Idāni [M 0.0021] sampayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadaṃ bhājetuṃ vedanākkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha ye sampayuttenasampayuttapadaniddese vedanākkhandhādayo dhammā uddhaṭā, sabbapucchāsu teyeva uddhaṭā. Tattha ye dhammā pucchāya uddhaṭapadena sampayuttā, tesaṃ yehi saṅgaho vā asaṅgaho vā hoti, tesaṃ vasena khandhādibhedo veditabbo.

417. Now, to analyze the term 'included and not included by what is associated,' the section beginning with 'with the aggregate of feeling,' etc., is commenced. Herein, those phenomena, such as the aggregate of feeling, etc., that were raised in the exposition of the term 'associated by what is associated', are the very same ones raised in all the questions. Herein, for those phenomena associated with the term raised in the question, the division into aggregates, etc., should be understood according to those with which there is inclusion or non-inclusion.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – vedanākkhandho hi saññādīhi sampayutto. Te saññādayo tīhi saññādikkhandhehi, dvīhi dhammāyatanamanāyatanehi, dhammadhātuyā ceva, sattahi ca viññāṇadhātūhīti aṭṭhahi dhātūhi saṅgahitā, sesāhi khandhāyatanadhātūhi asaṅgahitā. Iminā upāyena sabbattha attho veditabboti.

Here is the method: The aggregate of feeling is associated with perception and so on. Those perceptions and so on are included by the three aggregates beginning with perception, by the two bases—the mind-object base and the mind base—and by eight elements—namely, the mind-object element and the seven consciousness-elements. They are not included by the remaining aggregates, bases, and elements. By this method, the meaning should be understood everywhere.

Sampayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Term 'Included and Not Included by What Is Associated'.

13. Terasamanayo asaṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapadavaṇṇanā

13. The Thirteenth Method: The Explanation of the Term 'Associated and Dissociated by What Is Not Included'.

448. Idāni asaṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapadaṃ [P 0.0137] bhājetuṃ rūpakkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha ye pañcame asaṅgahitenaasaṅgahitapadaniddese rūpakkhandhena sadisapañhā dhammā, ye ca arūpabhavena sadisā, teyeva uddhaṭā. Sesā pana na ruhantīti na uddhaṭā. Vedanākkhandhena hi [V 0.0023] khandhādivasena pana rūpārūpadhammā asaṅgahitā honti. Tesañca sampayogo nāma natthi. Tasmā yāni padāni ruhanti, tāneva sadisavissajjanehi saddhiṃ samodhānetvā uddhaṭāni. Tattha ye dhammā pucchāya uddhaṭadhammehi khandhādivasena asaṅgahitā, te yehi sampayuttā ca vippayuttā ca, tesaṃ vasena khandhādivibhāgo veditabbo.

448. Now, to analyze the terms 'associated and dissociated by way of non-inclusion,' the section beginning with 'by the aggregate of form,' and so on, is commenced. Herein, in the fifth exposition of the term 'not included by what is not included,' those phenomena that have questions similar to the aggregate of form, and those that are similar by way of being formless, are the ones extracted. The rest, however, do not apply, hence they are not extracted. For by the aggregate of feeling, material and immaterial phenomena are not included by way of aggregates, etc. And for them, there is no such thing as association. Therefore, only those terms that apply are extracted, after being combined with similar answers. Herein, for those phenomena that are not included by way of aggregates, etc., by the phenomena extracted in the question, the division into aggregates, etc., should be understood according to those with which they are associated and dissociated.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – rūpakkhandhena tāva viññāṇameva tīhi saṅgahehi asaṅgahitaṃ. Taṃ vedanādīhi tīhi khandhehi, dhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu ca vedanādīheva sampayuttaṃ. Ekena rūpakkhandhena, dasahi rūpāyatanarūpadhātūhi, dhammāyatanadhammadhātūsu [M 0.0022] ca rūpanibbānadhammehi vippayuttaṃ. Taṃ sandhāya te dhammā tīhi khandhehītiādi vuttaṃ. Iminā nayena sabbattha attho veditabboti.

Herein, this is the method: Consciousness itself is not included by the aggregate of form by way of three inclusions. It is associated with the three aggregates beginning with feeling, and with feeling, etc., within the mind-object base and mind-object element. It is dissociated from the one aggregate of form, from the ten material bases and ten material elements, and from material phenomena and Nibbāna within the mind-object base and mind-object element. In reference to this, it is said, 'those phenomena by the three aggregates,' and so on. By this method, the meaning is to be understood everywhere.

Asaṅgahitenasampayuttavippayuttapadavaṇṇanā.

The explanation of the terms 'associated and dissociated by way of non-inclusion'.

14. Cuddasamanayo vippayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā

14. The Fourteenth Method: The Explanation of the Terms 'Included and Not Included' by way of Dissociation.

456. Idāni vippayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadaṃ bhājetuṃ rūpakkhandhenātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yesaṃ padānaṃ vippayogo na ruhati, tāni imasmiṃ vāre na gahitāni. Kāni pana tānīti? Dhammāyatanādīni. Dhammāyatanassa hi khandhādīsu ekenāpi vippayogo na ruhati. Dhammadhātuādīsupi eseva nayo. Tesaṃ idamuddānaṃ –

456. Now, to analyze the terms 'included and not included' by way of dissociation, the section beginning with 'by the aggregate of form,' etc., is commenced. Herein, those terms for which dissociation is not applicable are not taken up in this section. Which are those? The mind-object base, etc. For the mind-object base, dissociation is not applicable with even one of the aggregates, etc. The same method applies to the mind-object element, etc. This is their summary:

“Dhammāyatanaṃ dhammadhātu, jīvitindriyameva ca;

Nāmarūpapadañceva, saḷāyatanameva ca.

The mind-object base, the mind-object element, and the life faculty; the term 'name-and-form,' and the six sense bases as well.

“Jātiādittayaṃ ekaṃ, padaṃ vīsatime tike;

Tikāvasānikaṃ ekaṃ, satta cūḷantare padā.

The triad beginning with birth is one term; one term in the twentieth triad; one term concluding the triads; and seven terms in the minor intermediate section.

“Daseva [V 0.0024] gocchake honti, mahantaramhi cuddasa;

Cha padāni tato uddhaṃ sabbānipi samāsato;

Padāni ca na labbhanti, cattālīsañca satta cā”ti.

Ten are in the cluster, fourteen in the major intermediate section; six terms beyond that, all in brief; and the terms not found are forty-seven.

Pariyosāne [P 0.0138] ca – dhammāyatanaṃ dhammadhātūti gāthāpi imamevatthaṃ dīpetuṃ vuttā. Imāni pana ṭhapetvā sesāni sabbānipi labbhanti. Tesu khandhādivibhāgo vuttanayānusāreneva veditabboti.

And at the conclusion, the verse beginning 'mind-object base, mind-object element' was also spoken to illuminate this very meaning. But excluding these, all the remaining terms are found. Among them, the classification into aggregates, etc., should be understood according to the method already explained.

Vippayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Terms 'Included and Not Included by way of Dissociation'.

Nigamanakathā

The Concluding Discourse

Ettāvatā [M 0.0023] ca –

And thus far:

Dhātuppabhedakusalo, yaṃ dhātukathaṃ tathāgato āha;

Tassā nayamukhabheda-ppakāsanaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ hoti.

The Tathāgata, skilled in the analysis of elements, spoke the Dhātukathā; the exposition of the divisions of its methods and approaches is now completed.

Iminā nayamukhabheda-ppakāsanena hi vibhāvinā sakkā;

Ñātuṃ sabbepi nayā, saṅkhepakathāva iti vuttā.

For by this exposition of the divisions of its methods and approaches, a discerning person is able to understand all the methods, as it is said to be a concise discourse.

Ekekassa pana sace, padassa vitthārameva bhāseyyaṃ;

Vacanañca ativiya bahuṃ, bhaveyya attho ca aviseso.

But if I were to speak in detail about each and every term, the text would become exceedingly long, and the meaning undifferentiated.

Iti ūnabhāṇavāradvayāya, yaṃ tantiyā mayā etaṃ;

Kurunā pattaṃ puññaṃ, sukhāya taṃ hotu lokassāti.

Thus, whatever merit has been attained by me in composing this treatise of less than two recitation sections, may that be for the happiness of the world.

Dhātukathā-aṭṭhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary to the Dhātukathā is concluded.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Abhidhammapiṭake

In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka

Puggalapaññatti-aṭṭhakathā

The Commentary to the Puggalapaññatti

Nipuṇatthaṃ [P 0.0171][M 0.0025][V 0.0025] pakaraṇaṃ, dhātubhedappakāsano;

Satthā dhātukathaṃ nāma, desayitvā surālaye.

Having taught in the abode of the gods the discourse named Dhātukathā—a treatise of subtle meaning, revealing the distinctions of elements—the Teacher,

Anantaraṃ tassa jino, paññattibhedadīpanaṃ;

Āha puggalapaññattiṃ, yaṃ loke aggapuggalo.

the Victor, who is the foremost person in the world, immediately thereafter spoke the Puggalapaññatti, which illuminates the distinctions of designations.

Tassā saṃvaṇṇanokāso, yasmā dāni upāgato;

Tasmā naṃ vaṇṇayissāmi, taṃ suṇātha samāhitāti.

Since the occasion for its commentary has now arrived, therefore I shall expound upon it; listen to that attentively.

1. Mātikāvaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Mātikā

1. Cha [V 0.0026] paññattiyo – khandhapaññatti…pe… puggalapaññattīti ayaṃ tāva puggalapaññattiyā uddeso. Tattha chāti gaṇanaparicchedo. Tena ye dhamme idha paññapetukāmo tesaṃ gaṇanavasena saṃkhepato paññattiparicchedaṃ dasseti. Paññattiyoti paricchinnadhammanidassanaṃ. Tattha “ācikkhati deseti paññapeti paṭṭhapetī”ti (saṃ. ni. 2.20) āgataṭṭhāne paññāpanā dassanā pakāsanā paññatti nāma. “Supaññattaṃ mañcapīṭha”nti (pārā. 269) āgataṭṭhāne ṭhapanā nikkhipanā paññatti nāma. Idha ubhayampi vaṭṭati. Cha paññattiyoti hi cha paññāpanā, cha dassanā pakāsanātipi; cha ṭhapanā nikkhipanātipi idha adhippetameva. Nāmapaññatti hi te te dhamme dassetipi, tena tena koṭṭhāsena ṭhapetipi.

1. 'Six designations: the designation of aggregates… and so on… the designation of persons.' This, to begin with, is the table of contents of the Puggalapaññatti. Herein, 'six' is a numerical delimitation. By this, it shows a brief delimitation by way of number for the phenomena to be designated here. 'Designations' means the demonstration of delimited phenomena. Herein, in the context of the passage 'he points out, he teaches, he designates, he establishes' (Saṃ. Ni. 2.20), 'designation' (paññatti) means designating, showing, and making known. In the context of the passage 'a well-arranged bed and chair' (Pārā. 269), 'designation' (paññatti) means placing and setting down. Here, both are applicable. For 'six designations' indeed means six acts of designating, six acts of showing and making known; and six acts of placing and setting down are also intended here. For a name-designation both demonstrates those respective phenomena and places them in their respective categories.

Khandhapaññattītiādi pana saṃkhepato tāsaṃ paññattīnaṃ sarūpadassanaṃ. Tattha khandhānaṃ ‘khandhā’ti paññāpanā dassanā pakāsanā ṭhapanā nikkhipanā khandhapaññatti nāma. Āyatanānaṃ āyatanānīti, dhātūnaṃ dhātuyoti, saccānaṃ saccānīti, indriyānaṃ indriyānīti, puggalānaṃ puggalāti paññāpanā dassanā pakāsanā ṭhapanā nikkhipanā puggalapaññatti nāma.

The phrase 'designation of aggregates,' etc., is a brief demonstration of the nature of those designations. Herein, the designating, showing, making known, placing, and setting down of aggregates as 'aggregates' is called the 'designation of aggregates.' Similarly, the designating, showing, making known, placing, and setting down of sense bases as 'sense bases' is the 'designation of sense bases'; of elements as 'elements' is the 'designation of elements'; of truths as 'truths' is the 'designation of truths'; of faculties as 'faculties' is the 'designation of faculties'; and of persons as 'persons' is the 'designation of persons'.

Pāḷimuttakena [M 0.0026] pana aṭṭhakathānayena aparāpi cha paññattiyo – vijjamānapaññatti, avijjamānapaññatti, vijjamānena [P 0.0172] avijjamānapaññatti, avijjamānena vijjamānapaññatti, vijjamānena vijjamānapaññatti, avijjamānena avijjamānapaññattīti. Tattha kusalākusalasseva saccikaṭṭhaparamatthavasena vijjamānassa sato sambhūtassa dhammassa paññāpanā vijjamānapaññatti nāma. Tathā avijjamānassa lokaniruttimattasiddhassa itthipurisādikassa paññāpanā avijjamānapaññatti nāma. Sabbākārenapi anupalabbhaneyyassa vācāvatthumattasseva pañcamasaccādikassa titthiyānaṃ aṇupakatipurisādikassa vā paññāpanāpi avijjamānapaññattiyeva. Sā pana sāsanāvacarā na hotīti idha na gahitā. Iti imesaṃ vijjamānāvijjamānānaṃ vikappanavasena sesā veditabbā. ‘Tevijjo’, ‘chaḷabhiñño’tiādīsu hi tisso vijjā cha abhiññā ca vijjamānā, puggalo avijjamāno. Tasmā tisso vijjā assāti tevijjo, cha abhiññā assāti chaḷabhiññoti evaṃ vijjamānena avijjamānassa paññāpanato evarūpā vijjamānena avijjamānapaññatti nāma. ‘Itthirūpaṃ’, ‘purisarūpa’ntiādīsu [V 0.0027] pana itthipurisā avijjamānā, rūpaṃ vijjamānaṃ. Tasmā itthiyā rūpaṃ itthirūpaṃ, purisassa rūpaṃ purisarūpanti evaṃ avijjamānena vijjamānassa paññāpanato evarūpā avijjamānena vijjamānapaññatti nāma. Cakkhusamphasso, sotasamphassotiādīsu cakkhusotādayopi phassopi vijjamānoyeva. Tasmā cakkhumhi samphasso, cakkhuto jāto samphasso, cakkhussa vā phalabhūto samphasso cakkhusamphassoti evaṃ vijjamānena vijjamānassa paññāpanato evarūpā vijjamānena vijjamānapaññatti nāma. Khattiyaputto, brāhmaṇaputto, seṭṭhiputtotiādīsu khattiyādayopi avijjamānā, puttopi. Tasmā khattiyassa putto khattiyaputtoti evaṃ avijjamānena avijjamānassa paññāpanato evarūpā avijjamānena avijjamānapaññatti nāma. Tāsu imasmiṃ pakaraṇe purimā tissova paññattiyo labbhanti. “Khandhapaññatti…pe… indriyapaññattī”ti imasmiñhi [P 0.0173] ṭhāne vijjamānasseva paññāpitattā vijjamānapaññatti labbhati. “Puggalapaññattī”ti pade avijjamānapaññatti. Parato pana ‘tevijjo’, ‘chaḷabhiñño’tiādīsu vijjamānena avijjamānapaññatti labbhatīti.

But according to the commentary method outside the Pāḷi, there are six other designations: designation of the existent, designation of the non-existent, designation of the non-existent by the existent, designation of the existent by the non-existent, designation of the existent by the existent, and designation of the non-existent by the non-existent. Herein, the designating of wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, which are existent, real, and manifest in the ultimate sense, is called a designation of the existent. Similarly, the designating of what does not exist—such as conventional terms like 'woman' or 'man,' which are established merely by worldly convention—is called a designation of the non-existent. Even the designating of what is entirely unobtainable in all respects, merely a basis for speech, such as the 'fifth truth' of the sectarians or their concepts of atom, primal nature, and spirit, is also a designation of the non-existent. However, since that does not fall within the Dispensation, it is not taken up here. Thus, the remaining designations should be understood as variations based on these existent and non-existent ones. For instance, in terms like 'possessor of the threefold knowledge' or 'possessor of the sixfold direct knowledge,' the three knowledges and the six direct knowledges exist, but the person does not. Thus, 'one who has the three knowledges is a possessor of the threefold knowledge,' and 'one who has the six direct knowledges is a possessor of the sixfold direct knowledge'—such a designation of the non-existent by the existent is called a designation of the non-existent by the existent. In phrases like 'a woman’s form' or 'a man’s form,' however, the woman and man do not exist, but the form does. Thus, 'the form of a woman is a woman’s form,' and 'the form of a man is a man’s form'—such a designation of the existent by the non-existent is called a designation of the existent by the non-existent. In terms like 'eye-contact' or 'ear-contact,' both the eye, ear, etc., and the contact exist. Thus, 'contact in the eye is eye-contact,' 'contact arisen from the eye is eye-contact,' or 'contact that is the fruit of the eye is eye-contact'—such a designation of the existent by the existent is called a designation of the existent by the existent. In phrases like 'a khattiya’s son,' 'a brahmin’s son,' or 'a merchant’s son,' neither the khattiya, brahmin, etc., nor the son exists. Thus, 'the son of a khattiya is a khattiya’s son'—such a designation of the non-existent by the non-existent is called a designation of the non-existent by the non-existent. Among these, in this treatise, only the first three designations are found. For in the passage 'designation of aggregates… designation of faculties,' since what is designated exists, a designation of the existent is found. In the phrase 'designation of a person,' it is a designation of the non-existent. Furthermore, in terms like 'possessor of the threefold knowledge' or 'possessor of the sixfold direct knowledge,' a designation of the non-existent by the existent is found.

Aṭṭhakathāmuttakena pana ācariyanayena aparāpi cha paññattiyo – upādāpaññatti, upanidhāpaññatti, samodhānapaññatti, upanikkhittapaññatti, tajjāpaññatti, santatipaññattīti[M 0.0027]. Tattha yo rūpavedanādīhi ekattena vā aññattena vā rūpavedanādayo viya saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena anupalabbhasabhāvopi rūpavedanādibhede khandhe upādāya nissāya kāraṇaṃ katvā sammato satto. Tāni tāni aṅgāni upādāya ratho gehaṃ muṭṭhi uddhananti ca; te teyeva rūpādayo upādāya ghaṭo paṭo; candasūriyaparivattādayo upādāya kālo, disā; taṃ taṃ bhūtanimittañceva bhāvanānisaṃsañca upādāya nissāya kāraṇaṃ katvā sammataṃ tena tenākārena upaṭṭhitaṃ uggahanimittaṃ paṭibhāganimittanti ayaṃ evarūpā upādāpaññatti nāma. Paññapetabbaṭṭhena cesā paññatti nāma, na paññāpanaṭṭhena. Yā pana tassatthassa paññāpanā, ayaṃ avijjamānapaññattiyeva.

According to the teachers' method, outside the commentaries, there are six other designations: designation by grasping (upādāpaññatti), designation by comparison (upanidhāpaññatti), designation by combination (samodhānapaññatti), sequential designation (upanikkhittapaññatti), designation of its nature (tajjāpaññatti), and designation of continuity (santatipaññatti). Among these, that which—though its own nature is unobtainable in the ultimate sense, whether as one with or different from the aggregates of form, feeling, etc.—is conventionally regarded as a being by grasping, relying on, and taking as a cause those very aggregates. For example, a chariot, a house, a fist, or a furnace are designated by grasping their various parts; a pot or a cloth are designated by grasping those same forms and other elements; time and directions are designated by grasping the revolutions of the moon and sun, etc.; the learning sign and the counterpart sign, which appear in such and such a manner, are conventionally regarded as such by grasping, relying on, and taking as a cause that specific elemental sign and the benefits of meditation—this is called designation by grasping. It is called a designation in the sense of that which is to be designated, not in the sense of the act of designating. The designating of that object, however, is itself a designation of the non-existent.

Yā paṭhamadutiyādīni upanidhāya dutiyaṃ tatiyantiādikā, aññamaññañca upanidhāya dīghaṃ rassaṃ, dūraṃ, santikantiādikā paññāpanā; ayaṃ upanidhāpaññatti nāma. Apicesā upanidhāpaññatti – tadaññāpekkhūpanidhā, hatthagatūpanidhā, sampayuttūpanidhā, samāropitūpanidhā, avidūragatūpanidhā[V 0.0028], paṭibhāgūpanidhā, tabbahulūpanidhā, tabbisiṭṭhūpanidhātiādinā bhedena anekappakārā.

The designation of 'second,' 'third,' and so on, by comparing with 'first,' 'second,' etc., and designations like 'long,' 'short,' 'far,' 'near,' etc., by comparing with each other—this is called designation by comparison (upanidhāpaññatti). Moreover, this designation by comparison is of many kinds, such as: designation depending on something else (tadaññāpekkhūpanidhā), designation within reach (hatthagatūpanidhā), designation associated with (sampayuttūpanidhā), designation imputed (samāropitūpanidhā), designation of what is not far (avidūragatūpanidhā), designation of a counterpart (paṭibhāgūpanidhā), designation of what is abundant in that (tabbahulūpanidhā), and designation of what is distinguished by that (tabbisiṭṭhūpanidhā).

Tattha dutiyaṃ tatiyantiādikāva tadaññaṃ apekkhitvā vuttatāya tadaññāpekkhūpanidhā nāma. Chattapāṇi, satthapāṇītiādikā hatthagataṃ upanidhāya vuttatāya [P 0.0174] hatthagatūpanidhā nāma. Kuṇḍalī, sikharī, kiriṭītiādikā sampayuttaṃ upanidhāya vuttatāya sampayuttūpanidhā nāma. Dhaññasakaṭaṃ, sappikumbhotiādikā samāropitaṃ upanidhāya vuttatāya samāropitūpanidhā nāma. Indasālaguhā, piyaṅguguhā, serīsakantiādikā avidūragataṃ upanidhāya vuttatāya avidūragatūpanidhā nāma. Suvaṇṇavaṇṇo, usabhagāmītiādikā paṭibhāgaṃ upanidhāya vuttatāya paṭibhāgūpanidhā nāma. Padumassaro, brāhmaṇagāmotiādikā tabbahulaṃ upanidhāya vuttatāya tabbahulūpanidhā nāma. Maṇikaṭakaṃ, vajirakaṭakantiādikā tabbisiṭṭhaṃ upanidhāya vuttatāya tabbisiṭṭhūpanidhā nāma.

Here, 'second,' 'third,' and so on are called designation depending on something else (tadaññāpekkhūpanidhā) because they are stated in dependence on something else. 'Umbrella-bearer' (chattapāṇi), 'sword-bearer' (satthapāṇi), and similar terms are called designation within reach (hatthagatūpanidhā) because they are stated in dependence on what is held in the hand. 'Wearing earrings' (kuṇḍalī), 'wearing a crest' (sikharī), 'wearing a crown' (kiriṭī), and similar terms are called designation associated with (sampayuttūpanidhā) because they are stated in dependence on what is connected. 'Grain cart' (dhaññasakaṭaṃ), 'ghee pot' (sappikumbho), and similar terms are called designation imputed (samāropitūpanidhā) because they are stated in dependence on what is loaded. 'Indasāla cave' (indasālaguhā), 'Piyangu cave' (piyaṅguguhā), 'Serīsaka' (serīsakaṃ), and similar terms are called designation of what is not far (avidūragatūpanidhā) because they are stated in dependence on what is not far away. 'Golden-colored' (suvaṇṇavaṇṇo), 'bull-like gait' (usabhagāmī), and similar terms are called designation of a counterpart (paṭibhāgūpanidhā) because they are stated in dependence on what is comparable. 'Lotus pond' (padumassaro), 'Brahmin village' (brāhmaṇagāmo), and similar terms are called designation of what is abundant in that (tabbahulūpanidhā) because they are stated in dependence on what is abundant there. 'Jeweled bracelet' (maṇikaṭakaṃ), 'diamond bracelet' (vajirakaṭakaṃ), and similar terms are called designation of what is distinguished by that (tabbisiṭṭhūpanidhā) because they are stated in dependence on what is especially distinguished there.

Yā pana tesaṃ tesaṃ samodhānamapekkhitvā tidaṇḍaṃ, aṭṭhapadaṃ, dhaññarāsi, puppharāsītiādikā paññāpanā, ayaṃ samodhānapaññatti nāma. Yā purimassa purimassa upanikkhipitvā dve, tīṇi, cattārītiādikā paññāpanā, ayaṃ [M 0.0028] upanikkhittapaññatti nāma. Yā taṃ taṃ dhammasabhāvaṃ apekkhitvā pathavī, tejo, kakkhaḷatā, uṇhatātiādikā paññāpanā, ayaṃ tajjāpaññatti nāma. Yā pana santativicchedābhāvaṃ apekkhitvā āsītiko, nāvutikotiādikā paññāpanā, ayaṃ santatipaññatti nāma. Etāsu pana tajjāpaññatti vijjamānapaññattiyeva. Sesā avijjamānapakkhañceva, avijjamānena avijjamānapakkhañca bhajanti.

The designation that considers the combination of various things, such as 'the three sticks,' 'the chessboard,' 'the heap of grain,' 'the heap of flowers,' and so forth—this is called designation by combination (samodhānapaññatti). The designation that places one thing after another, such as 'two,' 'three,' 'four,' and so on—this is called sequential designation (upanikkhittapaññatti). The designation that considers the intrinsic nature of phenomena, such as 'earth,' 'fire,' 'hardness,' 'heat,' and so forth—this is called designation of its nature (tajjāpaññatti). The designation that considers the absence of interruption in continuity, such as 'an eighty-year-old,' 'a ninety-year-old,' and so forth—this is called designation of continuity (santatipaññatti). Among these, the designation of its nature is a designation of what exists. The rest belong to the category of the non-existent, and by means of the non-existent, they are classified as non-existent.

Aṭṭhakathāmuttakena ācariyanayeneva aparāpi cha paññattiyo – kiccapaññatti, saṇṭhānapaññatti, liṅgapaññatti, bhūmipaññatti, paccattapaññatti, asaṅkhatapaññattīti. Tattha bhāṇako, dhammakathikotiādikā kiccavasena paññāpanā kiccapaññatti nāma. Kiso, thūlo, parimaṇḍalo, caturassotiādikā saṇṭhānavasena paññāpanā saṇṭhānapaññatti [P 0.0175] nāma. Itthī, purisotiādikā liṅgavasena paññāpanā liṅgapaññati nāma. Kāmāvacarā, rūpāvacarā, arūpāvacarā, kosalakā, mādhurātiādikā bhūmivasena paññāpanā bhūmipaññatti nāma. Tisso[V 0.0029], nāgo, sumanotiādikā paccattanāmakaraṇamattavasena paññāpanā paccattapaññatti nāma. Nirodho, nibbānantiādikā asaṅkhatadhammassa paññāpanā asaṅkhatapaññatti nāma. Tattha ekaccā bhūmipaññatti asaṅkhatapaññatti ca vijjamānapaññattiyeva, kiccapaññatti vijjamānena avijjamānapakkhaṃ bhajati. Sesā avijjamānapaññattiyo nāma.

According to the teachers' method, beyond the commentaries, there are six other designations: functional designation (kiccapaññatti), shape designation (saṇṭhānapaññatti), gender designation (liṅgapaññatti), plane designation (bhūmipaññatti), individual designation (paccattapaññatti), and unconditioned designation (asaṅkhatapaññatti). Among these, designations such as 'reciter' and 'Dhamma preacher' based on function are called functional designation. Designations such as 'thin,' 'fat,' 'round,' and 'square' based on shape are called shape designation. Designations such as 'female' and 'male' based on gender are called gender designation. Designations such as 'sensuous plane,' 'form plane,' 'formless plane,' 'Kosala country,' and 'Madhura city' based on plane are called plane designation. Designations such as 'Tissa,' 'Nāga,' and 'Sumana' merely based on individual naming are called individual designation. Designations of the unconditioned Dhamma such as 'cessation' and 'Nibbāna' are called unconditioned designation. Among these, some plane designations and the unconditioned designation are designations of what exists; functional designation is a designation of the non-existent based upon the existent. The rest are designations of what does not exist.

2. Idāni yāsaṃ paññattīnaṃ uddesavāre saṅkhepato sarūpadassanaṃ kataṃ, saṅkhepatoyeva tāva tāsaṃ vatthuṃ vibhajitvā dassanavasena tā dassetuṃ kittāvatātiādimāha. Tattha pucchāya tāva evamattho veditabbo – yā ayaṃ khandhānaṃ ‘khandhā’ti paññāpanā, dassanā, ṭhapanā, sā kittakena hotīti kathetukamyatāpucchā. Parato kittāvatā āyatanānantiādīsupi eseva nayo. Vissajjanepi evamattho veditabbo – yattakena paññāpanena saṅkhepato pañcakkhandhāti vā pabhedato “rūpakkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho”ti vā; tatrāpi rūpakkhandho kāmāvacaro, sesā catubhūmikāti vā evarūpaṃ paññāpanaṃ hoti; ettakena khandhānaṃ ‘khandhā’ti paññatti hoti.

2. Now, since a brief overview of the nature of these designations has been given in the enumeration section, to show them by dividing their basis, even briefly, he states 'To what extent?' and so on. Here, the meaning of the question should first be understood thus: 'This designation of the aggregates as 'aggregates'—how much is involved in its presentation, description, or establishment?' The same method applies to questions like 'To what extent are the sense bases?' and so on. In the answer, the meaning should be understood thus: To the extent that there is a designation, either briefly as 'the five aggregates,' or in detail as 'the form aggregate... the consciousness aggregate,' and further, even within that, as 'the form aggregate belongs to the sensuous sphere, while the remaining four belong to the four planes'—to that extent, the designation of the aggregates as 'aggregates' is established.

3. Tathā yattakena paññāpanena saṅkhepato dvādasāyatanānīti vā, pabhedato “cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… dhammāyatana”nti vā; tatrāpi dasāyatanā kāmāvacarā[M 0.0029], dvāyatanā catubhūmikāti vā, evarūpaṃ paññāpanaṃ hoti; ettakena āyatanānaṃ āyatanānīti paññatti hoti.

3. Similarly, to the extent that there is a designation, either briefly, such as 'the twelve sense bases,' or in detail, such as 'the eye base... the mind-object base,' and within that, further distinctions like 'ten bases belong to the sensuous sphere, while two belong to the four planes'—to that extent, the designation of the sense bases as 'sense bases' is established.

4. Yattakena paññāpanena saṅkhepato aṭṭhārasa dhātuyoti vā[P 0.0176], pabhedato “cakkhudhātu…pe… manoviññāṇadhātū”ti vā; tatrāpi soḷasa dhātuyo kāmāvacarā, dve dhātuyo catubhūmikāti vā evarūpaṃ paññāpanaṃ hoti; ettakena dhātūnaṃ dhātūti paññatti hoti.

4. To the extent that a designation is made, either concisely as 'the eighteen elements,' or in detail as 'the eye element...the mind-consciousness element,' or even with further distinctions such as 'sixteen elements are of the sensuous sphere, while two elements are of the four planes'—to that extent, the designation of the elements as 'elements' is established.

5. Yattakena paññāpanena saṅkhepato cattāri saccānīti vā, pabhedato “dukkhasaccaṃ…pe… nirodhasacca”nti vā; tatrāpi dve saccā lokiyā, dve saccā lokuttarāti vā evarūpaṃ paññāpanaṃ hoti; ettakena saccānaṃ ‘saccānī’ti paññatti hoti.

5. To the extent that a designation is made, either in brief, such as 'the four truths,' or in detail, such as 'the truth of suffering...the truth of cessation,' and therein further distinctions like 'two truths are mundane, two truths are supramundane'—to this extent, the designation of the truths as 'truths' is established.

6. Yattakena paññāpanena saṅkhepato bāvīsatindriyānīti vā, pabhedato “cakkhundriyaṃ…pe… aññātāvindriya”nti vā; tatrāpi dasindriyāni kāmāvacarāni, navindriyāni [V 0.0030] missakāni, tīṇi indriyāni lokuttarānīti vā evarūpaṃ paññāpanaṃ hoti; ettakena indriyānaṃ indriyānīti paññatti hoti. Ettāvatā saṅkhepato vatthuṃ vibhajitvā dassanavasena pañca paññattiyo dassitā honti.

6. To the extent that a designation is made, either in brief, as 'the twenty-two faculties,' or in detail, as 'the eye-faculty... up to... the faculty of final knowledge'; and therein, ten faculties are of the sense sphere, nine are mixed, and three are supramundane—such a designation occurs. To this extent, the designation of the faculties as 'faculties' is established. Thus far, five designations have been shown by briefly analyzing their basis.

7. Idāni vitthārato vatthuṃ vibhajitvā dassanavasena puggalapaññattiṃ dassetuṃ samayavimutto asamayavimuttotiādimāha. Sammāsambuddhena hi tile visārayamānena viya, vāke hīrayamānena viya ca, heṭṭhā vibhaṅgappakaraṇe imāsaṃ pañcannaṃ paññattīnaṃ vatthubhūtā khandhādayo nippadesena kathitāti tena te idha ekadeseneva kathesi. Chaṭṭhā puggalapaññatti heṭṭhā akathitāva. Idhāpi uddesavāre ekadeseneva kathitā; tasmā taṃ vitthārato kathetukāmo samayavimutto asamayavimuttoti ekakato paṭṭhāya yāva dasakā mātikaṃ ṭhapesīti.

7. Now, to explain the designation of persons in detail by analyzing its basis, it is said: 'one liberated on occasion, one liberated out of season,' and so on. For just as the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One scattered sesame seeds or sifted husks from rice, in the earlier Vibhaṅga exposition, the aggregates and so forth—which are the basis for these five designations—were spoken of without remainder. Therefore, here He explained them only in part. The sixth, the designation of persons, was not explained at all earlier. Here too, in the enumeration section, it is explained only in part. Thus, wishing to explain it in detail, starting from the section of ones with 'one liberated on occasion, one liberated out of season,' He established the matrix up to the section of tens.

Mātikāvaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Matrix.

2. Niddesavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Exposition.

1. Ekakaniddesavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Exposition of Ones.

1. Idāni [M 0.0030][P 0.0177] yathāṭhapitaṃ mātikaṃ ādito paṭṭhāya vibhajitvā dassetuṃ – katamo ca puggalo samayavimuttotiādimāha. Tattha idhāti imasmiṃ sattaloke. Ekacco puggaloti eko puggalo. Kālena kālanti ettha bhummavasena attho veditabbo. Ekekasmiṃ kāleti vuttaṃ hoti. Samayena samayanti idaṃ purimasseva vevacanaṃ. Aṭṭha vimokkheti rūpāvacarārūpāvacaraaṭṭhasamāpattiyo. Tāsañhi paccanīkadhammehi vimuccanato vimokkhoti nāmaṃ. Kāyenāti vimokkhasahajātena nāmakāyena. Phusitvā viharatīti paṭilabhitvā iriyati. Katamasmiṃ panesa kāle vimokkhe phusitvā viharatīti? Samāpattiṃ samāpajjitukāmassa hi kālo nāma atthi, akālo nāma atthi. Tattha pātova sarīrapaṭijagganakālo, vattakaraṇakālo ca samāpajjanassa akālo nāma. Sarīraṃ pana paṭijaggitvā vattaṃ katvā vasanaṭṭhānaṃ [V 0.0031] pavisitvā nisinnassa yāva piṇḍāya gamanakālo nāgacchati, etasmiṃ antare samāpajjanassa kālo nāma.

1. Now, to explain the matrix as it was laid out, beginning from the start by analyzing it, it is said: 'And what sort of person is liberated on occasion?' and so on. Herein, 'here' means in this world of beings. 'A certain person' means one individual. 'From time to time' should be understood here in the sense of the locative case. It means 'at each and every time.' 'On occasion' is just a synonym for the previous term. 'The eight liberations' are the eight attainments of the form and formless realms. For they are called 'liberations' because one is liberated from opposing states. 'With the body' means with the mental body co-arisen with the liberation. 'Touches and dwells' means having attained, one abides. But at what time does one touch and dwell in these liberations? For one wishing to enter an attainment, there is indeed a proper time and an improper time. Herein, the time for attending to the body in the morning and the time for performing duties is called an improper time for entering an attainment. But after attending to the body and performing duties, having entered the dwelling place and sat down, until the time for going on alms round arrives—in this interval, it is called a proper time for entering an attainment.

Piṇḍāya gamanakālaṃ pana sallakkhetvā nikkhantassa cetiyavandanakālo, bhikkhusaṅghaparivutassa vitakkamāḷake ṭhānakālo piṇḍāya gamanakālo gāme caraṇakālo; āsanasālāya yāgupānakālo vattakaraṇakāloti ayampi samāpajjanassa akālo nāma. Āsanasālāya pana vivitte okāse sati yāva bhattakālo nāgacchati, etasmimpi antare samāpajjanassa kālo nāma. Bhattaṃ pana bhuñjanakālo, vihāragamanakālo, pattacīvarapaṭisāmanakālo, divāvattakaraṇakālo, paripucchādānakāloti ayampi samāpajjanassa akālo nāma. Yo akālo, sveva asamayo. Taṃ sabbampi ṭhapetvā avasese kāle kāle, samaye samaye vuttappakāre aṭṭha [P 0.0178] vimokkhe sahajātanāmakāyena paṭilabhitvā viharanto, “idhekacco puggalo…pe… viharatī”ti vuccati.

And having noted the time for going on alms round, for one who has gone forth, the time for paying homage at the shrine, the time for standing on the meditation terrace surrounded by the Saṅgha, the time for going on alms round, the time for walking in the village, the time for drinking rice gruel in the assembly hall, and the time for performing duties—this too is called an improper time for entering an attainment. But in the assembly hall, if there is a secluded spot, until the meal time arrives—in this interval too, it is called a proper time for entering an attainment. The time for eating the meal, the time for going to the monastery, the time for putting away the bowl and robes, the time for performing daytime duties, and the time for inquiry—this too is called an improper time for entering an attainment. Whatever is an improper time is also an improper occasion. Setting all that aside, during the remaining proper times and occasions, one who, having attained with the co-arisen mental body, dwells in the aforementioned eight liberations is called: 'Here, a certain person... dwells.'

Apicesa [M 0.0031] saphassakehi sahajātanāmadhammehi sahajātadhamme phusatiyeva nāma, upacārena appanaṃ phusatiyeva nāma. Purimāya appanāya aparaṃ appanaṃ phusatiyeva. Yena hi saddhiṃ ye dhammā sahajātā, tena te paṭiladdhā nāma honti. Phassenāpi phuṭṭhāyeva nāma honti. Upacārampi appanāya paṭilābhakāraṇameva, tathā purimā appanā aparaappanāya. Tatrāssa evaṃ sahajātehi sahajātānaṃ phusanā veditabbā – paṭhamajjhānañhi vitakkādīhi pañcaṅgikaṃ. Tasmiṃ ṭhapetvā tāni aṅgāni sesā atirekapaṇṇāsadhammā cattāro khandhā nāma honti. Tena nāmakāyena paṭhamajjhānasamāpattivimokkhaṃ phusitvā paṭilabhitvā viharati. Dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ pītisukhacittekaggatāhi tivaṅgikaṃ, tatiyaṃ sukhacittekaggatāhi duvaṅgikaṃ, catutthaṃ upekkhācittekaggatāhi duvaṅgikaṃ, tathā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanañca. Tattha ṭhapetvā tāni aṅgāni sesā atirekapaṇṇāsadhammā cattāro khandhā nāma honti. Tena nāmakāyena nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattivimokkhaṃ phusitvā paṭilabhitvā viharati.

Moreover, with the co-arisen mental states that have contact, one indeed contacts the co-arisen states; by way of access concentration, one indeed contacts absorption. By means of a previous absorption, one contacts a subsequent absorption. For, the states that are co-arisen with a certain factor are said to be obtained by means of that factor. They are indeed contacted by contact. Access concentration is also a cause for obtaining absorption, and likewise a previous absorption is for a subsequent absorption. Herein, the contacting of co-arisen states by co-arisen factors should be understood as follows: The first jhāna is fivefold, with initial application and so on. Having set aside those factors, the remaining fifty-plus states are called the four aggregates. With that mental body, one contacts, obtains, and dwells in the liberation of the first jhāna attainment. The second jhāna is threefold, with joy, happiness, and one-pointedness of mind; the third is twofold, with happiness and one-pointedness of mind; the fourth is twofold, with equanimity and one-pointedness of mind. Similarly, the base of infinite space... up to... the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Therein, having set aside those factors, the remaining fifty-plus states are called the four aggregates. With that mental body, one contacts, obtains, and dwells in the liberation of the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

Paññāya cassa disvāti vipassanāpaññāya saṅkhāragataṃ, maggapaññāya catusaccadhamme passitvā. Ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā hontīti upaḍḍhupaḍḍhā paṭhamamaggādivajjhā āsavā parikkhīṇā honti. Ayaṃ vuccati puggalo samayavimuttoti ettha aṭṭhasamāpattilābhī puthujjano tena [V 0.0032] nāmakāyena phusitvā viharatīti [P 0.0179] vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Pāḷiyaṃ pana “ekacce āsavā parikkhīṇā”ti vuttaṃ. Puthujjanassa ca khīṇā āsavā nāma natthi, tasmā so na gahito. Aṭṭhasamāpattilābhī khīṇāsavopi tena nāmakāyena phusitvā viharatīti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Tassa pana aparikkhīṇāsavā nāma natthi, tasmā sopi na gahito. Samayavimuttoti pana tiṇṇaṃ sotāpannasakadāgāmianāgāmīnaṃyevetaṃ nāmanti veditabbaṃ.

And 'having seen with wisdom' means having seen conditioned phenomena with insight-wisdom, and the phenomena of the four truths with path-wisdom. 'Some taints are destroyed' means the taints to be abandoned by the first path and so on are destroyed in part. This is called a person liberated on occasion. Here, it would be possible to say that an ordinary person who is an attainer of the eight attainments dwells having contacted them with that mental body. However, in the Pāli text, it is said, 'some taints are destroyed.' And since an ordinary person has no destroyed taints, such a one is not included. It would also be possible to say that even an attainer of the eight attainments whose taints are destroyed dwells having contacted them with that mental body. But since for such a one there are no undestroyed taints, that one too is not included. The term 'liberated on occasion,' however, should be understood as a name for only these three: the stream-enterer, the once-returner, and the non-returner.

2. Asamayavimuttaniddese – purimasadisaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Asamayavimuttoti panettha sukkhavipassakakhīṇāsavassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Sukkhavipassakā pana sotāpannasakadāgāmianāgāmino aṭṭhasamāpattilābhino ca khīṇāsavā puthujjanā ca imasmiṃ duke na labbhanti, dukamuttakapuggalā [M 0.0032] nāma honti. Tasmā satthā attano buddhasubuddhatāya heṭṭhā gahite ca aggahite ca saṅkaḍḍhitvā saddhiṃ piṭṭhivaṭṭakehi tantiṃ āropento sabbepi ariyapuggalātiādimāha. Tattha ariye vimokkheti kilesehi ārakattā ariyeti saṅkhaṃ gate lokuttaravimokkhe. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – bāhirānañhi aṭṭhannaṃ samāpattīnaṃ samāpajjantassa samayopi atthi asamayopi. Maggavimokkhena vimuccanassa samayo vā asamayo vā natthi. Yassa saddhā balavatī, vipassanā ca āraddhā, tassa gacchantassa tiṭṭhantassa nisīdantassa nipajjantassa khādantassa bhuñjantassa maggaphalapaṭivedho nāma na hotīti natthi. Iti maggavimokkhena vimuccanassa samayo vā asamayo vā natthīti heṭṭhā gahite ca aggahite ca saṅkaḍḍhitvā imaṃ piṭṭhivaṭṭakaṃ tantiṃ āropesi dhammarājā. Samāpattilābhī puthujjano imāyapi tantiyā aggahitova. Bhajāpiyamāno pana [P 0.0180] samāpattivikkhambhitānaṃ kilesānaṃ vasena samayavimuttabhāvaṃ bhajeyya.

2. In the explanation of 'timeless liberation' (asamayavimutta), it should be understood in the same way as previously stated. Here, 'timeless liberation' is a name for the dry-insight arahant. However, dry-insight stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arahants who have attained the eight attainments, and ordinary people are not found in this pair; they are called individuals excluded from the pair. Therefore, the Teacher, by virtue of his own supreme Buddhahood, having gathered both those included and those not included from below, and establishing the enumeration along with the supplementary sections, stated, 'all noble individuals,' and so on. Here, this refers to the supramundane liberation, which is designated 'noble' because it is far from defilements. This is what is meant: for one who enters the eight external attainments, there is both a time and a non-time. But for liberation by the path, there is neither a time nor a non-time. For one whose faith is strong and insight is initiated, it is not the case that there is no realization of the path and fruition, whether one is walking, standing, sitting, lying down, eating, or consuming. Thus, stating that for liberation by the path there is neither a time nor a non-time, the King of Dhamma, having gathered both those included and those not included from below, established this supplementary enumeration. An ordinary person who is an obtainer of the attainments is not included in this enumeration. However, when considered, by means of the defilements suppressed by the attainments, he may partake of the state of temporal liberation.

3. Kuppadhammākuppadhammaniddesesu – yassa adhigato samāpattidhammo kuppati nassati, so kuppadhammo. Rūpasahagatānanti rūpanimittasaṅkhātena rūpena sahagatānaṃ. Tena saddhiṃ pavattānaṃ na vinā rūpārammaṇānaṃ catunnaṃ rūpāvacarajjhānānanti attho. Arūpasahagatānanti rūpato aññaṃ, na rūpanti arūpaṃ. Arūpena sahagatānaṃ tena saddhiṃ pavattānaṃ na vinā arūpārammaṇānaṃ catunnaṃ arūpāvacarajjhānānanti attho. Na nikāmalābhīti pañcahākārehi aciṇṇavasitāya icchitākārena aladdhattā na nikāmalābhī. Appaguṇasamāpattikoti attho. Na akicchalābhīti kicchalābhī dukkhalābhī. Yo āgamanamhi kilese vikkhambhento upacāraṃ pāpento [V 0.0033] appanaṃ pāpento cittamañjūsaṃ labhanto dukkhena kicchena sasaṅkhārena sappayogena kilamanto taṃ sampadaṃ pāpuṇituṃ sakkoti, so na akicchalābhī nāma. Na akasiralābhīti avipulalābhī. Samāpattiṃ appetvā addhānaṃ pharituṃ na sakkoti. Ekaṃ dve cittavāre vattetvā sahasāva vuṭṭhātīti attho.

3. In the explanation of 'liable to fall' (kuppadhamma) and 'unshakable' (akuppadhamma): one whose attained state of attainment is liable to fall and perish is called 'liable to fall.' 'Associated with form' (rūpasahagatāni) means those associated with form, which is designated as a form-sign. This means the four form-sphere jhānas that arise together with, and not without, a form object. 'Associated with the formless' (arūpasahagatāni) means that which is other than form, that is, not form, is formless. This means the four formless-sphere jhānas that arise together with, and not without, a formless object. 'Not one who obtains at will' (na nikāmalābhī) means one who, due to not having practiced mastery in the five ways, does not obtain it in the desired manner, and is thus not one who obtains at will. This means one of weak attainment. 'Not one who obtains without difficulty' (na akicchalābhī) means one who obtains with difficulty, obtains painfully. One who, while suppressing defilements in the approach, bringing the mind to access concentration, bringing it to absorption, obtaining the casket of the mind, is able to reach that attainment only with difficulty, painfully, with effort, with exertion, becoming weary, is called 'not one who obtains without difficulty.' 'Not one who obtains without trouble' (na akasiralābhī) means one who does not obtain extensively. He is not able to pervade a period of time after having attained absorption. This means he arises suddenly after one or two thought-processes have occurred.

Yatthicchakanti yasmiṃ okāse samāpattiṃ appetvā nisīdituṃ icchati. Yadicchakanti kasiṇajjhānaṃ vā ānāpānajjhānaṃ vā brahmavihārajjhānaṃ vā asubhajjhānaṃ [M 0.0033] vāti yaṃ yaṃ samāpattiṃ appetvā nisīdituṃ icchati. Yāvaticchakanti addhānaparicchedena yattakaṃ kālaṃ icchati. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yattha yattha yaṃ yaṃ samāpattiṃ yattakaṃ addhānaṃ samāpajjitumpi vuṭṭhātumpi icchati, tattha tattha taṃ taṃ samāpattiṃ tattakaṃ addhānaṃ samāpajjitumpi vuṭṭhātumpi na sakkoti. Candaṃ vā sūriyaṃ vā ulloketvā ‘imasmiṃ [P 0.0181] cande vā sūriye vā ettakaṃ ṭhānaṃ gate vuṭṭhahissāmī’ti paricchinditvā jhānaṃ samāpanno yathāparicchedena vuṭṭhātuṃ na sakkoti, antarāva vuṭṭhāti; samāpattiyā appaguṇatāyāti.

Wherever one wishes—in whatever place one wishes to sit after attaining absorption. Whatever one wishes—whether it be a kasiṇa-jhāna, ānāpāna-jhāna, brahmavihāra-jhāna, or asubha-jhāna—whatever absorption one wishes to attain and sit in. For as long as one wishes—for whatever length of time one desires. This is what is meant: one is unable to attain whatever absorption one wishes, in whatever place one wishes, for as long as one wishes, and to emerge from it accordingly. Even if one gazes at the moon or sun and determines, 'When this moon or sun has reached such a position, I will emerge,' and enters absorption, one cannot emerge at the predetermined time but emerges prematurely—due to the weakness of the absorption.

Pamādamāgammāti pamādaṃ paṭicca. Ayaṃ vuccatīti ayaṃ evaṃvidho puggalo kuppadhammoti vuccati. Idaṃ pana aṭṭhasamāpattilābhino puthujjanassa sotāpannassa sakadāgāminoti tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ nāmaṃ. Etesañhi samādhipāribandhakā vipassanāpāribandhakā ca dhammā na suvikkhambhitā, na suvikkhālitā, tena tesaṃ samāpatti nassati parihāyati. Sā ca kho neva sīlabhedena, nāpattivītikkamena. Na garukamokkhadhammo panesa appamattakenapi kiccakaraṇīyena vā vattabhedamattakena vā nassati.

By falling into heedlessness means: on account of heedlessness. This is said: this kind of person is called 'liable to fall.' This term, however, applies to three types of individuals: an ordinary person who has attained the eight attainments, a stream-enterer, and a once-returner. For these, the factors that obstruct concentration and the factors that obstruct insight are not well suppressed or well cleansed; therefore, their attainment is lost or deteriorates. And this is not through a breach of moral conduct or transgression of an offense. But this is not a weighty state of liberation; it is lost even by a slight task to be done or by a mere breach of duty.

Tatridaṃ vatthu – eko kira thero samāpattiṃ vaḷañjeti. Tasmiṃ piṇḍāya gāmaṃ paviṭṭhe dārakā pariveṇe kīḷitvā pakkamiṃsu. Thero āgantvā ‘pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabba’nti cintetvā asammajjitvā vihāraṃ pavisitvā ‘samāpattiṃ appessāmī’ti nisīdi. So appetuṃ asakkonto, ‘kiṃ nu kho āvaraṇa’nti sīlaṃ āvajjanto appamattakampi vītikkamaṃ adisvā ‘vattabhedo nu kho atthī’ti olokento pariveṇassa asammaṭṭhabhāvaṃ ñatvā sammajjitvā pavisitvā nisīdanto samāpattiṃ appentova nisīdi.

Here is an account: It is said that a certain elder was practicing attainment. When he had gone to the village for alms, children played in his monastic precinct and then left. Upon returning, the elder thought, 'The monastic precinct should be swept,' but without sweeping it, he entered his dwelling and, sitting down, thought, 'I will enter into attainment.' Unable to enter, he reflected, 'What, I wonder, is the hindrance?' Reviewing his moral conduct, he saw no transgression, however minor. Then, considering, 'Could there be a breach of duty?', he realized that the monastic precinct had not been swept. After sweeping it and entering, as he was sitting down, he entered into attainment.

4. Akuppadhammaniddeso [V 0.0034] vuttapaṭipakkhavaseneva veditabbo. Akuppadhammoti idaṃ pana aṭṭhasamāpattilābhino anāgāmissa ceva khīṇāsavassa cāti dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ nāmaṃ. Tesañhi samādhipāribandhakā vipassanāpāribandhakā ca dhammā suvikkhambhitā suvikkhālitā; tena tesaṃ [P 0.0182] bhassasaṅgaṇikārāmādikiccena vā aññena vā yena kenaci attano anurūpena pamādena vītināmentānampi samāpatti na kuppati, na nassati. Sukkhavipassakā pana sotāpannasakadāgāmianāgāmikhīṇāsavā imasmiṃ duke [M 0.0034] na labbhanti; dukamuttakapuggalā nāma honti. Tasmā satthā attano buddhasubuddhatāya heṭṭhā gahite ca aggahite ca saṅkaḍḍhitvā imasmimpi duke saddhiṃ piṭṭhivaṭṭakehi tantiṃ āropento sabbepi ariyapuggalātiādimāha. Aṭṭhannañhi samāpattīnaṃ kuppanaṃ nassanaṃ bhaveyya, lokuttaradhammassa pana sakiṃ paṭividdhassa kuppanaṃ nassanaṃ nāma natthi, taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

4. The explanation of 'unshakable' (akuppadhamma) should be understood based on the opposing factors already stated. 'Unshakable' is a term for two types of individuals: non-returners who have attained the eight attainments and arahants. For them, the factors obstructive to concentration and obstructive to insight are fully suppressed and dispelled; therefore, even if they spend time in idle talk, socializing, enjoying parks and the like, or by any other suitable negligence of their own, their attainment does not waver, it is not lost. However, dry-insight practitioners—stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, and arahants—are not found in this pair; they are called individuals excluded from the pair. Thus, the Teacher, through his own perfect enlightenment, drawing together both those included and those not included from below, when establishing the enumeration even in this pair along with those counted in the category, says, 'all noble individuals,' and so on. For the eight attainments, there could be wavering and loss, but for the supramundane Dhamma, once penetrated, there is no such thing as wavering or loss; this is what is meant here.

5. Parihānadhammāparihānadhammaniddesāpi kuppadhammākuppadhammaniddesavaseneva veditabbā. Kevalañhi idha puggalassa pamādaṃ paṭicca dhammānaṃ parihānampi aparihānampi gahitanti idaṃ pariyāyadesanāmattameva nānaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha tādisameva.

5. The exposition on the qualities subject to decline and the qualities not subject to decline should also be understood in the same way as the exposition on qualities liable to fall and qualities unshakable. The only difference here is that this is merely a teaching by way of explanation, which takes into account both the decline and non-decline of qualities depending on a person's negligence. The rest is just the same in every respect.

7. Cetanābhabbaniddese – cetanābhabboti cetanāya aparihāniṃ āpajjituṃ bhabbo. Sace anusañcetetīti, sace samāpajjati. Samāpattiñhi samāpajjanto anusañceteti nāma. So na parihāyati, itaro parihāyati.

7. In the exposition on 'fit for intention' (cetanābhabbā): 'fit for intention' means fit to avoid decline by means of intention. 'If one intends repeatedly' means if one attains absorption. For one who attains absorption is said to intend repeatedly. Such a one does not decline; the other declines.

8. Anurakkhaṇābhabbaniddese – anurakkhaṇābhabboti anurakkhaṇāya aparihāniṃ āpajjituṃ bhabbo. Sace anurakkhatīti sace anupakāradhamme pahāya upakāradhamme sevanto samāpajjati. Evañhi paṭipajjanto anurakkhati nāma. So na parihāyati, itaro parihāyati.

8. In the exposition on 'fit for guarding' (anurakkhaṇābhabbā): 'fit for guarding' means fit to avoid decline by means of guarding. 'If one guards' means if one abandons unbeneficial qualities and cultivates beneficial qualities, thereby attaining. For one who practices in this way is said to guard. Such a one does not decline, while the other declines.

Ime dvepi samāpattiṃ ṭhapetuṃ thāvaraṃ kātuṃ paṭibalā. Cetanābhabbato pana anurakkhaṇābhabbova balavataro. Cetanābhabbo hi upakārānupakāre dhamme na jānāti. Ajānanto upakāradhamme nudati nīharati, anupakāradhamme sevati. So te sevanto samāpattito parihāyati[V 0.0035]. Anurakkhaṇābhabbo upakārānupakāre dhamme jānāti. Jānanto anupakāradhamme [P 0.0183] nudati nīharati, upakāradhamme sevati. So te sevanto samāpattito na parihāyati.

These two are both capable of establishing and making the attainment firm. However, the one fit for guarding is more powerful than the one fit for intention. For the one fit for intention does not know qualities that are helpful or unhelpful. Not knowing, he rejects and eliminates helpful qualities, and cultivates unhelpful qualities. Cultivating these, he falls away from the attainment. The one fit for guarding knows qualities that are helpful or unhelpful. Knowing, he rejects and eliminates unhelpful qualities, and cultivates helpful qualities. Cultivating these, he does not fall away from the attainment.

Yathā hi dve khettapālā eko paṇḍurogena sarogo akkhamo sītādīnaṃ, eko arogo sītādīnaṃ saho. Sarogo heṭṭhākuṭiṃ na otarati, rattārakkhaṃ divārakkhaṃ vijahati. Tassa divā sukamorādayo khettaṃ otaritvā sālisīsaṃ khādanti, rattiṃ migasūkarādayo pavisitvā khalaṃ [M 0.0035] tacchi taṃ viya chetvā gacchanti. So attano pamattakāraṇā puna bījamattampi na labhati. Itaro rattārakkhaṃ divārakkhaṃ na vijahati. So attano appamattakāraṇā ekakarīsato cattāripi aṭṭhapi sakaṭāni labhati.

For example, just as there are two field keepers: one diseased with paleness, sickly, incapable of enduring cold and such, and the other healthy, capable of enduring cold and such. The sickly one does not go down to the lower hut, and abandons guarding by night and guarding by day. For him, during the day, birds such as parrots and peacocks descend on the field and eat the rice heads. At night, animals such as deer and boars enter and, as if carving out the threshing floor, cut and depart. He, because of his own negligence, does not even obtain seed. The other does not abandon guarding by night and guarding by day. He, because of his own non-negligence, obtains four or even eight cartloads from just one karisa.

Tattha sarogakhettapālo viya cetanābhabbo, arogo viya anurakkhaṇābhabbo daṭṭhabbo. Sarogassa attano pamādena puna bījamattassapi alabhanaṃ viya cetanābhabbassa upakārānupakāre dhamme ajānitvā upakāre pahāya anupakāre sevantassa samāpattiyā parihānaṃ. Itarassa attano appamādena ekakarīsamattato catuaṭṭhasakaṭauddharaṇaṃ viya anurakkhaṇābhabbassa upakārānupakāre dhamme jānitvā anupakāre pahāya upakāre sevantassa samāpattiyā aparihānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Evaṃ cetanābhabbato anurakkhaṇābhabbova samāpattiṃ thāvaraṃ kātuṃ balavataroti veditabbo.

Here, the sickly field guard should be seen as like the one fit for intention, and the healthy one as like the one fit for guarding. Just as the sickly one, due to his own negligence, fails to obtain even a seed, so too the one fit for intention, not knowing helpful and unhelpful qualities, abandoning the helpful and cultivating the unhelpful, experiences decline from the attainment. The other, due to his diligence, obtains four or eight cartloads from just one karisa—this should be understood as like the one fit for guarding, who, knowing helpful and unhelpful qualities, abandons the unhelpful and cultivates the helpful, resulting in no decline from the attainment. Thus, it should be understood that the one fit for guarding is more powerful than the one fit for intention in making the attainment firm.

9. Puthujjananiddese – tīṇi saṃyojanānīti diṭṭhisaṃyojanasīlabbataparāmāsasaṃyojanavicikicchāsaṃyojanāni. Etāni hi phalakkhaṇe pahīnāni nāma honti. Ayaṃ pana phalakkhaṇepi na hotīti dasseti. Tesaṃ dhammānanti tesaṃ saṃyojanadhammānaṃ. Maggakkhaṇasmiñhi tesaṃ pahānāya paṭipanno nāma hoti. Ayaṃ pana maggakkhaṇepi na hoti. Ettāvatā vissaṭṭhakammaṭṭhāno thūlabālaputhujjanova idha kathitoti veditabbo.

9. In the explanation of the ordinary person—the three fetters are the fetter of views, the fetter of clinging to rites and observances, and the fetter of doubt. These are indeed abandoned at the moment of fruition. But this shows that this person is not even at the moment of fruition. “Of those phenomena” refers to those phenomena of the fetters. For at the moment of the path, one is said to be practicing for their abandonment. But this person is not even at the moment of the path. To this extent, it should be understood that here only a gross, foolish ordinary person who has abandoned his meditation subject is being discussed.

10. Gotrabhuniddese [P 0.0184] – yesaṃ dhammānanti yesaṃ gotrabhuñāṇena saddhiṃ uppannānaṃ paropaṇṇāsakusaladhammānaṃ. Ariyadhammassāti lokuttaramaggassa. Avakkanti hotīti okkanti nibbatti pātubhāvo hoti. Ayaṃ vuccatīti ayaṃ nibbānārammaṇena ñāṇena sabbaṃ puthujjanasaṅkhaṃ puthujjanagottaṃ [V 0.0036] puthujjanamaṇḍalaṃ puthujjanapaññattiṃ atikkamitvā ariyasaṅkhaṃ ariyagottaṃ ariyamaṇḍalaṃ ariyapaññattiṃ okkamanato gotrabhūpuggalo nāma vuccati.

10. In the explanation of the lineage-breaker—“of which qualities” refers to the wholesome qualities, over fifty in number, that arise together with the lineage-breaker knowledge. “The noble quality” refers to the supramundane path. “There is entry” means there is descent, production, manifestation. This person is called a lineage-breaker individual because, by means of knowledge that has Nibbāna as its object, he has transcended all the multitude of ordinary people, the lineage of ordinary people, the sphere of ordinary people, and the designation of ordinary people, and has entered into the multitude of noble ones, the lineage of noble ones, the sphere of noble ones, and the designation of noble ones.

11. Bhayūparataniddese – bhayena uparatoti bhayūparato. Sattapi sekkhā puthujjanā ca bhāyitvā pāpato oramanti pāpaṃ na karonti[M 0.0036]. Tattha puthujjanā duggatibhayaṃ, vaṭṭabhayaṃ, kilesabhayaṃ, upavādabhayanti cattāri bhayāni bhāyanti. Tesu bhāyitabbaṭṭhena duggatiyeva bhayaṃ duggatibhayaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Tattha puthujjano ‘sace tvaṃ pāpaṃ karissasi, cattāro apāyā mukhaṃ vivaritvā ṭhitacchātaajagarasadisā, tesu dukkhaṃ anubhavanto kathaṃ bhavissasī’ti duggatibhayaṃ bhāyitvā pāpaṃ na karoti. Anamataggasaṃsāravaṭṭaṃyeva pana vaṭṭabhayaṃ nāma. Sabbampi akusalaṃ kilesabhayaṃ nāma. Garahā pana upavādabhayaṃ nāma. Tānipi bhāyitvā puthujjano pāpaṃ na karoti. Sotāpannasakadāgāmianāgāmino pana tayo sekkhā duggatiṃ atītattā sesāni tīṇi bhayāni bhāyitvā pāpaṃ na karonti. Maggaṭṭhakasekkhā āgamanavasena vā asamucchinnabhayattā vā bhayūparatā nāma honti. Khīṇāsavo imesu catūsu bhayesu ekampi na bhāyati. So hi sabbaso samucchinnabhayo; tasmā abhayūparatoti vuccati. Kiṃ pana so upavādampi na bhāyatīti? Na bhāyati. Upavādaṃ pana rakkhatīti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Doṇuppalavāpigāme khīṇāsavatthero viya.

11. In the explanation of one restrained by fear: ‘restrained by fear’ means one who is restrained out of fear. The seven trainees and ordinary people, being afraid, abstain from evil and do not commit evil. Therein, ordinary people fear four kinds of fear: fear of a bad destination, fear of the round of rebirth, fear of defilements, and fear of blame. Among these, the bad destination itself is fear because it is to be feared; the same applies to the rest. Herein, an ordinary person, fearing the fear of a bad destination, thinks, “If you do evil, the four woeful states will open their mouths like hungry pythons standing ready; how will you be, experiencing suffering there?” and thus does not commit evil. The beginningless cycle of rebirth is called the fear of the round. All that is unwholesome is called the fear of defilements. Reproach is called the fear of blame. Fearing these, an ordinary person does not commit evil. The three trainees—stream-enterers, once-returners, and non-returners—having transcended the bad destination, abstain from evil out of fear of the remaining three fears. Those trainees who are on the path are called ‘restrained by fear’ either in relation to their potential return or because their fear is not fully eradicated. The one whose cankers are destroyed does not fear even one of these four fears. For he is entirely free from fear; thus, he is called ‘not restrained by fear.’ But does such a one not fear blame either? He does not fear it. However, it is fitting to say that he is careful regarding blame, like the elder whose cankers were destroyed in the village of Doṇuppalavāpi.

12. Abhabbāgamananiddese [P 0.0185] – sammattaniyāmāgamanassa abhabboti abhabbāgamano. Kammāvaraṇenāti pañcavidhena ānantariyakammena. Kilesāvaraṇenāti niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā. Vipākāvaraṇenāti ahetukaduhetukapaṭisandhiyā. Assaddhāti buddhadhammasaṅghesu saddhārahitā. Acchandikāti kattukamyatākusalacchandarahitā. Te ṭhapetvā jambudīpaṃ itaradīpattayavāsino veditabbā. Tesu hi manussā acchandikabhāvaṃ paviṭṭhā nāma. Duppaññāti bhavaṅgapaññārahitā. Abhabbāti appaṭiladdhamaggaphalūpanissayā. Niyāmanti magganiyāmaṃ, sammattaniyāmaṃ. Okkamitunti etaṃ kusalesu dhammesu sammattasaṅkhātaṃ niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ pavisituṃ tattha patiṭṭhātuṃ abhabbā.

12. In the explanation of ‘incapable of progress’: one who is incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness is ‘incapable of progress.’ By the obstacle of kamma: through the fivefold kamma with immediate result. By the obstacle of defilements: through fixed wrong view. By the obstacle of result: through rebirth-linking without root-causes or with two root-causes. Without faith: lacking faith in the Buddha, Dhamma, and Saṅgha. Without desire: devoid of the wholesome desire to act. Except for those in Jambudīpa, the inhabitants of the other three continents should be understood as such. For indeed, the people there are said to have entered a state of lacking desire. Unwise: lacking fundamental wisdom. Incapable: without having attained the decisive support for the path and fruition. Fixed course: the fixed course of the path, the fixed course of rightness. To enter: they are incapable of entering, penetrating, or establishing themselves in that fixed course called rightness among wholesome states.

13. Bhabbāgamananiddeso vuttapaṭipakkhanayena veditabbo. Evamimasmiṃ duke ye ca puggalā pañcānantariyakā, ye ca niyatamicchādiṭṭhikā, yehi ca ahetukaduhetukapaṭisandhi gahitā[V 0.0037], ye ca buddhādīnaṃ na saddahanti, yesañca kattukamyatāchando natthi, ye ca aparipuṇṇabhavaṅgapaññā, yesañca maggaphalānaṃ upanissayo natthi, te sabbepi sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamituṃ abhabbā, viparītā bhabbāti vuttā.

13. The explanation of ‘capable of progress’ should be understood by the opposite method to what has been stated. Thus, in this dyad, those individuals who have committed the five deeds with immediate result, those with fixed wrong view, those who have taken a rebirth-linking without root-causes or with two root-causes, those who do not have faith in the Buddha and so forth, those who lack the wholesome desire to act, those with undeveloped fundamental wisdom, and those without the decisive support for the paths and fruits—all these are incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness. The opposite are said to be capable.

14. Niyatāniyataniddese [M 0.0037] – ānantarikāti āntarikakammasamaṅgino. Micchādiṭṭhikāti niyatamicchādiṭṭhisamaṅgino. Sabbepi hete nirayassa atthāya niyatattā niyatā nāma. Aṭṭha pana ariyapuggalā sammābhāvāya uparūparimaggaphalatthāya ceva anupādāparinibbānatthāya ca niyatattā niyatā nāma. Avasesapuggalā pana anibaddhagatikā. Yathā ākāse khittadaṇḍo pathaviyaṃ patanto ‘aggena vā majjhena vā mūlena vā patissatī’ti na ñāyati; evameva ‘asukagatiyā nāma nibbattissantī’ti niyamābhāvā aniyatā nāmāti veditabbā. Yā pana uttarakurukānaṃ niyatagatikatā [P 0.0186] vuttā, na sā niyatadhammavasena. Micchattasammattaniyatadhammāyeva hi niyatā nāma. Tesañca vasenāyaṃ puggalaniyamo kathitoti.

14. In the explanation of 'fixed and unfixed': 'Those with kamma with immediate result' are persons endowed with such kamma. 'Those with wrong view' are persons endowed with fixed wrong view. All these are called 'fixed' because they are destined for hell. However, the eight noble individuals are called 'fixed' because they are destined for rightness, for the attainment of successively higher paths and fruits, and for final Nibbāna without clinging. The remaining individuals are of unfixed destination. Just as a stick thrown into the air, as it falls to the earth, it is not known whether it will fall on its tip, or its middle, or its base; even so, because there is no certainty as to which destination they will be reborn in, they are to be known as 'unfixed.' The fixed destination of the Uttarakuru beings, however, is not in terms of fixed principles. Only those principles fixed in wrongness or rightness are called 'fixed,' and this classification of individuals is spoken of based on them.

15. Paṭipannakaniddese – maggasamaṅginoti maggaṭṭhakapuggalā. Te hi phalatthāya paṭipannattā paṭipannakā nāma. Phalasamaṅginoti phalapaṭilābhasamaṅgitāya phalasamaṅgino. Phalapaṭilābhato paṭṭhāya hi te phalasamāpattiṃ asamāpannāpi phale ṭhitāyeva nāma.

15. In the explanation of ‘those practicing the path’: ‘those endowed with the path’ are individuals standing on the path. They are called ‘those practicing the path’ because they are practicing for the sake of the fruit. ‘Those endowed with the fruit’ are so called because they are endowed with the acquisition of the fruit. From the moment of attaining the fruit, even if they have not entered a fruition attainment, they are still considered to be established in the fruit.

16. Samasīsīniddese – apubbaṃ acarimanti apure apacchā, ekappahārenevāti attho. Pariyādānanti parikkhayo. Ayaṃ vuccatīti ayaṃ puggalo samasīsī nāma vuccati. So panesa tividho hoti – iriyāpathasamasīsī, rogasamasīsī, jīvitasamasīsīti. Tattha yo caṅkamantova vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā arahattaṃ patvā caṅkamantova parinibbāti padumatthero viya; ṭhitakova vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā arahattaṃ patvā ṭhitakova parinibbāti koṭapabbatavihāravāsītissatthero viya; nisinnova vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā arahattaṃ patvā nisinnova parinibbāti, nipannova vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā arahattaṃ patvā nipannova parinibbāti – ayaṃ iriyāpathasamasīsī nāma.

16. In the explanation of 'samasīsī': 'apubbaṃ acarimanti' means 'not before, not after'; the meaning is 'at a single stroke.' 'Pariyādānaṃ' means 'complete ending.' This person is called 'samasīsī.' This person is of three kinds: samasīsī in posture, samasīsī in illness, and samasīsī in life. Herein, one who establishes insight while walking and attains arahantship, then attains final Nibbāna while still walking, like the Elder Paduma; one who establishes insight while standing and attains arahantship, then attains final Nibbāna while still standing, like the Elder Tissa who dwelt at Koṭapabbata Monastery; one who establishes insight while sitting and attains arahantship, then attains final Nibbāna while still sitting; or one who establishes insight while lying down and attains arahantship, then attains final Nibbāna while still lying down—this is called 'samasīsī in posture.'

Yo pana ekaṃ rogaṃ patvā antorogeyeva vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā arahattaṃ patvā teneva rogena parinibbāti – ayaṃ rogasamasīsī nāma.

One who, having contracted a disease, establishes insight while still afflicted by that disease, attains arahantship, and then attains final Nibbāna by means of that very illness—this is called 'samasīsī in illness.'

Kataro [M 0.0038][V 0.0038] jīvitasamasīsī nāma? “Sīsanti terasa sīsāni – palibodhasīsañca taṇhā, vinibandhanasīsañca māno, parāmāsasīsañca diṭṭhi, vikkhepasīsañca uddhaccaṃ, saṃkilesasīsañca avijjā, adhimokkhasīsañca saddhā, paggahasīsañca vīriyaṃ, upaṭṭhānasīsañca sati, avikkhepasīsañca samādhi, dassanasīsañca paññā, pavattasīsañca jīvitindriyaṃ, gocarasīsañca vimokkho, saṅkhārasīsañca nirodho”ti (paṭi. ma. 1.87). Tattha kilesasīsaṃ avijjaṃ arahattamaggo pariyādiyati. Pavattasīsaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ cuticittaṃ pariyādiyati. Avijjāpariyādāyakaṃ [P 0.0187] cittaṃ jīvitindriyaṃ pariyādātuṃ na sakkoti. Jīvitindriyapariyādāyakaṃ cittaṃ avijjaṃ pariyādātuṃ na sakkoti. Avijjāpariyādāyakaṃ cittaṃ aññaṃ, jīvitindriyapariyādāyakaṃ cittaṃ aññaṃ. Yassa cetaṃ sīsadvayaṃ samaṃ pariyādānaṃ gacchati, so jīvitasamasīsī nāma.

Who is one called 'one with life and head equal'? 'A "head" means thirteen heads: the head of obstruction, namely craving; the head of bondage, namely conceit; the head of grasping, namely wrong view; the head of scattering, namely restlessness; the head of defilement, namely ignorance; the head of conviction, namely faith; the head of striving, namely energy; the head of establishing, namely mindfulness; the head of non-scattering, namely concentration; the head of seeing, namely wisdom; the head of continuing, namely the life-faculty; the head of range, namely liberation; the head of formations, namely cessation' (Patisambhidamagga 1.87). Here, the path of arahantship completely ends the head of defilement, which is ignorance. The death-consciousness completely ends the head of continuing, which is the life-faculty. The consciousness that completely ends ignorance cannot completely end the life-faculty. The consciousness that completely ends the life-faculty cannot completely end ignorance. The consciousness that completely ends ignorance is one, the consciousness that completely ends the life-faculty is another. One for whom these two heads come to an equal ending is called 'one with life and head equal'.

Kathamidaṃ samaṃ hotīti? Vārasamatāya. Yasmiñhi vāre maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti – sotāpattimagge pañca paccavekkhaṇāni, sakadāgāmimagge pañca, anāgāmimagge pañca, arahattamagge cattārīti ekūnavīsatiyā paccavekkhaṇañāṇe patiṭṭhāya bhavaṅgaṃ otaritvā parinibbāyati. Imāya vārasamatāya idaṃ ubhayasīsapariyādānaṃ samaṃ hoti nāma. Tenāyaṃ puggalo jīvitasamasīsīti vuccati. Ayameva ca idha adhippeto.

How is this equal? By the equality of occasions. For in whichever occasion the path arises – in the stream-entry path, five reviewing cognitions; in the once-returner path, five; in the non-returner path, five; in the arahant path, four – thus, based on nineteen reviewing cognitions, having descended into the life-continuum, one attains final Nibbāna. By this equality of occasions, this complete ending of both heads is called equal. Therefore, this person is called 'one with life and head equal.' And this is precisely what is meant here.

17. Ṭhitakappīniddese – ṭhito kappoti ṭhitakappo, ṭhitakappo assa atthīti ṭhitakappī. Kappaṃ ṭhapetuṃ samatthoti attho. Uḍḍayhanavelā assāti jhāyanakālo bhaveyya. Neva tāvāti yāva esa maggasamaṅgī puggalo sotāpattiphalaṃ na sacchikaroti, neva tāva kappo jhāyeyya. Jhāyamānopi ajjhāyitvāva tiṭṭheyya. Kappavināso hi nāma mahāvikāro mahāpayogo koṭisatasahassacakkavāḷassa jhāyanavasena mahālokavināso. Ayampi evaṃ mahāvināso tiṭṭheyya vāti vadati. Sāsane pana dharamāne ayaṃ kappavināso nāma natthi. Kappavināse sāsanaṃ natthi. Gatakoṭike hi kāle kappavināso nāma hoti. Evaṃ santepi satthā antarāyābhāvaṃ dīpetuṃ idaṃ kāraṇaṃ āhari – “idampi bhaveyya, maggasamaṅgino pana phalassa antarāyo na sakkā kātu”nti. Ayaṃ pana puggalo kappaṃ ṭhapento kittakaṃ kālaṃ ṭhapeyyāti? Yasmiṃ [M 0.0039] vāre maggavuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, atha bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭentaṃ manodvārāvajjanaṃ uppajjati. Tato tīṇi anulomāni, ekaṃ gotrabhucittaṃ, ekaṃ maggacittaṃ, dve phalacittāni, pañca [V 0.0039] paccavekkhaṇañāṇānīti [P 0.0188] ettakaṃ kālaṃ ṭhapeyya. Imaṃ panatthaṃ bāhirāya āgantukūpamāyapi evaṃ dīpayiṃsu. Sace hi sotāpattimaggasamaṅgissa matthakūpari yojanikaṃ ekagghanaselaṃ tivaṭṭāya rajjuyā bandhitvā olambeyya, ekasmiṃ vaṭṭe chinne dvīhi olambeyya, dvīsu chinnesu ekena olambeyyeva, tasmimpi chinne abbhakūṭaṃ viya ākāse tiṭṭheyya, na tveva tassa puggalassa maggānantaraphalassa antarāyaṃ kareyyāti. Ayaṃ pana dīpanā parittā, purimāva mahantā. Na kevalaṃ pana sotāpattimaggaṭṭhova kappaṃ ṭhapeti, itare maggasamaṅginopi ṭhapentiyeva. Tena bhagavā heṭṭhā gahitañca aggahitañca sabbaṃ saṅkaḍḍhitvā saddhiṃ piṭṭhivaṭṭakapuggalehi imaṃ tantiṃ āropesi – “sabbepi maggasamaṅgino puggalā ṭhitakappino”ti.

17. In the explanation of 'one who keeps the aeon stable' (ṭhitakappī) – ṭhito kappo means 'a stable aeon'; 'one who has a stable aeon' is a ṭhitakappī. The meaning is 'one who is capable of keeping the aeon stable.' Uḍḍayhanavelā assā means 'the time for its burning up.' 'Not yet' means: as long as this individual endowed with the path has not realized the fruit of stream-entry, the aeon would not yet burn up. Even if it were burning up, it would remain without having burned. For the destruction of an aeon is a great calamity, a tremendous undertaking – the great destruction of a hundred thousand million world-systems through burning. It is said that even such a great destruction as this would remain. However, as long as the Dispensation endures, there is no such thing as the destruction of an aeon. When an aeon is destroyed, there is no Dispensation. For the destruction of an aeon occurs only when an incalculable period has passed. Even so, the Teacher cited this reason to show the absence of obstacles: 'This too might happen, but for one endowed with the path, no obstacle can be made to the fruit.' Now, for how long would this individual keep the aeon stable? At the moment when there is an arising from the path, then the mind-door adverting cognition arises, turning away from the life-continuum. Then follow three conformity cognitions, one change-of-lineage cognition, one path cognition, two fruition cognitions, and five reviewing cognitions – for that length of time, one would keep it stable. This meaning was also illustrated by an external simile. For if a solid rock a league in size were tied with a three-stranded rope and suspended above the head of one endowed with the stream-entry path, and if one strand were cut, it would hang by two; if two were cut, it would hang by one; and if that too were cut, it would remain in the sky like a cloud peak – yet even that would not create an obstacle to the fruit immediately following the path of that individual. This illustration is minor; the previous one is major. Not only does one standing on the stream-entry path keep the aeon stable, but those endowed with the other paths also keep it stable. Therefore, the Blessed One, gathering all that was taken below and not taken, along with those with rounded shoulders, established this teaching: 'All individuals endowed with the path are those who keep the aeon stable.'

18. Ariyaniddese – kilesehi ārakattā ariyā. Sadevakena lokena araṇīyattā ariyā. Ariyaṭṭho nāma parisuddhaṭṭhoti parisuddhattāpi ariyā. Sesā aparisuddhatāya anariyā.

18. In the explanation of 'noble' (ariya) – they are noble because they are far from defilements. They are noble because they are worthy of veneration by the world with its devas. The meaning of 'noble' is 'pure'; thus, they are noble because of their purity. The rest, being impure, are ignoble.

19. Sekkhaniddese – maggasamaṅgino maggakkhaṇe, phalasamaṅgino ca phalakkhaṇe, adhisīlasikkhādikā tissopi sikkhā sikkhantiyevāti sekkhā. Arahatā pana arahattaphalakkhaṇe tisso sikkhā sikkhitā.
