Tena pana nayena sakkā so idha avuttopi jānitunti taṃ avatvā niddesavārova āraddho. Imasmiṃ pana pavattivārasaṅkhāte mahāvāre uppādavāro, nirodhavāro, uppādanirodhavāroti tayo antaravārā honti. Tesu paṭhamo dhammānaṃ uppādalakkhaṇassa dīpitattā uppādavāroti vuccati. Dutiyo tesaññeva nirodhalakkhaṇassa dīpitattā nirodhavāroti vuccati. Tatiyo ubhinnampi lakkhaṇānaṃ dīpitattā uppādanirodhavāroti vuccati. Uppādavārena cettha dhammānaṃ uppajjanākārova dīpito. Nirodhavārena ‘uppannaṃ nāma niccaṃ natthī’ti tesaññeva aniccatā dīpitā. Uppādanirodhavārena tadubhayaṃ.

50-205. Now the section on occurrence has been commenced by way of the method beginning with 'for whom the aggregate of form,' and so on. Why is the summary section not stated here? Because the method has been shown previously. For indeed, in the section on designations, the method was shown in the summary section. By that method, it is possible to understand it even if it is not stated here; therefore, without stating it, only the detailed section has been commenced. In this great section, however, known as the section on occurrence, there are three intermediate sections: the section on arising, the section on cessation, and the section on arising and cessation. Among these, the first is called the section on arising because it reveals the characteristic of arising of phenomena. The second is called the section on cessation because it reveals the characteristic of cessation of those same phenomena. The third is called the section on arising and cessation because it reveals both characteristics. Here, by the section on arising, only the mode of origination of phenomena is revealed. By the section on cessation, the impermanence of those same phenomena is revealed, as in: 'What has arisen is indeed not permanent.' By the section on arising and cessation, both are revealed.

Tattha uppādavāre tāva tiṇṇaṃ addhānaṃ vasena cha kālabhedā honti – paccuppanno, atīto, anāgato, paccuppannenātīto, paccuppannenānāgato, atītenānāgatoti. Tesu ‘yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjatī’ti paccuppannābhidhānavasena paccuppanno veditabbo. So paccuppannānaṃ dhammānaṃ paccakkhato gahetabbattā ativiya suviññeyyoti paṭhamaṃ vutto. Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjitthāti atītābhidhānavasena atīto veditabbo. So paccakkhato anubhūtapubbānaṃ atītadhammānaṃ anumānena anāgatehi suviññeyyatarattā dutiyaṃ vutto. Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjissatīti anāgatābhidhānavasena anāgato veditabbo. So paccakkhato ca anubhūtapubbavasena ca gahitadhammānumānena ‘anāgatepi evarūpā dhammā uppajjissantī’ti gahetabbato [P 0.0062] tatiyaṃ vutto.

Here, in the section on arising, there are first six divisions of time by way of the three periods: present, past, future, present-past, present-future, and past-future. Among these, 'for whom the aggregate of form arises' is to be understood as the present, by way of the designation of the present. It is stated first because it is very easily understood, since present phenomena are to be directly apprehended. 'For whom the aggregate of form arose' is to be understood as the past, by way of the designation of the past. It is stated second because it is more easily understood than future phenomena, being inferred from past phenomena that were previously experienced directly. 'For whom the aggregate of form will arise' is to be understood as the future, by way of the designation of the future. It is stated third because it is to be apprehended by inference based on phenomena already grasped through direct experience and past experience, thinking, 'such phenomena will also arise in the future.'

Yassa [V 0.0296] rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjitthāti paccuppannena saddhiṃ atītābhidhānavasena paccuppannenātīto veditabbo. So missakesu tīsu suviññeyyatarattā catutthaṃ vutto. Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti paccuppannena saddhiṃ anāgatābhidhānavasena paccuppannenānāgato veditabbo. So paccakkhato gahetabbānaṃ dhammānaṃ atthitāya atthato suviññeyyataroti pañcamaṃ vutto. Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjissatīti atītena [M 0.0297] saddhiṃ anāgatābhidhānavasena atītenānāgato veditabbo. So purimehi duviññeyyoti chaṭṭhaṃ vutto.

'For whom the aggregate of form arises, for him the aggregate of feeling arose' — this is to be understood as the present-past, by way of designating the past together with the present. It is stated as the fourth because it is more easily understood among the three mixed cases. 'For whom the aggregate of form arises, for him the aggregate of feeling will arise' — this is to be understood as the present-future, by way of designating the future together with the present. It is stated as the fifth because it is more easily understood in reality due to the existence of phenomena to be directly apprehended. 'For whom the aggregate of form arose, for him the aggregate of feeling will arise' — this is to be understood as the past-future, by way of designating the future together with the past. It is stated as the sixth because it is more difficult to understand than the previous ones.

Evametesu chasu kālabhedesu yvāyaṃ paṭhamo paccuppanno, tattha puggalato, okāsato, puggalokāsatoti tayo vārā honti. Tesu yassāti puggalavasena khandhānaṃ uppattidīpano puggalavāro. Yatthāti okāsavasena khandhānaṃ uppattidīpano okāsavāro. Yassa yatthāti puggalokāsavasena khandhānaṃ uppattidīpano puggalokāsavāro. Ime pana tayopi vārā paṭhamaṃ anulomanayena niddisitvā pacchā paṭilomanayena niddiṭṭhā. Tesu ‘uppajjati’ ‘uppajjittha,’ ‘uppajjissatī’ti vacanato uppattidīpano anulomanayo. ‘Nuppajjati’, ‘nuppajjittha,’ ‘nuppajjissatī’ti vacanato anuppattidīpano paṭilomanayo.

Thus, among these six divisions of time, in the first, which is the present, there are three sections: by way of the individual, by way of the location, and by way of the individual and location. Among these, 'whose' refers to the section on the individual, which reveals the arising of aggregates by way of the individual. 'Where' refers to the section on the location, which reveals the arising of aggregates by way of the location. 'Whose where' refers to the section on the individual and location, which reveals the arising of aggregates by way of the individual and location. These three sections, however, are first specified in direct order and then specified in reverse order. Among these, the direct order reveals arising with statements like 'arises,' 'arose,' and 'will arise.' The reverse order reveals non-arising with statements like 'does not arise,' 'did not arise,' and 'will not arise.'

Tattha paccuppannakāle tāva puggalavārassa anulomanaye “yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjati. Yassa vā pana vedanākkhandho uppajjati, tassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati. Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho, viññāṇakkhandho, uppajjati. Yassa vā pana viññāṇakkhandho uppajjati, tassa rūpakkhandho uppajjatī”ti evaṃ rūpakkhandhamūlakāni cattāri yamakāni; “yassa vedanākkhandho uppajjati, tassa saññākkhandho uppajjatī”tiādinā nayena vedanākkhandhamūlakāni tīṇi; saññākkhandhamūlakāni dve; saṅkhārakkhandhamūlakaṃ ekanti aggahitaggahaṇena dasa yamakāni honti.

Here, in the present time, in the section on the individual, in the direct order: "For whom the form aggregate arises, for them the feeling aggregate arises. Or, for whom the feeling aggregate arises, for them the form aggregate arises. For whom the form aggregate arises, for them the perception aggregate, the formation aggregate, and the consciousness aggregate arise. Or, for whom the consciousness aggregate arises, for them the form aggregate arises." Thus, there are four pairs rooted in the form aggregate. "For whom the feeling aggregate arises, for them the perception aggregate arises," and so on; in this manner there are three rooted in the feeling aggregate; two rooted in the perception aggregate; one rooted in the formation aggregate. Thus, by taking what has not been taken, there are ten pairs.

Tattha [P 0.0063] rūpakkhandhamūlakesu catūsu ādito ekameva vissajjitaṃ. Sesāni tena sadisavissajjanānīti tantiyā lahubhāvatthaṃ saṅkhittāni. Vedanākkhandhādimūlakesupi ‘āmantā’ti ekasadisameva vissajjanaṃ. Tasmā tānipi tantiyā lahubhāvatthaṃ saṅkhittānevāti evametāni paccuppannakāle puggalavāre anulomanaye ekayamakavissajjaneneva dasa yamakāni vissajjitāni [V 0.0297] nāma hontīti veditabbāni. Yathā ca puggalavāre dasa, evaṃ okāsavāre dasa, puggalokāsavāre dasāti paccuppannakāle tīsu vāresu anulomanaye tiṃsa yamakāni honti. Yathā ca anulomanaye, evaṃ paṭilomanayepīti sabbānipi paccuppannakāle saṭṭhi [M 0.0298] yamakāni honti. Tesu vīsapucchāsataṃ, cattārīsāni ca dve atthasatāni hontīti veditabbāni. Evaṃ sesesupi pañcasu kālabhedesu puggalādibhedato anulomapaṭilomanayavasena cha cha vārā. Ekekasmiṃ vāre dasa dasa katvā saṭṭhi saṭṭhi yamakānīti tīṇi yamakasatāni. Tāni purimehi saddhiṃ saṭṭhādhikāni tīṇi yamakasatāni, vīsādhikāni sattapucchāsatāni, cattārīsāni ca cuddasa atthasatāni honti. Idaṃ tāva uppādavāre pāḷivavatthānaṃ. Yathā ca uppādavāre, tathā nirodhavārepi, uppādanirodhavārepīti sabbasmimpi pavattimahāvāre asīti yamakasahassaṃ, saṭṭhisatādhikāni dve pucchāsahassāni, vīsaṃ tisatādhikāni ca cattāri atthasahassāni veditabbāni.

Here, among the four pairs rooted in the form aggregate, only one is resolved at the beginning. The rest are abbreviated for the sake of brevity in the text, as their resolutions are similar to that one. Even regarding those rooted in the feeling aggregate and so on, the resolution is simply 'yes,' being of one similar kind. Therefore, these too are abbreviated for the sake of brevity in the text. Thus, it should be understood that in the present time, in the section on individuals, in the progressive order, these ten pairs are resolved by the resolution of a single pair. Just as there are ten in the section on individuals, so too there are ten in the section on locations, and ten in the section on individuals and locations. Thus, in the present time, in the three sections in the progressive order, there are thirty pairs. And just as in the progressive order, so too in the reverse order—thus, in all, in the present time, there are sixty pairs. Among these, it should be understood that there are 120 questions and 240 answers. Similarly, in the remaining five divisions of time, based on the divisions of individuals and so forth, following both progressive and reverse orders, there are six sections each. In each section, counting ten pairs each, there are sixty pairs, totaling three hundred pairs. These, together with the previous ones, make 360 pairs, 720 questions, and 1,440 answers. This, for now, is the arrangement of the Pali text in the arising section. Just as in the arising section, so too in the cessation section, and in the arising and cessation section—thus, in the entire great section on occurrence, it should be understood that there are 80,000 pairs, 2,160 questions, and 4,320 answers.

Pāḷi pana uppādavāre nirodhavāre ca tīsu asammissakakālabhedesu tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vāre ekekameva yamakaṃ vissajjetvā saṅkhittā. Tīsu missakakālabhedesu ‘yassa vedanākkhandho uppajjati, tassa saññākkhandho uppajjitthā’tiādinā nayena vedanākkhandhādimūlakesupi ekaṃ yamakaṃ vissajjitaṃ. Uppādanirodhavāre pana chasupi kālabhedesu taṃ vissajjitameva. Sesāni tena samānavissajjanattā saṅkhittānīti. Idaṃ sakalepi pavattimahāvāre pāḷivavatthānaṃ.

The Pali text, however, in the arising section and the cessation section, is abbreviated, having resolved just one pair in each of the three unmixed time divisions for each section. In the three mixed time divisions, one pair is resolved even in those rooted in the feeling aggregate and so on, in the manner of “for whom the feeling aggregate arises, for them had the perception aggregate arisen,” etc. In the arising-and-cessation section, however, that is resolved in all six time divisions. The rest are abbreviated because their resolution is similar to that. This is the arrangement of the Pali text in the entire great section on occurrence.

Atthavinicchayatthaṃ panassa idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ – imasmiñhi pavattimahāvāre catunnaṃ pañhānaṃ pañca vissajjanāni sattavīsatiyā ṭhānesu pakkhipitvā atthavinicchayo veditabbo. Tattha [P 0.0064] purepañho, pacchāpañho, paripuṇṇapañho, moghapañhoti ime cattāro pañhā nāma. Ekekasmiñhi yamake dve dve pucchā. Ekekapucchāyapi dve dve padāni. Tattha yāya pucchāya vissajjane ekeneva padena gahitakkhandhassa uppādo vā nirodho vā labbhati[V 0.0298], ayaṃ purepañho nāma. Yāya pana pucchāya vissajjane dvīhipi padehi gahitakkhandhānaṃ uppādo vā nirodho vā labbhati, ayaṃ pacchāpañho nāma. Yāya pana pucchāya vissajjane ekenapi padena gahitakkhandhassa dvīhipi padehi gahitakkhandhānaṃ uppādo vā, nirodho vā labbhati, ayaṃ paripuṇṇapañho nāma. Yāya pana pucchāya vissajjane paṭikkhepo vā, paṭisedho vā labbhati, ayaṃ moghapañho nāma. Yasmā panesa adassiyamāno na sakkā jānituṃ, tasmā naṃ dassayissāma.

For the determination of its meaning, this characteristic should be known: in this great section on occurrence, the meaning should be discerned by placing the five resolutions of the four questions in twenty-seven instances. Herein, there are four types of questions: the prior question, the subsequent question, the complete question, and the futile question. In each pair, there are two questions. Each question also has two terms. Herein, the question where, in the resolution, the arising or cessation of the aggregate taken with just one term is obtained, this is called the prior question. The question where, in the resolution, the arising or cessation of the aggregates taken with both terms is obtained, this is called the subsequent question. The question where, in the resolution, the arising or cessation of the aggregate taken with one term, or of the aggregates taken with both terms, is obtained, this is called the complete question. The question where, in the resolution, rejection or denial is obtained, this is called the futile question. Since this cannot be known unless it is shown, therefore we will demonstrate it.

‘Yattha [M 0.0299] rūpakkhandho nuppajjati, tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjatī’ti pucchāya tāva uppajjatīti imasmiṃ vissajjane ekeneva padena gahitassa vedanākkhandhassa uppādo labbhati, iti ayañceva añño ca evarūpo pañho purepañhoti veditabbo. ‘Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjitthā’ti pucchāya pana ‘āmantā’ti imasmiṃ vissajjane dvīhi padehi gahitānaṃ rūpavedanākkhandhānaṃ yassa kassaci sattassa atīte uppādo labbhati. Iti ayañceva añño ca evarūpo pañho pacchāpañhoti veditabbo.

In the question, “Where the form aggregate does not arise, does the feeling aggregate not arise there?” in the resolution ‘it arises,’ the arising of the feeling aggregate, taken with just one term, is obtained. Thus, this and other such questions should be understood as prior questions. In the question, “For whom the form aggregate had arisen, for them had the feeling aggregate arisen?” however, in the resolution ‘yes,’ the arising of both form and feeling aggregates in the past for any being is obtained. Thus, this and other such questions should be understood as subsequent questions.

‘Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjatī’ti imāya pana paṭhamapucchāya ‘asaññasattaṃ upapajjantāna’ntiādike imasmiṃ vissajjane ‘asaññasattaṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ vedanākkhandho uppajjatī’ti imasmiṃ koṭṭhāse ekeneva padena gahitassa rūpakkhandhassapi uppādo labbhati. ‘Pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho ca uppajjati vedanākkhandho ca uppajjatī’ti imasmiṃ koṭṭhāse dvīhipi padehi saṅgahitānaṃ rūpavedanākkhandhānampi uppādo labbhati. Iti ayañceva añño ca evarūpo pañho paripuṇṇapañhoti veditabbo. Purepacchāpañhotipi [P 0.0065] etasseva nāmaṃ. Etassa hi vissajjane purimakoṭṭhāse ekena padena saṅgahitassa rūpakkhandhasseva uppādo dassito. Dutiyakoṭṭhāse dvīhi padehi saṅgahitānaṃ rūpavedanākkhandhānaṃ. Imināyeva ca lakkhaṇena yattha ekena padena saṅgahitassa khandhassa uppādo vā nirodho vā labbhati, so purepañhoti vutto. Yattha dvīhipi padehi saṅgahitānaṃ khandhānaṃ uppādo vā nirodho vā labbhati, so pacchāpañhoti vutto.

However, in this first question, ‘For whom the form aggregate arises, for them does the feeling aggregate arise?’, in this resolution beginning with ‘those arising in the non-percipient realm,’ in this section, ‘For those arising in the non-percipient realm, the form aggregate arises, but for them the feeling aggregate does not arise,’ the arising of the form aggregate, encompassed by one term, is obtained. In this section, ‘For those arising in the five-constituent existence, the form aggregate arises, and the feeling aggregate also arises,’ the arising of the form and feeling aggregates, encompassed by two terms, is also obtained. Thus, this and any other such question should be understood as a complete question. This is also called a ‘prior-and-subsequent question.’ For in its resolution, in the first section, only the arising of the form aggregate, encompassed by one term, is shown. In the second section, the arising of the form and feeling aggregates, encompassed by two terms, is shown. And by this very characteristic, wherever the arising or cessation of an aggregate, encompassed by one term, is obtained, that is called a prior question. Wherever the arising or cessation of aggregates, encompassed by two terms, is obtained, that is called a subsequent question.

‘Yassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho nuppajjitthā’ti imāya pana pucchāya ‘natthī’ti imasmiṃ vissajjane paṭikkhepo labbhati. ‘Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho nirujjhatī’ti pucchāya ‘no’ti imasmiṃ vissajjane paṭisedho labbhati. Tasmā ayañceva duvidho añño ca evarūpo pañho moghapañhoti veditabbo. Tucchapañhotipi vuccati. Evaṃ tāva cattāro pañhā veditabbā.

However, in the question ‘For whom the form aggregate did not arise, for them did the feeling aggregate not arise?’, in this resolution ‘it does not exist,’ rejection is obtained. In the question ‘For whom the form aggregate arises, for them does the feeling aggregate cease?’, in this resolution ‘no,’ denial is obtained. Therefore, this twofold question and others like it should be understood as futile questions. They are also called empty questions. Thus, these four questions should be understood.

Pāḷigatiyā [V 0.0299] vissajjanaṃ, paṭivacanavissajjanaṃ, sarūpadassanena vissajjanaṃ, paṭikkhepena vissajjanaṃ, paṭisedhena vissajjananti imāni pana pañca vissajjanāni nāma[M 0.0300]. Tattha yaṃ vissajjanaṃ pāḷipadameva hutvā atthaṃ vissajjeti, idaṃ pāḷigatiyā vissajjanaṃ nāma. Taṃ purepañhe labbhati. ‘Yattha rūpakkhandho nuppajjati tattha vedanākkhandho nuppajjatī’ti hi pañhe ‘uppajjatī’ti idaṃ vissajjanaṃ pāḷipadameva hutvā atthaṃ vissajjayamānaṃ gataṃ, tasmā evarūpesu ṭhānesu pāḷigatiyā vissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana vissajjanaṃ paṭivacanabhāvena atthaṃ vissajjeti, idaṃ paṭivacanavissajjanaṃ nāma. Taṃ pacchāpañhe labbhati. ‘Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjitthā’ti hi pañhe ‘āmantā’ti idaṃ vissajjanaṃ paṭivacanavaseneva atthaṃ vissajjayamānaṃ gataṃ, tasmā evarūpesu ṭhānesu paṭivacanavissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Yaṃ [P 0.0066] vissajjanaṃ sarūpena dassetvā atthaṃ vissajjeti; idaṃ sarūpadassanena vissajjanaṃ nāma. Taṃ paripuṇṇapañhe labbhati. ‘Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati; tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjatī’ti hi pañhe ‘asaññasattaṃ upapajjantāna’nti idaṃ vissajjanaṃ ‘imesaṃ rūpakkhandho uppajjati, no ca vedanākkhandho, imesaṃ rūpakkhandho ca uppajjati, vedanākkhandho cā’ti sarūpadassaneneva atthaṃ vissajjayamānaṃ gataṃ. Tasmā evarūpesu ṭhānesu sarūpadassanena vissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana vissajjanaṃ tathārūpassa atthassābhāvato atthapaṭikkhepena pañhaṃ vissajjeti, idaṃ paṭikkhepena vissajjanaṃ nāma. Yaṃ tathārūpassa atthassa ekakkhaṇe alābhato atthapaṭisedhanena pañhaṃ vissajjeti, idaṃ paṭisedhena vissajjanaṃ nāma. Taṃ moghapañhe labbhati. ‘Yassa rūpakkhandho nuppajjittha, tassa vedanākkhandho nuppajjitthā’ti hi pañhe ‘natthī’ti idaṃ vissajjanaṃ; evarūpo nāma satto natthīti atthapaṭikkhepena pañhaṃ vissajjayamānaṃ gataṃ; tasmā evarūpesu ṭhānesu paṭikkhepena vissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ. ‘Yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjati, tassa vedanākkhandho nirujjhatī’ti pañhe pana ‘no’ti idaṃ vissajjanaṃ ekasmiṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe uppādena saddhiṃ nirodho nāma na labbhatīti atthapaṭisedhanena pañhaṃ vissajjayamānaṃ gataṃ, tasmā evarūpesu ṭhānesu paṭisedhena vissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Now, there are these five types of resolutions: resolution by textual quotation, resolution by direct answer, resolution by specification, resolution by rejection, and resolution by denial. Among these, a resolution that resolves the meaning by being a direct quotation from the Pāli text is called a resolution by textual quotation. This is found in a prior question. For example, in the question, ‘Where the form aggregate does not arise, does the feeling aggregate not arise?’ the resolution ‘It arises’ resolves the meaning by being a direct quotation from the Pāli text. Therefore, in such cases, it should be understood as a resolution by textual quotation. A resolution that resolves the meaning by way of a direct answer is called a resolution by direct answer. This is found in a subsequent question. For example, in the question, ‘For whom the form aggregate has arisen, has the feeling aggregate arisen?’ the resolution ‘Yes’ resolves the meaning by way of a direct answer. Therefore, in such cases, it should be understood as a resolution by direct answer. A resolution that resolves the meaning by showing its own nature is called a resolution by specification. This is found in a complete question. For example, in the question, ‘For whom the form aggregate arises, does the feeling aggregate arise?’ the resolution ‘For those being reborn in the non-percipient realm…’ resolves the meaning by specification, thus: ‘For these, the form aggregate arises but not the feeling aggregate; for these, both the form aggregate and the feeling aggregate arise.’ Therefore, in such cases, it should be understood as a resolution by specification. A resolution that answers a question by rejecting its premise, due to the absence of such a thing, is called a resolution by rejection. A resolution that answers a question by denying its premise, due to its not being obtainable in a single moment, is called a resolution by denial. These are found in a futile question. For example, in the question, ‘For whom the form aggregate has not arisen, has the feeling aggregate not arisen?’ the resolution ‘There is not’ answers the question by rejecting its premise, stating, ‘Such a being does not exist.’ Therefore, in such cases, it should be understood as a resolution by rejection. In the question, ‘For whom the form aggregate arises, does the feeling aggregate cease?’ the resolution ‘No’ answers the question by denying its premise, stating, ‘Cessation together with arising in a single moment of rebirth-linking is not obtainable.’ Therefore, in such cases, it should be understood as a resolution by denial.

Idāni ime cattāro pañhā, imāni ca pañca vissajjanāni, yesu sattavīsatiyā ṭhānesu pakkhipitabbāni, tāni evaṃ veditabbāni – asaññasattaṃ upapajjantānanti ekaṃ ṭhānaṃ, asaññasatte tatthāti ekaṃ, asaññasattānanti ekaṃ; asaññasattā cavantānanti ekaṃ; arūpaṃ upapajjantānanti ekaṃ, arūpe tatthāti ekaṃ, arūpānanti ekaṃ, arūpā cavantānanti ekaṃ[V 0.0300], arūpe pacchimabhavikānanti [M 0.0301] ekaṃ, arūpe parinibbantānanti ekaṃ; ye ca arūpaṃ [P 0.0067] upapajjitvā parinibbāyissantīti ekaṃ; pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantānanti ekaṃ, pañcavokāre tatthāti ekaṃ, pañcavokārānanti ekaṃ pañcavokārā cavantānanti ekaṃ, pañcavokāre pacchimabhavikānanti ekaṃ, pañcavokāre parinibbantānanti ekaṃ; suddhāvāsaṃ upapajjantānanti ekaṃ, suddhāvāse tatthāti ekaṃ, suddhāvāsānanti ekaṃ, suddhāvāse parinibbantānanti ekaṃ; sabbesaṃ upapajjantānanti ekaṃ, sabbesaṃ cavantānanti ekaṃ; sabbasādhāraṇavasena pacchimabhavikānanti ekaṃ, parinibbantānanti ekaṃ, catuvokāraṃ pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantānanti ekaṃ, cavantānanti ekaṃ. Evaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ pañhānaṃ imāni pañca vissajjanāni imesu sattavīsatiyā ṭhānesu pakkhipitvā imasmiṃ pavattimahāvāre atthavinicchayo veditabbo. Evaṃ viditvā hi pañhaṃ vissajjantena suvissajjito hoti, atthañca vinicchayantena suvinicchito hoti.

Now these four questions and these five replies are to be placed in twenty-seven instances, which should be understood as follows: 'For those being reborn into the non-percipient realm'—one instance; 'for those dwelling there in the non-percipient realm'—one instance; 'for non-percipient beings'—one instance; 'for non-percipient beings passing away'—one instance; 'for those being reborn into the formless realm'—one instance; 'for those dwelling there in the formless realm'—one instance; 'for formless beings'—one instance; 'for formless beings passing away'—one instance; 'for those in their last existence in the formless realm'—one instance; 'for those attaining final Nibbāna in the formless realm'—one instance; 'for those who, having been reborn into the formless realm, will attain final Nibbāna'—one instance; 'for those being reborn into the five-aggregate realm'—one instance; 'for those dwelling there in the five-aggregate realm'—one instance; 'for five-aggregate beings'—one instance; 'for five-aggregate beings passing away'—one instance; 'for those in their last existence in the five-aggregate realm'—one instance; 'for those attaining final Nibbāna in the five-aggregate realm'—one instance; 'for those being reborn into the Pure Abodes'—one instance; 'for those dwelling there in the Pure Abodes'—one instance; 'for Pure Abode beings'—one instance; 'for those attaining final Nibbāna in the Pure Abodes'—one instance; 'for all beings being reborn'—one instance; 'for all beings passing away'—one instance; 'for those in their last existence in a universal sense'—one instance; 'for those attaining final Nibbāna'—one instance; 'for those being reborn into the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms'—one instance; 'for those passing away'—one instance. Thus, these five replies to the four questions are to be placed in these twenty-seven instances, and the meaning should be discerned accordingly in this great section on the course of existence. For, having understood thus, one who answers the questions answers well, and one who discerns the meaning discerns well.

Tatthāyaṃ nayo – yassa rūpakkhandho uppajjatīti yassa puggalassa uppādakkhaṇasamaṅgitāya rūpakkhandho uppajjati. Tassa vedanākkhandho uppajjatīti vedanākkhandhopi tassa tasmiññeva khaṇe uppajjatīti pucchati. Asaññasattaṃ upapajjantānanti acittakapaṭisandhivasena asaññasattabhavaṃ upapajjantānaṃ. Tesaṃ rūpakkhandho uppajjatīti tesaṃ ekantena rūpakkhandho uppajjatiyeva. Pavatte uppannānaṃ rūpakkhandho uppajjatipi nirujjhatipi, tasmā ‘asaññasattāna’nti avatvā’asaññasattaṃ upapajjantāna’nti vuttaṃ. No ca tesaṃ vedanākkhandho uppajjatīti acittakattā pana tesaṃ vedanākkhandho nuppajjateva. Idaṃ sattavīsatiyā ṭhānesu paṭhame ṭhāne paripuṇṇapañhassa purimakoṭṭhāse sarūpadassanena vissajjanaṃ. Pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantānanti rūpārūpamissakapaṭisandhivasena pañcavokārabhavaṃ upapajjantānaṃ. Tesaṃ rūpakkhandho ca uppajjati, vedanākkhandho cāti tesaṃ ekantena rūpavedanākkhandhasaṅkhātā dvepi khandhā uppajjantiyeva. Pavatte pana tattha uppannānaṃ te khandhā uppajjantipi [P 0.0068] nirujjhantipi, tasmā ‘pañcavokārāna’nti avatvā ‘pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantāna’nti vuttaṃ. Idaṃ pañcavokāraṃ upapajjantānanti ṭhāne paripuṇṇapañhassa pacchimakoṭṭhāse sarūpadassanena vissajjanaṃ. Iminā upāyena sabbāni vissajjanāni veditabbāni.

Herein, the method is as follows: 'For whom the material aggregate arises'—this refers to the person for whom the material aggregate arises, being endowed with the moment of its origination. 'For them the feeling aggregate arises'—this asks whether the feeling aggregate also arises for that same person at that very moment. 'For those being reborn into the non-percipient realm'—this refers to those who are being reborn into the non-percipient state of existence by way of rebirth-linking without consciousness. For them, the material aggregate certainly arises. For those who have arisen in the course of existence, the material aggregate both arises and ceases; therefore, instead of saying 'for non-percipient beings,' it is said 'for those being reborn into the non-percipient realm.' But for them, the feeling aggregate does not arise because they are without consciousness. This is the reply by specification, in the first part of the complete question in the first instance among the twenty-seven instances. 'For those being reborn into the five-aggregate realm'—this refers to those who are being reborn into the five-aggregate state of existence by way of rebirth-linking comprising both material and immaterial factors. For them, both aggregates, namely the material aggregate and the feeling aggregate, certainly arise. However, for those who have arisen there in the course of existence, these aggregates both arise and cease; therefore, instead of saying 'for five-aggregate beings,' it is said 'for those being reborn into the five-aggregate realm.' This is the reply by specification, in the latter part of the complete question in the instance 'for those being reborn into the five-aggregate realm.' By this method, all the replies should be understood.

Idaṃ panettha uppādanirodhesu niyamalakkhaṇaṃ – sakalepi hi imasmiṃ khandhayamake tattha tattha uppannānaṃ [V 0.0301] pavatte yāva maraṇā khandhānaṃ apariyantesu uppādanirodhesu [M 0.0302] vijjamānesupi lahuparivattānaṃ dhammānaṃ vinibbhogaṃ katvā uppādanirodhe dassetuṃ na sukaranti pavattiyaṃ uppādanirodhe anāmasitvā abhinavaṃ vipākavaṭṭaṃ nipphādayamānena nānākammena nibbattānaṃ paṭisandhikhandhānaṃ uppādaṃ dassetuṃ sukhanti paṭisandhikāle uppādavaseneva uppādavāro kathito. Uppannassa pana vipākavaṭṭassa pariyosānena nirodhaṃ dassetuṃ sukhanti maraṇakāle nirodhavasena nirodhavāro kathito.

Herein, this is the principle of determination regarding arising and ceasing: For, throughout this entire Khandhayamaka, even though for those who have arisen here and there in the course of existence until death there are endless arisings and ceasings of aggregates, it is not easy to distinguish and show the arising and ceasing of phenomena that are swift in their transformations. Therefore, without referring to the arising and ceasing in the course of existence, it is easy to show the arising of the rebirth-linking aggregates, which are produced by various kamma and bring forth a new round of results. Thus, the section on arising is taught by way of arising only at the time of rebirth-linking. And since it is easy to show the cessation at the conclusion of the arisen round of results, the section on cessation is taught by way of cessation only at the time of death.

Kiṃ panettha pavattiyaṃ uppādanirodhānaṃ anāmaṭṭhabhāve pamāṇanti? Pāḷiyeva. Pāḷiyañhi visesena uppādavārassa anāgatakālavāre ‘pacchimabhavikānaṃ tesaṃ rūpakkhandho ca nuppajjissati, vedanākkhandho ca nuppajjissatī’ti ayaṃ pāḷi atipamāṇameva. Pacchimabhavikānañhi pavatte rūpārūpadhammānaṃ uppajjituṃ yuttabhāve satipi ‘rūpakkhandho ca nuppajjissati, vedanākkhandho ca nuppajjissatī’ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvā vuttabhāvena pavatte uppādo na gahitoti veditabbo. ‘Suddhāvāse parinibbantānaṃ tesaṃ tattha saññākkhandho na nirujjhittha, no ca tesaṃ tattha vedanākkhandho na nirujjhatī’ti ayaṃ pana pāḷi pavatte nirodhassa anāmaṭṭhabhāve ativiya pamāṇaṃ. Suddhāvāse parinibbantānañhi cuticittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe ṭhitānaṃ paṭisandhito paṭṭhāya pavatte uppajjitvā niruddhasaññākkhandhānaṃ gaṇanapatho natthi. ‘Evaṃ santepi tesaṃ tattha saññākkhandho na nirujjhitthā’ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvā vuttabhāvena pavatte nirodho na gahitoti veditabbo.

What is the authority here for the non-inclusion of arising and cessation in the course of existence? The Pāḷi itself. For in the Pāḷi, specifically in the future tense section of the arising section, this statement is ample authority: ‘For those in their final existence, their material aggregate will not arise, and their feeling aggregate will not arise.’ For, even though it is suitable for material and immaterial phenomena to arise in the course of existence for those in their final existence, because it is stated after making the conclusion, ‘the material aggregate will not arise, and the feeling aggregate will not arise,’ it should be understood that arising in the course of existence is not included. This Pāḷi statement, ‘For those attaining final Nibbāna in the Pure Abodes, their perception aggregate did not cease there, but it is not that their feeling aggregate does not cease there,’ is, however, very great authority for the non-inclusion of cessation in the course of existence. For those attaining final Nibbāna in the Pure Abodes, who are at the dissolution moment of the death-consciousness, there is no way to count the perception aggregates that arose and ceased in the course of existence from rebirth-linking onwards. Because it is stated after making the conclusion, ‘Even so, their perception aggregate did not cease there,’ it should be understood that cessation in the course of existence is not included.

Evamettha uppādanirodhesu niyamalakkhaṇaṃ viditvā paṭisandhiuppādameva cutinirodhameva ca gahetvā tesu [P 0.0069] tesu ṭhānesu āgatānaṃ vissajjanānaṃ atthavinicchayo veditabbo. So pana sakkā ādivissajjane vuttanayena sabbattha viditunti vissajjanapaṭipāṭiyā na vitthārito. Iminā pana evaṃ dinnenapi nayena yo etesaṃ atthavinicchayaṃ jānituṃ na sakkoti, tena ācariye payirupāsitvā sādhukaṃ sutvāpi jānitabbo.

Having thus understood the characteristic of definiteness in arising and cessation in this matter, one should understand the determination of meaning for the answers that appear in their respective places by taking only rebirth-arising and only death-cessation. But this can be understood everywhere by the method stated in the initial answer, so it is not elaborated in detail in the sequence of answers. Yet, even with this method thus given, if someone is unable to understand the determination of meaning of these, they should approach a teacher, listen carefully, and then understand it.

Uppādassa nirodhassa, uppannañcāpi ekato;

Nayassa anulomassa, paṭilomanayassa ca.

Of the arising and the ceasing, and also of what has arisen together; of the method in direct order, and of the method in reverse order.

Vasena [V 0.0302] yāni khandhesu, yamakāni ca pañcasu;

Puggalaṃ atha okāsaṃ, puggalokāsameva ca.

The pairs concerning the five aggregates, by means of which; the individual, then the location, and the individual-location as well.

Āmasitvā [M 0.0303] pavattesu, ṭhānesu kathayī jino;

Tesaṃ pāḷivavatthānaṃ, dassitaṃ anupubbato.

Having contemplated, the Conqueror spoke in the sections on continuity; the determination of those Pāḷi texts was shown in due order.

Vinicchayatthaṃ atthassa, pañhāvissajjanāni ca;

Vissajjanānaṃ ṭhānāni, yāni tāni ca sabbaso.

For the purpose of determining the meaning, the questions and answers; the bases for answers, and all those entirely.

Dassetvā ekapañhasmiṃ, yojanāpi pakāsitā;

Vitthārena gate ettha, pañhāvissajjanakkame.

Having shown in a single question, the applications were also made clear; in this, which proceeds in detail in the sequence of questions and answers.

Atthaṃ vaṇṇayatā kātuṃ, kiṃ nu sakkā ito paraṃ;

Nayena iminā tasmā, atthaṃ jānantu paṇḍitāti.

In explaining the meaning, what more can be done than this? Therefore, let the wise understand the meaning by this method.

Pavattimahāvāravaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Great Section on Continuity.

3. Pariññāvāravaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Section on Full Understanding.

206-208. Tadanantare pariññāvārepi chaḷeva kālabhedā. Anulomapaṭilomato dveyeva nayā. Puggalavāro, okāsavāro, puggalokāsavāroti imesu pana tīsu puggalavārova labbhati, na itare dve. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Sadisavissajjanatāya. Yo hi koci puggalo yattha katthaci ṭhāne rūpakkhandhaṃ ce parijānāti, vedanākkhandhampi parijānātiyeva. Vedanākkhandhaṃ ce parijānāti, rūpakkhandhampi parijānātiyeva. Rūpakkhandhaṃ ce na parijānāti, vedanākkhandhampi na parijānātiyeva. Vedanākkhandhaṃ ce na parijānāti, rūpakkhandhampi na parijānātiyeva. Tasmā tesupi ‘yattha rūpakkhandhaṃ parijānāti, tattha vedanākkhandhaṃ parijānātī’ti ādivasena pucchaṃ [V 0.0303] katvā ‘āmantā’tveva vissajjanaṃ kātabbaṃ[P 0.0070]. Siyāti sadisavissajjanatāya te idha na labbhantīti veditabbā.

206-208. Immediately following, in the section on full understanding as well, there are only six divisions by time. There are only two methods: direct and reverse. But among these three—the individual section, the location section, and the individual-location section—only the individual section is found, not the other two. What is the reason? Because of the similarity of the answers. For whatever individual in whatever place fully understands the form aggregate, they indeed also fully understand the feeling aggregate. If they fully understand the feeling aggregate, they indeed also fully understand the form aggregate. If they do not fully understand the form aggregate, they indeed also do not fully understand the feeling aggregate. If they do not fully understand the feeling aggregate, they indeed also do not fully understand the form aggregate. Therefore, in those cases also, after asking a question beginning with, ‘Where one fully understands the form aggregate, there one also fully understands the feeling aggregate,’ the answer must be given simply as, ‘Yes.’ It should be understood that those two are not found here due to the similarity of the answers.

Atha vā pariññākiccaṃ nāma puggalasseva hoti, no okāsassa, puggalova parijānituṃ samattho, no okāsoti puggalavārovettha gahito, na okāsavāro. Tassa pana aggahitattā tadanantaro puggalokāsavāro labbhamānopi na gahito. Yo panesa puggalavāro gahito, tattha paccuppannakāle rūpakkhandhamūlakāni cattāri, vedanākkhandhamūlakāni tīṇi, saññākkhandhamūlakāni dve, saṅkhārakkhandhamūlakaṃ ekanti [M 0.0304] heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva anulomanaye aggahitaggahaṇena dasa yamakāni. Paṭilomanaye dasāti vīsati. Tathā sesesupīti ekekasmiṃ kāle vīsati vīsati katvā chasu kālesu vīsaṃ yamakasataṃ, cattārīsāni dve pucchāsatāni, asītyādhikāni cattāri atthasatāni ca hontīti idamettha pāḷivavatthānaṃ.

Alternatively, the task of full understanding belongs only to the individual, not to the location. Only the individual is capable of fully understanding, not the location; hence, only the section on individuals is taken here, not the section on locations. And because the latter is not taken, the immediately following individual-location section, though obtainable, is also not taken. As for this section on individuals that is taken, in the present time, there are four rooted in the form aggregate, three rooted in the feeling aggregate, two rooted in the perception aggregate, and one rooted in the formations aggregate—making ten pairs in the direct method by including what was not previously included, as explained below. In the reverse method, there are ten—thus twenty. Similarly, in the remaining cases, with twenty pairs in each of the six time periods, there are one hundred and twenty pairs, two hundred and forty questions, and four hundred and eighty meanings. This is the textual determination here.

Atthavinicchaye panettha atītānāgatapaccuppannasaṅkhātā tayo addhā pavattivāre viya cutipaṭisandhivasena na labbhanti. Pavatte cittakkhaṇavaseneva labbhanti. Tenevettha ‘yo rūpakkhandhaṃ parijānāti, so vedanākkhandhaṃ parijānātī’tiādīsu pucchāsu ‘āmantā’ti vissajjanaṃ kataṃ. Lokuttaramaggakkhaṇasmiñhi nibbānārammaṇena cittena pañcasu khandhesu pariññākiccanibbattiyā yaṃ kiñci ekaṃ khandhaṃ parijānanto itarampi parijānātīti vuccati. Evamettha ‘parijānātī’ti pañhesu anulomanaye pariññākiccassa matthakappattaṃ aggamaggasamaṅgiṃ sandhāya ‘āmantā’ti vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Paṭilomanaye pana ‘na parijānātī’ti pañhesu puthujjanādayo sandhāya ‘āmantā’ti vuttaṃ. ‘Parijānitthā’ti imasmiṃ pana atītakālavāre maggānantaraaggaphale ṭhitopi pariññākiccassa niṭṭhitattā parijānitthayeva nāma.

Here in the determination of meaning, the three periods designated as past, future, and present are not found by way of death and rebirth as in the section on continuity. They are found only by way of mind-moments in the course of existence. Therefore, here, in questions such as, ‘Does one who fully understands the form aggregate also fully understand the feeling aggregate?’, the answer given is, ‘Yes.’ For at the moment of the supramundane path, with consciousness taking Nibbāna as its object, by the accomplishment of the task of full understanding regarding the five aggregates, one who fully understands any one aggregate is said to fully understand the others as well. Thus, here in the direct method, in the questions, ‘Does one fully understand?’, it should be understood that the answer ‘Yes’ is stated in reference to one endowed with the supreme path who has reached the culmination of the task of full understanding. In the reverse method, however, in the questions, ‘Does one not fully understand?’, the answer ‘Yes’ is stated in reference to ordinary persons and others. In this past-tense section, regarding the question ‘Had one fully understood?’, even one established in the supreme fruition immediately after the path, because the task of full understanding is completed, is indeed said to have fully understood.

209. Yo rūpakkhandhaṃ parijānāti, so vedanākkhandhaṃ parijānitthāti pañhena aggamaggasamaṅgiṃ pucchati. Yasmā panesa khandhapañcakaṃ parijānātiyeva nāma, na tāva niṭṭhitapariññākicco; tasmā ‘no’ti paṭisedho kato. Dutiyapañhe pana parijānitthāti arahantaṃ pucchati. Yasmā paneso niṭṭhitapariññākicco. Natthi tassa pariññeyyaṃ nāma; tasmā [P 0.0071] ‘no’ti paṭisedho kato. Paṭilomanayavissajjane panettha arahā rūpakkhandhaṃ na parijānātīti arahato pariññāya abhāvena vuttaṃ. Aggamaggasamaṅgī vedanākkhandhaṃ na parijānitthāti [V 0.0304] arahattamaggaṭṭhassa aniṭṭhitapariññākiccatāya vuttaṃ. Na kevalañca vedanākkhandhameva, ekadhammampi so na parijānittheva. Idaṃ pana pucchāvasena vuttaṃ. No ca rūpakkhandhanti idampi pucchāvaseneva vuttaṃ. Aññampi pana so khandhaṃ parijānāti.

209. With the question, ‘One who fully understands the form aggregate, has he fully understood the feeling aggregate?’, it asks about one endowed with the supreme path. Since this one indeed fully understands the five aggregates, but has not yet completed the task of full understanding, the denial ‘no’ is made. In the second question, however, ‘has he fully understood?’ asks about an arahant. Since this one has completed the task of full understanding, there is nothing left for him to fully understand; therefore, the denial ‘no’ is made. Here in the answer in the reverse method, the statement that ‘the arahant does not fully understand the form aggregate’ is said because of the absence of any further full understanding for an arahant. The statement that ‘the one endowed with the supreme path has not fully understood the feeling aggregate’ is said because the one at the path of arahantship has not yet completed the task of full understanding. And not only the feeling aggregate, but he has not fully understood even a single phenomenon. This, however, is said in the context of the question. ‘And not the form aggregate’—this too is said in the context of the question. But he does fully understand another aggregate.

210-211. Yo rūpakkhandhaṃ parijānāti, so vedanākkhandhaṃ parijānissatīti ettha yasmā maggaṭṭhapuggalo ekacittakkhaṇiko, tasmā so parijānissatīti saṅkhaṃ na gacchati. Tena vuttaṃ ‘no’ti. Te rūpakkhandhañca na [M 0.0305] parijānitthāti pucchāsabhāgena vuttaṃ, na parijāniṃsūti panettha attho. Iminā upāyena sabbattha atthavinicchayo veditabboti.

210-211. Regarding the question, “Will one who fully understands the form aggregate fully understand the feeling aggregate?”—here, because the person standing on the path exists for a single mind-moment, the designation ‘he will fully understand’ does not apply. Hence, it is said, ‘No.’ The statement, “They did not fully understand the form aggregate,” is expressed in the manner of a question, but the meaning here is, “they did not fully understand.” In this way, the determination of the meaning should be understood in all instances.

Pariññāvāravaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Section on Full Understanding.

Khandhayamakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Yamaka of Aggregates is concluded.

3. Āyatanayamakaṃ

3. The Yamaka of Sense Bases

1. Paṇṇattiuddesavāravaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Recitation Section on Designations.

1-9. Idāni mūlayamake desiteyeva kusalādidhamme āyatanavasenāpi saṅgaṇhitvā khandhayamakānantaraṃ desitassa āyatanayamakassa vaṇṇanā hoti. Tattha khandhayamake vuttanayeneva pāḷivavatthānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Yatheva hi tattha paṇṇattivāro, pavattivāro, pariññāvāroti tayo mahāvārā honti, tathā idhāpi. Vacanatthopi nesaṃ tattha vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Idhāpi ca paṇṇattivāro uddesaniddesavasena dvidhā vavatthito. Itare niddesavaseneva. ‘Tattha dvādasāyatanānī’ti padaṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva nāyatanā na manoti, tāva paṇṇattivārassa uddesavāro veditabbo. Tattha dvādasāyatanānīti ayaṃ yamakavasena pucchitabbānaṃ [P 0.0072] āyatanānaṃ uddeso. Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… dhammāyatananti tesaññeva pabhedato nāmavavatthānaṃ. Yamakavasena pucchāsukhatthañcettha paṭhamaṃ paṭipāṭiyā ajjhattarūpāyatanāni vuttāni. Pacchā bāhirarūpāyatanāni. Pariyosāne manāyatanadhammāyatanāni.

1-9. Now, the exposition of the Sense-Base Yamaka, which was taught after the Aggregate Yamaka, is undertaken, having also organized by way of the sense bases the wholesome and other phenomena already taught in the Root Yamaka. Herein, the arrangement of the Pāḷi should be understood in the same way as stated in the Aggregate Yamaka. Just as there are three great sections there—the section on designations, the section on occurrence, and the section on full understanding—so too here. The meaning of their terms should also be understood in the same way as explained there. Here too, the section on designations is established in two parts: the recitation and the exposition. The others are only by way of exposition. Beginning with the phrase, “Therein, the twelve sense bases,” and continuing up to, “is not a sense base, is not the mind,” this should be understood as the recitation section of the chapter on designations. Herein, “the twelve sense bases” is the enumeration of the sense bases to be questioned by way of the Yamaka. “The eye-base... up to... the mind-object base” is the establishment of their names according to their classification. For the sake of ease in questioning by way of the Yamaka, the internal form-bases are stated first in sequence, followed by the external form-bases. At the end are the mind-base and the mind-object base.

Yathā [V 0.0305] pana heṭṭhā khandhavasena, evamidha imesaṃ āyatanānaṃ vasena padasodhanavāro, padasodhanamūlacakkavāro, suddhāyatanavāro, suddhāyatanamūlacakkavāroti, cattārova nayavārā honti. Ekeko cettha anulomapaṭilomavasena duvidhoyeva. Tesamattho tattha vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Yathā pana khandhayamake padasodhanavārassa anulomavāre ‘rūpaṃ rūpakkhandho, rūpakkhandho rūpa’ntiādīni pañca yamakāni, tathā idha ‘cakkhu, cakkhāyatanaṃ; cakkhāyatanaṃ; cakkhū’tiādīni dvādasa. Paṭilomavārepi ‘na cakkhu, na cakkhāyatanaṃ; na cakkhāyatanaṃ, na cakkhū’tiādīni dvādasa[M 0.0306], padasodhanamūlacakkavārassa panettha anulomavāre ekekāyatanamūlakāni ekādasa ekādasa katvā dvattiṃsasataṃ yamakāni. Paṭilomavārepi dvattiṃsasatameva. Suddhāyatanavārassāpi anulomavāre dvādasa, paṭilomavāre dvādasa, suddhāyatanamūlacakkavārassāpi anulomavāre ekekāyatanamūlakāni ekādasa ekādasa katvā dvattiṃsasataṃ yamakāni. Paṭilomavārepi dvattiṃsasatamevāti evamidha chasattatādhikehi pañcahi yamakasatehi, dvipaññāsādhikehi ekādasahi pucchāsatehi, caturādhikehi tevīsāya atthasatehi ca paṭimaṇḍito paṇṇattivārassa uddesavāro veditabbo.

Just as below in the section on aggregates, here too there are four sections of method with regard to these sense-bases: the term-analysis section, the root-wheel section of term-analysis, the pure sense-base section, and the root-wheel section of pure sense-bases. Each of these is twofold, in forward and reverse order. Their meaning should be understood according to the method explained there. Just as in the Aggregate Yamaka, in the forward order of the term-analysis section, there are five dyads such as 'form is the form aggregate, the form aggregate is form,' so here there are twelve dyads like 'the eye, the eye-base; the eye-base, the eye.' In the reverse order, there are also twelve dyads like 'not the eye, not the eye-base; not the eye-base, not the eye.' Here, in the forward order of the root-wheel section of term-analysis, there are eleven dyads for each sense-base as a root, amounting to three thousand two hundred dyads. In the reverse order also, three thousand two hundred. In the pure sense-base section, there are twelve dyads in the forward order and twelve in the reverse. In the root-wheel section of pure sense-bases, there are eleven dyads for each sense-base as a root, amounting to three thousand two hundred dyads. In the reverse order also, three thousand two hundred. Thus, the recitation section of the designation chapter should be understood as adorned with 576 dyads, 1,152 questions, and 2,304 explanations.

Paṇṇattiuddesavāravaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Recitation Section on Designations.

1. Paṇṇattiniddesavāravaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Exposition Section on Designations.

10-17. Niddesavāre pana heṭṭhā khandhayamakassa paṇṇattivāraniddese vuttanayeneva attho veditabbo. Aññatra visesā. Tatrāyaṃ viseso – dibbacakkhūti dutiyavijjāñāṇaṃ. Paññācakkhūti tatiyavijjāñāṇaṃ. Dibbasotanti dutiyaabhiññāñāṇaṃ. Taṇhāsotanti taṇhāva. Avaseso kāyoti nāmakāyo, rūpakāyo, hatthikāyo, assakāyoti evamādi. Avasesaṃ rūpanti rūpāyatanato sesaṃ bhūtupādāyarūpañceva [P 0.0073] piyarūpasātarūpañca. Sīlagandhotiādīni vāyanaṭṭhena sīlādīnaṃyeva nāmāni. Attharasotiādīnipi sādhumadhuraṭṭhena atthādīnaññeva nāmāni. Avaseso dhammoti pariyattidhammādianekappabhedoti ayamettha viseso.

10-17. In the exposition section, however, the meaning should be understood in the same way as explained in the exposition of the designation section of the Aggregate Yamaka below, except for the special points. Herein, the special points are as follows: “Divine eye” refers to the knowledge of the second science. “Wisdom eye” refers to the knowledge of the third science. “Divine ear” refers to the knowledge of the second supernormal knowledge. “Stream of craving” means craving itself. “The remaining body” refers to the mental body, physical body, elephant body, horse body, and so on. “The remaining form” means form apart from the form sense-base, including primary and derived matter, as well as pleasing and delightful form. “Fragrance of virtue” and similar terms are merely names for virtue and so on, in the sense of wafting. “Essence of meaning” and similar terms are merely names for meaning and so on, in the sense of being excellent and sweet. “The remaining Dhamma” refers to the various classifications, such as the Dhamma of the scriptures and so on. This is the special point here.

Paṇṇattiniddesavāravaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Exposition Section on Designations.

2. Pavattivāravaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Occurrence Section.

18-21. Idhāpi [V 0.0306] ca pavattivārassa uppādavārādīsu tīsu antaravāresu ekekasmiṃ chaḷeva kālabhedā. Tesaṃ ekekasmiṃ kāle puggalavārādayo tayo vārā. Te sabbepi anulomapaṭilomanayavasena duvidhāva [M 0.0307] honti. Tattha paccuppannakāle puggalavārassa anulomanaye yathā khandhayamake rūpakkhandhamūlakāni cattāri, vedanākkhandhamūlakāni tīṇi, saññākkhandhamūlakāni dve, saṅkhārakkhandhamūlakaṃ ekanti aggahitaggahaṇena dasa yamakāni honti. Evaṃ “yassa cakkhāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa sotāyatanaṃ uppajjati; yassa vā pana sotāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa cakkhāyatanaṃ uppajjati; yassa cakkhāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa ghāṇāyatanaṃ, jivhāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, saddāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ, uppajjati; yassa vā pana dhammāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa cakkhāyatanaṃ uppajjatī”ti evaṃ cakkhāyatanamūlakāni ekādasa. “Yassa sotāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa ghānāyatanaṃ uppajjatī”tiādinā nayena sotāyatanamūlakāni dasa; ghānāyatanamūlakāni nava, jivhāyatanamūlakāni aṭṭha; kāyāyatanamūlakāni satta; rūpāyatanamūlakāni cha; saddāyatanamūlakāni pañca; gandhāyatanamūlakāni cattāri; rasāyatanamūlakāni tīṇi; phoṭṭhabbāyatanamūlakāni dve; manāyatanamūlakaṃ ekanti aggahitaggahaṇena chasaṭṭhi yamakāni honti.

18-21. Here also, in the occurrence section, within its three intermediate sections beginning with the arising section, there are six divisions of time in each. In each of these times, there are three sections: the individual section and so on. All of these are twofold according to the forward and reverse methods. In the present time, regarding the forward method of the individual section, as in the Aggregate Dyad, there are four rooted in the aggregate of form, three rooted in the aggregate of feeling, two rooted in the aggregate of perception, and one rooted in the aggregate of formations—thus, by taking what has not yet been taken, there are ten dyads. Similarly: 'For whom the eye-base arises, for them the ear-base arises; or alternatively, for whom the ear-base arises, for them the eye-base arises. For whom the eye-base arises, for them the nose-base, tongue-base, body-base, form-base, sound-base, smell-base, taste-base, tactile-base, mind-base, and mental-object base arise; or alternatively, for whom the mental-object base arises, for them the eye-base arises.' Thus, there are eleven dyads rooted in the eye-base. Following the same method: 'For whom the ear-base arises, for them the nose-base arises,' and so on—there are ten dyads rooted in the ear-base; nine rooted in the nose-base; eight rooted in the tongue-base; seven rooted in the body-base; six rooted in the form-base; five rooted in the sound-base; four rooted in the smell-base; three rooted in the taste-base; two rooted in the tactile-base; and one rooted in the mind-base—thus, by taking what has not yet been taken, there are sixty-six dyads.

Tattha cakkhāyatanamūlakesu ekādasasu “yassa cakkhāyatanaṃ uppajjati, tassa sotāyatanaṃ, ghānāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ, manāyatanaṃ, dhammāyatanaṃ uppajjatī”ti imāni pañceva vissajjitāni. Tesu paṭhamaṃ vissajjetabbaṃ tāva vissajjitaṃ. Dutiyaṃ kiñcāpi [P 0.0074] paṭhamena sadisavissajjanaṃ, cakkhusotāyatanānaṃ pavattiṭṭhāne pana ghānāyatanassa na ekantena pavattito “kathaṃ nu kho etaṃ vissajjetabba”nti vimatinivāraṇatthaṃ vissajjitaṃ. Rūpāyatanamanāyatanadhammāyatanehi saddhiṃ tīṇi yamakāni asadisavissajjanattā vissajjitāni. Sesesu jivhāyatanakāyāyatanehi tāva saddhiṃ dve yamakāni purimehi dvīhi saddhiṃ sadisavissajjanāni. Saddāyatanassa paṭisandhikkhaṇe anuppattito tena saddhiṃ yamakassa vissajjanameva natthi. Gandharasaphoṭṭhabbāyatanehipi saddhiṃ tīṇi yamakāni purimehi dvīhi sadisavissajjanāneva hontīti tantiyā lahubhāvatthaṃ saṅkhittāni. Sotāyatanamūlakesu yaṃ labbhati[V 0.0307], taṃ purimehi sadisavissajjanamevāti ekampi pāḷiṃ nāruḷhaṃ. Ghānāyatanamūlakesu rūpāyatanena saddhiṃ ekaṃ, manāyatanadhammāyatanehi saddhiṃ dveti tīṇi yamakāni pāḷiṃ āruḷhāni. Sesāni ghānāyatanayamakena sadisavissajjanattā nāruḷhāni. Tathā jivhāyatanakāyāyatanamūlakāni. Rūpāyatanamūlakesu [M 0.0308] manāyatanadhammāyatanehi saddhiṃ dveyeva vissajjitāni. Gandharasaphoṭṭhabbehi pana saddhiṃ tīṇi rūpāyatanamanāyatanehi saddhiṃ sadisavissajjanāni. Yatheva hettha “sarūpakānaṃ acittakāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ, tathā idhāpi “sarūpakānaṃ agandhakānaṃ, arasakānaṃ aphoṭṭhabbakāna”nti yojanā veditabbā. Gandhādīni cettha āyatanabhūtāneva adhippetāni. Tasmā “sarūpakānaṃ sagandhāyatanāna”nti āyatanavasenettha attho daṭṭhabbo.

Here, among the eleven dyads rooted in the eye-base, the five statements—'For whom the eye-base arises, for them the ear-base, nose-base, form-base, mind-base, and mental-object base arise'—have been answered. Among these, the first has already been answered. The second, though it has a similar answer to the first, has been answered to resolve the doubt, 'How should this be answered?', since the nose-base does not necessarily arise in the place of occurrence of the eye- and ear-bases. The three dyads with the form-base, mind-base, and mental-object base have been answered due to their dissimilar answers. The remaining two dyads with the tongue-base and body-base have similar answers to the first two. Since the sound-base does not arise at the moment of rebirth-linking, there is no answer at all for the dyad concerning it. The three dyads with the smell, taste, and tangible bases also have similar answers to the first two; for the sake of the text's brevity, they have been abbreviated. Among the dyads rooted in the ear-base, whatever is applicable has a similar answer to the previous ones, and thus not even one Pāḷi passage has been included. Among the dyads rooted in the nose-base, three have been included in the Pāḷi: one with the form-base, and two with the mind-base and mental-object base. The rest have not been included, as they have a similar answer to the nose-base dyad. The same applies to the dyads rooted in the tongue-base and body-base. Among the dyads rooted in the form-base, only two have been answered—those with the mind-base and mental-object base. However, the three dyads with the smell, taste, and tangible bases have similar answers to those with the form-base and mind-base. Just as it was stated here, 'of those with form but without consciousness,' and so on, so too here the application should be understood as: 'of those with form but without odour, without taste, without tactile sensation.' And here, odour and so on are intended as being the bases themselves. Therefore, the meaning here should be understood in terms of the bases, as 'of those with form and with the odour-base,' and so on.

Saddāyatanamūlakāni atthābhāvato pāḷiṃ nāruḷhāneva. Gandharasaphoṭṭhabbamūlakāni cattāri tīṇi dve ca heṭṭhimehi sadisavissajjanattā pāḷiṃ nāruḷhāni. Manāyatanamūlakaṃ vissajjitamevāti evametāni paccuppannakāle puggalavārassa anulomanaye katipayayamakavissajjaneneva chasaṭṭhiyamakāni vissajjitāni nāma hontīti veditabbāni. Yathā ca puggalavāre, evaṃ okāsavārepi puggalokāsavārepi chasaṭṭhīti paccuppannakāle tīsu vāresu anulomanaye aṭṭhanavutisataṃ [P 0.0075] yamakāni honti. Yathā ca anulomanaye, evaṃ paṭilomanayepīti sabbānipi paccuppannakāle channavutādhikāni tīṇi yamakasatāni honti. Tesu dvānavutādhikāni satta pucchāsatāni, caturāsītādhikāni ca pannarasa atthasatāni hontīti veditabbāni. Evaṃ sesesupi pañcasu kālabhedesūti sabbānipi chasattatādhikāni tevīsati yamakasatāni. Tato diguṇā pucchā, tato diguṇā atthāti idamettha uppādavāre pāḷivavatthānaṃ. Nirodhavārauppādanirodhavāresupi eseva nayoti. Sabbasmimpi pavattivāre aṭṭhavīsāni ekasattati yamakasatāni. Tato diguṇā pucchā, tato diguṇā atthā veditabbā. Pāḷi pana manāyatanaṃ dhammāyatanañca ekasadisaṃ, nānaṃ natthi. Upari pana “vārasaṅkhepo hotī”tiādīni vatvā tattha tattha saṅkhittā. Tasmā yaṃ tattha tattha saṅkhittaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ asammuyhantehi sallakkhetabbaṃ.

The yamakas rooted in the sound base are not included in the Pāli text due to the absence of meaning. The four, three, and two yamakas rooted in the smell, taste, and touch bases are not included in the Pāli text because their answers are similar to the preceding ones. The yamaka rooted in the mind base has already been answered. Thus it should be understood that in the present time, in the forward order of the person-section, by the answering of only a few yamakas, these sixty-six yamakas are considered answered. Just as in the person-section, so too in the location-section and the person-location section, there are sixty-six; thus in the present time, across the three sections in the forward order, there are one hundred and ninety-eight yamakas. And just as in the forward order, so too in the reverse order; thus all together in the present time, there are three hundred and ninety-six yamakas. Among these, it should be understood that there are seven hundred and ninety-two questions, and one thousand five hundred and eighty-four meanings. Similarly, in the remaining five divisions of time, all together there are two thousand three hundred and seventy-six yamakas. From this, the questions are doubled, and from that the meanings are doubled; this is the arrangement of the Pāli text in the arising-section. The same method applies in the cessation-section and the arising-cessation section. In the entire process-section, there are seven thousand one hundred and twenty-eight yamakas. From this, the questions are doubled, and from that the meanings are to be understood as doubled. However, in the Pāli text, the mind base and the mental-object base are treated as identical; there is no distinction. Above, after stating, “a summary of the section occurs,” and so forth, it is abbreviated in various places. Therefore, whatever is abbreviated in various places should be carefully noted by those who are not confused.

Atthavinicchaye panettha idaṃ nayamukhaṃ. Sacakkhukānaṃ asotakānanti apāye jātibadhiraopapātikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. So hi sacakkhuko asotako hutvā upapajjati. Yathāha [V 0.0308] – “kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe kassaci aparāni dasāyatanāni pātubhavanti. Opapātikānaṃ petānaṃ[M 0.0309], opapātikānaṃ asurānaṃ, opapātikānaṃ tiracchānagatānaṃ, opapātikānaṃ nerayikānaṃ; jaccabadhirānaṃ upapattikkhaṇe dasāyatanāni pātubhavanti, cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpaghānagandhajivhārasakāyaphoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manāyatanaṃ dhammāyatana”nti. Sacakkhukānaṃ sasotakānanti sugatiduggatīsu paripuṇṇāyatane ca opapātike rūpībrahmāno ca sandhāya vuttaṃ. Te hi sacakkhukā sasotakā hutvā upapajjanti. Yathāha – “kāmadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe kassaci ekādasāyatanāni pātubhavanti; kāmāvacarānaṃ devānaṃ, paṭhamakappikānaṃ manussānaṃ, opapātikānaṃ petānaṃ, opapātikānaṃ asurānaṃ, opapātikānaṃ tiracchānagatānaṃ, opapātikānaṃ nerayikānaṃ, paripuṇṇāyatanānaṃ. Rūpadhātuyā upapattikkhaṇe pañcāyatanāni pātubhavanti, cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpasotamanāyatanaṃ dhammāyatana”nti.

Herein, this is the guiding principle for the determination of meaning. The phrase 'of those with eyes but without ears' is stated in reference to a spontaneously arisen, congenitally deaf being in the plane of misery. For such a one is reborn with eyes but without ears. As it is said: “At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere, for some, ten sense bases appear: for spontaneously arisen hungry ghosts, spontaneously arisen titans, spontaneously arisen animals, and spontaneously arisen hell-beings; for the congenitally deaf, at the moment of rebirth, ten sense bases appear: the eye base, form base, nose base, smell base, tongue base, taste base, body base, tangible-object base, mind base, and mental-object base.” The phrase 'of those with eyes and with ears' is stated in reference to spontaneously arisen beings with complete sense bases in good and bad destinations, and also to the form-realm Brahmās. For they are reborn with eyes and with ears. As it is said: “At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere, for some, eleven sense bases appear: for sense-sphere devas, humans of the first aeon, spontaneously arisen hungry ghosts, spontaneously arisen titans, spontaneously arisen animals, spontaneously arisen hell-beings, and those with complete sense bases. At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, five sense bases appear: the eye base, the form base, the ear base, the mind base, and the mental-object base.”

Aghānakānanti brahmapārisajjādayo sandhāya vuttaṃ. Te hi sacakkhukā aghānakā hutvā upapajjanti. Kāmadhātuyaṃ [P 0.0076] pana aghānako opapātiko natthi. Yadi bhaveyya “kassaci aṭṭhāyatanāni pātubhavantī”ti vedayya. Yo gabbhaseyyako pana aghānako siyā, so “sacakkhukāna”nti vacanato idha anadhippeto. Sacakkhukānaṃ saghānakānanti jaccabadhirampi paripuṇṇāyatanampi opapātikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Saghānakānaṃ acakkhukānanti jaccandhampi jaccabadhirampi opapātikaṃ sandhāya vuttameva. Saghānakānaṃ sacakkhukānanti paripuṇṇāyatanameva opapātikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

The phrase 'of those without a nose' is stated in reference to the attendants of Brahmā and others. For they are reborn with eyes but without a nose. In the sense-sphere, however, there is no spontaneously arisen being who is noseless. If there were, it would be stated, ‘For some, eight sense bases appear.’ A womb-born being who might be noseless, however, is not intended here by the statement ‘of those with eyes.’ The phrase 'of those with eyes and a nose' is stated in reference to a spontaneously arisen being who is congenitally deaf, as well as one with complete sense bases. The phrase 'of those with a nose but without eyes' is stated in reference to a spontaneously arisen being who is either congenitally blind or congenitally deaf. The phrase 'of those with a nose and with eyes' is stated in reference only to a spontaneously arisen being with complete sense bases.

Sarūpakānaṃ acakkhukānanti ettha jaccandhajaccabadhiraopapātikesu aññataropi gabbhaseyyakopi labbhatiyeva. Sacittakānaṃ acakkhukānanti ettha heṭṭhā vuttehi jaccandhādīhi tīhi saddhiṃ arūpinopi labbhanti. Acakkhukānanti ettha purimapade vuttehi catūhi saddhiṃ asaññasattāpi labbhanti. Sarūpakānaṃ aghānakānanti ettha gabbhaseyyakā ca asaññasattā ca sesarūpībrahmāno ca labbhanti. Sacittakānaṃ aghānakānanti ettha gabbhaseyyakā ca rūpārūpabrahmāno ca labbhanti. Acittakānaṃ arūpakānantipadesu pana ekavokāracatuvokārasattāva labbhantīti iminā nayena sabbesu puggalavāresu puggalavibhāgo veditabbo.

In the case of 'of those with form but without eyes,' here one finds any one of the spontaneously arisen who are congenitally blind or congenitally deaf, and also a womb-born being. In the case of 'of those with consciousness but without eyes,' here, in addition to the three types mentioned above, formless beings are also found. In the case of 'of those without eyes,' here, along with the four types mentioned in the previous phrase, non-percipient beings are also found. In the case of 'of those with form but without a nose,' here, womb-born beings, non-percipient beings, and the remaining form-realm Brahmās are found. In the case of 'of those with consciousness but without a nose,' here, womb-born beings and the form-realm and formless-realm Brahmās are found. But in the phrases 'of those without consciousness' and 'of the formless,' only beings with one constituent or four constituents are found. In this way, the classification of individuals should be understood in all person-sections.

22-254. Okāsavāre yattha cakkhāyatananti rūpībrahmalokaṃ pucchati. Teneva āmantāti vuttaṃ[V 0.0309]. Tasmiñhi tale niyamato tāni āyatanāni [M 0.0310] paṭisandhiyaṃ uppajjanti. Idamettha nayamukhaṃ. Iminā nayamukhena sakalepi pavattivāre attho veditabbo. Pariññāvāro khandhayamake vuttanayoyevāti.

22-254. In the location-section, when the question is asked, “Where does the eye base arise?”, it refers to the form-realm Brahma-world. Therefore, the answer is given in the affirmative. For in that plane, those bases invariably arise at rebirth-linking. This is the guiding principle here. By this guiding principle, the meaning in the entire process-section should be understood. The section on full understanding follows the same method as explained in the Aggregate-Yamaka.

Pavattivāravaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Process-Section.

Āyatanayamakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Āyatanayamaka is concluded.

4. Dhātuyamakaṃ

4. The Yamaka on Elements.

1-19. Idāni teyeva mūlayamake desite kusalādidhamme dhātuvasena saṅgaṇhitvā āyatanayamakānantaraṃ desitassa dhātuyamakassa vaṇṇanā hoti. Tattha āyatanayamake vuttanayeneva pāḷivavatthānaṃ vetidabbaṃ. Idhāpi [P 0.0077] hi paṇṇattivārādayo tayo mahāvārā, avasesā antaravārā ca saddhiṃ kālappabhedādīhi āyatanayamake āgatasadisāyeva. Idhāpi ca yamakapucchāsukhatthaṃ paṭipāṭiyā ajjhattikabāhirā rūpadhātuyova vatvā viññāṇadhātuyo vuttā. Dhātūnaṃ pana bahuttā idha āyatanayamakato bahutarāni yamakāni, yamakadiguṇā pucchā, pucchādiguṇā ca atthā honti. Tattha cakkhudhātumūlakādīsu yamakesu labbhamānānaṃ yamakānaṃ atthavinicchayo āyatanayamake vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Taṃsadisāyeva hettha atthagati, teneva ca kāraṇena pāḷipi saṅkhittā. Pariññāvāro pākatikoyevāti.

Now, having grouped by way of elements those same wholesome and other phenomena that were pointed out in the Root Dyad, the explanation of the Dyad of Elements, which follows the Dyad of Bases, is to be given. Here, the arrangement of the Pāli text should be understood in the same way as stated in the Dyad of Bases. For here as well, the three great sections—the section on designations and others—along with the remaining intermediate sections, together with the divisions of time and so forth, are similar to those found in the Dyad of Bases. Moreover, for the sake of ease in answering the dyadic questions, the internal and external elements of form are mentioned in order first, followed by the elements of consciousness. However, due to the greater number of elements here, there are more dyads than in the Dyad of Bases, questions are double the dyads, and meanings are double the questions. In the dyads rooted in the eye-element and so forth, the determination of meaning for the dyads that arise should be understood in the same way as explained in the Dyad of Bases. The treatment of meaning here is similar, and for this reason, the Pāli text is concise. The section on full understanding is just as before.

Dhātuyamakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Dyad of Elements is concluded.

5. Saccayamakaṃ

5. The Dyad of Truths

1. Paṇṇattivāravaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Section on Designations

1-9. Idāni [V 0.0310] teyeva mūlayamake desite kusalādidhamme saccavasena saṅgaṇhitvā dhātuyamakānantaraṃ desitassa saccayamakassa vaṇṇanā hoti. Tatthāpi heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva paṇṇattivārādayo tayo mahāvārā [M 0.0311] antaravārādayo ca avasesappabhedā veditabbā. Paṇṇattivāre panettha catunnaṃ saccānaṃ vasena padasodhanavāro, padasodhanamūlacakkavāro, suddhasaccavāro, suddhasaccamūlacakkavāroti imesu catūsu vāresu yamakagaṇanā veditabbā.

Now, having grouped those very wholesome and other phenomena, which were taught in the Root Dyad, by way of the truths, the explanation of the Dyad of Truths, which follows the Dyad of Elements, is given. Here too, the three major sections—the section on designations, etc.—and the remaining subdivisions should be understood as previously explained. In the section on designations here, the counting of the dyads should be understood in these four sections: the section on analysis of terms, the root-cycle section of analysis of terms, the section on pure truths, and the root-cycle section of pure truths.

10-26. Paṇṇattivāraniddese pana avasesaṃ dukkhasaccanti dukkhavedanāya ceva taṇhāya ca vinimuttā tebhūmakadhammā veditabbā. Avaseso samudayoti saccavibhaṅge niddiṭṭhakāmāvacarakusalādibhedo dukkhasaccassa paccayo. Avaseso nirodhoti tadaṅgavikkhambhanasamucchedapaṭipassaddhinirodho ceva khaṇabhaṅganirodho ca. Avaseso maggoti “tasmiṃ kho pana samaye pañcaṅgiko maggo hoti, aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, micchāmaggo, jaṅghamaggo, sakaṭamaggo”ti evamādiko.

In the exposition of the section on designations, the remaining aspect of the truth of suffering should be understood as the phenomena of the three realms that are free from both painful feeling and craving. The remaining aspect of the origin is the cause of the truth of suffering, with distinctions such as wholesome sense-sphere states and the like, as defined in the Analysis of the Truths. The remaining aspect of cessation is cessation by substitution, by suppression, by eradication, and by tranquility, as well as momentary cessation. The remaining aspect of the path refers to such things as: “At that time, the path is fivefold, the path is eightfold, the wrong path, the footpath, the cart-path,” and so forth.

Paṇṇattivāravaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Section on Designations

2. Pavattivāravaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Section on Occurrence

27-164. Pavattivāre [P 0.0078] panettha paccuppannakāle puggalavārassa anulomanaye “yassa dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjati, tassa samudayasaccaṃ uppajjati; yassa vā pana samudayasaccaṃ uppajjati, tassa dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjatī”ti dukkhasaccamūlakehi tīhi, samudayasaccamūlakehi dvīhi, nirodhasaccamūlakena ekenāti labbhamānañca alabbhamānañca gahetvā pāḷivasena chahi yamakehi [V 0.0311] bhavitabbaṃ. Tesu yasmā nirodhassa neva uppādo, na nirodho yujjati, tasmā dukkhasaccamūlakāni samudayasaccamaggasaccehi saddhiṃ dve, samudayasaccamūlakaṃ maggasaccena saddhiṃ ekanti tīṇi yamakāni āgatāni. Tassa paṭilomanayepi okāsavārādīsupi eseva nayo. Evamettha sabbavāresu tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇaṃ yamakānaṃ vasena yamakagaṇanā veditabbā. Atthavinicchaye panettha idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ – imassa hi saccayamakassa pavattivāre nirodhasaccaṃ tāva na labbhateva. Sesesu pana tīsu samudayasaccamaggasaccāni ekantena pavattiyaṃyeva labbhanti. Dukkhasaccaṃ cutipaṭisandhīsupi pavattepi labbhati. Paccuppannādayo pana tayo kālā cutipaṭisandhīnampi pavattiyāpi vasena labbhanti. Evamettha yaṃ yaṃ labbhati, tassa tassa vasena atthavinicchayo veditabbo.

In the section on occurrence, regarding the present time in the individual section, in the forward order: “For whom the truth of suffering arises, for them the truth of origin arises; or for whom the truth of origin arises, for them the truth of suffering arises.” Based on the truth of suffering as the root, three dyads are formed; based on the truth of origin as the root, two dyads; and based on the truth of cessation as the root, one dyad. Thus, considering both what is obtainable and unobtainable, six dyads should be formed according to the text. Among these, because neither arising nor cessation is applicable to cessation, therefore, two dyads are formed by combining the truth of suffering as the root with the truths of origin and path, and one dyad is formed by combining the truth of origin as the root with the truth of path—thus, three dyads are obtained. In the reverse order, as well as in sections like the occasion section, the same method applies. Thus, in all sections, the counting of dyads should be understood on the basis of three dyads each. In the analysis of meaning here, this is the characteristic: in the section on occurrence of this Dyad of Truths, the truth of cessation is not obtainable at all. Among the remaining three, the truths of origin and path are definitely obtainable only in occurrence. The truth of suffering is obtainable in death and rebirth-linking as well as in occurrence. The three times—present, etc.—are obtainable based on death and rebirth-linking as well as occurrence. Thus, here, the analysis of meaning should be understood according to whatever is obtainable.

Tatridaṃ [M 0.0312] nayamukhaṃ – sabbesaṃ upapajjantānanti antamaso suddhāvāsānampi. Tepi hi dukkhasacceneva upapajjanti. Taṇhāvippayuttacittassāti idaṃ dukkhasaccasamudayasaccesu ekakoṭṭhāsassa uppattidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmā pañcavokāravaseneva gahetabbaṃ. Catuvokāre pana taṇhāvippayuttassa phalasamāpatticittassa uppādakkhaṇe ekampi saccaṃ nuppajjati. Idaṃ idha na gahetabbaṃ. Tesaṃ dukkhasaccañcāti tasmiñhi khaṇe taṇhaṃ ṭhapetvā sesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ nāma hotīti sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Maggassa uppādakkhaṇepi eseva nayo. Tattha pana rūpameva dukkhasaccaṃ nāma. Sesā maggasampayuttakā dhammā saccavinimuttā. Teneva kāraṇena [P 0.0079] “arūpe maggassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ maggasaccaṃ uppajjati, no ca tesaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ uppajjatī”ti vuttaṃ. Sabbesaṃ upapajjantānaṃ pavatte taṇhāvippayuttacittassa uppādakkhaṇe tesaṃ tatthāti tesaṃ tasmiṃ upapattikkhaṇe taṇhāvippayuttacittuppattikkhaṇe cāti evamettha khaṇavasena okāso veditabbo. Aññesupi evarūpesu eseva nayo. Anabhisametāvīnanti catusaccapaṭivedhasaṅkhātaṃ abhisamayaṃ appattasattānaṃ. Abhisametāvīnanti abhisamitasaccānanti. Iminā nayamukhena sabbattha atthavinicchayo veditabbo.

Here is the method—for all beings who are reborn, even including those in the Pure Abodes. For they too are reborn only through the truth of suffering. “The mind free from craving”—this is stated to show the arising of one aspect of the truths of suffering and the origin of suffering. Therefore, it should be understood only in terms of the five-constituent existence. However, in the four-constituent existence, at the moment of the arising of the fruition-attainment mind free from craving, not even a single truth arises. This is not to be taken here. “Of them, the truth of suffering”—this is stated intending that at that moment, apart from craving, the remainder is called the truth of suffering. The same applies at the moment of the arising of the path. There, only form is called the truth of suffering. The remaining path-associated states are freed from the truths. For this reason, it is said: “In the formless realm, at the moment of the path's arising, the truth of the path arises for them, but the truth of suffering does not arise for them.” For all beings who are reborn, at the moment of the arising of a mind free from craving in the course of existence—for them, there—that is, for them at that moment of rebirth and at the moment of the arising of a mind free from craving—the occasion should be understood in terms of these moments. The same applies in other similar cases. “Those who have not penetrated”—refers to beings who have not attained the penetration known as the realization of the four truths. “Those who have penetrated”—refers to those who have realized the truths. Through this method, the meaning should be discerned in all cases.

Pavattivāravaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Section on Occurrence

3. Pariññāvāravaṇṇanā

3. Exposition of the Section on Full Understanding

165-170. Pariññāvāre [V 0.0312] pana ñātapariññā, tīraṇapariññā, pahānapariññāti tissopettha pariññāyo labbhanti. Yasmā ca lokuttaradhammesu pariññā nāma natthi; tasmā idha dve saccāni gahitāni. Tattha dukkhasaccaṃ parijānātīti ñātatīraṇapariññāvaseneva vuttaṃ. Samudayasaccaṃ pajahatīti ñātapahānapariññāvasena. Iti imāsaṃ pariññānaṃ vasena sabbapadesu attho veditabboti.

165-170. In the section on comprehension, the three comprehensions are obtained here: comprehension as the known, comprehension as scrutinizing, and comprehension as abandoning. And since there is no such thing as comprehension in the supramundane states, therefore two truths are taken here. Therein, 'one fully understands the truth of suffering' is stated only by way of comprehension as the known and as scrutinizing. 'One abandons the truth of the origin' is stated by way of comprehension as the known and as abandoning. Thus, the meaning in all passages should be understood by way of these comprehensions.

Pariññāvāravaṇṇanā.

Exposition of the Section on Comprehension.

Saccayamakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of the Pairs of Truths is concluded.

6. Saṅkhārayamakaṃ

6. The Pairs of Formations

1. Paṇṇattivāravaṇṇanā

1. Exposition of the Section on Designations.

1. Idāni [M 0.0313] tesaññeva mūlayamake desitānaṃ kusalādidhammānaṃ labbhamānavasena ekadesaṃ saṅgaṇhitvā saccayamakānantaraṃ desitassa saṅkhārayamakassa vaṇṇanā hoti. Tatthāpi heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva paṇṇattivārādayo tayo mahāvārā, antaravārādayo ca avasesapabhedā veditabbā. Ayaṃ panettha viseso – paṇṇattivāre tāva yathā heṭṭhā khandhādayo dhamme uddisitvā “rūpaṃ rūpakkhandho; cakkhu cakkhāyatanaṃ; cakkhu cakkhudhātu; dukkhaṃ dukkhasacca”nti padasodhanavāro āraddho. Tathā anārabhitvā “assāsapassāsā kāyasaṅkhāro”ti paṭhamaṃ tayopi saṅkhārā vibhajitvā dassitā.

1.
