Āsevanaṭṭhena anantarānaṃ paguṇabalavabhāvāya upakārako dhammo āsevanapaccayo, ganthādīsu purimāpurimābhiyogo viya. So kusalākusalakiriyajavanavasena tividho hoti. Yathāha – purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo[V 0.0349]. Purimā purimā akusalā…pe… kiriyābyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kiriyābyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayoti.

The phenomenon that is helpful by way of repetition, for the sake of the proficiency and strength of the immediately succeeding phenomena, is the repetition condition, like the repeated application in texts, etc. It is threefold by way of wholesome, unwholesome, and functional javanas. As it is said: “The preceding wholesome phenomena are a condition for the subsequent wholesome phenomena by way of the repetition condition. The preceding unwholesome…pe…functional indeterminate phenomena are a condition for the subsequent functional indeterminate phenomena by way of the repetition condition.”

Cittapayogasaṅkhātena kiriyābhāvena upakārako dhammo kammapaccayo. So nānākkhaṇikāya ceva kusalākusalacetanāya sahajātāya ca sabbāyapi cetanāya vasena duvidho hoti. Yathāha – kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃ samuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayoti.

The phenomenon that is helpful by way of being an action, designated as mental exertion, is the kamma condition. It is twofold: by way of wholesome and unwholesome volition occurring at different moments, and by way of all co-nascent volition. As it is said: “Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for the resultant aggregates and for materiality produced by kamma by way of the kamma condition. Volition is a condition for its associated phenomena and the materiality originated by it by way of the kamma condition.”

Nirussāhasantabhāvena nirussāhasantabhāvāya upakārako vipākadhammo vipākapaccayo. So pavatte cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ, paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattā ca [M 0.0350] rūpānaṃ, sabbattha ca sampayuttadhammānaṃ vipākapaccayo hoti. Yathāha – vipākābyākato eko khandho tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ, cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ, vipākapaccayena paccayo…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākato eko khandho…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo. Khandhā vatthussa vipākapaccayena paccayoti.

The resultant phenomenon that is helpful by way of being free from exertion and tranquil, for the sake of being free from exertion and tranquil, is the result condition. It is a result condition for consciousness-originated materiality in the course of existence, for kamma-originated materiality at rebirth, and for associated phenomena everywhere. As it is said: “One resultant-indeterminate aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and consciousness-originated materiality by way of the result condition…pe… At the moment of rebirth, one resultant-indeterminate aggregate…pe… two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates and kamma-originated materiality by way of the result condition. The aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of the result condition.”

Rūpārūpānaṃ upatthambhakaṭṭhena upakārakā cattāro āhārā āhārapaccayo. Yathāha – kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. Arūpino āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayoti. Pañhāvāre pana “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo”tipi vuttaṃ.

The four kinds of nutriment that are helpful by way of supporting material and immaterial phenomena are the nutriment condition. As it is said: “Physical nutriment is a condition for this body by way of the nutriment condition. Immaterial nutriments are a condition for associated phenomena and for the materiality originated by them by way of the nutriment condition.” In the section on questions, it is also stated: “At the moment of rebirth, resultant-indeterminate nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-originated materiality by way of the nutriment condition.”

Adhipatiyaṭṭhena upakārakā itthindriyapurisindriyavajjā vīsatindriyā indriyapaccayo. Tattha cakkhundriyādayo pañca arūpadhammānaṃyeva, sesā rūpārūpānaṃ paccayā honti. Yathāha – cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā, sota… ghāna… jivhā… kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Arūpino indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayoti. Pañhāvāre pana “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo”tipi vuttaṃ.

Twenty faculties, excluding the femininity and masculinity faculties, that are helpful by way of dominance are the faculty condition. Among them, the five sense faculties such as the eye faculty are conditions only for immaterial phenomena, while the remaining ones are conditions for both material and immaterial phenomena. As it is said: 'The eye faculty is a condition for the eye-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the faculty condition. The ear… nose… tongue… body faculty is a condition for the body-consciousness element and for the states associated with it by way of the faculty condition. The material life faculty is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the faculty condition. The immaterial faculties are conditions for associated states and for the materiality originating from them by way of the faculty condition.' In the section on questions, it is also stated: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate faculties are conditions for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the faculty condition.'

Upanijjhāyanaṭṭhena [V 0.0350] upakārakāni ṭhapetvā dvipañcaviññāṇesu kāyikasukhadukkhavedanādvayaṃ sabbānipi kusalādibhedāni satta jhānaṅgāni jhānapaccayo. Yathāha – jhānaṅgāni jhānasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayoti. Pañhāvāre pana paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatāni jhānaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo”tipi vuttaṃ.

The seven jhāna factors of all types, such as wholesome, which are helpful by way of close contemplation—excluding the pair of bodily pleasant and painful feeling in the two sets of five sense-consciousnesses—are the jhāna condition. As it is said: 'Jhāna factors are a condition for jhāna-associated states and for material phenomena originating from them by way of the jhāna condition.' In the section on questions, it is also stated: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate jhāna factors are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the jhāna condition.'

Yato tato vā niyyānaṭṭhena upakārakāni kusalādibhedāni dvādasa maggaṅgāni maggapaccayo. Yathāha – “maggaṅgāni maggasampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo”ti. Pañhāvāre pana “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatāni maggaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ [M 0.0351] maggapaccayena paccayo”ti vuttaṃ. Na ete pana dvepi jhānamaggapaccayā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ dvipañcaviññāṇāhetukacittesu labbhantīti veditabbā.

The twelve path factors of all types, such as wholesome, which are helpful by way of leading out from this or that, are the path condition. As it is said: 'Path factors are a condition for path-associated states and for material phenomena originating from them by way of the path condition.' In the section on questions, it is stated: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate path factors are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the path condition.' It should be understood that these two, the jhāna and path conditions, are not found respectively in the two sets of five sense-consciousnesses and in the rootless consciousnesses.

Ekavatthukaekārammaṇaekuppādekanirodhasaṅkhātena sampayuttabhāvena upakārakā arūpadhammā sampayuttapaccayo. Yathāha – “cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Immaterial phenomena that are helpful through their state of association—characterized by a single base, a single object, a single arising, and a single ceasing—are the association condition. As it is said: 'The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the association condition.'

Ekavatthukādibhāvānupagamena upakārakā rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ, arūpino dhammā rūpīnaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. So sahajātapacchājātapurejātavasena tividho hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ – sahajātā kusalā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā kusalā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayoti. Abyākatapadassa pana sahajātavibhaṅge “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Khandhā vatthussa, vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo”ti vuttaṃ. Purejātaṃ pana cakkhundriyādivatthuvaseneva veditabbaṃ. Yathāha – purejātaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu vipākābyākatānaṃ kiriyābyākatānaṃ khandhānaṃ vatthu kusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ, vatthu akusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayoti.

Material phenomena helpful to immaterial phenomena, and immaterial phenomena helpful to material phenomena, by not undergoing the state of having a single base, etc., are a condition by way of dissociation. It is threefold: by way of conascence, post-nascence, and pre-nascence. And this has been stated: 'Conascent wholesome aggregates are a condition for consciousness-originated materiality by way of the dissociation condition. Post-nascent wholesome aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of the dissociation condition.' Regarding the term 'indeterminate,' in the section on conascence, it is stated: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant-indeterminate aggregates are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the dissociation condition. The aggregates are a condition for the base, and the base is a condition for the aggregates, by way of the dissociation condition.' Pre-nascence, however, should be understood only in terms of the bases such as the eye faculty. As it is said: 'The pre-nascent eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of the dissociation condition. The base is a condition for resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate aggregates; the base is a condition for wholesome aggregates; the base is a condition for unwholesome aggregates by way of the dissociation condition.'

Paccuppannalakkhaṇena atthibhāvena tādisasseva dhammassa upatthambhakaṭṭhena upakārako dhammo atthipaccayo[V 0.0351]. Tassa arūpakkhandhamahābhūtanāmarūpacittacetasikamahābhūtāyatanavatthuvasena sattadhā mātikā nikkhittā. Yathāha – cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; cattāro mahābhūtā aññamaññaṃ, okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpaṃ aññamaññaṃ, cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇadhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ manodhātuyā taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāya manodhātu ca manoviññāṇadhātu ca vattanti, taṃ rūpaṃ manodhātuyā ca manoviññāṇadhātuyā ca taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayoti. Pañhāvāre pana sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyantipi nikkhipitvā sahajāte tāva “eko khandho tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca [M 0.0352] rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo”tiādinā nayena niddeso kato. Purejāte purejātānaṃ cakkhādīnaṃ vasena niddeso kato. Pacchājāte purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ paccayavasena niddeso kato. Āhārindriyesu pana “kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ niddeso katoti.

A phenomenon that is helpful by way of supporting a similar phenomenon through its state of presence, which is characterized as present, is the presence condition. Its matrix is set forth in seven ways: by way of the immaterial aggregates, the great elements, name-and-form, mind and mental factors, the great elements, the sense bases, and the physical base. As it is said: 'The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of the presence condition; the four great elements are a condition for one another; at the moment of conception, name-and-form are a condition for one another; mind and mental factors are a condition for mind-originated materiality; the great elements are a condition for derived materiality; the eye base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element… and so on… the body base… the form base… the tangible base is a condition for the body-consciousness element and its associated phenomena by way of the presence condition. The form base… and so on… the tangible base is a condition for the mind element and its associated phenomena by way of the presence condition. That material form depending on which the mind element and the mind-consciousness element occur, that material form is a condition for the mind element, the mind-consciousness element, and their associated phenomena by way of the presence condition.' In the question section, however, having laid down conascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty, the exposition regarding conascence is made in this way: 'One aggregate is a condition for the other three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of the presence condition,' and so on. Regarding pre-nascence, the exposition is made by way of the pre-arisen eye, etc. Regarding post-nascence, the exposition is made by way of the post-nascent mind and mental factors being a condition for this pre-arisen body. Regarding nutriment and faculty, the exposition is made thus: 'Physical nutriment is a condition for this body by way of the presence condition. The material life faculty is a condition for kamma-born materiality by way of the presence condition.'

Attano anantaraṃ uppajjamānānaṃ arūpadhammānaṃ pavattiokāsassa dānena upakārakā samanantaraniruddhā arūpadhammā natthipaccayo. Yathāha – samanantaraniruddhā cittacetasikā dhammā paṭuppannānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ dhammānaṃ natthipaccayena paccayoti.

Immaterial phenomena that have just ceased, being helpful by giving an opportunity for the occurrence of immaterial phenomena arising immediately after them, are the absence condition. As it is said: 'Just-ceased mind and mental factors are a condition for presently arisen mind and mental factors by way of the absence condition.'

Te eva vigatabhāvena upakārakattā vigatapaccayo. Yathāha – samanantaravigatā cittacetasikā dhammā paṭuppannānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ dhammānaṃ vigatapaccayena paccayoti.

Those same phenomena, being helpful by way of their disappearance, are the disappearance condition. As it is said: 'Just-disappeared mind and mental factors are a condition for presently arisen mind and mental factors by way of the disappearance condition.'

Atthipaccayadhammā eva avigatabhāvena upakārakattā avigatapaccayoti veditabbā. Desanāvilāsena pana tathā vinetabbaveneyyavasena vā ayaṃ duko vutto; sahetukadukaṃ vatvāpi hetusampayuttaduko viyāti.

The phenomena of the presence condition should be understood as the non-disappearance condition, as they are helpful by way of their non-disappearance. This pair, however, is stated for the sake of elegance in teaching or according to the disposition of those to be trained, just as the 'associated-with-a-root pair' is stated after stating the 'with-a-root pair'.

Imesu pana catuvīsatiyā paccayesu asammohatthaṃ –

Now, for the sake of non-confusion regarding these twenty-four conditions:

Dhammato [V 0.0352] kālato ceva, nānappakārabhedato;

Paccayuppannato ceva, viññātabbo vinicchayo.

The determination should be understood by way of the phenomena, by way of time, by way of various distinctions, and by way of the conditioned phenomena.

Tattha dhammatoti – imesu hi paccayesu hetupaccayo tāva nāmarūpadhammesu nāmadhammekadeso. Ārammaṇapaccayo saddhiṃ paññattiyā ca abhāvena sabbepi nāmarūpadhammā. Adhipatipaccaye sahajātādhipati nāmadhammekadeso, tathā kammajhānamaggapaccayā. Ārammaṇādhipati sabbepi garukātabbā ārammaṇadhammā. Anantarasamanantarapacchājātaāsevanavipākasampayuttanatthivigatapaccayā nāmadhammāva. Nibbānassa asaṅgahitattā nāmadhammekadesotipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Purejātapaccayo rūpekadeso. Sesā yathālābhavasena nāmarūpadhammāti evaṃ tāvettha dhammato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Therein, 'by way of the phenomena' means: among these conditions, the root condition is a portion of mental phenomena within mentality-materiality phenomena. The object condition, together with concepts and absence, comprises all mentality-materiality phenomena. In the dominance condition, conascent dominance is a portion of mental phenomena; likewise for the kamma, jhāna, and path conditions. Object-dominance comprises all object-phenomena that are to be regarded as weighty. The contiguity, immediacy, post-nascence, repetition, result, association, absence, and disappearance conditions are solely mental phenomena. As Nibbāna is unincluded, it is also fitting to call it a portion of mental phenomena. The pre-nascence condition is a portion of material phenomena. The remaining conditions are mentality-materiality phenomena, as they may be found. Thus, the determination should first be understood by way of the phenomena.

Kālatoti [M 0.0353] –

'By way of time' means:

Paccuppannāva hontettha, paccayā dasa pañca ca;

Atītā eva pañceko, te kāle dvepi nissito;

Tayo tikālikā ceva, vimuttā cāpi kālatoti.

Herein, fifteen conditions are only present; five are only past; one depends on both times; three are of the three times; and one is free from time.

Etesu hi hetupaccayo sahajātaaññamaññanissayapurejātapacchājātavipākaāhāraindriyajhānamaggasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatapaccayoti ime pannarasa paccayā paccuppannadhammāva honti. Anantarapaccayo samanantaraāsevananatthivigatapaccayoti ime pañca atītāyeva honti. Eko pana kammapaccayo, so paccuppannātīte dvepi kāle nissito hoti. Sesā ārammaṇapaccayo adhipatipaccayo upanissayapaccayoti ime tayo paccayā tekālikāpi honti, paññattiyā saddhiṃ nibbānassa saṅgahitattā kālavimuttāpīti. Evamettha kālatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Among these, the root, conascence, mutuality, support, pre-nascence, post-nascence, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance conditions—these fifteen conditions are only present phenomena. The contiguity, immediacy, repetition, absence, and disappearance conditions—these five are only past. The kamma condition, however, depends on both times, present and past. The remaining three conditions—object, dominance, and decisive support—are of the three times; and as they include Nibbāna along with concepts, they are also timeless. Thus, the determination should also be understood by way of time.

Nānappakārabhedato paccayuppannatoti imesaṃ pana dvinnaṃ padānaṃ attho niddesavāre āvibhavissatīti.

The meaning of these two terms, 'by way of various distinctions' and 'by way of the conditioned phenomena,' will become manifest in the section on the exposition.

Paccayuddesavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Summary of Conditions.

Paccayaniddeso

The Exposition of Conditions

1. Hetupaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Exposition of the Root Condition

1. Idāni [V 0.0353] sabbepi te paccaye uddiṭṭhapaṭipāṭiyā niddisitvā dassetuṃ hetupaccayoti hetū hetusampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayotiādimāha. Tattha hetupaccayoti catuvīsatiyā paccayesu nikkhittapaṭipāṭiyā sabbapaṭhamaṃ bhājetabbassa paduddhāro. Sesapaccayesupi imināva nayena paṭhamaṃ bhājetabbapadaṃ uddharitvā vissajjanaṃ katanti veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha sambandho – yo paccayuddese hetupaccayoti uddiṭṭho, so niddesato “hetū hetusampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ veditabbo[M 0.0354]. Iminā upāyena sabbapaccayesu bhājetabbassa padassa vissajjanena saddhiṃ sambandho veditabbo.

1. Now, to explain all those conditions in the order they were enumerated, one begins by stating the root condition: 'Roots are a condition by way of root condition for the states associated with them and for the material phenomena originating from them.' Herein, the term 'root condition' is the extraction of the first phrase to be analyzed among the twenty-four conditions arranged in sequence. For the remaining conditions as well, it should be understood that the phrase to be analyzed is first extracted in the same way and then explained. The connection here is this: what was stated in the enumeration of conditions as 'root condition' should be understood from the detailed exposition as, 'Roots are a condition by way of root condition for the states associated with them and for the material phenomena originating from them.' By this method, the connection of the phrase to be analyzed with its explanation should be understood for all conditions.

Idāni hetū hetusampayuttakānanti ettha “hetusampayuttakāna”nti avatvā “hetū hetusampayuttakāna”nti kasmā vuttanti? Paccayassa ceva paccayuppannānañca vavatthāpanato. Hetusampayuttakānanti hi vutte hetunā sampayuttakānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayoti attho bhaveyya. Evaṃ sante asuko nāma dhammo hetupaccayena paccayoti paccayavavatthānaṃ na paññāyeyya. Athāpi hetunā sampayuttakānaṃ hetusampayuttakānanti atthaṃ aggahetvāva yesaṃ kesañci sampayuttakānaṃ hetū hetupaccayena paccayoti attho bhaveyya, evaṃ sante hetunā vippayuttā cakkhuviññāṇādayopi sampayuttakāyeva, hetunā sampayuttā kusalādayopi. Tattha ayaṃ hetu asukassa nāma sampayuttakadhammassa paccayoti paccayuppannavavatthānaṃ na paññāyeyya. Tasmā paccayañceva paccayuppannañca vavatthāpento “hetū hetusampayuttakāna”nti āha. Tassattho – hetusampayuttakānaṃ kusalādidhammānaṃ yo hetu sampayuttako, so hetupaccayena paccayoti. Tatrāpi “paccayo”ti avatvā “hetupaccayenā”ti vacanaṃ hetuno aññathā paccayabhāvapaṭisedhanatthaṃ. Ayañhi hetu hetupaccayenāpi paccayo hoti, sahajātādipaccayenāpi. Tatrāssa yvāyaṃ sahajātādipaccayavasena aññathāpi paccayabhāvo, tassa paṭisedhanatthaṃ hetupaccayenāti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ santepi “taṃsampayuttakāna”nti avatvā kasmā “hetusampayuttakāna”nti vuttanti? Niddisitabbassa apākaṭattā. Taṃsampayuttakānanti hi vutte yena te taṃsampayuttakā nāma honti[V 0.0354], ayaṃ nāma soti niddisitabbo apākaṭo. Tassa apākaṭattā yena sampayuttā te taṃsampayuttakāti vuccanti, taṃ sarūpatova dassetuṃ “hetusampayuttakāna”nti vuttaṃ.

Now, in the phrase 'hetū hetusampayuttakānaṃ,' why is it said thus and not just 'hetusampayuttakānaṃ'? It is for the purpose of defining both the condition and the conditioned phenomena. For if it were said 'hetusampayuttakānaṃ,' the meaning would be '[a condition] for states associated with a root,' and in that case, the definition of the condition would not be apparent. Or again, if, without taking 'hetusampayuttakānaṃ' to mean 'those associated with a root,' the meaning were 'roots are a condition by way of root condition for any associated phenomena,' then in that case, phenomena dissociated from roots—such as eye-consciousness and others—would also be considered 'associated,' as would wholesome and other phenomena associated with roots. In that case, the definition of the conditioned phenomenon—that is, for which specific associated state this root is a condition—would not be apparent. Therefore, to define both the condition and the conditioned, it is said, 'hetū hetusampayuttakānaṃ.' Its meaning is this: for states associated with roots, such as wholesome states, the associated root is a condition for them by way of root condition. Here, instead of simply saying 'paccayo' (a condition), the phrase 'hetupaccayena' (by way of root condition) is used to preclude the root's being a condition in another way. For this root is a condition both by way of root condition and by way of other conditions like conascence. To preclude its being a condition in other ways, such as by conascence, the phrase 'hetupaccayena' is used. Even so, why is it said 'hetusampayuttakānaṃ' instead of 'taṃsampayuttakānaṃ'? Because that which is to be specified is not manifest. If it were said 'taṃsampayuttakānaṃ,' that with which they are associated would not be manifest. Due to this lack of clarity, to show in its own form that with which they are associated, the phrase 'hetusampayuttakānaṃ' is used.

Taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti ettha pana niddisitabbassa pākaṭattā taṃ-gahaṇaṃ kataṃ. Ayañhettha attho – te hetū ceva hetusampayuttakā ca dhammā samuṭṭhānaṃ etesanti taṃsamuṭṭhānāni. Tesaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānaṃ, hetuto ceva hetusampayuttadhammehi ca nibbattānanti attho. Iminā cittasamuṭṭhānarūpaṃ gaṇhāti[M 0.0355]. Kiṃ pana taṃ cittato aññenapi samuṭṭhātīti? Āma, samuṭṭhāti. Sabbepi hi cittacetasikā ekato hutvā rūpaṃ samuṭṭhāpenti. Lokiyadhammadesanāyaṃ pana cittassa adhikabhāvato tathāvidhaṃ rūpaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānanti vuccati. Tenevāha cittacetasikā dhammā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayoti.

In the term 'taṃsamuṭṭhānānaṃ,' however, the prefix 'taṃ' (that) is used because what is to be specified is manifest. Herein, the meaning is: those roots and the states associated with the roots are the origin of these material phenomena; therefore, they are called 'taṃsamuṭṭhānāni' (originating from them). 'Tesaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānaṃ' means: for those originating from them, that is, arisen from those roots and from the states associated with the roots. By this, he includes mind-originated matter. But does that matter arise from something other than mind as well? Yes, it does. For all mind and mental factors, having come together, produce matter. However, in the teaching of worldly phenomena, because of the predominance of mind, such matter is called 'mind-originated.' Therefore, it is said: 'Mind and mental factors are a condition by way of conascence for mind-originated matter.'

Yadi evaṃ idhāpi “taṃsamuṭṭhānāna”nti avatvā cittasamuṭṭhānānanti kasmā na vuttanti? Acittasamuṭṭhānānampi saṅgaṇhanato. Pañhāvārasmiñhi “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayoti āgataṃ”. Tassa saṅgaṇhanatthaṃ idha cittasamuṭṭhānānanti avatvā taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti vuttaṃ. Tassattho – cittajarūpaṃ ajanayamānāpi te hetū hetusampayuttakā dhammā sahajātādipaccayavasena samuṭṭhānaṃ etesanti taṃsamuṭṭhānāni. Tesaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānaṃ pavatte cittajānaṃ paṭisandhiyañca kaṭattārūpānampi hetū hetupaccayena paccayoti. Iminā upāyena aññesupi taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti āgataṭṭhānesu attho veditabbo.

If that is so, why is 'taṃsamuṭṭhānānaṃ' (originating from them) used here instead of 'cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ' (originating from mind)? It is to include that which does not originate from mind. For in the Question Section, it is stated: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant-indeterminate roots are a condition by way of root condition for the associated aggregates and for the materiality produced by kamma.' To include that, 'originating from them' is said here instead of 'originating from mind.' Its meaning is this: even while not generating mind-originated matter, those roots and states associated with the roots are the origin of this kamma-produced matter by way of conascence and other conditions; thus, they are called 'originating from them.' For these phenomena 'originating from them'—namely, for mind-originated matter in the course of existence and for kamma-produced matter at rebirth-linking—the roots are a condition by way of root condition. In this way, the meaning should be understood in other places where 'originating from them' is mentioned.

Kasmā panāyaṃ hetu paṭisandhiyameva kaṭattārūpānaṃ hetupaccayo hoti, na pavatteti? Paṭisandhiyaṃ kammajarūpānaṃ cittapaṭibaddhavuttitāya. Paṭisandhiyañhi kammajarūpānaṃ cittapaṭibaddhā pavatti, cittavasena uppajjanti ceva tiṭṭhanti ca. Tasmiñhi khaṇe cittaṃ cittajarūpaṃ janetuṃ na sakkoti, tānipi vinā cittena uppajjituṃ vā ṭhātuṃ vā na sakkonti. Tenevāha – “viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, tasmiṃ patiṭṭhite viññāṇe nāmarūpassa avakkanti hotī”ti (saṃ. ni. 2.39). Pavattiyaṃ pana tesaṃ citte vijjamānepi kammapaṭibaddhāva pavatti, na cittapaṭibaddhā. Avijjamāne cāpi citte nirodhasamāpannānaṃ uppajjantiyeva.

But why is this root a condition for kamma-produced matter only at rebirth-linking, and not in the course of existence? Because at rebirth-linking, kamma-produced matter has an occurrence that is bound up with consciousness. For at rebirth-linking, the occurrence of kamma-produced matter is bound up with consciousness; it arises and persists dependent on consciousness. At that moment, consciousness is not able to generate mind-originated matter, nor can that kamma-produced matter arise or persist without consciousness. Therefore it is said: 'With consciousness as condition, there is name-and-form; when that consciousness is established, there is the descent of name-and-form' (SN 12.39). In the course of existence, however, although consciousness is present for that kamma-produced matter, its occurrence is bound up with kamma, not with consciousness. And it arises even when consciousness is absent, as for those who have attained the cessation attainment.

Kasmā pana paṭisandhikkhaṇe cittaṃ cittajarūpaṃ janetuṃ na sakkotīti? Kammavegakkhittatāya [V 0.0355] ceva appatiṭṭhitavatthutāya ca dubbalattā. Tañhi tadā kammavegakkhittaṃ apurejātavatthukattā ca appatiṭṭhitavatthukanti dubbalaṃ hoti. Tasmā papāte patitamatto puriso kiñci sippaṃ kātuṃ viya rūpaṃ janetuṃ na sakkoti; kammajarūpameva panassa cittasamuṭṭhānarūpaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati. Tañca kammajarūpasseva bījaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhati. Kammaṃ panassa khettasadisaṃ, kilesā [M 0.0356] āpasadisā. Tasmā santepi khette āpe ca paṭhamuppattiyaṃ bījānubhāvena rukkhuppatti viya paṭisandhikkhaṇe cittānubhāvena rūpakāyassa uppatti. Bīje pana vigatepi pathavīāpānubhāvena rukkhassa uparūpari pavatti viya; vinā cittena kammatova kaṭattārūpānaṃ pavatti hotīti veditabbā. Vuttampi cetaṃ – “kammaṃ khettaṃ viññāṇaṃ bījaṃ taṇhā sneho”ti (a. ni. 3.77).

Why then is consciousness unable to produce mind-originated matter at the moment of rebirth-linking? Because it is weak, due to being propelled by the force of kamma and having an unestablished base. For at that time, being propelled by the force of kamma and lacking a pre-arisen base, it has an unestablished base and is thus weak. Therefore, just as a man who has just fallen from a precipice is unable to perform any skill, so too consciousness cannot produce matter; instead, for that being, kamma-produced matter stands in the place of mind-originated matter. And that consciousness itself stands in the position of a seed for that very kamma-produced matter. Moreover, kamma is like the field, and defilements are like water. Thus, even though the field and water are present, just as a tree first sprouts through the power of the seed, so too at the moment of rebirth-linking, the arising of the material body occurs through the power of consciousness. And just as when the seed is gone, the tree continues to grow upwards through the power of the earth and water, so too it should be understood that even without consciousness, the continuation of matter produced by that kamma occurs from kamma alone. And this has also been said: 'Kamma is the field, consciousness the seed, and craving the moisture' (A.N. 3.77).

Ayañca panattho okāsavaseneva gahetabbo. Tayo hi okāsā – nāmokāso, rūpokāso, nāmarūpokāsoti. Tattha arūpabhavo nāmokāso nāma. Tatra hi hadayavatthumattampi rūpapaccayaṃ vinā arūpadhammāva uppajjanti. Asaññabhavo rūpokāso nāma. Tatra hi paṭisandhicittamattampi arūpapaccayaṃ vinā rūpadhammāva uppajjanti. Pañcavokārabhavo nāmarūpokāso nāma. Tatra hi vatthurūpamattampi vinā paṭisandhiyaṃ arūpadhammā, paṭisandhicittañca vinā kammajāpi rūpadhammā nuppajjanti. Yuganaddhāva rūpārūpānaṃ uppatti. Yathā hi sassāmike sarājake gehe sadvārapālake rājāṇattiṃ vinā paṭhamappaveso nāma natthi, aparabhāge pana vināpi āṇattiṃ purimāṇattiānubhāveneva hoti, evameva pañcavokāre paṭisandhiviññāṇarājassa sahajātādipaccayataṃ vinā rūpassa paṭisandhivasena paṭhamuppatti nāma natthi. Aparabhāge pana vināpi paṭisandhiviññāṇassa sahajātādipaccayānubhāvaṃ purimānubhāvavasena laddhappavesassa kammato pavatti hoti. Asaññabhavo pana yasmā arūpokāso na hoti, tasmā tattha vināva arūpapaccayā asaññokāsattā rūpaṃ pavattati, assāmike suññagehe attano gehe ca purisassa paveso viya. Arūpabhavopi yasmā rūpokāso na hoti, tasmā tattha vināva rūpapaccayā aññokāsattā arūpadhammā pavattanti. Pañcavokārabhavo pana rūpārūpokāsoti natthettha arūpapaccayaṃ vinā paṭisandhikkhaṇe rūpānaṃ uppattīti. Iti ayaṃ hetu paṭisandhiyameva kaṭattārūpānaṃ paccayo hoti, na pavatteti.

This matter should be understood by way of the spheres. There are three kinds of spheres: the sphere of mentality, the sphere of materiality, and the sphere of mentality-materiality. Here, the formless existence is called the sphere of mentality. There, only immaterial phenomena arise, without a material condition, not even a heart-base. The non-percipient existence is called the sphere of materiality. There, only material phenomena arise, without an immaterial condition, not even a rebirth-linking consciousness. The five-aggregate existence is called the sphere of mentality-materiality. There, at rebirth, immaterial phenomena do not arise without a material base, nor do kamma-produced material phenomena arise without the rebirth-linking consciousness. The arising of materiality and immateriality is yoked together. Just as in a house with an owner, a king, and a gatekeeper, there is no first entry without the king's command, but later, even without a command, entry occurs due to the power of the previous command—just so, in the five-aggregate existence, there is no first arising of materiality by way of rebirth without the co-nascent conditionality and so on of the king that is the rebirth-linking consciousness. But later, even without the power of the co-nascent conditionality and so on of the rebirth-linking consciousness, the continuation of what has gained entry by way of the former power occurs from kamma. The non-percipient existence, however, since it is not the sphere of mentality, materiality continues there even without an immaterial condition, because it is the non-percipient sphere, like the entry of a man into an unowned, empty house, or into his own house. The formless existence, too, since it is not the sphere of materiality, immaterial phenomena continue there even without a material condition, because it is the other sphere. But the five-aggregate existence is the sphere of mentality-materiality, so there is no arising of materiality at the rebirth moment without an immaterial condition. Thus, this cause is a condition for kamma-produced matter only at rebirth, not in the course of existence.

Nanu “hetū sahajātānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayoti vutte sabbopi ayamattho gahito hoti, atha [V 0.0356] kasmā “hetusampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ taṃsamuṭṭhānānañca rūpāna”nti idaṃ gahitanti? Pavattiyaṃ kaṭattārūpādīnaṃ paccayabhāvapaṭibāhanato. Evañhi sati yāni pavattiyaṃ hetunā [M 0.0357] saha ekakkhaṇe kaṭattārūpāni ceva utuāhārasamuṭṭhānāni ca jāyanti, tesampi hetū hetupaccayoti āpajjeyya, na ca so tesaṃ paccayo. Tasmā tesaṃ paccayabhāvassa paṭibāhanatthametaṃ gahitanti veditabbaṃ.

Is it not the case that when it is said, 'Roots are a condition for co-nascent phenomena by way of the root condition,' all this meaning is understood? Then why is this phrase 'for the phenomena associated with the roots and for the material phenomena originating from them' included? To prevent [the root] from being a condition for kamma-produced matter and so on in the course of existence. For if this were not so, then in the course of existence, it would follow that the roots are also a root-condition for the kamma-produced matter and the matter originating from temperature and nutriment which arise at the same moment as the roots; but it is not a condition for them. Therefore, it should be understood that this is included to prevent its being a condition for them.

Idāni “nānappakārabhedato paccayuppannato”ti imesaṃ padānaṃ vasenettha viññātabbo vinicchayo. Tesu nānappakārabhedatoti ayañhi hetu nāma jātito kusalākusalavipākakiriyabhedato catubbidho. Tattha kusalahetu bhūmantarato kāmāvacarādibhedena catubbidho, akusalahetu kāmāvacarova vipākahetu kāmāvacarādibhedena catubbidho, kiriyahetu kāmāvacaro rūpāvacaro arūpāvacaroti tividho. Tattha kāmāvacarakusalahetu nāmato alobhādivasena tividho. Rūpāvacarādikusalahetūsupi eseva nayo. Akusalahetu lobhādivasena tividho. Vipākakiriyahetū pana alobhādivasena tayo tayo honti. Taṃtaṃcittasampayogavasena pana tesaṃ tesaṃ hetūnaṃ nānappakārabhedoyevāti evaṃ tāvettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Now, the analysis of the phrases 'due to the diversity of kinds' and 'from the condition-produced' is to be understood here. Among these, regarding 'due to the diversity of kinds': this root, by nature, is fourfold, divided into wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional. Among these, the wholesome root is fourfold, being divided according to the various planes into sense-sphere and so on. The unwholesome root is only of the sense-sphere. The resultant root is fourfold, being divided into sense-sphere and so on. The functional root is threefold: of the sense-sphere, form-sphere, and formless-sphere. Among these, the sense-sphere wholesome root is threefold by name: by way of non-greed and so on. The same method applies to the wholesome roots of the form-sphere and so on. The unwholesome root is threefold: by way of greed and so on. The resultant and functional roots, however, are each threefold: by way of non-greed and so on. Moreover, due to their association with various types of consciousness, there is indeed a diversity of kinds among these roots. Thus, first, the analysis should be understood here with respect to 'due to the diversity of kinds'.

Paccayuppannatoti iminā paccayena ime dhammā uppajjanti, imesaṃ nāma dhammānaṃ ayaṃ paccayoti evampi viññātabbo vinicchayoti attho. Tattha imasmiṃ tāva hetupaccaye kāmāvacarakusalahetu kāmabhavarūpabhavesu attanā sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca hetupaccayo hoti, arūpabhave sampayuttadhammānaṃyeva. Rūpāvacarakusalahetu kāmabhavarūpabhavesuyeva sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca hetupaccayo. Arūpāvacarakusalahetu kāmāvacarakusalahetusadisova. Tathā apariyāpannakusalahetu, tathā akusalahetu. Kāmāvacaravipākahetu pana kāmabhavasmiṃyeva attanā sampayuttadhammānaṃ, paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ, pavatte cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca hetupaccayo. Rūpāvacaravipākahetu rūpabhave vuttappakārānaññeva hetupaccayo. Arūpāvacaravipākahetu arūpabhave sampayuttakānaññeva hetupaccayo. Apariyāpannavipākahetu kāmabhavarūpabhavesu sampayuttakānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca arūpabhave arūpadhammānaññeva hetupaccayo. Kiriyahetūsu pana tebhūmakesupi [M 0.0358] kusalahetusadisova paccayoti. Evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

'As being produced by the condition' means that these phenomena arise through this condition, or that this is the condition for these phenomena—this is how the analysis is to be understood. Here, in this root condition, the sense-sphere wholesome root is a root condition for its associated phenomena and for the material phenomena originating from consciousness in the sense-sphere and form-sphere existences, and only for its associated phenomena in the formless existence. The form-sphere wholesome root is a root condition for its associated phenomena and for the material phenomena originating from consciousness only in the sense-sphere and form-sphere existences. The formless-sphere wholesome root is similar to the sense-sphere wholesome root. Likewise for the supramundane wholesome root, and also the unwholesome root. The sense-sphere resultant root, however, is a root condition only in the sense-sphere existence for its associated phenomena, for kamma-produced form at rebirth, and for the material phenomena originating from consciousness in the course of existence. The form-sphere resultant root is a root condition in the form-sphere existence for the aforementioned types. The formless-sphere resultant root is a root condition only for its associated phenomena in the formless-sphere existence. The supramundane resultant root is a root condition for its associated phenomena and the material phenomena originating from consciousness in the sense-sphere and form-sphere existences, and for immaterial phenomena alone in the formless-sphere existence. As for the functional roots, in all three planes of existence, they are conditions similar to the wholesome roots. Thus, here the analysis is to be understood also from the perspective of the condition-produced phenomena.

Hetupaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Root Condition.

2. Ārammaṇapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Exposition of the Object Condition.

2. Ārammaṇapaccayaniddese [V 0.0357] rūpāyatananti rūpasaṅkhātaṃ āyatanaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyāti cakkhuviññāṇasaṅkhātāya dhātuyā. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Taṃsampayuttakānanti tāya cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā sampayuttakānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ, sabbesampi cakkhupasādavatthukānaṃ catunnaṃ khandhānaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayoti attho. Ito paresupi eseva nayo. Manodhātuyāti sasampayuttadhammāya tividhāyapi manodhātuyā rūpāyatanādīni pañca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo, no ca kho ekakkhaṇe. Sabbe dhammāti etāni ca rūpāyatanādīni pañca avasesā ca sabbepi ñeyyadhammā imā cha dhātuyo ṭhapetvā sesāya sasampayuttadhammāya manoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇapaccayena paccayoti attho. Yaṃ yaṃ dhammaṃ ārabbhāti iminā ye ete etāsaṃ sattannaṃ viññāṇadhātūnaṃ ārammaṇadhammā vuttā, te tāsaṃ dhātūnaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā uppajjanakkhaṇeyeva ārammaṇapaccayo hontīti dīpeti. Evaṃ hontāpi ca na ekato honti, yaṃ yaṃ ārabbha ye ye uppajjanti, tesaṃ tesaṃ te te visuṃ visuṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hontītipi dīpeti. Uppajjantīti idaṃ yathā najjo sandanti, pabbatā tiṭṭhantīti sabbakālasaṅgahavasena, evaṃ vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tena yepi ārabbha ye uppajjiṃsu, yepi uppajjissanti, te sabbe ārammaṇapaccayeneva uppajjiṃsu ca uppajjissanti cāti siddhaṃ hoti. Cittacetasikā dhammāti idaṃ “ye ye dhammā”ti vuttānaṃ sarūpato nidassanaṃ. Te te dhammāti te te ārammaṇadhammā. Tesaṃ tesanti tesaṃ tesaṃ cittacetasikadhammānaṃ. Ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

2. In the exposition of the object condition, 'base of form' (rūpāyatana) means the base that is reckoned as form. The same method applies to the rest. 'For the eye-consciousness element' (cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā) means for the element that is reckoned as eye-consciousness. The same method applies to the remaining terms. 'For those associated with it' (taṃsampayuttakānaṃ) means that the base of form is a condition by way of object for the three aggregates associated with that eye-consciousness element, and for all four aggregates based on the eye-sensitivity. The same method applies to what follows. 'For the mind-element' (manodhātuyā) means that the five objects beginning with the base of form are conditions by way of object for the mind-element together with its associated states in its threefold function, but not in a single moment. 'All phenomena' (sabbe dhammā) means that these five objects beginning with the base of form, and all the remaining knowable phenomena—except for these six elements—are conditions by way of object for the mind-consciousness element together with its associated states. 'Depending on whatever phenomenon' (yaṃ yaṃ dhammaṃ ārabbha) indicates that these object-phenomena which have been stated as objects for these seven consciousness-elements, become an object-condition for those elements precisely at the moment of their arising. And even while being so, they do not occur simultaneously; it also indicates that depending on whatever phenomenon, whatever states arise, those phenomena become separate object-conditions for those respective states. 'They arise' (uppajjanti) should be understood as spoken by way of encompassing all time, just as it is said, “rivers flow, mountains stand.” By that, it is established that also those phenomena on which states arose in the past and those on which states will arise in the future, all arose and will arise only by way of object-condition. 'Mental and associated phenomena' (cittacetasikā dhammā) is an example illustrating the nature of what was stated as “whatever phenomena” (ye ye dhammā). 'Those phenomena' (te te dhammā) refers to those object-phenomena. 'For them' (tesaṃ tesaṃ) means for those respective mental and associated phenomena. This, for now, is the explanation of the Pāli.

Idaṃ pana ārammaṇaṃ nāma rūpārammaṇaṃ saddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbadhammārammaṇanti koṭṭhāsato chabbidhaṃ hoti. Tattha ṭhapetvā paññattiṃ avasesaṃ bhūmito [M 0.0359] kāmāvacaraṃ…pe… apariyāpannanti catubbidhaṃ hoti. Tattha kāmāvacaraṃ kusalākusalavipākakiriyarūpabhedato pañcavidhaṃ; rūpāvacaraṃ kusalavipākakiriyato tividhaṃ, tathā arūpāvacaraṃ, apariyāpannaṃ kusalavipākanibbānavasena tividhaṃ hoti. Sabbameva vā etaṃ kusalākusalavipākakiriyarūpanibbānapaññattibhedato sattavidhaṃ hoti. Tattha kusalaṃ bhūmibhedato catubbidhaṃ hoti, akusalaṃ kāmāvacarameva, vipākaṃ catubhūmakaṃ, kiriyaṃ tibhūmakaṃ, rūpaṃ ekabhūmakaṃ kāmāvacarameva, nibbānampi ekabhūmakaṃ apariyāpannameva, paññatti bhūmivinimuttāti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Now, this object is sixfold by way of division: form-object, sound-object, smell-object, taste-object, touch-object, and mental-object. Herein, excepting concepts, the remainder is fourfold in terms of plane: sense-sphere, fine-material sphere, immaterial sphere, and supramundane. Among these, the sense-sphere is fivefold by division into wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, functional, and form. The fine-material sphere is threefold as wholesome, resultant, and functional; similarly the immaterial sphere. The supramundane is threefold as wholesome, resultant, and Nibbāna. Alternatively, all this is sevenfold by division into wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, functional, form, Nibbāna, and concepts. Herein, the wholesome is fourfold by division of planes; the unwholesome is only of the sense-sphere; the resultant is of four planes; the functional is of three planes; form is of one plane, only the sense-sphere; Nibbāna is also of one plane, only the supramundane; concepts are beyond planes. Thus, the analysis here should be understood according to its various kinds of divisions.

Evaṃ [V 0.0358] bhinne panetasmiṃ ārammaṇe kāmāvacarakusalārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacarakusalassa, rūpāvacarakusalassa, akusalassa, kāmāvacaravipākassa, kāmāvacarakiriyassa, rūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarakusalārammaṇaṃ tesu chasu rāsīsu kāmāvacaravipākavajjānaṃ pañcannaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacarakusalārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacarakusalassa, rūpāvacarakusalassa, arūpāvacarakusalassa, akusalassa, arūpāvaracaravipākassa, kāmāvacarakiriyassa, rūpāvacarakiriyassa, arūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Apariyāpannakusalārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarato kusalakiriyānameva ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Akusalārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalassa, akusalassa, kāmāvacaravipākassa, kāmāvacararūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti.

When this object is thus divided, the object of sense-sphere wholesome states is an object-condition for these six groups: sense-sphere wholesome, fine-material-sphere wholesome, unwholesome, sense-sphere resultant, sense-sphere functional, and fine-material-sphere functional. The object of fine-material-sphere wholesome states is an object-condition for five groups among those six, excluding the sense-sphere resultant. The object of immaterial-sphere wholesome states is an object-condition for these eight groups: sense-sphere wholesome, fine-material-sphere wholesome, immaterial-sphere wholesome, unwholesome, immaterial-sphere resultant, sense-sphere functional, fine-material-sphere functional, and immaterial-sphere functional. The object of supramundane wholesome states is an object-condition only for the wholesome and functional states of the sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere. The object of unwholesome states is an object-condition for these six groups: sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere wholesome, unwholesome, sense-sphere resultant, and sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere functional.

Kāmāvacaravipākārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalassa, akusalassa, kāmāvacaravipākassa, kāmāvacararūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacaravipākārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalassa, akusalassa, kāmāvacararūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ pañcannaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacaravipākārammaṇampi imesaṃyeva pañcannaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Apariyāpannavipākārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalakiriyānaññeva ārammaṇapaccayo hoti.

The object of the sense-sphere resultant is an object-condition for these six groups of states: sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere wholesome, unwholesome, sense-sphere resultant, and sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere functional. The object of the fine-material-sphere resultant is an object-condition for these five groups of states: sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere wholesome, unwholesome, and sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere functional. The object of the immaterial-sphere resultant is also an object-condition for these same five groups of states. The object of the supramundane resultant is an object-condition only for sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere wholesome and functional states.

Kāmāvacarakiriyārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalassa, akusalassa, kāmāvacaravipākassa, kāmāvacararūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ [M 0.0360] ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarakiriyārammaṇaṃ imesu chasu rāsīsu kāmāvacaravipākavajjānaṃ pañcannaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacarakiriyārammaṇaṃ tesaṃ pañcannaṃ arūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Catusamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpakkhandhasaṅkhātaṃ rūpārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalassa akusalassa kāmāvacaravipākassa kāmāvacararūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Nibbānārammaṇaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarakusalassa, apariyāpannato kusalavipākassa, kāmāvacararūpāvacarakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarakusalakiriyānaṃ keci nicchanti, taṃ yuttito upadhāretabbaṃ. Nānappakārakaṃ pana [V 0.0359] paññattiārammaṇaṃ tebhūmakakusalassa, akusalassa, rūpāvacaravipākassa, arūpāvacaravipākassa, tebhūmakakiriyassa cāti imesaṃ navannaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇapaccayo hoti. Tattha yaṃ yaṃ ārammaṇaṃ yesaṃ yesaṃ paccayo, te te taṃtaṃpaccayuppannā nāma hontīti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

The object of sense-sphere functional states is an object-condition for these six groups of states: sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere wholesome, unwholesome, sense-sphere resultant, and sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere functional. The object of fine-material-sphere functional states is an object-condition for five of these six groups of states, excluding the sense-sphere resultant. The object of immaterial-sphere functional states is an object-condition for these six groups of states: the aforementioned five and immaterial-sphere functional. Material form, designated as the aggregate of form arising from the four origins, is an object-condition for these six groups of states: sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere wholesome, unwholesome, sense-sphere resultant, and sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere functional. Nibbāna as an object is an object-condition for these six groups of states: sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere wholesome, supramundane wholesome and resultant, and sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere functional. Some maintain that it is also an object for fine-material-sphere wholesome and functional states; this should be examined by reason. A concept-object of various kinds is an object-condition for these nine groups of states: wholesome of the three planes, unwholesome, fine-material-sphere resultant, immaterial-sphere resultant, and functional of the three planes. Herein, whatever object is a condition for whichever states, those states are said to be conditionally arisen from that particular condition. Thus, the determination should also be understood from the standpoint of the conditionally arisen.

Ārammaṇapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Object Condition.

3. Adhipatipaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Dominance Condition

3. Adhipatipaccayaniddese chandādhipatīti chandasaṅkhāto adhipati. Chandaṃ dhuraṃ katvā chandaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā cittuppattikāle uppannassa kattukamyatāchandassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Kasmā pana yathā hetupaccayaniddese hetū hetusampayuttakāna”nti vuttaṃ, evamidha “adhipatī adhipatisampayuttakānanti avatvā “chandādhipati chandasampayuttakāna”ntiādinā nayena desanā katāti? Ekakkhaṇe abhāvato. Purimanayasmiñhi dve tayo hetū ekakkhaṇepi hetupaccayo honti mūlaṭṭhena. Upakārakabhāvassa avijahanato. Adhipati pana jeṭṭhakaṭṭhena upakārako, na ca ekakkhaṇe bahū jeṭṭhakā nāma honti. Tasmā ekato uppannānampi nesaṃ ekakkhaṇe adhipatipaccayabhāvo natthi. Tassa adhipatipaccayabhāvassa ekakkhaṇe abhāvato idha evaṃ desanā katāti.

3. In the exposition of the Dominance Condition, 'desire-dominance' means the dominance reckoned as desire. Making desire the foremost, making desire the chief, this is the name for the desire-to-act that arises at the moment of the arising of consciousness. The same method applies to the rest. But why, just as in the exposition of the Root Condition it was said, 'roots are for the root-associated states,' here it is not said, 'dominance is for the dominance-associated states,' but instead the teaching is given in the manner of 'desire-dominance is for the desire-associated states,' and so on? Because of its non-existence in a single moment. For in the previous method, two or three roots can be a root-condition even in a single moment by way of being a root, since their supportive nature is not abandoned. But dominance is supportive by way of being chief, and there cannot be many chiefs in a single moment. Therefore, even for those that have arisen together, there is no state of being a dominance-condition in a single moment. Because of the non-existence of that state of being a dominance-condition in a single moment, the teaching is given in this way here.

Evaṃ [M 0.0361] sahajātādhipatiṃ dassetvā idāni ārammaṇādhipatiṃ dassetuṃ yaṃ yaṃ dhammaṃ garuṃ katvātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yaṃ yaṃ dhammanti yaṃ yaṃ ārammaṇadhammaṃ. Garuṃ katvāti garukāracittīkāravasena vā assādavasena vā garuṃ bhāriyaṃ laddhabbaṃ avijahitabbaṃ anavaññātaṃ katvā. Te te dhammāti te te garukātabbadhammā. Tesaṃ tesanti tesaṃ tesaṃ garukārakadhammānaṃ. Adhipatipaccayenāti ārammaṇādhipatipaccayena paccayo hotīti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

Having thus shown the conascence-dominance condition, now, in order to show the object-dominance condition, the passage beginning with 'whatever phenomenon one makes weighty' is commenced. Herein, 'whatever phenomenon' means whatever object-phenomenon. 'Makes weighty' means having made it weighty, heavy, to be obtained, not to be abandoned, not to be despised, by way of esteem and respect, or by way of savoring. 'Those phenomena' refers to those phenomena that are to be made weighty. 'Of those' means of those phenomena that make weighty. 'By the Dominance Condition' means it is a condition by way of the object-dominance condition. This, indeed, is the explanation of the Pali text here.

Ayaṃ [V 0.0360] pana adhipati nāma sahajātārammaṇavasena duvidho. Tattha sahajāto chandādivasena catubbidho. Tesu ekeko kāmāvacarādivasena bhūmito catubbidho. Tattha kāmāvacaro kusalākusalakiriyavasena tividho. Akusalaṃ patvā panettha vīmaṃsādhipati na labbhati. Rūpārūpāvacaro kusalakiriyavasena duvidho, apariyāpanno kusalavipākavasena duvidho. Ārammaṇādhipati pana jātibhedato kusalākusalavipākakiriyarūpanibbānānaṃ vasena chabbidhoti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This Adhipati-Condition, however, is twofold by way of conascence and object. Therein, the conascent is fourfold by way of desire, etc. Among these, each is fourfold by way of the planes, such as the sense-sphere, etc. Therein, the sense-sphere Adhipati-Condition is threefold by way of wholesome, unwholesome, and functional. However, with respect to the unwholesome, the dominance of investigation is not found here. The form-sphere and formless-sphere Adhipati-Conditions are twofold by way of wholesome and functional; the unincluded Adhipati-Condition is twofold by way of wholesome and resultant. The object Adhipati-Condition, however, is sixfold by way of the distinction of class: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, functional, form, and Nibbāna. Thus, the ascertainment here should be understood by way of various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha sahajātādhipatimhi tāva kāmāvacarakusalakiriyasaṅkhāto adhipati duhetukatihetukesu cittuppādesu chandādīnaṃ aññataraṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā uppattikāle attanā sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca adhipatipaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarakusalakiriyasaṅkhātepi eseva nayo. Ayaṃ pana ekanteneva labbhati. Na hi te dhammā sahajātādhipatiṃ vinā uppajjanti. Arūpāvacarakusalakiriyasaṅkhāto pana pañcavokāre rūpāvacaraadhipatisadisova catuvokāre pana sampayuttadhammānaññeva adhipatipaccayo hoti. Tathā tatthuppanno sabbopi kāmāvacarādhipati. Apariyāpanno kusalatopi vipākatopi pañcavokāre ekanteneva sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca adhipatipaccayo hoti, catuvokāre arūpadhammānaññeva. Akusalo kāmabhave micchattaniyatacittesu ekanteneva sampayuttakānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca adhipatipaccayo hoti. Aniyato kāmabhavarūpabhavesu [M 0.0362] attano adhipatikāle tesaññeva. Arūpabhave arūpadhammānaññeva adhipatipaccayo hoti. Ayaṃ tāva sahajātādhipatimhi nayo.

Thus, among these distinctions, first, regarding the conascent Adhipati-Condition: the Adhipati-Condition reckoned as wholesome or functional in the sense-sphere, in arisings of consciousness that are two-rooted or three-rooted, by making one of desire, etc., the chief, at the time of its arising, is an Adhipati-Condition for its associated states and for mind-originated matter. The same method applies to that reckoned as wholesome or functional in the form-sphere. This, however, is obtained absolutely, for those states do not arise without a conascent Adhipati-Condition. As for that reckoned as wholesome or functional in the formless-sphere, in the five-aggregate existence it is similar to the form-sphere Adhipati-Condition, but in the four-aggregate existence it is an Adhipati-Condition only for the associated states. The same applies to any sense-sphere Adhipati-Condition arising there. The unincluded, whether wholesome or resultant, in the five-aggregate existence, is absolutely an Adhipati-Condition for its associated states and for mind-originated matter; in the four-aggregate existence, only for immaterial states. The unwholesome, in the sense-sphere existence, in consciousness fixed in wrong view, is absolutely an Adhipati-Condition for its associated states and for mind-originated matter. The indeterminate, in the sense-sphere and form-sphere existences, at the time of its own dominance, is a condition for those same states. In the formless existence, it is an Adhipati-Condition only for immaterial states. This, then, is the method regarding the conascent Adhipati-Condition.

Ārammaṇādhipatimhi pana kāmāvacarakusalo ārammaṇādhipati kāmāvacarakusalassa lobhasahagatākusalassāti imesaṃ dvinnaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇādhipatipaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarārūpāvacarepi kusalārammaṇādhipatimhi eseva nayo. Apariyāpannakusalo pana ārammaṇādhipati kāmāvacarato ñāṇasampayuttakusalassa ceva ñāṇasampayuttakiriyassa ca ārammaṇādhipatipaccayo hoti. Akusalo pana ārammaṇādhipati nāma lobhasahagatacittuppādo vuccati. So lobhasahagatākusalasseva ārammaṇādhipatipaccayo hoti. Kāmāvacaro pana vipākārammaṇādhipati lobhasahagatākusalasseva ārammaṇādhipatipaccayo hoti. Tathā rūpāvacarārūpāvacaravipākārammaṇādhipati. Lokuttaro pana vipākārammaṇādhipati kāmāvacarato ñāṇasampayuttakusalakiriyānaññeva [V 0.0361] ārammaṇādhipatipaccayo hoti. Kāmāvacarādibhedato pana tividhopi kiriyārammaṇādhipati lobhasahagatākusalasseva ārammaṇādhipatipaccayo hoti. Catusamuṭṭhānikarūpasaṅkhāto rūpakkhandho ārammaṇādhipati lobhasahagatākusalasseva ārammaṇādhipatipaccayo hoti. Nibbānaṃ kāmāvacarato ñāṇasampayuttakusalassa ñāṇasampayuttakiriyassa lokuttarakusalassa lokuttaravipākassa cāti imesaṃ catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ ārammaṇādhipatipaccayo hotīti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Regarding the object Adhipati-Condition, however: the sense-sphere wholesome as object Adhipati-Condition is an object Adhipati-Condition for these two groups: sense-sphere wholesome consciousness and unwholesome consciousness accompanied by greed. The same method applies to the wholesome object Adhipati-Condition in the form-sphere and formless-sphere. But the unincluded wholesome as object Adhipati-Condition is an object Adhipati-Condition for sense-sphere knowledge-associated wholesome consciousness and knowledge-associated functional consciousness. The unwholesome as object Adhipati-Condition, however, is called an arising of consciousness accompanied by greed. It is an object Adhipati-Condition only for unwholesome consciousness accompanied by greed. But the sense-sphere resultant as object Adhipati-Condition is an object Adhipati-Condition only for unwholesome consciousness accompanied by greed. Similarly for the resultant object Adhipati-Condition in the form-sphere and formless-sphere. The supramundane resultant as object Adhipati-Condition, however, is an object Adhipati-Condition only for sense-sphere knowledge-associated wholesome and functional consciousness. But the functional as object Adhipati-Condition, of all three kinds distinguished by sense-sphere, etc., is an object Adhipati-Condition only for unwholesome consciousness accompanied by greed. The aggregate of form, reckoned as arisen from four causes, as object Adhipati-Condition, is an object Adhipati-Condition only for unwholesome consciousness accompanied by greed. Nibbāna, as object Adhipati-Condition, is an object Adhipati-Condition for these four groups: sense-sphere knowledge-associated wholesome consciousness, knowledge-associated functional consciousness, supramundane wholesome consciousness, and supramundane resultant consciousness. Thus, the ascertainment here should be understood also from the perspective of the conditioned states.

Adhipatipaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Dominance Condition.

4. Anantarapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Contiguity Condition.

4. Anantarapaccayaniddese manodhātuyāti vipākamanodhātuyā. Manoviññāṇadhātuyāti santīraṇakiccāya ahetukavipākamanoviññāṇadhātuyā. Tato paraṃ pana voṭṭhabbanajavanatadārammaṇabhavaṅgakiccā manoviññāṇadhātuyo [M 0.0363] vattabbā siyuṃ, tā avuttāpi imināva nayena veditabbāti nayaṃ dassetvā desanā saṅkhittā. “Purimā purimā kusalā dhammā”tiādike ca chaṭṭhanaye tā saṅgahitātipi idha na vuttāti veditabbā. Tattha purimā purimāti chasu dvāresupi anantarātītā kusalajavanadhammā daṭṭhabbā. Pacchimānaṃ pacchimānanti anantarauppajjamānānaññeva. Kusalānanti sadisakusalānaṃ. Abyākatānanti idaṃ pana kusalānantaraṃ tadārammaṇabhavaṅgaphalasamāpattivasena vuttaṃ. Akusalamūlake abyākatānanti tadārammaṇabhavaṅgasaṅkhātānaññeva. Abyākatamūlake abyākatānanti āvajjanajavanavasena vā bhavaṅgavasena vā pavattānaṃ kiriyavipākābyākatānaṃ kiriyamanodhātuto paṭṭhāya pana yāva voṭṭhabbanakiccā manoviññāṇadhātu, tāva pavattesu vīthicittesupi ayaṃ nayo labbhateva. Kusalānanti pañcadvāre voṭṭhabbanānantarānaṃ manodvāre āvajjanāntarānaṃ paṭhamajavanakusalānaṃ. Akusalānanti padepi eseva nayo. Yesaṃ yesanti idaṃ sabbesampi anantarapaccayadhammānaṃ. Saṅkhepalakkhaṇanti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

4. In the exposition of the Contiguity Condition, 'mind-element' refers to the resultant mind-element. 'Mind-consciousness-element' refers to the rootless resultant mind-consciousness-element that performs the function of investigating. Beyond that, however, the mind-consciousness-elements that perform the functions of determining, impulsion, registration, and life-continuum should be mentioned. Though not stated, they are to be understood by this same method; the teaching is concise because the method has been shown. It should be understood that they are not mentioned here because they are included in the sixth method, in such phrases as 'preceding, preceding wholesome states.' Therein, 'preceding, preceding' should be understood as the immediately past wholesome impulsion-states in the six doors. 'Of subsequent, subsequent' refers only to those arising immediately after. 'Of wholesome states' refers to similar wholesome states. 'Of undeclared states,' however, is stated with reference to registration, life-continuum, and fruition attainment that immediately follow a wholesome state. 'Of undeclared states rooted in unwholesome' refers only to those reckoned as registration and life-continuum. 'Of undeclared states rooted in undeclared' refers to functional and resultant undeclared states that occur either by way of adverting and impulsion or by way of life-continuum. Starting from the functional mind-element up to the mind-consciousness-element with the function of determining, this method is indeed found even in the cognitive processes that have occurred. 'Of wholesome states' refers to the first wholesome impulsions immediately after determining in the five doors and after adverting in the mind door. In the phrase 'of unwholesome states,' the method is the same. 'Of whichever states' applies to all states that are a contiguity condition. This is the characteristic in brief. So far, this is the commentary on the Pāli text.

Ayaṃ [V 0.0362] pana anantarapaccayo nāma ṭhapetvā nibbānaṃ catubhūmako arūpadhammarāsiyevāti veditabbo. So jātivasena kusalākusalavipākakiriyato catudhā bhijjati. Tattha kusalo kāmāvacarādibhedato catubbidho hoti, akusalo kāmāvacarova vipāko catubhūmako, kiriyānantarapaccayo pana te bhūmakoti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This Condition of Contiguity, however, should be understood as the aggregate of immaterial states belonging to the four planes, excluding Nibbāna. It is divided into four kinds according to its nature: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional. Herein, the wholesome is fourfold, by way of the sense-sphere and so forth. The unwholesome is only of the sense-sphere. The resultant is of the four planes. As for the functional Condition of Contiguity, however, it is of the three planes. Thus, the determination here should be understood by way of various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha kāmāvacarakusalo attanā sadisasseva kāmāvacarakusalassa anantarapaccayo hoti. Ñāṇasampayuttakāmāvacarakusalo pana rūpāvacarakusalassa arūpāvacarakusalassa lokuttarakusalassāti imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Kāmāvacarakusalo ca kāmāvacaravipākassa, rūpāvacarārūpāvacaravipākassa, ñāṇasampayutto lokuttaravipākassāpīti imesaṃ catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarakusalo rūpāvacarakusalassa, ñāṇasampayuttakāmāvacaravipākassa, rūpāvacaravipākassāti imesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacarakusalo tesaṃ dvinnaṃ vipākānaṃ attano [M 0.0364] kusalassa vipākassa cāti avisesena catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Visesena panettha nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakusalo anāgāmiphalasaṅkhātassa lokuttaravipākassapi anantarapaccayo hoti. Lokuttarakusalo lokuttaravipākasseva anantarapaccayo hoti. Akusalo avisesena akusalassa ceva kusalākusalavipākassa ca. Visesena panettha sukhamajjhattavedanāsampayutto akusalo rūpāvacarārūpāvacaravipākassāpīti imesaṃ catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti.

Here, when thus distinguished, sense-sphere wholesome consciousness becomes the Condition of Contiguity for similar sense-sphere wholesome consciousness. Sense-sphere wholesome consciousness associated with knowledge, however, becomes the Condition of Contiguity for these three groups: form-sphere wholesome consciousness, formless-sphere wholesome consciousness, and supramundane wholesome consciousness. Sense-sphere wholesome consciousness becomes the Condition of Contiguity for these four groups: sense-sphere resultant consciousness, form-sphere and formless-sphere resultant consciousness, and—when it is associated with knowledge—also for supramundane resultant consciousness. Form-sphere wholesome consciousness becomes the Condition of Contiguity for these three groups: form-sphere wholesome consciousness, sense-sphere resultant consciousness associated with knowledge, and form-sphere resultant consciousness. Formless-sphere wholesome consciousness becomes, without distinction, the Condition of Contiguity for four groups: those two resultant consciousnesses, its own wholesome consciousness, and its own resultant consciousness. Specifically here, wholesome consciousness in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception also becomes the Condition of Contiguity for supramundane resultant consciousness consisting of the fruit of non-returner. Supramundane wholesome consciousness becomes the Condition of Contiguity only for supramundane resultant consciousness. Unwholesome consciousness, without distinction, becomes the Condition of Contiguity for unwholesome consciousness and for the resultant of wholesome and unwholesome consciousness. Specifically here, unwholesome consciousness associated with pleasant or neutral feeling also becomes the Condition of Contiguity for these four groups, including form-sphere and formless-sphere resultant consciousness.

Kāmāvacaravipākassa ñāṇasampayutto vā ñāṇavippayutto vā vipāko kāmāvacarakiriyāvajjanassa, ñāṇasampayuttavipāko panettha paṭisandhivasena uppajjamānassa rūpāvacarārūpāvacaravipākassāpīti imesaṃ catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacaravipāko sahetukakāmāvacaravipākassa rūpāvacarārūpāvacaravipākassa kāmāvacarakiriyāvajjanassāti imesaṃ catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacaravipāko tihetukakāmāvacaravipākassa arūpāvacaravipākassa kāmāvacarakiriyāvajjanassāti tiṇṇaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Lokuttaravipāko tihetukakāmāvacaravipākassa rūpāvacarārūpāvacaralokuttaravipākassāti catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti.

Sense-sphere resultant consciousness, whether associated with knowledge or dissociated from knowledge, is the Condition of Contiguity for sense-sphere functional adverting. Here, resultant consciousness that is associated with knowledge is also the Condition of Contiguity for form-sphere and formless-sphere resultant consciousness arising by way of rebirth-linking. Thus, it is the Condition of Contiguity for these four groups. Form-sphere resultant consciousness is the Condition of Contiguity for four groups: sense-sphere resultant consciousness with roots, form-sphere and formless-sphere resultant consciousness, and sense-sphere functional adverting. Formless-sphere resultant consciousness is the Condition of Contiguity for three groups: sense-sphere resultant consciousness with three roots, formless-sphere resultant consciousness, and sense-sphere functional adverting. Supramundane resultant consciousness is the Condition of Contiguity for four groups: sense-sphere resultant consciousness with three roots, form-sphere, formless-sphere, and supramundane resultant consciousness.

Kāmāvacarakiriyaṃ kāmāvacarakusalākusalassa catubhūmakavipākassa tebhūmakakiriyassāti navannaṃ [V 0.0363] rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarakiriyaṃ tihetukakāmāvacaravipākassa rūpāvacaravipākassa rūpāvacarakiriyassāti tiṇṇaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacarakiriyaṃ tihetukakāmāvacaravipākassa rūpāvacarārūpāvacaralokuttaravipākassa arūpāvacarakiriyassāti pañcannaṃ rāsīnaṃ anantarapaccayo hotīti. Evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Sense-sphere functional consciousness is the Condition of Contiguity for nine groups: sense-sphere wholesome and unwholesome consciousness, resultant consciousness of the four planes, and functional consciousness of the three planes. Form-sphere functional consciousness is the Condition of Contiguity for three groups: sense-sphere resultant consciousness with three roots, form-sphere resultant consciousness, and form-sphere functional consciousness. Formless-sphere functional consciousness is the Condition of Contiguity for five groups: sense-sphere resultant consciousness with three roots, form-sphere, formless-sphere, and supramundane resultant consciousness, and formless-sphere functional consciousness. Thus, the determination here should be understood also from the perspective of the conditioned.

Anantarapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Exposition of the Contiguity Condition.

5. Samanantarapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Exposition of the Proximity Condition

5. Samanantarapaccayaniddesopi [M 0.0365] iminā samānagatikova. Ime pana dve paccayā mahāvitthārā, tasmā sabbacittuppattivasena tesaṃ upaparikkhitvā vitthāro gahetabboti.

5. The exposition of the proximity condition is also of a similar nature to this. However, these two conditions are very extensive; therefore, their extensive details should be examined and grasped in relation to all instances of the arising of consciousness.

Samanantarapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Exposition of the Proximity Condition.

6. Sahajātapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Exposition of the Co-nascence Condition

6. Sahajātapaccayaniddese aññamaññanti añño aññassa. Iminā etesaṃ dhammānaṃ ekakkhaṇe paccayabhāvañceva paccayuppannabhāvañca dīpeti. Okkantikkhaṇeti pañcavokārabhave paṭisandhikkhaṇe. Tasmiñhi khaṇe nāmarūpaṃ okkantaṃ viya pakkhandantaṃ viya paralokato imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā pavisantaṃ viya uppajjati, tasmā so khaṇo “okkantikkhaṇo”ti vuccati. Ettha ca rūpanti hadayavatthumattameva adhippetaṃ. Tañhi nāmassa, nāmañca tassa aññamaññaṃ sahajātapaccayaṭṭhaṃ pharati. Cittacetasikāti pavattiyaṃ cattāro khandhā. Sahajātapaccayenāti ettha cittasamuṭṭhānarūpā cittacetasikānaṃ paccayaṭṭhaṃ na pharanti, tasmā “aññamañña”nti [V 0.0364] na vuttaṃ. Tathā upādārūpā bhūtānaṃ. Rūpino dhammā arūpīnaṃ dhammānanti hadayavatthu catunnaṃ khandhānaṃ. Kiñci kāleti kismiñci kāle. Sahajātapaccayenāti paṭisandhiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Na sahajātapaccayenāti pavattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

6. In the exposition of the co-nascence condition, "each other" means one to another. By this, it shows both the state of being a condition and the state of being conditionally arisen for these phenomena in a single moment. "The moment of descent" refers to the moment of rebirth-linking in the five-aggregate existence. At that moment, name-and-form arises as if descending, as if plunging, or as if coming from another world to enter this world. Therefore, that moment is called "the moment of descent." Here, "material form" refers only to the heart-base. That indeed is for name, and name for that; they function as a co-nascence condition for each other. "Mind and mental factors" refers to the four aggregates during the course of existence. Regarding the co-nascence condition, here mind-originated material forms do not function as a condition for mind and mental factors; hence "each other" is not stated. Similarly, derived material forms do not function as a condition for the primary elements. "Material phenomena for immaterial phenomena" means the heart-base for the four aggregates. "At some time" means at any time. "By the co-nascence condition" is stated with reference to rebirth-linking. "Not by the co-nascence condition" is stated with reference to the course of existence.

Ayaṃ pana ‘cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo’ti evaṃ chahi koṭṭhāsehi ṭhito. Tattha tayo koṭṭhāsā aññamaññavasena vuttā, tayo na aññamaññavasena. Tattha paṭhamakoṭṭhāse arūpameva paccayo ceva paccayuppannañca, dutiye rūpameva, tatiye nāmarūpaṃ, catutthe paccayo arūpaṃ, paccayuppannaṃ rūpaṃ; pañcame paccayopi paccayuppannampi rūpameva; chaṭṭhe paccayo rūpaṃ, paccayuppannaṃ arūpanti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

Moreover, this (relation) is established in six sections as follows: 'The four immaterial aggregates are a condition for one another by way of co-nascence condition.' Herein, three sections are stated in terms of mutuality, and three are not in terms of mutuality. In the first section, both the condition and the conditionally arisen are immaterial. In the second, both are material. In the third, both are name-and-form. In the fourth, the condition is immaterial, and the conditionally arisen is material. In the fifth, both the condition and the conditionally arisen are material. In the sixth, the condition is material, and the conditionally arisen is immaterial. This, indeed, is the explanation of the Pāli text here.

Ayaṃ pana sahajātapaccayo jātivasena kusalo akusalo vipāko kiriyaṃ rūpanti pañcadhā bhijjati. Tattha kusalo bhūmito catubbidho [M 0.0366] hoti, akusalo ekavidhova vipāko catubbidho, kiriyasaṅkhāto tividho, rūpaṃ ekavidhaṃ kāmāvacaramevāti evaṃ tāvettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This co-nascence condition, by way of its nature, is divided into five types: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, functional, and material. Herein, the wholesome is fourfold according to the planes; the unwholesome is only onefold; the resultant is fourfold; that which is termed functional is threefold; and the material is onefold, belonging only to the sense-sphere. Thus, the determination here should be understood according to these various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha catubhūmakampi kusalaṃ pañcavokārabhave attanā sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca sahajātapaccayo hoti, tathā akusalaṃ. Yaṃ panettha arūpe uppajjati, taṃ arūpadhammānaṃyeva sahajātapaccayo hoti.

Among these divisions, the wholesome of the four planes, in the five-aggregate existence, is a co-nascence condition for its associated states and for mind-originated material form. Similarly, the unwholesome. But whatever arises herein in the formless existence, that is a co-nascence condition only for the formless states.

Kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipākaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ceva sampayuttadhammānañca sahajātapaccayo hoti. Yaṃ panettha rūpaṃ na samuṭṭhāpeti, taṃ sampayuttadhammānaññeva. Yaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ uppajjati, taṃ kaṭattārūpānañcāpi sahajātapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacaravipākaṃ sampayuttadhammānaññeva. Lokuttaravipākaṃ pañcavokāre sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca, catuvokāre arūpānaññeva. Kāmāvacaraarūpāvacarakiriyā pañcavokāre sampayuttakānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca sahajātapaccayo hoti, catuvokāre arūpānaññeva. Rūpāvacarakiriyā sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca ekantena sahajātapaccayo hoti.

Sense-sphere and fine-material-sphere resultant consciousness is a co-nascence condition for mind-originated material form and its associated states. That (resultant consciousness) which herein does not originate material form, is a condition only for the associated states.
