That which arises at rebirth-linking is also a co-nascence condition for kamma-produced material forms. Formless-sphere resultant consciousness is a condition only for the associated states. Supramundane resultant consciousness, in the five-aggregate existence, is a condition for the associated states and mind-originated material forms, while in the four-aggregate existence, it is a condition only for the immaterial states. Sense-sphere and formless-sphere functional consciousness, in the five-aggregate existence, is a co-nascence condition for the associated states and mind-originated material forms, while in the four-aggregate existence, it is a condition only for the immaterial states. Fine-material-sphere functional consciousness is invariably a co-nascence condition for the associated states and mind-originated material forms.

Catusamuṭṭhānikassa [V 0.0365] rūpassa kammasamuṭṭhānarūpe ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇaṃ, tīṇi ekassa, dve dvinnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ, mahābhūtā upādārūpassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Kāmāvacararūpāvacarapaṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthurūpaṃ vipākakkhandhānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Utucittāhārasamuṭṭhānesu pana mahābhūtāni aññamaññañceva upādārūpassa ca sahajātapaccayena paccayoti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Of material phenomena with fourfold origination, in the case of kamma-produced material phenomena, one great element is a condition for three, three for one, and two for two great elements; the great elements are a condition for derived material phenomena by way of co-nascence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking in the sense-sphere and the fine-material sphere, the physical basis is a condition for the resultant aggregates by way of co-nascence condition. However, in the cases of those originated by temperature, consciousness, and nutriment, the great elements are a condition for one another and for derived material phenomena by way of co-nascence condition. Thus, the determination herein should also be understood from the side of the conditionally arisen.

Sahajātapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Co-nascence Condition.

7. Aññamaññapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Mutuality Condition.

7. Aññamaññapaccayaniddese sahajātapaccayaniddesassa purimānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ koṭṭhāsānaṃ vasena pāḷi āgatā. Tassā tattha vuttasadisāva vaṇṇanāti puna na gahitā. Ayampi ca aññamaññapaccayo jātivasena kusalo akusalo vipāko kiriyaṃ rūpanti pañcadhā bhinno. Tattha kusalo bhūmito [M 0.0367] catubbidho. Sabbaṃ purimasadisamevāti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

7. In the exposition of the mutuality condition, the Pāli text is given by way of the first three sections of the exposition of the co-nascence condition. Its commentary is similar to what was stated there, thus it is not taken up again. This mutuality condition is also divided into five kinds by way of its nature: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, functional, and material. Herein, the wholesome is fourfold by way of plane. All is just as in the preceding. Thus, the determination herein should be understood by way of the various kinds of distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha sabbampi catubhūmakaṃ kusalaṃ attanā sampayuttadhammānaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Tathā akusalaṃ. Vipāke pana kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipākaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ vatthurūpassa, pavatte sampayuttadhammānaññeva. Arūpāvacaralokuttaravipākaṃ attanā sampayuttadhammānaññeva aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Sabbampi kiriyaṃ sampayuttadhammānaññeva aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Catusamuṭṭhānikarūpassa kammasamuṭṭhāne ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇaṃ, tīṇi ekassa, dve dvinnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Kāmāvacararūpāvacarapaṭisandhiyaṃ vatthurūpaṃ vipākakkhandhānaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Utucittāhārasamuṭṭhānesu mahābhūtāneva mahābhūtānaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayoti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Among these divisions, all wholesome states of the four planes are a condition for their associated phenomena by way of the mutuality condition. Similarly, the unwholesome. As for resultant states, the resultant of the sense-sphere and fine-material sphere is a condition for the physical basis at rebirth-linking, and in the course of existence, for its associated phenomena only. The resultant of the formless sphere and the supramundane is a condition for its associated phenomena only by way of the mutuality condition. All functional states are a condition for their associated phenomena only by way of the mutuality condition. Of material phenomena with fourfold origination, in the case of the kamma-produced, one great element is a condition for the three others, three for one, and two for two great elements by way of the mutuality condition. At rebirth-linking in the sense-sphere and fine-material sphere, the physical basis is a condition for the resultant aggregates by way of the mutuality condition. In the cases of those originated by temperature, consciousness, and nutriment, the great elements are a condition for the other great elements by way of the mutuality condition. Thus, the determination herein should also be understood from the side of the conditionally arisen.

Aññamaññapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Mutuality Condition.

8. Nissayapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

8. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Dependence Condition.

8. Nissayapaccayaniddese [V 0.0366] sahajātapaccayaniddesassa purimānaṃ pañcannaṃ koṭṭhāsānaṃ vasena sahajātanissayanayaṃ dassetvā puna chaṭṭhena koṭṭhāsena purejātanissayanayaṃ dassetuṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāyāti vatthurūpaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tañhi nissāya tividhā manodhātu, ṭhapetvā arūpavipākaṃ dvāsattatividhā manoviññāṇadhātūti imāni pañcasattati cittāni vattantīti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā. Ayampi nissayapaccayo jātivasena kusalādibhedato pañcadhāva bhijjati. Tattha kusalo bhūmito catubbidhova akusalo ekavidho vipāko catubbidho, kiriyasaṅkhāto tividho, rūpaṃ ekavidhamevāti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

8. In the exposition of the dependence condition, having shown the co-nascent dependence method by way of the first five sections of the exposition of the co-nascence condition, then with the sixth section, to show the pre-nascent dependence method, the passage beginning, 'the eye-base for the eye-consciousness element,' and so on, is commenced. Herein, the phrase 'depending on which material form' is stated in reference to the physical basis. For, depending on that, the three kinds of mind-element and—excluding the formless resultant—the seventy-two kinds of mind-consciousness element, thus these seventy-five consciousnesses, occur. This, for a start, is the explanation of the Pāli text here. This dependence condition is also divided into five kinds by way of its nature, with the distinctions of wholesome, etc. Herein, the wholesome is fourfold by way of plane; the unwholesome is onefold; the resultant is fourfold; that which is termed functional is threefold; and the material is simply onefold. Thus, the determination herein should be understood by way of the various kinds of distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha catubhūmakampi kusalaṃ pañcavokāre sampayuttakkhandhānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca nissayapaccayena paccayo hoti. Tathā akusalaṃ[M 0.0368]. Yaṃ panettha āruppe uppajjati, taṃ arūpadhammānaññeva nissayapaccayo hoti. Kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipākaṃ pavatte sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattārūpassāpi nissayapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacaravipākaṃ sampayuttakkhandhānaṃyeva hoti. Lokuttaravipākaṃ pañcavokāre; sampayuttakānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, catuvokāre arūpasseva nissayapaccayo hoti. Kāmāvacaraarūpāvacarakiriyā pañcavokāre sampayuttakānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca nissayapaccayo hoti, catuvokāre arūpānaññeva. Rūpāvacarakiriyā sampayuttakānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca ekantena nissayapaccayo hoti.

Although thus divided, all wholesome states of the four planes are a dependence condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena in the five-aggregate existence. Similarly, the unwholesome. Whatever arises in the formless plane here becomes a dependence condition only for formless phenomena. As for resultant states, the resultant states of the sense-sphere and fine-material sphere are a dependence condition for their associated phenomena and for mind-originated material phenomena in the course of existence, and also for kamma-originated material phenomena at rebirth. The resultant states of the formless sphere are a dependence condition only for their associated aggregates. Supramundane resultant states are a dependence condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena in the five-aggregate existence; in the four-aggregate existence, for formless phenomena only. Functional states of the sense-sphere and formless-sphere are a dependence condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena in the five-aggregate existence; in the four-aggregate existence, only for formless phenomena. Functional states of the fine-material sphere are exclusively a dependence condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena.

Catusamuṭṭhānikarūpassa ca kammasamuṭṭhānarūpe ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇaṃ, tīṇi ekassa, dve dvinnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ, mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ, vatthurūpaṃ pañcavokārabhave catubhūmakakusalassa, akusalassa, ṭhapetvā āruppavipākañceva dve pañcaviññāṇāni ca sesatebhūmakavipākassa, tebhūmakakiriyassāti imesaṃ catunnaṃ dhammarāsīnaṃ nissayapaccayo hoti. Cakkhāyatanādīni pañca sasampayuttānaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ nissayapaccayo hoti. Utucittāhārasamuṭṭhānesu pana mahābhūtā mahābhūtānañceva upādārūpassa ca nissayapaccayena paccayoti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Of the four-originated material phenomena, in the kamma-originated material phenomena, one great element is a dependence condition for the three others, three for one, and two for two great elements; the great elements are a dependence condition for the derived material phenomena. The physical basis is a dependence condition in the five-aggregate existence for wholesome states of the four planes, for unwholesome states, and—excluding the formless resultant and the two sets of five consciousnesses—for the remaining resultant states of the three planes, and for the functional states of the three planes—thus for these four groups of phenomena. The eye-base and the other four bases are a dependence condition for their associated eye-consciousness and the others. But in the cases of temperature-, consciousness-, and nutriment-originated material phenomena, the great elements are a dependence condition for the great elements and for the derived material phenomena by way of the dependence condition. Thus, here the determination should be understood also from the conditionally arisen phenomena.

Nissayapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Dependence Condition.

9. Upanissayapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Decisive Support Condition.

9. Upanissayapaccayaniddese [V 0.0367] purimā purimāti anantarūpanissaye samanantarātītā labbhanti, ārammaṇūpanissayapakatūpanissayesu nānāvīthivasena purimatarā. Te tayopi rāsayo kusalavasena kusalapade labbhanti, kusalena pana akusale samanantarātītā na labbhanti. Teneva vuttaṃ – “akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ kesañci upanissayapaccayena paccayo”ti[M 0.0369]. Idañhi – “kusalo dhammo akusalassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo; ārammaṇūpanissayo pakatūpanissayo. Ārammaṇūpanissayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati diṭṭhi uppajjati. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgaṃ paññaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Saddhā sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgo paññā rāgassa dosassa mohassa mānassa diṭṭhiyā patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo”ti imaṃ nayaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kusalena abyākate tayopi labbhanti, tathā akusalena akusale.

9. In the exposition of the decisive support condition, in contiguous decisive support, the 'earlier and earlier' states are those that are immediately past; in object decisive support and natural decisive support, they are even earlier states arising by way of various thought-processes. Those three kinds are obtained in the wholesome category by way of wholesome states, but through a wholesome state, an unwholesome state is not obtained as immediately past. Therefore, it is said: "For some unwholesome states, there is a condition by way of decisive support." This is said with reference to the method: "A wholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support and natural decisive support. Object decisive support: having given a gift, having undertaken morality, having performed the Uposatha observance, one savors and delights in that, and regarding that as important, lust arises, wrong view arises; having savored and delighted in previously well-performed deeds, and regarding them as important, lust arises, wrong view arises. Having emerged from jhāna, one savors and delights in the jhāna, and regarding it as important, lust arises, wrong view arises. Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one cherishes pride, takes up wrong view; relying on morality, learning, generosity, or wisdom, one cherishes pride, takes up wrong view. Faith, morality, learning, generosity, and wisdom are conditions for lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, and aspiration by way of decisive support condition." Through the wholesome, all three are obtained in the indeterminate category; likewise, through the unwholesome, they are obtained in the unwholesome category.

Akusalena pana kusale samanantarātītā na labbhanti. Tena vuttaṃ – “kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ kesañci upanissayapaccayena paccayo”ti. Idampi hi – “akusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pakatūpanissayo – rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti, jhānaṃ uppādeti vipassanaṃ uppādeti, maggaṃ uppādeti, abhiññaṃ uppādeti, samāpattiṃ uppādeti; dosaṃ mohaṃ mānaṃ diṭṭhiṃ patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Rāgo doso moho māno diṭṭhi patthanā saddhāya sīlassa sutassa cāgassa paññāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pāṇaṃ hantvā tassa paṭighātatthāya dānaṃ detī”tiādinā nayena pañhāvāre āgataṃ pakatūpanissayameva sandhāya vuttaṃ. Akusalaṃ pana kusalassa ārammaṇūpanissayo na hoti. Kasmā? Taṃ garuṃ katvā tassa appavattanatoti yathā anantarūpanissayo, evaṃ ārammaṇūpanissayopettha na labbhatīti veditabbo. Akusalena abyākatapade ārammaṇūpanissayova na labbhati. Na hi abyākatā dhammā akusalaṃ garuṃ karonti[V 0.0368]. Yasmā pana anantaratā labbhati, tasmā ettha “kesañcī”ti na vuttaṃ. Abyākatena pana abyākate kusale akusaleti tīsu nayesu tayopi upanissayā labbhanteva. Puggalopi senāsanampīti idaṃ dvayaṃ pakatūpanissayavasena vuttaṃ. Idañhi dvayaṃ kusalākusalapavattiyā balavapaccayo hoti. Paccayabhāvo [M 0.0370] cassa panettha pariyāyavasena veditabboti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

However, an unwholesome state is not obtained as an immediately past condition for a wholesome state. Therefore, it is said: "For some wholesome states, there is a condition by way of decisive support." This too is said with reference to the method: "An unwholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of decisive support condition. Natural decisive support: relying on lust, one gives a gift, undertakes morality, performs the Uposatha observance, produces jhāna, produces insight, produces the path, produces higher knowledge, produces meditative absorption; relying on hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, or aspiration, one gives a gift… produces meditative absorption. Lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, and aspiration are conditions for faith, morality, learning, generosity, and wisdom by way of decisive support condition. Having killed a living being, one gives a gift for its counteraction," and so on. This is said in the question section with reference to natural decisive support alone. But an unwholesome state is not an object decisive support for a wholesome state. Why? Because a wholesome state does not arise by regarding an unwholesome one as important; just as contiguous decisive support, so too object decisive support is not obtained here, it should be understood. In the indeterminate category, by way of an unwholesome state, object decisive support is not obtained. For indeterminate states do not regard an unwholesome state as weighty. However, since contiguity is obtained, therefore "for some" is not said here. But by way of the indeterminate, in the indeterminate, wholesome, and unwholesome categories, all three types of decisive support are indeed obtained. "A person and a dwelling"—these two are said by way of natural decisive support. For these two are strong conditions for the occurrence of wholesome and unwholesome states. Here, their role as conditions should be understood indirectly. This, then, is the commentary on the Pāli text here.

Ayaṃ pana upanissayapaccayo nāma saddhiṃ ekaccāya paññattiyā sabbepi catubhūmakadhammā. Vibhāgato pana ārammaṇūpanissayādivasena tividho hoti. Tattha ārammaṇūpanissayo ārammaṇādhipatinā ninnānākaraṇoti heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva nānappakārabhedato gahetabbo. Anantarūpanissayo anantarapaccayena ninnānākaraṇo, sopi heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva nānappakārabhedato veditabbo. Paccayuppannatopi nesaṃ tattha vuttanayeneva vinicchayo veditabbo. Pakatūpanissayo pana jātivasena kusalākusalavipākakiriyarūpabhedato pañcavidho hoti, kusalādīnaṃ pana bhūmibhedato anekavidhoti evaṃ tāvettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This decisive support condition, together with certain concepts, comprises all phenomena of the four planes. However, when analyzed, it is of three kinds: by way of object decisive support, and so on. Herein, object decisive support is not different from the object-dominance condition, and thus should be understood as having various distinctions according to the method previously stated. Contiguous decisive support is not different from the contiguous condition, and it too should be understood as having various distinctions according to the method previously stated. The determination of their conditioned states should also be understood in the manner stated there. Natural decisive support, however, is fivefold by way of type: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, functional, and material. Moreover, the wholesome, etc., are of many kinds due to differences in planes. Thus, the determination here should be understood as having various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha tebhūmakakusalo catubhūmakassāpi kusalassa akusalassa vipākakiriyassāti catunnaṃ rāsīnaṃ pakatūpanissayo hoti. Lokuttaro akusalasseva na hoti. Amhākaṃ ācariyena “lokuttaradhammo nibbattito”ti iminā pana nayena aññesaṃ akusalassāpi hoti. Yassa vā uppajjissati, tassāpi anuttaresu vimokkhesu pihaṃ upaṭṭhāpayato iminā nayena hotiyeva. Akusalo sabbesampi catubhūmakānaṃ khandhānaṃ pakatūpanissayo hoti, tathā tebhūmakavipāko. Lokuttaravipāke heṭṭhimāni tīṇi phalāni akusalasseva na honti, upariṭṭhimaṃ kusalassāpi. Purimanayena pana aññesaṃ vā yassa vā uppajjissati, tassa santāne sabbopi lokuttaravipāko sabbesaṃ kusalādīnaṃ arūpakkhandhānaṃ pakatūpanissayo hoti. Kiriyasaṅkhātopi pakatūpanissayo catubhūmakānaṃ akusalādikhandhānaṃ hotiyeva, tathā rūpasaṅkhāto. Sayaṃ pana rūpaṃ imasmiṃ paṭṭhānamahāpakaraṇe āgatanayena upanissayapaccayaṃ na labhati, suttantikapariyāyena pana labhatīti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Thus, when distinguished here, the wholesome of the three planes is a natural decisive support for the four kinds—wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional—of the four planes. The supramundane is not a natural decisive support for the unwholesome alone. But according to our teacher's saying, 'the supramundane dhamma is produced,' by this method it is also a natural decisive support for the unwholesome for others. Or for one in whom it will arise, by establishing longing for the unsurpassed liberations, it certainly is a natural decisive support in this way. The unwholesome is a natural decisive support for all aggregates of the four planes, as is the resultant of the three planes. In the supramundane resultant, the lower three fruits are not a natural decisive support for the unwholesome alone, while the highest is for the wholesome as well. But according to the previous method, for others or for one in whom it will arise, all supramundane resultants in their continuum are a natural decisive support for all of the immaterial aggregates of the wholesome, etc. The functional, so designated, is certainly a natural decisive support for the aggregates of the unwholesome, etc., of the four planes, as is materiality, so designated. However, materiality itself, in this great treatise on the Paṭṭhāna, does not obtain the decisive support condition according to the method that has come down here, but it is fitting to say that it obtains it according to the Suttanta method. Thus, the determination here should also be understood in terms of conditioned states.

Upanissayapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Decisive Support Condition.

10. Purejātapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Pre-arisen Condition.

10. Purejātapaccayaniddese [M 0.0371][V 0.0369] purejātapaccayena paccayoti ettha purejātaṃ nāma yassa paccayo hoti, tato purimataraṃ jātaṃ jātikkhaṇaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhitikkhaṇappattaṃ. Cakkhāyatanantiādi vatthupurejātavasena vuttaṃ. Rūpāyatanantiādi ārammaṇapurejātavasena. Kiñcikāle purejātapaccayenāti pavattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kiñcikāle na purejātapaccayenāti paṭisandhiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Evaṃ sabbathāpi pañcadvāre vatthārammaṇavasena, manodvāre vatthuvasenevāyaṃ pāḷi āgatā, pañhāvāre pana “ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – sekkhā vā puthujjanā vā cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassantī”ti āgatattā manodvārepi ārammaṇapurejātaṃ labbhateva. Idha pana sāvasesavasena desanā katāti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

10. In the exposition of the pre-arisen condition, regarding the phrase 'by the pre-arisen condition as condition': here, 'pre-arisen' refers to that which is a condition for something, having been born before it, passed the moment of arising, and reached the moment of persistence. 'The eye-base, etc.' is stated by way of the physical base being pre-arisen. 'The visible-form base, etc.' is stated by way of the object being pre-arisen. 'At some time by the pre-arisen condition' is said with reference to the course of existence. 'At some time not by the pre-arisen condition' is said with reference to rebirth-linking. Thus, in all cases, this Pāli passage has come down as applying in the five sense-doors by way of physical base and object, and in the mind-door by way of physical base alone. But in the question section, since it has come down that 'pre-arisen as object—trainees or ordinary people contemplate the eye as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self,' pre-arisen as object is certainly obtained in the mind-door as well. Here, however, the teaching is given in a non-exhaustive manner. This, then, is the explanation of the Pāli text here.

Ayaṃ pana purejātapaccayo suddharūpameva hoti. Tañca kho uppādakkhaṇaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhitippattaṃ aṭṭhārasavidhaṃ rūparūpameva. Taṃ sabbampi vatthupurejātaṃ ārammaṇapurejātanti dvidhā ṭhitaṃ. Tattha cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ vatthurūpanti idaṃ vatthupurejātaṃ nāma. Sesaṃ imāya pāḷiyā āgatañca anāgatañca vaṇṇo saddo gandho raso catasso dhātuyo tīṇi indriyāni kabaḷīkāro āhāroti dvādasavidhaṃ rūpaṃ ārammaṇapurejātapaccayo nāmāti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This pre-arisen condition, however, is purely material form. And that, indeed, is the eighteenfold material form itself, which, having passed the moment of arising, has reached the moment of persistence. All of that stands twofold: as base-pre-arisen and object-pre-arisen. Herein, the eye-base...pe... the body-base, being base-materiality, is called base-pre-arisen. The rest—what is mentioned in this Pāli text and what is not—namely, color, sound, odor, taste, the four great elements, the three faculties, and edible food, these twelve kinds of material form are called the object-pre-arisen condition. Thus, the determination should be understood here in its various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha cakkhāyatanaṃ dvinnaṃ cakkhuviññāṇānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo, tathā itarāni cattāri sotaviññāṇādīnaṃ. Vatthurūpaṃ pana ṭhapetvā dvipañcaviññāṇāni cattāro ca āruppavipāke sesānaṃ sabbesampi catubhūmakānaṃ kusalākusalābyākatānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ purejātapaccayo hoti. Rūpādīni pana pañcārammaṇāni dvipañcaviññāṇānañceva manodhātūnañca ekanteneva purejātapaccayā honti. Aṭṭhārasavidhampi panetaṃ rūparūpaṃ kāmāvacarakusalassa rūpāvacarato abhiññākusalassa akusalassa tadārammaṇabhāvino kāmāvacaravipākassa kāmāvacarakiriyassa rūpāvacarato abhiññākiriyassāti imesaṃ channaṃ rāsīnaṃ purejātapaccayo [M 0.0372] hotīti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Thus, when distinguished here, the eye-base is a condition for the two eye-consciousnesses by way of the pre-arisen condition; similarly, the other four bases are for the ear-consciousnesses, etc. Base-materiality, however, excluding the two sets of fivefold consciousness and the four immaterial resultants, is a pre-arisen condition for all the remaining wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate consciousness and mental factors of the four planes. The five objects—visible forms, etc.—are exclusively pre-arisen conditions for the two sets of fivefold consciousness and for the mind-elements. Moreover, these eighteen kinds of material form are a pre-arisen condition for these six classes: sense-sphere wholesome consciousness, form-sphere wholesome consciousness of higher knowledge, unwholesome consciousness, sense-sphere resultant consciousness that performs registering, sense-sphere functional consciousness, and form-sphere functional consciousness of higher knowledge. Thus, the determination should also be understood here from the side of the conditioned states.

Purejātapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Pre-arisen Condition.

11. Pacchājātapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

11. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Post-arisen Condition.

11. Pacchājātapaccayaniddese [V 0.0370] pacchājātāti yassa kāyassa paccayā honti, tasmiṃ uppajjitvā ṭhite jātā. Purejātassāti tesaṃ uppādato paṭhamataraṃ jātassa jātikkhaṇaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhitippattassa. Imassa kāyassāti imassa catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikabhūtaupādārūpasaṅkhātassa kāyassa. Ettha ca tisamuṭṭhānikakāyoti āhārasamuṭṭhānassa abhāvato brahmapārisajjādīnaṃ kāyo veditabbo. Ayamettha pāḷivaṇṇanā. Ayaṃ pana pacchājātapaccayo nāma saṅkhepato ṭhapetvā āruppavipāke avasesā catubhūmakā arūpakkhandhā. So jātivasena kusalākusalavipākakiriyabhedena catudhā bhijjatīti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

11. In the exposition of the post-nascent condition, 'post-nascent' refers to those [states] which are born after a body has arisen and is established, for which body they are conditions. 'Pre-nascent' refers to that [body] which is born earlier than their arising, having passed the moment of arising and reached the stage of presence. 'This body' means this body, reckoned as materiality consisting of the primary elements and derived matter, originating from four or three causes. Here, 'a body originating from three causes' should be understood as the body of Brahma's retinue and so on, due to the absence of nutriment-originated materiality. This is the textual explanation here. This post-nascent condition, in brief, comprises the immaterial aggregates of the four planes, excluding the formless resultants. It is divided into four kinds by way of its nature—wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional. Thus, the determination here should be understood according to these various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha pañcavokārabhave uppannaṃ catubhūmakakusalañca akusalañca uppādakkhaṇaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhitippattassa catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikarūpakāyassa pacchājātapaccayo hoti. Vipākepi ṭhapetvā paṭisandhivipākaṃ avaseso kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipāko tasseva ekantena pacchājātapaccayo hoti. Lokuttaropi pañcavokāre uppannavipāko tasseva pacchājātapaccayo hoti. Tebhūmakakiriyāpi pañcavokāre uppannāva vuttappakārassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayo hotīti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

When thus divided, wholesome and unwholesome consciousness of the four planes, arisen in the five-constituent existence, is a post-nascent condition for the material body—originated from four or three causes—which has passed its moment of arising and reached the stage of presence. Among resultants, excluding the rebirth-linking resultant, the remaining sense-sphere and form-sphere resultants are entirely a post-nascent condition for that same [body]. The supramundane resultant arisen in the five-constituent existence is also a post-nascent condition for that same [body]. The functional consciousness of the three planes, when arisen in the five-constituent existence, is a post-nascent condition for the body of the aforementioned kind. Thus, the determination here should also be understood from the perspective of the conditioned state.

Pacchājātapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Post-Nascent Condition.

12. Āsevanapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

12. Commentary on the Exposition of the Repetition Condition

12. Āsevanapaccayaniddese purimā purimāti sabbanayesu samanantarātītāva daṭṭhabbā. Kasmā panettha anantarapaccaye viya “purimā purimā kusalā [M 0.0373] dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ abyākatānaṃ dhammāna”ntiādinā nayena bhinnajātikehi saddhiṃ niddeso na katoti? Attano gatiṃ gāhāpetuṃ asamatthatāya. Bhinnajātikā hi bhinnajātikānaṃ arūpadhammānaṃ āsevanaguṇena paguṇabalavabhāvaṃ [V 0.0371] sādhayamānā attano kusalādibhāvasaṅkhātaṃ gatiṃ gāhāpetuṃ na sakkonti. Tasmā tehi saddhiṃ niddesaṃ akatvā ye yesaṃ vāsanāsaṅkhātena āsevanena paguṇatarabalavatarabhāvavisiṭṭhaṃ attano kusalādibhāvasaṅkhātaṃ gatiṃ gāhāpetuṃ sakkonti, tesaṃ tehi samānajātikeheva saddhiṃ niddeso katoti veditabbo. Atha vipākābyākataṃ kasmā na gahitanti? Āsevanābhāvena. Vipākañhi kammavasena vipākabhāvappattaṃ kammapariṇāmitaṃ hutvā vattati nirussāhaṃ dubbalanti taṃ āsevanaguṇena attano sabhāvaṃ gāhāpetvā paribhāvetvā neva aññaṃ vipākaṃ uppādetuṃ sakkoti, na purimavipākānubhāvaṃ gahetvā uppajjitunti. Kammavegakkhittaṃ pana patitaṃ viya hutvā uppajjatīti sabbathāpi vipāke āsevanaṃ natthīti āsevanābhāvena vipākaṃ na gahitaṃ. Kusalākusalakiriyānantaraṃ uppajjamānampi cetaṃ kammapaṭibaddhavuttitāya āsevanaguṇaṃ na gaṇhātīti kusalādayopissa āsevanapaccayā na honti. Apica nānājātikattāpete na hontiyeva. Bhūmito pana ārammaṇato vā nānājātikattaṃ nāma natthi. Tasmā kāmāvacarakusalakiriyāmahaggatakusalakiriyānampi, saṅkhārārammaṇañca anulomakusalaṃ nibbānārammaṇassa gotrabhukusalassa āsevanapaccayo hotiyevāti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā. Ayaṃ pana āsevanapaccayo jātito tāva kusalo akusalo kiriyābyākatoti tidhā ṭhito. Tattha kusalo bhūmito kāmāvacaro rūpāvacaro arūpāvacaroti tividho hoti, akusalo kāmāvacarova kiriyābyākato kāmāvacaro rūpāvacaro arūpāvacaroti tividhova, lokuttaro āsevanapaccayo nāma natthīti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

12. In the exposition of the repetition condition, the phrase 'the preceding, preceding' should be understood in all methods as referring to what is immediately past. Why, then, is the exposition here not made with states of different natures, as in the case of the contiguity condition, by a method such as, 'The preceding, preceding wholesome states are a condition for the subsequent, subsequent indeterminate states'? Because they are incapable of causing [the subsequent states] to acquire their own nature. For states of different natures, while bringing about a state of proficiency and strength in other immaterial states through the quality of repetition, cannot cause them to acquire their own nature, designated as wholesome and so on. Therefore, the exposition is not made with those. It should be understood that the exposition is made only with those of the same nature, which are capable of causing [subsequent states] to acquire their own nature—designated as wholesome and so on—which is distinguished by a state of being more proficient and stronger through repetition, which is termed 'imprinting.' Now, why is the resultant-indeterminate not included? Due to the absence of repetition. For the resultant, having attained the state of a resultant through the force of kamma, proceeds as something transformed by kamma, devoid of energy and weak. Thus, it can neither produce another resultant by taking up the quality of repetition to cause it to acquire and develop its own nature, nor can it arise by grasping the influence of a previous resultant. Rather, it arises as if thrown by the force of kamma, like something that has fallen. Therefore, in every respect, there is no repetition in resultants; hence, the resultant is not included due to the absence of repetition. And even when this [resultant] arises immediately after a wholesome, unwholesome, or functional [state], it does not take up the quality of repetition, as its occurrence is bound to kamma. Thus, wholesome states and so on are not repetition conditions for it. Moreover, being of different natures, they are not [such conditions] at all. However, there is no difference of nature based on plane or object. Therefore, a sense-sphere wholesome [state] is indeed a repetition condition for a sublime wholesome [state], and conformity-wholesome with formations as its object is a repetition condition for change-of-lineage-wholesome with Nibbāna as its object. This much is the textual explanation here. This repetition condition, by its nature, is threefold: wholesome, unwholesome, and functional-indeterminate. Therein, the wholesome is threefold by plane: sense-sphere, form-sphere, and formless-sphere. The unwholesome is only of the sense-sphere. The functional-indeterminate is also threefold: sense-sphere, form-sphere, and formless-sphere. There is no such thing as a supramundane repetition condition. Thus, the determination here should be understood according to these various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha kāmāvacarakusalaṃ attano anantarassa kāmāvacarakusalasseva. Yaṃ panettha ñāṇasampayuttaṃ, taṃ attanā sadisavedanassa rūpāvacarakusalassa arūpāvacarakusalassa lokuttarakusalassāti imesaṃ [M 0.0374] rāsīnaṃ āsevanapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarakusalaṃ pana rūpāvacarakusalasseva. Arūpāvacarakusalaṃ arūpāvacarakusalasseva. Akusalaṃ pana akusalasseva āsevanapaccayo hoti. Kiriyato pana kāmāvacarakiriyasaṅkhāto tāva kāmāvacarakiriyasseva. Yo panettha ñāṇasampayutto, so attanā sadisavedanassa rūpāvacarakiriyassa arūpāvacarakiriyassāti imesaṃ rāsīnaṃ āsevanapaccayo hoti. Rūpāvacarakiriyasaṅkhāto pana rūpāvacarakiriyasseva, arūpāvacarakiriyasaṅkhāto arūpāvacarakiriyasseva āsevanapaccayo hoti. Vipāko pana ekadhammassāpi ekadhammopi vā koci [V 0.0372] vipākassa āsevanapaccayo natthīti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

When thus divided, a wholesome state of the sense sphere is a repetition condition only for its own immediately subsequent wholesome state of the sense sphere. But that [wholesome state] which is associated with knowledge is a repetition condition for these groups of states with feeling similar to its own: the wholesome state of the form sphere, the wholesome state of the formless sphere, and the supramundane wholesome state. A wholesome state of the form sphere, however, is a repetition condition only for a wholesome state of the form sphere. A wholesome state of the formless sphere is a repetition condition only for a wholesome state of the formless sphere. An unwholesome state, however, is a repetition condition only for an unwholesome state. As for functional states, that designated as a functional state of the sense sphere is a repetition condition only for a functional state of the sense sphere. But that [functional state] which is associated with knowledge is a repetition condition for these groups of states with feeling similar to its own: the functional state of the form sphere and the functional state of the formless sphere. That designated as a functional state of the form sphere, however, is a repetition condition only for a functional state of the form sphere; that designated as a functional state of the formless sphere is a repetition condition only for a functional state of the formless sphere. As for the resultant, however, no single state whatsoever is a repetition condition for any resultant. Thus, the determination should be understood here also from the perspective of the conditioned states.

Āsevanapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Repetition Condition.

13. Kammapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

13. Commentary on the Exposition of the Kamma Condition

13. Kammapaccayaniddese kammanti cetanākammameva. Kaṭattā ca rūpānanti kammassa kaṭattā uppannarūpānaṃ. Kammapaccayenāti anekānampi kappakoṭīnaṃ matthake attano phalaṃ uppādetuṃ samatthena nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayenāti attho. Kusalākusalañhi kammaṃ attano pavattikkhaṇe phalaṃ na deti. Yadi dadeyya, yaṃ manusso devalokūpagaṃ kusalakammaṃ karoti, tassānubhāvena tasmiṃyeva khaṇe devo bhaveyya. Yasmiṃ pana khaṇe taṃ kataṃ, tato aññasmiṃ khaṇe avijjamānampi kevalaṃ kaṭattāyeva diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye avasesapaccayasamāyoge sati phalaṃ uppādeti niruddhāpi purimasippādikiriyā viya kālantare pacchimasippādikiriyāya. Tasmā nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayoti vuccati. Cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānanti yā kāci cetanā attanā sampayuttakānaṃ dhammānaṃ. Taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti iminā paṭisandhikkhaṇe kaṭattārūpampi gaṇhāti. Kammapaccayenāti idaṃ sahajātacetanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kusalādīsu hi yā kāci sahajātacetanā sesadhammānaṃ cittapayogasaṅkhātena kiriyābhāvena [M 0.0375] upakārikā hoti. Tasmā sahajātakammapaccayoti vuccati. Ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

13. In the exposition of the kamma condition, “kamma” means volitional action (cetanā) itself. “And of materiality due to having-been-done-ness” means of material forms arisen due to kamma’s having-been-done-ness. “By kamma condition” means by the different-moment kamma condition, which is capable of producing its own fruit even after countless crores of eons. For wholesome and unwholesome kamma does not yield its result in the very moment of its occurrence. If it did, then when a human performs a wholesome kamma leading to the heavenly realm, they would become a deity in that same moment. But even though it is non-existent in a moment other than that in which it was done, merely by its having-been-done-ness, it produces its fruit when there is a conjunction of the remaining conditions—whether in this very life, in the next life, or in a subsequent life—just as a prior skilled action, though ceased, produces a subsequent skilled action at a later time. Therefore, it is called the “different-moment kamma condition.” “Of volition for associated states” refers to any volition for its own associated states. By “for those originated from it,” this also includes kamma-produced materiality at the moment of rebirth-linking. “By kamma condition” here is said in reference to co-nascent volition. For in wholesome and other such states, any co-nascent volition assists the remaining phenomena by means of its functional nature, which is designated as mental application. Therefore, it is called the “co-nascent kamma condition.” This, for now, is the explanation of the Pāli here.

Ayaṃ pana kammapaccayo atthato catubhūmikacetanāmattameva. So hi jātibhedato kusalo akusalo vipāko kiriyāti catudhā bhijjati. Tattha kusalo bhūmito kāmāvacarādivasena catudhā bhijjati. Akusalo ekadhāva vipāko catudhā, kiriyā tidhāvāti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This condition of kamma is, in its meaning, simply volition in the four planes. It is divided into four kinds by way of class: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional. Of these, the wholesome is divided into four according to plane, beginning with the sense-sphere. The unwholesome is of one kind, the resultant of four kinds, and the functional of three kinds. Thus, the analysis here should be understood by way of various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha sahajātā kāmāvacarakusalacetanā pañcavokāre attanā sampayuttadhammānañceva [V 0.0373] cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, catuvokāre sampayuttakkhandhānaññeva sahajātakammapaccayo hoti. Uppajjitvā niruddhā pana attano vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena paccayo hoti. Sā ca kho pañcavokāreyeva, na aññattha. Sahajātā rūpāvacarakusalacetanā attanā sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca ekanteneva sahajātakammapaccayena paccayo. Uppajjitvā niruddhā pana attano vipākānañceva kaṭattārūpānañca nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena paccayo. Arūpāvacarā pana lokuttarā ca sahajātā kusalacetanā pañcavokāre attanā sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca, catuvokāre sampayuttakkhandhānaññeva sahajātakammapaccayena paccayo. Uppajjitvā niruddhā panesā duvidhāpi attano attano vipākakkhandhānaññeva nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā akusalacetanā pañcavokāre attanā sampayuttakkhandhānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānañca catuvokāre arūpakkhandhānaññeva sahajātakammapaccayena paccayo. Uppajjitvā niruddhā pana vipākakkhandhānañceva kaṭattārūpānañca nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena paccayo.

When divided in this way, the co-nascent wholesome volition of the sense sphere here becomes a condition by way of co-nascent kamma for the associated states and for mind-produced materiality in the five-constituent existence, and for the associated aggregates alone in the four-constituent existence. Having arisen and ceased, it then becomes a condition by way of kamma at different moments for its resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality. This, however, applies only in the five-constituent existence, not elsewhere. The co-nascent wholesome volition of the form sphere becomes a condition by way of co-nascent kamma exclusively for the associated states and for mind-produced materiality. Having arisen and ceased, it then becomes a condition by way of kamma at different moments for its own resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality. The co-nascent wholesome volition of the formless sphere and the supramundane becomes a condition by way of co-nascent kamma for the associated states and for mind-produced materiality in the five-constituent existence, and for the associated aggregates alone in the four-constituent existence. Having arisen and ceased, both these become conditions by way of kamma at different moments for their respective resultant aggregates alone. The co-nascent unwholesome volition becomes a condition by way of co-nascent kamma for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced materiality in the five-constituent existence, and for the formless aggregates alone in the four-constituent existence. Having arisen and ceased, it then becomes a condition by way of kamma at different moments for the resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality.

Kāmāvacararūpāvacarato vipākacetanā attanā sampayuttadhammānaṃ pavatte cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānaṃ, paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattārūpānañca sahajātakammapaccayena paccayo. Arūpāvacaravipākacetanā attanā sampayuttadhammānaññeva sahajātakammapaccayena paccayo. Lokuttaravipākacetanā pañcavokāre attanā sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, catuvokāre arūpasseva sahajātakammapaccayena paccayo. Tebhūmikā kiriyacetanā pañcavokāre [M 0.0376] sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca sahajātakammapaccayena paccayo. Yā panettha āruppe uppajjati, sā arūpadhammānaññeva sahajātakammapaccayena paccayoti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

The resultant volition of the sense sphere and the form sphere is a condition, by way of the co-nascent kamma condition, for the associated states and for the mind-produced materiality that arises in the course of life, as well as for the kamma-produced materiality at rebirth. The resultant volition of the formless sphere is a condition, by way of the co-nascent kamma condition, only for its associated states. The supramundane resultant volition in the five-constituent existence is a condition, by way of the co-nascent kamma condition, for its associated states and for the mind-produced materiality, but in the four-constituent existence, it is a condition only for the formless states. The three-plane functional volition in the five-constituent existence is a condition, by way of the co-nascent kamma condition, for its associated states and for the mind-produced materiality. However, that volition which arises in the formless sphere is a condition, by way of the co-nascent kamma condition, only for the formless states. Thus, the analysis should be understood here also from the perspective of the conditioned states.

Kammapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Kamma Condition.

14. Vipākapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

14. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Result Condition.

14. Vipākapaccayaniddese [V 0.0374] vipākā cattāro khandhāti yasmā kammasamuṭṭhānāpi rūpā vipākā na honti, tasmā “vipākā”ti vatvā “cattāro khandhā”ti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ ayaṃ pāḷi arūpadhammānaññeva vipākapaccayavasena āgatā. Pañhāvāre pana “vipākābyākato eko khandho tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo”ti āgatattā cittasamuṭṭhānakammasamuṭṭhānarūpānampi vipākapaccayo labbhati. Idha pana sāvasesavasena desanā katāti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā. Ayaṃ pana vipākapaccayo vipākabhāvena jātito ekavidho, bhūmibhedato kāmāvacarādivasena catudhā bhijjatīti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

14. In the exposition of the result condition, it is said that “the four aggregates are results.” This is because material forms originated by kamma are not termed ‘results.’ Therefore, having said “results,” it is stated “four aggregates.” Thus, this Pāli passage refers only to immaterial phenomena by way of the result condition. However, in the Question Section, it is stated: “One resultant-indeterminate aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-originated material forms by way of the result condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, one resultant-indeterminate aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for kamma-originated material forms by way of the result condition.” Because of this statement, the result condition is also obtained for mind-originated and kamma-originated material forms. Here, however, the teaching is given in a partial manner. This, then, is the explanation of the Pāli here. This result condition, by way of its nature as result, is of one kind by class. But by distinction of planes, it is divided into four kinds, beginning with the sense-sphere. Thus, the analysis here should be understood by way of various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipāko attanā sampayuttadhammānaṃ pavatte cittasamuṭṭhānarūpānaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattārūpānañca vipākapaccayo hoti. Arūpāvacaravipāko sampayuttadhammānaññeva. Lokuttaravipāko pañcavokāre sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, catuvokāre sampayuttakkhandhānaññeva vipākapaccayo hotīti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Thus, when divided in this way, the sense-sphere and form-sphere resultants are a condition for their associated phenomena, for mind-originated material forms in the course of existence, and for kamma-originated material forms at rebirth-linking by way of the result condition. The formless-sphere resultant is a condition only for its associated phenomena. The supramundane resultant is a condition for its associated phenomena and for mind-originated material form in the five-aggregate existence, and only for its associated aggregates in the four-aggregate existence. Thus, in this case, the analysis should also be understood from the standpoint of the conditioned states.

Vipākapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Exposition of the Result Condition.

15. Āhārapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

15. Commentary on the Exposition of the Nutriment Condition.

15. Āhārapaccayaniddese [M 0.0377] kabaḷīkāro āhāroti catusantatisamuṭṭhāne rūpe ojā āhāro nāma. So pana yasmā kabaḷaṃ karitvā ajjhoharitova āhārakiccaṃ karoti, na bahi ṭhito, tasmā āhāroti avatvā “kabaḷīkāro āhāro”ti vuttaṃ. Kabaḷaṃ karitvā ajjhoharitabbavatthukattā vā kabaḷīkāroti nāmametaṃ tassa. Arūpino āhārāti phassacetanāviññāṇāhārā[V 0.0375]. Taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti idhāpi kammasamuṭṭhānāni gahitāneva. Vuttañhetaṃ pañhāvāre – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayoti. Ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

15. In the exposition of the nutriment condition, “morsel food” refers to the nutritive essence (ojā) in material form arisen from the four continuities. But because it performs the function of nutriment only after being made into a morsel and ingested, not while remaining outside, it is not called simply “nutriment” but “morsel food.” Or, because its nature is to be made into a morsel and ingested, this is its name, “morsel food.” The immaterial nutriments are the nutriment of contact, the nutriment of volition, and the nutriment of consciousness. “Those arisen from them” here also includes those arisen from kamma. For it was stated in the section on questions: “At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant-indeterminate nutriments are a condition, by way of the nutriment condition, for the associated aggregates and for kamma-originated material forms.” This, then, is the commentary on the passage here.

Ayaṃ pana āhārapaccayo saṅkhepato kabaḷīkāro āhāro, phasso, cetanā, viññāṇanti cattārova dhammā honti. Tattha ṭhapetvā kabaḷīkārāhāraṃ sesā tayo arūpāhārā jātivasena kusalākusalavipākakiriyabhedato catudhā bhijjanti. Puna bhūmibhedena kusalo catudhā, akusalo ekadhā, vipāko catudhā, kiriyā tidhāti evaṃ anekadhā bhijjanti. Kabaḷīkārāhāro pana jātito abyākato, bhūmito kāmāvacarovāti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This nutriment condition, in brief, consists of just four phenomena: morsel food, contact, volition, and consciousness. Among these, apart from morsel food, the remaining three immaterial nutriments are divided into four types by way of their origin: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional. Furthermore, by distinction of planes, the wholesome is divided into four, the unwholesome into one, the resultant into four, and the functional into three—thus they are divided in many ways. As for morsel food, by origin it is indeterminate, and by plane it is confined to the sense-sphere. Thus, the analysis here should be understood by way of various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha catubhūmakāpi tayo kusalāhārā pañcavokāre attanā sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca āhārapaccayena paccayo, ṭhapetvā pana rūpāvacaraṃ avasesā āruppe sampayuttadhammānaññeva āhārapaccayena paccayo. Akusalāhāresupi eseva nayo. Catubhūmakavipākāhārā pana sabbattha sampayuttakānaṃ āhārapaccayā honti. Kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipākā panettha pañcavokāre uppajjamānā pavatte cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattārūpassāpi āhārapaccayā honti. Lokuttarā pana cittasamuṭṭhānarūpasseva, āruppe uppannā rūpassa paccayā na honti. Tebhūmakāpi tayo kiriyāhārā pañcavokāre sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, kāmāvacarārūpāvacarā pana āruppe sampayuttadhammānaññeva āhārapaccayena paccayo[M 0.0378]. Catusantatisamuṭṭhāno kabaḷīkārāhāro kiñcāpi “imassa kāyassā”ti avisesato vutto, visesato panāyamettha āhārasamuṭṭhānarūpassa janako ceva anupālako ca hutvā āhārapaccayena paccayo hoti, sesatisantatisamuṭṭhānassa anupālakova hutvā āhārapaccayena paccayo hotīti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Thus, when divided in this way, the three wholesome nutriments of the four planes are a condition by way of nutriment for their associated phenomena and for mind-originated material form in the five-aggregate existence. However, excluding the form-sphere, the remaining ones are a condition by way of nutriment only for their associated phenomena in the formless sphere. The same method applies to the unwholesome nutriments. The resultant nutriments of the four planes, however, are conditions by way of nutriment for their associated phenomena everywhere. Here, the sense-sphere and form-sphere resultants, when arising in the five-aggregate existence, are conditions by way of nutriment for mind-originated material form in the course of existence and for kamma-originated material form at rebirth-linking. The supramundane nutriments, however, are conditions only for mind-originated material form, and when arisen in the formless sphere, they are not conditions for material form. The three functional nutriments of the three planes are also conditions by way of nutriment for their associated phenomena and for mind-originated material form in the five-aggregate existence. However, the sense-sphere and formless-sphere ones are conditions by way of nutriment only for their associated phenomena in the formless sphere. Although morsel food, arisen from the four continuities, is spoken of generally as “for this body,” specifically here it is a condition by way of nutriment, being both the producer and sustainer of nutriment-originated material form. For material form arisen from the remaining three continuities, it is only a sustainer as a condition by way of nutriment. Thus, the analysis here should also be understood from the standpoint of the conditioned states.

Āhārapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Exposition of the Nutriment Condition.

16. Indriyapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

16. Commentary on the Exposition of the Faculty Condition.

16. Indriyapaccayaniddese [V 0.0376] cakkhundriyanti cakkhusaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ. Indriyapaccayenāti sayaṃ purejāto hutvā arūpadhammānaṃ uppādato paṭṭhāya yāva bhaṅgā indriyapaccayena paccayo hoti. Sotindriyādīsupi eseva nayo. Arūpino indriyāti ettha arūpajīvitindriyampi saṅgahitaṃ. Taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti ettha heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva kaṭattārūpampi saṅgahitaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ pañhāvāre – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayoti. Evaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā veditabbā.

16. In the exposition on the faculty condition, 'eye faculty' means the faculty called the eye. By 'faculty condition' is meant that, having arisen earlier itself, from the arising of immaterial phenomena until their dissolution, it is a condition by way of the faculty condition. The same method applies to the ear faculty and so on. Here, among the immaterial faculties, the immaterial life faculty is also included. As for 'those arisen from it,' here kamma-produced materiality is also included, as explained earlier. For it was said in the question section: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant-indeterminate faculties are a condition by way of the faculty condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality.' Thus far, the commentary on the Pāli text should be understood here.

Ayaṃ pana indriyapaccayo itthindriyapurisindriyavajjānaṃ samavīsatiyā indriyānaṃ vasena ṭhito. Itthindriyapurisindriyāni hi kiñcāpi itthiliṅgapurisaliṅgādīnaṃ bījabhūtāni, kalalādikāle pana vijjamānesupi tesu itthiliṅgapurisaliṅgādīnaṃ abhāvā tāni neva tesaṃ, na aññesaṃ indriyapaccayataṃ pharanti. Indriyapaccayo hi attano vijjamānakkhaṇe avinibbhuttadhammānaṃ indriyapaccayataṃ apharanto nāma natthi, tasmā tāni indriyapaccayā na honti. Yesaṃ panetāni bījabhūtāni, tesaṃ tāni suttantikapariyāyena pakatūpanissayabhāvaṃ bhajanti. Iti indriyapaccayo samavīsatiyā indriyānaṃ vasena ṭhitoti veditabbo. So jātito kusalākusalavipākakiriyarūpavasena pañcadhā bhijjati. Tattha kusalo bhūmivasena catudhā, akusalo kāmāvacarova vipāko catudhāva kiriyāsaṅkhāto tidhā, rūpaṃ kāmāvacaramevāti evaṃ anekadhā bhijjatīti evaṃ tāvettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This faculty condition, however, is established based on the twenty faculties, excluding the female faculty and the male faculty. Although the female faculty and the male faculty are indeed the seeds for female characteristics, male characteristics, and so on, yet during stages such as the embryo, even when they are present, because of the absence of female characteristics, male characteristics, and so on, they do not extend the faculty condition to those or to others. For there is no faculty condition that does not extend the faculty condition to phenomena inseparable from it at the moment of its existence; therefore, those are not faculty conditions. However, for those for which these serve as seeds, they function as natural decisive support according to the Suttanta method. Thus, it should be understood that the faculty condition is established based on the twenty faculties. It is divided into five types by way of origin: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, functional, and material. Herein, the wholesome is fourfold according to the planes; the unwholesome is solely of the sense-sphere; the resultant is fourfold; the functional, known as kiriyā, is threefold; and material is only of the sense-sphere. Thus, it is divided in many ways. Thus, the analysis should be understood here by way of its various divisions.

Evaṃ [M 0.0379] bhinne panettha catubhūmakopi kusalindriyapaccayo pañcavokāre sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca indriyapaccayena paccayo, tathā akusalo. Ṭhapetvā pana rūpāvacarakusalaṃ avasesā kusalākusalā āruppe sampayuttadhammānaññeva indriyapaccayena paccayo. Catubhūmako vipākindriyapaccayo ekanteneva sampayuttakānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Kāmāvacararūpāvacarā panettha pañcavokāre uppajjanato pavatte cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa, paṭisandhiyaṃ kaṭattārūpassāpi indriyapaccayena paccayā honti. Lokuttarā cittasamuṭṭhānarūpasseva. Āruppe uppannā lokuttaravipākā indriyā rūpassa paccayā na honti. Tebhūmakā kiriyindriyā pañcavokāre sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, kāmāvacarārūpāvacarā pana āruppe sampayuttadhammānaññeva [V 0.0377] indriyapaccayataṃ pharanti. Cakkhundriyādivasena chabbidhe rūpindriye cakkhundriyaṃ kusalākusalavipākato sampayuttadhammānaṃ dvinnaṃ cakkhuviññāṇānaṃ, sotindriyādīni tathāvidhānaññeva sotaviññāṇādīnaṃ, rūpajīvitindriyaṃ attanā sahajātarūpānaṃ ṭhitikkhaṇe indriyapaccayena paccayo. Sahajātapaccayatā pana tassa natthīti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

When thus divided, the wholesome faculty condition, even in the four planes, is a condition by way of the faculty condition for associated phenomena and mind-produced materiality in the five-constituent existence; and similarly for the unwholesome. However, excluding the fine-material-sphere wholesome, the remaining wholesome and unwholesome faculties in the formless sphere are conditions only for associated phenomena by way of the faculty condition. The resultant faculty condition in the four planes is exclusively a condition for associated phenomena by way of the faculty condition. Herein, those of the sense-sphere and fine-material sphere are conditions by way of the faculty condition for mind-produced materiality arising in the five-constituent existence during the course of existence, and also for kamma-produced materiality at rebirth-linking. The supramundane faculties are conditions only for mind-produced materiality. The supramundane resultant faculties that have arisen in the formless sphere are not conditions for materiality. The functional faculties of the three planes are conditions for associated phenomena and mind-produced materiality in the five-constituent existence, while those of the sense-sphere and formless sphere, however, extend their faculty conditionality only to associated phenomena in the formless sphere. Among the six kinds of material faculties, such as the eye faculty, the eye faculty is a condition for the two kinds of eye-consciousness—wholesome-resultant and unwholesome-resultant—and their associated phenomena; the ear faculty and others are similarly conditions for their respective ear-consciousness and so on; the material life faculty is a condition by way of the faculty condition for its co-nascent material states at the moment of their duration. However, it does not have the state of being a co-nascence condition. Thus, the analysis here should also be understood from the standpoint of the conditioned.

Indriyapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Faculty Condition.

17. Jhānapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

17. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Jhāna Condition

17. Jhānapaccayaniddese jhānaṅgānīti dvipañcaviññāṇavajjesu sesacittesu uppannāni vitakkavicārapītisomanassadomanassupekkhācittekaggatāsaṅkhātāni satta aṅgāni. Pañcannaṃ pana viññāṇakāyānaṃ abhinipātamattattā tesu vijjamānānipi upekkhāsukhadukkhāni upanijjhānākārassa abhāvato jhānaṅgānīti na uddhaṭāni. Tattha pacchinnattā pana sesāhetukesupi jhānaṅgaṃ na uddhaṭameva. Taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti idhāpi kaṭattārūpaṃ saṅgahitanti veditabbaṃ. Vuttañhetaṃ pañhāvāre – “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatāni jhānaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena [M 0.0380] paccayo”ti. Ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā. Ayaṃ pana jhānapaccayo sattannaṃ jhānaṅgānaṃ vasena ṭhitopi jātibhedato kusalākusalavipākakiriyavasena catudhā bhijjati, puna bhūmivasena catudhā; ekadhā, catudhā, tidhāti dvādasadhā bhijjatīti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

17. In the exposition on the jhāna condition, the 'jhāna factors' are the seven factors called initial application, sustained application, joy, happiness, displeasure, equanimity, and one-pointedness of mind, which arise in all consciousnesses except the two sets of fivefold sense consciousnesses. However, although equanimity, pleasure, and pain are present in the five groups of consciousness, they are not designated as jhāna factors because of the absence of the characteristic of absorption, due to their being merely impingements. Furthermore, in the remaining rootless consciousnesses, a jhāna factor is not designated either, because of their deficient nature. Here, 'those arisen from it' should be understood to include kamma-produced materiality. For it was said in the section of questions: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant and indeterminate jhāna factors are a condition by way of the jhāna condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality.' Thus far, this is the Pāli explanation here. This jhāna condition, however, though established on the basis of the seven jhāna factors, is divided into four types based on the distinction of origin: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional. Again, it is divided into four based on the planes; it is divided twelvefold as one, fourfold, and threefold. In this way, the analysis should be understood here according to its various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha catubhūmakampi kusalajhānaṅgaṃ pañcavokāre sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, ṭhapetvā rūpāvacaraṃ avasesaṃ āruppe sampayuttadhammānaññeva jhānapaccayena paccayo. Akusalepi eseva nayo. Kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipākaṃ pavatte sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, paṭisandhiyaṃ sampayuttadhammānañceva kaṭattārūpassa ca, āruppavipākaṃ sampayuttadhammānaññeva, yañca āruppe lokuttaravipākaṃ uppajjati, tañca. Pañcavokāre pana taṃ cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassapi jhānapaccayena paccayo hoti. Tebhūmakampi kiriyajhānaṅgaṃ [V 0.0378] pañcavokāre sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca. Yaṃ panettha āruppe uppajjati, taṃ sampayuttadhammānaññeva jhānapaccayena paccayoti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

When thus divided, the wholesome jhāna factor, even in the four planes, is a condition by way of the jhāna condition for associated phenomena and mind-produced materiality in the five-constituent existence; but, excluding the fine-material-sphere, the remaining wholesome jhāna factor in the formless sphere is a condition only for associated phenomena. The same principle applies to the unwholesome. The resultant jhāna factors of the sense-sphere and fine-material sphere, in the course of existence, are conditions for both associated phenomena and mind-produced materiality; at rebirth-linking, they are conditions for both associated phenomena and kamma-produced materiality. The formless resultant jhāna factors are conditions only for associated phenomena, and this also applies to whatever supramundane resultant jhāna factors arise in the formless sphere. However, in the five-constituent existence, that supramundane resultant jhāna factor is also a condition by way of the jhāna condition for mind-produced materiality. The functional jhāna factor, even in the three planes, is a condition for associated phenomena and mind-produced materiality in the five-constituent existence. Whatever of this arises in the formless sphere is a condition only for associated phenomena by way of the jhāna condition. Thus, the analysis here should also be understood from the standpoint of the conditioned.

Jhānapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Jhāna Condition.

18. Maggapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

18. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Path Condition

18. Maggapaccayaniddese maggaṅgānīti ahetukacittuppādavajjesu sesacittesu uppannāni paññā, vitakko, sammāvācākammantājīvā, vīriyaṃ, sati, samādhi, micchādiṭṭhi, micchāvācākammantājīvāti imāni dvādasaṅgāni. Maggassa pana hetupacchimakattā ahetukacittesu maggaṅgāni na uddhaṭāni. Taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti idhāpi kaṭattārūpaṃ saṅgahitameva. Vuttañhetaṃ pañhāvāre – “paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatāni maggaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo”ti. Ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

18. In the exposition of the path condition, the 'path factors' are these twelve factors: wisdom, thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration, wrong view, wrong speech, wrong action, and wrong livelihood. These arise in the remaining consciousnesses, excluding rootless consciousness-moments. However, because the path has roots as its essential foundation, path factors are not designated in rootless consciousnesses. 'That which originates from them'—here, kamma-produced materiality is also included. For it is said in the section of questions: 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant and indeterminate path factors are a condition by way of the path condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality.' Thus far, this is the Pāli explanation here.

Ayaṃ pana maggapaccayo dvādasannaṃ maggaṅgānaṃ vasena ṭhitopi jātibhedato kusalādivasena catudhā, kusalādīnañca kāmāvacarādibhūmibhedato dvādasadhā bhijjatīti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo[M 0.0381]. Evaṃ bhinne panettha catubhūmakampi kusalamaggaṅgaṃ pañcavokāre sampayuttadhammānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, ṭhapetvā rūpāvacaraṃ avasesaṃ āruppe sampayuttadhammānaññeva maggapaccayena paccayoti sabbaṃ jhānapaccaye viya vitthāretabbanti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

This path condition, though established on the basis of the twelve path factors, is divided in four ways according to the distinction of type—wholesome, etc.—and these are further divided in twelve ways according to the distinction of planes—sense-sphere, etc. Thus, the analysis here should be understood through its various distinctions. When thus divided, the wholesome path factor of the four planes, in the five-constituent existence, is a condition by way of the path condition for associated phenomena and for mind-produced materiality; and, excluding the fine-material sphere, the remainder in the formless sphere is a condition for associated phenomena only. Everything should be elaborated as in the case of the jhāna condition. Thus, the analysis here should also be understood from the standpoint of the conditioned.

Maggapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Path Condition.

19. Sampayuttapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

19. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Associated Condition

19. Sampayuttapaccayaniddese [V 0.0379] pāḷi uttānatthā eva. Ayaṃ pana sampayuttapaccayo nāma saṅkhepato sabbepi arūpino khandhā. Pabhedato panesa jātito kusalādīnaṃ, bhūmito ca kāmāvacarādīnaṃ vasena anekadhā bhijjatīti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo. Evaṃ bhinne panettha catubhūmakesupi kusalakkhandhesu eko khandho tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ, tayo ekassa, dve dvinnanti evaṃ sabbepi aññamaññaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo. Akusalavipākakiriyakkhandhesupi eseva nayoti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

19. In the exposition of the associated condition, the Pāli is of plain meaning. This associated condition refers, in brief, to all immaterial aggregates. In detail, however, it is divided in many ways according to the distinction of type, such as wholesome, etc., and according to the distinction of planes, such as the sense-sphere, etc. Thus, the analysis here should be understood through various distinctions. Among these divisions, in the wholesome aggregates of the four planes, one aggregate is a condition for three aggregates, three aggregates for one, and two aggregates for two—thus, all are mutually conditions for each other through the associated condition. The same method applies to the unwholesome, resultant, and functional aggregates. Thus, the analysis here should also be understood from the perspective of the conditioned phenomena.

Sampayuttapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Associated Condition.

20. Vippayuttapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

20. The Explanation of the Exposition of the Dissociated Condition

20. Vippayuttapaccayaniddese rūpino dhammā arūpīnanti idaṃ tāva hadayavatthuno ceva cakkhundriyādīnañca vasena veditabbaṃ. Rūpadhammesu hi eteyeva cha koṭṭhāsā arūpakkhandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayā honti. Rūpāyatanādayo pana ārammaṇadhammā kiñcāpi vippayuttadhammā, vippayuttapaccayā pana na honti. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Sampayogāsaṅkāya abhāvato. Arūpino hi khandhā cakkhādīnaṃ vatthūnaṃ abbhantarato nikkhamantā viya uppajjanti. Tattha āsaṅkā hoti – “kiṃ nu kho ete etehi sampayuttā, udāhu vippayuttā”ti. Ārammaṇadhammā pana vatthunissayena uppajjamānānaṃ ārammaṇamattā hontīti natthi tesu sampayogāsaṅkā. Iti sampayogāsaṅkāya [M 0.0382] abhāvato na te vippayuttapaccayā. Hadayavatthuādīsu eva panāyaṃ vippayuttapaccayatā veditabbā. Vuttampi cetaṃ pañhāvāre – vatthu kusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu akusalānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Sota… ghāna… jivhā… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu vipākābyākatānaṃ kiriyābyākatānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayoti.

20. In the exposition of the dissociated condition, the statement ‘material phenomena for immaterial phenomena’ should first be understood in terms of the heart-base and the eye-faculty, etc. For among material phenomena, these six divisions alone are conditions for the immaterial aggregates by way of the dissociated condition. However, the sense-object of form, etc., though they are dissociated phenomena, are not conditions by way of dissociation. What is the reason? Because there is no suspicion of association. For the immaterial aggregates arise as if emerging from within the bases of the eye, etc. Here, a suspicion arises: “Are these associated with those, or are they dissociated?” However, object-phenomena are merely objects for the mental states arising in dependence on a base, so there is no suspicion of association regarding them. Thus, because there is no suspicion of association, they are not conditions by way of dissociation. This dissociated conditionality should be understood only in relation to the heart-base, etc. And this has been stated in the section of questions: “The base is a condition for the wholesome aggregates by way of the dissociated condition. The base is a condition for the unwholesome aggregates by way of the dissociated condition. The eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness by way of the dissociated condition. The ear… nose… tongue… body-base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of the dissociated condition. The base is a condition for the resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate aggregates by way of the dissociated condition.”

Arūpino [V 0.0380] dhammā rūpīnanti idaṃ pana catunnaṃ khandhānaṃ vasena veditabbaṃ. Arūpadhammesu hi cattāro khandhāva sahajātapurejātānaṃ rūpadhammānaṃ vippayuttapaccayā honti, nibbānaṃ pana arūpampi samānaṃ rūpassa vippayuttapaccayo na hoti. “Catūhi sampayogo catūhi vippayogo”ti hi vuttaṃ. Iti catunnaṃ arūpakkhandhānaṃyeva vippayuttapaccayatā veditabbā. Vuttampi cetaṃ pañhāvāre – sahajātā kusalā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā kusalā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vipākābyākatā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, khandhā vatthussāti. Evaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā veditabbā.

The statement ‘immaterial phenomena for material phenomena,’ however, should be understood in terms of the four aggregates. For among immaterial phenomena, the four aggregates alone are conditions for co-nascent and pre-arisen material phenomena by way of the dissociated condition. Nibbāna, though immaterial, is not a dissociated condition for material phenomena. For it is said: “Association is with four; dissociation is with four.” Thus, the nature of dissociated conditionality should be understood only in relation to the four immaterial aggregates. This is also stated in the section of questions: “Co-nascent wholesome aggregates are a condition for mind-produced materiality by way of the dissociated condition. Post-nascent wholesome aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of the dissociated condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the resultant-indeterminate aggregates are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the dissociated condition, and the aggregates for the base.” Thus far, the explanation of the Pāli should be understood here.

Ayaṃ pana vippayuttapaccayo nāma saṅkhepato pañcavokārabhave vattamānā rūpārūpadhammā. Tesu rūpaṃ vatthuno cakkhādīnañca vasena chadhā bhinnaṃ, arūpaṃ pañcavokārabhave uppannakusalākusalavipākakiriyavasena catudhā bhinnaṃ. Tassa bhūmito kāmāvacarādivasena catudhā, ekadhā, tidhā, tidhāti ekadasadhā bhedo hoti. Āruppavipākañhi vippayuttapaccayo na hotīti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

This dissociated condition, in brief, is the material and immaterial phenomena occurring in the five-constituent existence. Among them, materiality is divided into six kinds based on the base and the eye, etc. Immateriality, arising in the five-constituent existence, is divided into four kinds based on wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional states. From the standpoint of planes, its division is elevenfold: fourfold, single, threefold, and threefold. For the formless resultant is not a dissociated condition. Thus, the analysis here should be understood through various distinctions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha pañcavokārabhave uppannaṃ catubhūmakampi kusalaṃ akusalañca attanā samuṭṭhāpitacittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa sahajātavippayuttapaccayena paccayo hoti. Uppādakkhaṇaṃ pana atikkamitvā ṭhitikkhaṇaṃ pattassa purejātassa catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikarūpakāyassa pacchājātavippayuttapaccayena paccayo hoti. Ettha ca tisamuṭṭhānikakāyoti āhārasamuṭṭhānassa abhāvato brahmapārisajjādīnaṃ kāyo veditabbo. Kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipākaṃ pana pavatte cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa, paṭisandhiyaṃ [M 0.0383] kaṭattārūpassa ca sahajātavippayuttapaccayena paccayo hoti. Lokuttaravipākaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānarūpasseva. Tividhampi panetaṃ purejātassa catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikakāyassa pacchājātavippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Tebhūmakampi kiriyaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānassa sahajātavippayuttapaccayena paccayo, purejātassa catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikakāyassa pacchājātavippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Chadhā ṭhitesu pana rūpesu vatthurūpaṃ paṭisandhikkhaṇe kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipākānaṃ sahajātavippayuttapaccayena paccayo, pavatte uppajjamānānaṃ catubhūmakakusalānaṃ akusalānaṃ dvipañcaviññāṇavajjānaṃ tebhūmakavipākānaṃ tebhūmakakiriyānañca purejātavippayuttapaccayena [V 0.0381] paccayo. Cakkhāyatanādīni cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ purejātavippayuttapaccayena paccayoti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Thus, in this division, the wholesome and unwholesome states of the four planes that have arisen in the five-constituent existence are a condition for mind-originated matter produced by themselves, by way of conascent-dissociated condition. Having passed the moment of arising and reached the moment of presence, however, they are a condition for the pre-arisen material body of four origins and three origins by way of postnascent-dissociated condition. And here, the body of three origins should be understood as the body of the Brahmā's retinue and so on, due to the absence of nutriment-originated matter. The sense-sphere and form-sphere resultant states, during the course of existence, are a condition for mind-originated matter, and at rebirth-linking, for kamma-originated matter, by way of conascent-dissociated condition. The supramundane resultant state is a condition for mind-originated matter only. All three of these types are also a condition for the pre-arisen material body of four origins and three origins by way of postnascent-dissociated condition. The functional states of the three planes are a condition for mind-originated matter by way of conascent-dissociated condition, and for the pre-arisen material body of four origins and three origins by way of postnascent-dissociated condition. Among the material phenomena established in six ways, the base-materiality, at the moment of rebirth-linking, is a condition for the sense-sphere and form-sphere resultant states by way of conascent-dissociated condition; and during the course of existence, it is a condition for the wholesome and unwholesome states of the four planes (excluding the two sets of fivefold sense-consciousness), the resultant states of the three planes, and the functional states of the three planes, by way of pre-arisen-dissociated condition. The eye-base and so on are conditions for eye-consciousness and so on by way of pre-arisen-dissociated condition. Thus the analysis here should also be understood from the perspective of the conditioned phenomena.

Vippayuttapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Exposition of the Dissociated Condition.

21. Atthipaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

21. Explanation of the Exposition of the Presence Condition.

21. Atthipaccayaniddese cattāro khandhātiādīhi sahajātavasena atthipaccayo niddiṭṭho. Cakkhāyatanantiādīhi purejātavasena. Yaṃ rūpaṃ nissāyāti ettha sahajātapurejātavasena atthipaccayo niddiṭṭho. Evamayaṃ pāḷi sahajātapurejātānaññeva atthipaccayānaṃ vasena āgatā. Pañhāvāre pana sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyanti imesaṃ vasena āgatattā pacchājātaāhārindriyavasenāpi atthipaccayo labbhati.
