Idha pana sāvasesavasena desanā katāti ayaṃ tāvettha pāḷivaṇṇanā.

21. In the exposition of the presence condition, by 'the four aggregates,' and so on, the presence condition is expounded by way of conascence. By 'the eye-base,' and so on, it is by way of prenascence. In the phrase 'depending on that material form,' the presence condition is expounded by way of both conascence and prenascence. Thus, this Pāli text is presented only by way of the conascent and prenascent presence conditions. However, in the Question Section, since it is presented by way of conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty, the presence condition is also obtained by way of postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. Here, however, the teaching is given in a non-exhaustive manner. This, for now, is the explanation of the Pāli text here.

Ayaṃ pana atthipaccayo nāma duvidho – aññamaññato, na aññamaññato. Tattha aññamaññaṃ tividhaṃ – arūpaṃ arūpena, rūpaṃ rūpena, rūpārūpaṃ rūpārūpena. “Cattāro khandhā arūpino”ti ettha hi sabbacittuppattivasena arūpaṃ arūpena vuttaṃ. “Cattāro mahābhūtā”ti ettha sabbasantativasena rūpaṃ rūpena. “Okkantikkhaṇe nāmarūpa”nti ettha paṭisandhikhandhānañceva vatthuno ca vasena rūpārūpaṃ rūpārūpena vuttaṃ. Na aññamaññampi tividhaṃ – “arūpaṃ rūpassa, rūpaṃ rūpassa, rūpaṃ [M 0.0384] arūpassa cittacetasikā dhammā”ti ettha hi pañcavokāravasena arūpaṃ rūpassa vuttaṃ. “Mahābhūtā upādārūpāna”nti ettha sabbasantativasena rūpaṃ rūpassa. “Cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā”tiādīsu vatthārammaṇavasena rūpaṃ arūpassa atthipaccayoti vuttaṃ.

This presence condition is of two kinds: with mutuality and without mutuality. Therein, that with mutuality is threefold: immaterial with immaterial, material with material, and material-and-immaterial with material-and-immaterial. In the phrase, 'The four immaterial aggregates,' immaterial with immaterial is stated by way of all occurrences of consciousness. In 'The four great elements,' material with material is stated by way of all continuity. In 'At the moment of descent, name-and-form,' material-and-immaterial with material-and-immaterial is stated by way of the rebirth-linking aggregates and the base. That without mutuality is also threefold: immaterial for material, material for material, and material for immaterial. Here, in the case of 'consciousness and mental factors,' immaterial for material is stated by way of the five-constituent existence. In 'The great elements for derived material forms,' material for material is stated by way of all continuity. In 'The eye-base for the eye-consciousness element,' and so on, material for immaterial is stated as a presence condition by way of base and object.

Apicesa atthipaccayo nāma saṅkhepato khaṇattayappattaṃ nāmañceva rūpañca, vattamānā pañcakkhandhātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati. So jātibhedato kusalākusalavipākakiriyarūpavasena pañcadhā bhijjati[V 0.0382]. Tattha kusalo sahajātapacchājātavasena duvidho hoti, tathā akusalo vipākakiriyasaṅkhāto ca. Tesu kusalo kāmāvacarādibhedena catudhā bhijjati, akusalo kāmāvacarova vipāko catubhūmako, kiriyāsaṅkhāto tibhūmako. Rūpasaṅkhāto atthipaccayo kāmāvacarova. So pana sahajātapurejātavasena duvidho. Tattha pañca vatthūni ārammaṇāni ca purejātāneva, hadayavatthu sahajātaṃ vā hoti purejātaṃ vā. Pañhāvāre pana āgato āhāro indriyañca sahajātādibhedaṃ na labhatīti evamettha nānappakārabhedato viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Furthermore, this presence condition, in brief, can be said to be name-and-form that has reached the three moments, and also the present five aggregates. It is divided into five kinds based on the distinction of nature: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, functional, and material. Therein, the wholesome is twofold, by way of conascence and postnascence; similarly the unwholesome, and also the resultant and the functional. Among these, the wholesome is divided into four kinds based on the distinction of the sense-sphere and so on; the unwholesome is only of the sense-sphere; the resultant is of the four planes; the functional is of the three planes. The presence condition termed material is only of the sense-sphere. It, however, is twofold: by way of conascence and prenascence. Therein, the five physical bases and objects are only prenascent, while the heart-base may be conascent or prenascent. In the Question Section, however, the nutriment and faculty that are mentioned do not obtain the divisions of conascence and so on. Thus the analysis here should be understood according to its various divisions.

Evaṃ bhinne panettha catubhūmakakusalopi sahajāto atthipaccayo pañcavokāre “eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhāna”ntiādinā nayena aññamaññaṃ khandhānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca ṭhapetvā pana rūpāvacarakusalaṃ avaseso āruppe sampayuttakkhandhānaññeva sahajātakusalo atthipaccayena paccayo hoti. Catubhūmako panesa pañcavokāre catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikakāyassa pacchājāto kusalo atthipaccayena paccayo hoti. Akusalepi eseva nayo. Sopi hi pañcavokāre sampayuttakkhandhānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca, catuvokāre sampayuttakkhandhānaññeva sahajātākusalo atthipaccayena paccayo. Pañcavokāre catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikakāyassa pacchājātākusalo atthipaccayena paccayo.

Thus, when divided here, the wholesome of the four planes, as a conascent presence condition in the five-constituent existence, is a condition for the aggregates mutually and for mind-originated matter, according to the method 'one aggregate for three aggregates,' and so on. But, excluding the form-sphere wholesome, the remainder, in the formless realm, is a conascent wholesome presence condition only for the associated aggregates. This wholesome of the four planes, in the five-constituent existence, is also a condition for the material body of four origins and three origins by way of postnascent wholesome presence condition. The same method applies to the unwholesome. For that too, in the five-constituent existence, is a conascent unwholesome presence condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter, while in the four-constituent existence, it is a conascent unwholesome presence condition only for the associated aggregates. In the five-constituent existence, it is a postnascent unwholesome presence condition for the material body of four origins and three origins.

Vipākato pana kāmāvacararūpāvacaro atthipaccayo niyameneva paṭisandhikkhaṇe khandhānañceva kaṭattārūpassa ca sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo. Pavatte [M 0.0385] pana sampayuttakkhandhānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo, ṭhitippattassa catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikakāyassa pacchājātatthipaccayena paccayo. Arūpāvacaravipāko pana āruppe uppannalokuttaravipāko ca attanā sampayuttakkhandhānaññeva sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo. Pañcavokāre lokuttaravipāko sampayuttakkhandhānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo, catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikakāyassa pacchājātatthipaccayena paccayo. Kiriyato rūpāvacaro atthipaccayo sampayuttakkhandhānañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa ca sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo, catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikakāyassa pacchājātatthipaccayena paccayo. Kāmāvacarārūpāvacaro pana āruppe sampayuttakkhandhānaññeva, pañcavokāre cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassāpi sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo, catusamuṭṭhānikatisamuṭṭhānikakāyassa pacchājātatthi paccayena paccayo.

Regarding the resultants, the sense-sphere and form-sphere resultant is a presence condition by way of the co-nascent presence condition, necessarily at the moment of rebirth-linking, for both the aggregates and kamma-originated material form. In the course of existence, it is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material form by way of the co-nascent presence condition, and for the material body originating from four sources and three sources that has attained duration by way of the post-nascent presence condition. The formless-sphere resultant, and the supramundane resultant arisen in the formless realm, are conditions only for their associated aggregates by way of the co-nascent presence condition. The supramundane resultant in the five-aggregate existence is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material form by way of the co-nascent presence condition, and for the material body originating from four sources and three sources by way of the post-nascent presence condition. Regarding functional consciousness, the form-sphere functional is a presence condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material form by way of the co-nascent presence condition, and for the material body originating from four sources and three sources by way of the post-nascent presence condition. The sense-sphere and formless-sphere functional, in the formless realm, is a condition only for the associated aggregates; and in the five-aggregate existence, it is also a condition for mind-originated material form by way of the co-nascent presence condition, and for the material body originating from four sources and three sources by way of the post-nascent presence condition.

Rūpasaṅkhāto pana atthipaccayo sahajāto, purejāto, āhāro, indriyanti catubbidho. Tattha sahajātarūpatthipaccayo catusamuṭṭhānavasena catudhā ṭhito. Tattha kammasamuṭṭhāno ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ, tīṇi ekassa, dve dvinnaṃ, mahābhūtā upādārūpānanti evaṃ sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo hoti. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthurūpaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacaravipākakkhandhānaṃ sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo hoti. Tesampi tisamuṭṭhānikarūpaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ, tīṇi ekassa, dve dvinnaṃ, mahābhūtā upādārūpānanti evaṃ sahajātatthipaccayena paccayo hoti. Purejātatthipaccayo pana vatthupurejātaārammaṇapurejātavasena duvidho hoti. So duvidhopi heṭṭhā purejātapaccaye vuttanayeneva yojetvā gahetabbo. Āhāratthipaccayopi heṭṭhā kabaḷīkārāhārapaccaye yojitanayeneva yojetabbo. Idha panesa attano aniruddhakkhaṇe paccayabhāvena atthipaccayoti vutto. Rūpajīvitindriyampi heṭṭhā indriyapaccaye rūpajīvitindriyayojanāyaṃ vuttanayeneva yojetabbaṃ. Idha panetampi attano aniruddhakkhaṇeyeva paccayabhāvena atthipaccayoti vuttanti evamettha paccayuppannatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

The presence condition regarding material form is fourfold: co-nascent, pre-nascent, nutriment, and faculty. Herein, the co-nascent material presence condition is established in four ways according to the four sources of origin. Here, regarding kamma-originated matter: one great element is a condition for three great elements, three for one, two for two, and the great elements for the derived material forms—thus, it is a condition by way of co-nascent presence. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical basis is a condition by way of co-nascent presence for the sense-sphere and form-sphere resultant aggregates. For the material form originating from the other three sources as well: one great element is a condition for three great elements, three for one, two for two, and the great elements for the derived material forms—thus, it is a condition by way of co-nascent presence. The pre-nascent presence condition, however, is twofold: as the pre-nascent physical basis and as the pre-nascent object. Both should be understood by applying the method explained earlier under the pre-nascent condition. The nutriment presence condition should also be applied in the manner explained earlier under the edible food condition. Here, however, it is called the presence condition because it functions as a condition at the moment of its own non-cessation. The material life faculty, too, should be applied in the manner explained earlier in the application of the material life faculty under the faculty condition. Here, however, this too is called the presence condition because it functions as a condition at the very moment of its own non-cessation. Thus, the analysis here should be understood also from the side of the conditionally arisen phenomena.

Atthipaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Presence Condition.

22. Natthipaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

22. The Explanation of the Exposition of the Absence Condition

22. Natthipaccayaniddese [M 0.0386] samanantaraniruddhāti aññena cittuppādena anantarikā hutvā samanantaraniruddhā. Paṭuppannānanti paccuppannānaṃ. Iminā natthipaccayassa okāsadānaṭṭhena natthipaccayabhāvaṃ sādheti. Purimesu hi nirodhavasena pacchimānaṃ pavattanokāsaṃ adentesu tesaṃ paṭuppannabhāvo na siyāti ayamettha pāḷivaṇṇanā. Sesaṃ sabbaṃ anantarapaccaye vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Paccayalakkhaṇameva hettha nānaṃ, paccayānaṃ pana paccayuppannānañca nānākaraṇaṃ natthi. Kevalaṃ pana tattha “cakkhuviññāṇadhātu taṃsampayuttakā ca dhammā manodhātuyā”tiādinā nayena paccayā ca paccayuppannā ca sarūpato dassitā. Idha pana “samanantaraniruddhā cittacetasikā dhammā [V 0.0384] paṭuppannānaṃ cittacetasikānaṃ dhammāna”nti sabbepi te nirodhuppādavasena sāmaññato dassitāti.

22. In the exposition of the absence condition, ‘immediately ceased’ means they have ceased immediately, having become without interval to another arising of consciousness. ‘For the present’ means for those that are present. By this, it establishes the nature of the absence condition as giving an opportunity. For if the preceding states, by their cessation, did not give an opportunity for the subsequent states to arise, their present existence would not be possible—this is the explanation of the Pāli here. All the rest should be understood in the same way as explained in the immediately contiguous condition. Only the characteristic of the condition is different here, but there is no differentiation of the conditions and the conditioned states. However, there, the conditions and the conditioned states are shown in their own form, in the way such as ‘the eye-consciousness element and the mental factors associated with it are conditions for the mind element’ and so forth. Here, however, with ‘immediately ceased consciousness and mental factors are conditions for present consciousness and mental factors,’ all these are shown generally by way of cessation and arising.

Natthipaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Absence Condition.

23. Vigatapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

23. The Explanation of the Exposition of the Disappearance Condition

23. Vigatapaccayaniddese samanantaravigatāti samanantarameva vigatā. Iminā vigatapaccayassa vigacchamānabhāveneva paccayabhāvaṃ dasseti. Iti natthipaccayassa ca imassa ca byañjanamatteyeva nānattaṃ, na attheti.

23. In the exposition of the disappearance condition, ‘immediately disappeared’ means disappeared immediately. This shows the nature of the disappearance condition as being a condition precisely through its state of disappearing. Thus, there is only a verbal difference between the absence condition and this one, not a difference in meaning.

Vigatapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Disappearance Condition.

24. Avigatapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā

24. The Explanation of the Exposition of the Non-Disappearance Condition

24. Avigatapaccayaniddese cattāro khandhātiādīnaṃ sabbākārena atthipaccayaniddese vuttanayeneva attho veditabbo. Imassapi hi paccayassa atthipaccayena saddhiṃ byañjanamatteyeva nānattaṃ, na attheti.

24. In the exposition of the non-disappearance condition, the meaning of ‘the four aggregates’ and so forth should be understood in all aspects in the same way as stated in the exposition of the presence condition. For this condition too, there is only a verbal difference with the presence condition, not a difference in meaning.

Avigatapaccayaniddesavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Exposition of the Non-Disappearance Condition.

Paccayaniddesapakiṇṇakavinicchayakathā

The Discourse on the Miscellaneous Analysis of the Exposition of Conditions

Idāni [M 0.0387] evaṃ uddesaniddesato dassitesu imesu catuvīsatiyā paccayesu ñāṇacārassa visadabhāvatthaṃ [V 0.0385] anekadhammānaṃ ekapaccayabhāvato, ekadhammassa anekapaccayabhāvato, ekapaccayassa anekapaccayabhāvato, paccayasabhāgato, paccayavisabhāgato, yugaḷakato, janakājanakato, sabbaṭṭhānikāsabbaṭṭhānikato, rūpaṃ rūpassātiādivikappato, bhavabhedatoti imesaṃ dasannaṃ padānaṃ vasena pakiṇṇakavinicchayo veditabbo. Tattha anekadhammānaṃ ekapaccayabhāvatoti etesu hi ṭhapetvā kammapaccayaṃ avasesesu tevīsatiyā paccayesu anekadhammā ekato paccayā honti. Kammapaccayo pana eko cetanādhammoyevāti evaṃ tāvettha anekadhammānaṃ ekapaccayabhāvato vinicchayo veditabbo.

Now, for the sake of clarity in the course of knowledge regarding these twenty-four conditions, which have thus been shown by way of summary and exposition, the miscellaneous analysis should be understood by way of these ten terms: the state of many phenomena being one condition, the state of one phenomenon being many conditions, the state of one condition being many conditions, similarity of conditions, dissimilarity of conditions, pairing, productive and non-productive, universal and non-universal, the distinction of ‘matter as condition for matter’ and so forth, and the division of existence. Herein, ‘the state of many phenomena being one condition’ means that among these, excluding the kamma condition, in the remaining twenty-three conditions, many phenomena are collectively a condition. However, the kamma condition is solely the one phenomenon of volition. Thus, first, the analysis of the state of many phenomena being one condition should be understood here.

Ekadhammassa anekapaccayabhāvatoti hetupaccaye tāva amoho eko dhammo. So purejātakammāhārajhānapaccayova na hoti, sesānaṃ vīsatiyā paccayānaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Alobhādosā indriyamaggapaccayāpi na honti, sesānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena paccayā honti. Lobhamohā vipākapaccayāpi na honti, sesānaṃ sattarasannaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena paccayā honti. Doso adhipatipaccayopi na hoti, sesānaṃ soḷasannaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Ārammaṇapaccaye rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇapurejātaatthiavigatavasena catudhā paccayo; tathā manodhātuyā ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ca. Sahetukāya pana ārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayavasenāpi paccayo hoti. Iminā nayena sabbesaṃ ārammaṇapaccayadhammānaṃ anekapaccayabhāvo veditabbo.

‘The state of one phenomenon being many conditions’ means that in the root condition, for example, non-delusion is a single phenomenon. It is not a condition by way of pre-arisen, kamma, nutriment, or jhāna conditions, but it is a condition by way of the remaining twenty conditions. Non-greed and non-hatred are not conditions by way of faculty or path conditions, but they are conditions by way of the remaining eighteen conditions. Greed and delusion are not conditions by way of result condition, but they are conditions by way of the remaining seventeen conditions. Hatred is not a condition by way of dominance condition, but it is a condition by way of the remaining sixteen conditions. In the object condition, the form base is a condition for the eye-consciousness element in four ways: as object, pre-arisen, presence, and non-disappearance; similarly for the mind-element and the rootless mind-consciousness element. However, for the rooted consciousness, it is also a condition by way of object, object-dominance, and object-decisive support. In this way, the manifold conditionality of all phenomena of the object condition should be understood.

Adhipatipaccaye ārammaṇādhipatino ārammaṇapaccaye vuttanayeneva anekapaccayabhāvo veditabbo. Sahajātādhipatīsu vīmaṃsā amohahetu viya vīsatidhā paccayo hoti. Chando hetupurejātakammaāhāraindriyajhānamaggapaccayo na hoti, sesānaṃ sattarasannaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Cittaṃ hetupurejātakammajhānamaggapaccayo na hoti, sesānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā paccayānaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Vīriyaṃ hetupurejātakammāhārajhānapaccayo na hoti, sesānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā vasena paccayo hoti.

In the dominance condition, the manifold conditionality of object-dominance should be understood in the same way as explained in the object condition. Among the conascent dominants, investigation (vīmaṃsā) is a condition in twenty ways, like the root of non-delusion (amoha). Desire (chando) is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, or path conditions, but it is a condition by way of the remaining seventeen conditions. Consciousness (cittaṃ) is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, jhāna, or path conditions, but it is a condition by way of the remaining nineteen conditions. Energy (vīriyaṃ) is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, nutriment, or jhāna conditions, but it is a condition by way of the remaining nineteen conditions.

Anantarapaccaye [M 0.0388] “cakkhuviññāṇadhātū”tiādinā nayena vuttesu catūsu khandhesu vedanākkhandho hetupurejātakammāhāramaggapaccayo na hoti, sesānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā vasena paccayo hoti. Saññākkhandho indriyajhānapaccayopi na hoti, sesānaṃ sattarasannaṃ vasena paccayo [V 0.0386] hoti. Saṅkhārakkhandhe hetū hetupaccaye vuttanayena, chandavīriyāni adhipatipaccaye vuttanayeneva paccayā honti. Phasso hetupurejātakammaindriyajhānamaggapaccayo na hoti, sesānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Cetanā hetupurejātaindriyajhānamaggapaccayo na hoti. Sesānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā vasena paccayo hoti. Vitakko hetupurejātakammāhārindriyapaccayo na hoti, sesānaṃ ekūnavīsatiyā vasena paccayo hoti. Vicāro maggapaccayopi na hoti, sesānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Pīti tesaññeva vasena paccayo hoti. Cittekaggatā hetupurejātakammāhārapaccayo na hoti, sesānaṃ vīsatiyā vasena paccayo hoti. Saddhā hetupurejātakammāhārajhānamaggapaccayo na hoti, sesānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Sati tehi ceva maggapaccayena cāti ekūnavīsatiyā vasena paccayo hoti. Jīvitindriyaṃ saddhāya vuttānaṃ aṭṭhārasannaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Hirottappaṃ tato indriyapaccayaṃ apanetvā sesānaṃ sattarasannaṃ vasena paccayo hoti. Tathā kāyapassaddhādīni yugaḷakāni, yevāpanakesu adhimokkhamanasikāratatramajjhattatā karuṇāmuditā ca. Viratiyo pana tehi ceva maggapaccayena cāti aṭṭhārasadhā paccayā honti. Micchādiṭṭhi tato vipākapaccayaṃ apanetvā sattarasadhā, micchāvācākammantājīvā tehi ceva kammāhārapaccayehi cāti ekūnavīsatidhā. Ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ māno thinaṃ middhaṃ uddhaccanti ime hetupurejātakammavipākāhārindriyajhānamaggapaccayā na honti, sesānaṃ pana soḷasannaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena paccayā honti. Vicikicchāissāmacchariyakukkuccāni tato adhipatipaccayaṃ apanetvā pannarasadhā viññāṇakkhandhassa. Adhipatipaccaye vuttanayeneva anekapaccayabhāvo veditabbo. Samanantarapaccayepi eseva nayo.

In the proximity condition, among the four aggregates mentioned in the way of ‘the eye-consciousness element’ and so forth, the feeling aggregate is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, nutriment, or path, but it is a condition by way of the remaining nineteen. The perception aggregate is also not a condition by way of faculty or jhāna, but it is a condition by way of the remaining seventeen. In the formations aggregate, the roots are conditions in the way stated in the root condition, and desire and energy are conditions in the way stated in the dominance condition. Contact is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, faculty, jhāna, or path, but it is a condition by way of the remaining eighteen. Volition is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, faculty, jhāna, or path, but it is a condition by way of the remaining nineteen. Applied thought is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, nutriment, or faculty, but it is a condition by way of the remaining nineteen. Sustained thought is also not a condition by way of path, but it is a condition by way of the remaining eighteen. Joy is a condition in the same ways. One-pointedness of mind is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, or nutriment, but it is a condition by way of the remaining twenty. Faith is not a condition by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, nutriment, jhāna, or path, but it is a condition by way of the remaining eighteen. Mindfulness is a condition in nineteen ways, since it is a condition by way of those eighteen and also by way of path condition. The life faculty is a condition by way of the eighteen stated for faith. Moral shame and moral dread are conditions by way of the remaining seventeen, having excluded the faculty condition from those eighteen. The same applies to the pairs such as bodily tranquility, and among the miscellaneous factors, to resolution, attention, equanimity, compassion, and altruistic joy. The abstinences, however, are conditions in eighteen ways, since they are conditions by way of those seventeen and also by way of path condition. Wrong view is a condition in seventeen ways, having excluded the result condition from those eighteen; wrong speech, wrong action, and wrong livelihood are conditions in nineteen ways, since they are conditions by way of those seventeen and also by way of kamma and nutriment conditions. Shamelessness, moral fearlessness, conceit, sloth, torpor, and restlessness are not conditions by way of root, pre-arisen, kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, or path, but they are conditions by way of the remaining sixteen. Doubt, envy, avarice, and worry are conditions in fifteen ways, having excluded the dominance condition from those sixteen. For the consciousness aggregate, its manifold conditionality should be understood in the same way as stated in the dominance condition. This same method applies also to the contiguity condition.

Sahajātapaccaye catūsu tāva khandhesu ekekassa dhammassa anekapaccayabhāvo vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Cattāri mahābhūtāni ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayaupanissayapurejātaatthiavigatavasena [M 0.0389] navadhā paccayā honti. Hadayavatthu tesañceva vippayuttassa ca vasena dasadhā paccayo hoti. Aññamaññapaccaye apubbaṃ natthi. Nissayapaccaye cakkhāyatanādīni ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatinissayaupanissayapurejātaindriyavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena navadhā paccayā honti. Upanissaye apubbaṃ natthi. Purejātapaccaye rūpasaddagandharasāyatanāni ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatiupanissayapurejātaatthiavigatavasena chadhā paccayā honti. Ettakamevettha apubbaṃ. Pacchājātādīsu apubbaṃ natthi. Āhārapaccaye kabaḷīkārāhāro [V 0.0387] ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatiupanissayaāhāraatthiavigatavasena chadhā paccayo hoti. Indriyādīsu apubbaṃ natthi. Evamettha ekadhammassa anekapaccayabhāvatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

In the conascence condition, the manifold conditionality of each phenomenon among the four aggregates should be understood in the same way as stated. The four great elements become conditions in nine ways: as object, object-dominance, conascence, mutuality, dependence, decisive support, pre-arisen, presence, and non-disappearance. The heart-base becomes a condition in ten ways: by those same and also by dissociation. In the mutuality condition, there is nothing new. In the dependence condition, the eye-base and so forth become conditions in nine ways: as object, object-dominance, dependence, decisive support, pre-arisen, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. In the decisive support condition, there is nothing new. In the pre-arisen condition, the bases of form, sound, odor, and taste become conditions in six ways: as object, object-dominance, decisive support, pre-arisen, presence, and non-disappearance. Only this much is new here. In post-arisen and other conditions, there is nothing new. In the nutriment condition, edible food becomes a condition in six ways: as object, object-dominance, decisive support, nutriment, presence, and non-disappearance. In the faculty and other conditions, there is nothing new. Thus, the determination here should also be understood from the manifold conditionality of a single phenomenon.

Ekapaccayassa anekapaccayabhāvatoti hetupaccayādīsu yassa kassaci ekassa paccayassa yenākārena yenatthena yo paccayuppannānaṃ paccayo hoti, taṃ ākāraṃ taṃ atthaṃ avijahitvāva aññehipi yehākārehi yehi atthehi so tasmiññeva khaṇe tesaṃ dhammānaṃ anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati, tato anekapaccayabhāvato tassa vinicchayo veditabboti attho. Seyyathidaṃ – amoho hetupaccayo, so hetupaccayattaṃ avijahantova adhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākaindriyamaggasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi ekādasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Alobhādosā tato adhipatiindriyamaggapaccaye tayo apanetvā sesānaṃ vasena anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchanti. Idaṃ vipākahetūsuyeva labbhati, kusalakiriyesu pana vipākapaccayatā parihāyati. Lobhadosamohā te tayo vipākañcāti cattāro apanetvā sesānaṃ vasena anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchanti.

From a single condition becoming a multiple condition: Among the root condition and so on, whatever single condition functions as a condition for conditioned phenomena in a particular manner and meaning, without abandoning that manner and meaning, it also becomes a multiple condition for those phenomena in that very moment through other manners and meanings. Therefore, the determination of this should be understood from its nature as a multiple condition. For example: Non-delusion is a root condition. Without abandoning its nature as a root condition, it also becomes a multiple condition through eleven other modes—namely, dominance, conascence, mutuality, dependence, result, faculty, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. Non-greed and non-hatred, excluding the three conditions of dominance, faculty, and path, become multiple conditions by way of the remaining. This is obtained only in resultant roots; but in wholesome and functional states, the resultant conditionality is absent. Greed, hatred, and delusion, by excluding those three and the resultant condition—thus four—become multiple conditions by way of the remaining.

Ārammaṇapaccayo taṃ ārammaṇapaccayattaṃ avijahantaṃyeva ārammaṇādhipatinissayaupanissayapurejātavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi sattahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Ayamettha ukkaṭṭhaparicchedo, arūpadhammānaṃ pana atītānāgatānaṃ vā rūpadhammānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayabhāve sati ārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayamattaññeva uttari [M 0.0390] labbhati. Adhipatipaccaye vīmaṃsā amohasadisā. Chando adhipatipaccayo adhipatipaccayattaṃ avijahantova sahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi aṭṭhahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Vīriyaṃ tesañceva indriyamaggapaccayānañcāti imesaṃ vasena aparehipi dasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Cittaṃ tato maggapaccayaṃ apanetvā āhārapaccayaṃ pakkhipitvā imesaṃ vasena adhipatipaccayato uttari dasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Ārammaṇādhipatino pana heṭṭhā ārammaṇapaccaye vuttanayeneva anekapaccayabhāvo veditabbo.

The object condition, without abandoning its nature as an object condition, becomes a multiple condition in seven other modes through object-dominance, dependence, decisive support, pre-arisen, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. This is the most extensive classification here. However, for immaterial phenomena, or for past and future material phenomena, when they are object conditions, only object-dominance and object-decisive-support are further obtained. In the dominance condition, the investigation is similar to that for non-delusion. Desire, while remaining a dominance condition, becomes a multiple condition in eight other modes through conascence, mutuality, dependence, result, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. Energy, through these same modes and the faculty and path conditions, becomes a multiple condition in ten other modes. Mind, by excluding the path condition from those and including the nutriment condition, becomes a multiple condition in ten other modes in addition to the dominance condition. As for the object-dominance condition, its nature as a multiple condition should be understood in the same way as explained earlier under the object condition.

Anantarasamanantarapaccayā anantarasamanantarapaccayattaṃ avijahantāva upanissayakammaāsevananatthivigatānaṃ [V 0.0388] vasena aparehipi pañcahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchanti. Ariyamaggacetanāyeva cettha kammapaccayataṃ labhati, na sesadhammā. Sahajātapaccayo sahajātapaccayattaṃ avijahantova hetuadhipatiaññamaññanissayakammavipākaāhāraindriyajhānamaggasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehi cuddasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Ayampi ukkaṭṭhaparicchedo vatthusahajātādīnaṃ pana vasenettha hetupaccayādīnaṃ abhāvopi veditabbo. Aññamaññapaccayepi eseva nayo.

The contiguity and immediate contiguity conditions, without abandoning their nature as contiguity and immediate contiguity conditions, become multiple conditions in five other modes through decisive support, kamma, repetition, absence, and disappearance. Here, only the volition of the Noble Path obtains kamma conditionality, not the remaining states. The conascence condition, without abandoning its nature as a conascence condition, becomes a multiple condition in fourteen other modes through root, dominance, mutuality, dependence, kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. This too is the most extensive classification. However, here, in the case of base-conascent factors and so on, the absence of root conditions and so on should also be understood. The same method applies to the mutuality condition.

Nissayapaccayo nissayapaccayattaṃ avijahantova catuvīsatiyā paccayesu attano nissayapaccayattañceva anantarasamanantarapacchājātaāsevananatthivigatapaccaye ca cha apanetvā sesānaṃ vasena aparehipi sattarasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Ayampi ukkaṭṭhaparicchedova vatthunissayādīnaṃ pana vasenettha hetupaccayādīnaṃ ābhāvopi veditabbo.

The dependence condition, without abandoning its nature as a dependence condition, among the twenty-four conditions, by excluding its own dependence conditionality and the six conditions—contiguity, immediate contiguity, post-nascence, repetition, absence, and disappearance—becomes a multiple condition in seventeen other modes by way of the remaining. This too is the most extensive classification. However, here, in the case of base-dependence factors and so on, the absence of root conditions and so on should also be understood.

Upanissayapaccaye ārammaṇūpanissayo ārammaṇādhipatisadiso. Anantarūpanissayo anantarūpanissayapaccayattaṃ avijahantova anantarasamanantarakammaāsevananatthivigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi chahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Ariyamaggacetanāyeva cettha kammapaccayataṃ labhati, na sesadhammā. Pakatūpanissayo pakatūpanissayova. Purejātapaccayo attano purejātapaccayattaṃ avijahantova ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatinissayaupanissayaindriyavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi [M 0.0391] aṭṭhahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Ayampi ukkaṭṭhaniddesova ārammaṇapurejāte panettha nissayaindriyavippayuttapaccayatā na labbhati. Ito uttaripi labbhamānālabbhamānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Pacchājātapaccayo attano pacchājātapaccayabhāvaṃ avijahantova vippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi tīhākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Āsevanapaccayo āsevanapaccayattaṃ avijahantova anantarasamanantaraupanissayanatthivigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi pañcahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati.

In the decisive support condition, object decisive support is similar to object dominance. The immediate decisive support condition, without abandoning its nature as an immediate decisive support condition, becomes a multiple condition in six other modes through immediate contiguity, contiguity, kamma, repetition, absence, and disappearance. Here, only the volition of the Noble Path obtains the condition of kamma, not the remaining states. The natural decisive support condition is simply the natural decisive support condition. The pre-nascence condition, without abandoning its nature as a pre-nascence condition, becomes a multiple condition in eight other modes through object, object dominance, dependence, decisive support, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. This too is an exposition of the strongest cases. However, in the case of object pre-nascence, the conditions of dependence, faculty, and dissociation are not obtained here. What is obtainable and unobtainable beyond this should also be understood. The post-nascence condition, without abandoning its nature as a post-nascence condition, becomes a multiple condition in three other modes through dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. The repetition condition, without abandoning its nature as a repetition condition, becomes a multiple condition in five other modes through immediate contiguity, contiguity, decisive support, absence, and disappearance.

Kammapaccayo kammapaccayattaṃ avijahantova ekakkhaṇiko tāva sahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākaāhārasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi navahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Nānākkhaṇiko upanissayaanantarasamanantaranatthivigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi pañcahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Vipākapaccayo [V 0.0389] vipākapaccayattaṃ avijahantova hetuadhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayakammaāhāraindriyajhānamaggasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi cuddasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Āhārapaccaye kabaḷīkāro āhāro āhārapaccayattaṃ avijahantova atthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi dvīhākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Sesā tayo āhārapaccayattaṃ avijahantāva yathānurūpaṃ adhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayakammavipākaindriyasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi ekādasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchanti.

The kamma condition, without abandoning its nature as a kamma condition, when simultaneous, becomes a multiple condition in nine other modes through co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, result, nutriment, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. The non-simultaneous kamma becomes a multiple condition in five other modes through decisive support, immediate contiguity, contiguity, absence, and disappearance. The result condition, without abandoning its nature as a result condition, becomes a multiple condition in fourteen other modes through root, dominance, co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, kamma, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. In the nutriment condition, edible food, without abandoning its nature as a nutriment condition, becomes a multiple condition in two other modes through presence and non-disappearance. The remaining three nutriments, without abandoning their nature as nutriment conditions, become multiple conditions in eleven other modes, as appropriate, through dominance, co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, kamma, result, faculty, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance.

Indriyapaccaye rūpino pañcindriyā indriyapaccayattaṃ avijahantāva nissayapurejātavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi pañcahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchanti. Rūpajīvitindriyampi indriyapaccayattaṃ avijahantaññeva atthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi dvīhākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Arūpino indriyānipi yathānurūpaṃ indriyapaccayattaṃ avijahantāneva hetuadhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākaāhārajhānamaggasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi terasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchanti. Jhānapaccayo jhānapaccayattaṃ avijahantova yathānurūpaṃ [M 0.0392] sahajātaaññamaññanissayavipākaindriyamaggasampayuttavippayuttaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi dasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Maggapaccayo maggapaccayattaṃ avijahantova yathānurūpaṃ jhānapaccaye vuttānaṃ dasannaṃ hetuadhipatīnañcāti imesaṃ vasena aparehipi dvādasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati.

In the faculty condition, the five material faculties, without abandoning their nature as faculty conditions, become multiple conditions in five other modes through dependence, pre-nascence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. The material life faculty also, without abandoning its nature as a faculty condition, becomes a multiple condition in two other modes through presence and non-disappearance. The immaterial faculties also, without abandoning their nature as faculty conditions, become multiple conditions in thirteen other modes, as appropriate, through root, dominance, co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, result, nutriment, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. The jhāna condition, without abandoning its nature as a jhāna condition, becomes a multiple condition in ten other modes, as appropriate, through co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, result, faculty, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. The path condition, without abandoning its nature as a path condition, becomes a multiple condition in twelve other modes, as appropriate, through the ten mentioned for the jhāna condition, and also through root and dominance.

Sampayuttapaccayo sampayuttapaccayattaṃ avijahantova yathānurūpaṃ hetuadhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayakammavipākaāhāraindriyajhānamaggaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena aparehipi terasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Vippayuttapaccayo vippayuttapaccayattaṃ avijahantova anantarasamanantaraāsevanasampayuttanatthivigatasaṅkhāte cha paccaye apanetvā sesānaṃ vasena yathānurūpaṃ aparehipi sattarasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Tattha rūpassa ca arūpassa ca paccayavibhāgo veditabbo. Atthipaccayo atthipaccayattaṃ avijahantova anantarasamanantaraāsevananatthivigatasaṅkhāte pañca paccaye apanetvā sesānaṃ vasena yathānurūpaṃ aparehi aṭṭhārasahākārehi anekapaccayabhāvaṃ gacchati. Natthipaccayavigatapaccayā anantarapaccayasadisā[V 0.0390]. Avigatapaccayo atthipaccayasadisoyevāti evamettha ekapaccayassa anekapaccayabhāvatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

The association condition, without abandoning its nature as an association condition, becomes a multiple condition in thirteen other modes, as appropriate, through root, dominance, co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, presence, and non-disappearance. The dissociation condition, without abandoning its nature as a dissociation condition, having excluded the six conditions—immediate contiguity, contiguity, repetition, association, absence, and disappearance—becomes a multiple condition in seventeen other modes, as appropriate, through the remaining conditions. Here, the division of conditions regarding material and immaterial phenomena should be understood. The presence condition, without abandoning its nature as a presence condition, having excluded the five conditions—immediate contiguity, contiguity, repetition, absence, and disappearance—becomes a multiple condition in eighteen other modes, as appropriate, through the remaining conditions. The absence condition and the disappearance condition are similar to the immediate contiguity condition. The non-disappearance condition is just like the presence condition. Thus, the determination should be understood from this analysis of how a single condition also becomes a multiple condition.

Paccayasabhāgatoti etesu hi catuvīsatiyā paccayesu anantarasamanantaraanantarūpanissayaāsevananatthivigatā sabhāgā, tathā ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayāti iminā upāyenettha paccayasabhāgatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Similarity of conditions: Among these twenty-four conditions, immediate contiguity, contiguity, immediate decisive support, repetition, absence, and disappearance are of a similar nature. Likewise, by this method, the determination regarding the similarity of conditions should also be understood concerning the object condition, the object dominance condition, and the object decisive support condition.

Paccayavisabhāgatoti purejātapaccayo panettha pacchājātapaccayena visabhāgo, tathā sampayuttapaccayo vippayuttapaccayena, atthipaccayo natthipaccayena, vigatapaccayo avigatapaccayenāti iminā upāyenettha paccayavisabhāgatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Regarding the dissimilarity of conditions: Here, the pre-nascence condition is dissimilar to the post-nascence condition; likewise, the associated condition to the dissociated condition, the presence condition to the absence condition, and the disappearance condition to the non-disappearance condition. Thus, through this method, the dissimilarity of conditions should also be understood in this analysis.

Yugaḷakatoti etesu ca atthasarikkhatāya, saddasarikkhatāya, kālapaṭipakkhatāya, hetuphalatāya, aññamaññapaṭipakkhatāyāti imehi kāraṇehi yugaḷakato viññātabbo vinicchayo. Anantarasamanantarā hi atthasarikkhatāya ekaṃ yugaḷakaṃ nāma; nissayūpanissayā saddasarikkhatāya, purejātapacchājātā [M 0.0393] kālapaṭipakkhatāya, kammapaccayavipākapaccayā hetuphalatāya, sampayuttavippayuttapaccayā aññamaññapaṭipakkhatāya ekaṃ yugaḷakaṃ nāma, tathā atthinatthipaccayā, vigatāvigatapaccayā cāti evamettha yugaḷakatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo. Janakājanakatoti etesu ca anantarasamanantarānantarūpanissayapakatūpanissayāsevanapaccayā nānākkhaṇiko, kammapaccayo, natthivigatapaccayāti ime paccayā janakāyeva, na ajanakā. Pacchājātapaccayo kevalaṃ upatthambhakoyeva, na janako. Sesā janakā ca ajanakā ca upatthambhakā cāti attho. Evamettha janakājanakatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Regarding pairs: In these, the analysis should be understood as being paired due to these reasons: similarity in meaning, similarity in sound, opposition in time, cause and effect, and mutual opposition. For instance, contiguity and immediacy form one pair due to similarity in meaning; dependence and decisive support due to similarity in sound; pre-nascence and post-nascence due to opposition in time; the kamma condition and the result condition due to cause and effect; the associated condition and the dissociated condition due to mutual opposition; likewise, the presence and absence conditions, and the disappearance and non-disappearance conditions. Thus, in this analysis, the analysis should also be understood in terms of being paired. Regarding generative and non-generative conditions: Among these, contiguity, immediacy, immediate decisive support, natural decisive support, repetition, the kamma condition of different moments, and the absence and disappearance conditions are solely generative, not non-generative. The post-nascence condition is merely supportive, not generative. The meaning is that the remaining conditions are generative, non-generative, and supportive. Thus, in this analysis, the analysis should also be understood in terms of generative and non-generative conditions.

Sabbaṭṭhānikāsabbaṭṭhānikatoti etesu ca sahajātanissayaatthiavigatapaccayā sabbaṭṭhānikā nāma, sabbesaṃ saṅkhatānaṃ rūpārūpadhammānaṃ ṭhānabhūtā kāraṇabhūtāti attho. Etehi vinā uppajjamāno ekadhammopi natthīti. Ārammaṇaārammaṇādhipatianantarasamanantarānantarūpanissayapakatūpanissayāsevanasampayuttanatthivigatapaccayā asabbaṭṭhānikā nāma. Na sabbesaṃ rūpārūpadhammānaṃ ṭhānabhūtā, arūpakkhandhānaññeva pana ṭhānabhūtā kāraṇabhūtāti attho. Arūpadhammāyeva hi etehi uppajjanti, na rūpadhammā. Purejātapacchājātāpi asabbaṭṭhānikā arūparūpānaññeva [V 0.0391] yathākkamena paccayabhāvato. Vuttāvasesāpi ekaccānaṃ rūpārūpadhammānaṃ uppattihetuto na sabbaṭṭhānikāti evamettha sabbaṭṭhānikā sabbaṭṭhānikatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Regarding universal and non-universal conditions: Among these, the co-nascence, dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions are called universal, meaning that they are the basis and cause for all conditioned phenomena, both material and immaterial. This means that not a single phenomenon arises without them. The object, object predominance, contiguity, immediacy, immediate decisive support, natural decisive support, repetition, associated, absence, and disappearance conditions are called non-universal. This means that they are not the basis for all material and immaterial phenomena, but only the basis and cause for the immaterial aggregates. Indeed, only immaterial phenomena arise through these, not material phenomena. Even the pre-nascence and post-nascence conditions are non-universal, as they are conditions for immaterial and material phenomena respectively. The remaining conditions, too, are non-universal because they are the cause of the arising of only some material and immaterial phenomena. Thus, in this analysis, the analysis should also be understood in terms of universal and non-universal conditions.

Rūpaṃ rūpassātiādivikappatoti etesu ca catuvīsatiyā paccayesu ekapaccayopi ekantena rūpameva hutvā rūpasseva paccayo nāma natthi, ekantena pana rūpaṃ hutvā arūpasseva paccayo nāma atthi. Kataro panesoti? Purejātapaccayo. Purejātapaccayo hi ekantena rūpameva hutvā arūpasseva paccayo hoti. Ekantena rūpameva hutvā rūpārūpasseva paccayo nāmātipi natthi, ekantena pana arūpaṃ hutvā arūpasseva paccayo nāma atthi. Kataro panesoti? Anantarasamanantaraāsevanasampayuttanatthivigatavasena chabbidho. So hi sabbopi ekantena arūpameva hutvā arūpasseva paccayo hoti. Ekantena arūpameva hutvāpi ekantena rūpasseva paccayo nāmātipi atthi. Kataro panesoti? Pacchājātapaccayo. So hi ekantena [M 0.0394] arūpaṃ hutvā rūpasseva paccayo hoti; ekantena pana arūpadhammova hutvā rūpārūpānaṃ paccayopi atthi. Kataro panesoti? Hetukammavipākajhānamaggavasena pañcavidho. So hi sabbopi ekantena arūpameva hutvā rūpadhammānaṃ arūpadhammānampi paccayo hoti. Ekantena pana rūpārūpameva hutvā rūpasseva paccayo nāmātipi natthi, arūpasseva pana hoti. Kataro panesoti? Ārammaṇapaccayo ceva upanissayapaccayo ca. Idañhi dvayaṃ ekantena rūpārūpameva hutvā arūpasseva paccayo hoti. Ekantena rūpārūpameva hutvā pana rūpārūpasseva paccayo nāmātipi atthi. Kataro panesoti? Adhipatisahajātaaññamaññanissayaāhāraindriyavippayuttaatthiavigatavasena navavidho. So hi sabbopi ekantena rūpārūpameva hutvā rūpārūpasseva paccayo hotīti evamettha rūpaṃ rūpassātiādivikappatopi viññātabbo vinicchayo.

Regarding the classifications such as 'form is a condition for form': Among these twenty-four conditions, there is no condition that is exclusively form and serves only as a condition for form. However, there is a condition that is exclusively form and serves only as a condition for non-form. Which one is that? The pre-nascence condition. The pre-nascence condition is exclusively form and serves only as a condition for non-form. There is no condition that is exclusively form and serves as a condition for both form and non-form. However, there is a condition that is exclusively non-form and serves only as a condition for non-form. Which one is that? The sixfold condition consisting of contiguity, immediacy, repetition, association, absence, and disappearance. All of these are exclusively non-form and serve only as a condition for non-form. There is also a condition that is exclusively non-form and serves only as a condition for form. Which one is that? The post-nascence condition. This is exclusively non-form and serves only as a condition for form. There is also a condition that is exclusively non-form and serves as a condition for both form and non-form. Which one is that? The fivefold condition consisting of root, kamma, result, jhāna, and path. All of these are exclusively non-form and serve as a condition for both form and non-form phenomena. There is no condition that is exclusively both form and non-form and serves only as a condition for form, but there is one that serves only as a condition for non-form. Which one is that? The object condition and the decisive support condition. These two are exclusively both form and non-form and serve only as a condition for non-form. There is also a condition that is exclusively both form and non-form and serves as a condition for both form and non-form. Which one is that? The ninefold condition consisting of predominance, co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, nutriment, faculty, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance. All of these are exclusively both form and non-form and serve as a condition for both form and non-form. Thus, in this analysis, the analysis should also be understood in terms of the classifications such as 'form is a condition for form'.

Bhavabhedatoti imesu pana catuvīsatiyā paccayesu pañcavokārabhave tāva na koci paccayo na labbhati nāma. Catuvokārabhave pana tayo purejātapacchājātavippayuttapaccaye apanetvā sesā ekavīsatimeva labbhanti. Ekavokārabhave sahajātaaññamaññanissayakammaindriyaatthiavigatavasena satteva labbhanti. Bāhire pana anindriyabaddharūpe sahajātaaññamaññanissayaatthiavigatavasena pañceva labbhantīti evamettha bhavabhedatopi viññātabbo vinicchayoti.

Regarding the distinction of planes of existence: Among these twenty-four conditions, in the five-aggregate plane of existence, there is no condition that is not found. In the four-aggregate plane of existence, only twenty-one are found, excluding the three conditions—pre-nascence, post-nascence, and dissociation. In the one-aggregate plane of existence, only seven are found: co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, kamma, faculty, presence, and non-disappearance. In external non-faculty-bound material phenomena, only five are found: co-nascence, mutuality, dependence, presence, and non-disappearance. Thus, in this analysis, the analysis should also be understood in terms of the distinction of planes of existence.

Paccayaniddesavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the explanation of the Chapter on the Exposition of Conditions.

Pucchāvāro

The Chapter of Questions

1. Paccayānulomavaṇṇanā

1. Exposition of the Positive Method

Evaṃ [V 0.0392] anulomapaṭṭhānādīsu tikapaṭṭhānādivasena catuvīsatisamantapaṭṭhānasamodhāne paṭṭhānamahāpakaraṇe ye tikādayo nissāya niddiṭṭhattā etaṃ tikapaṭṭhānaṃ, dukapaṭṭhānaṃ…pe… dukadukapaṭṭhānanti vuttaṃ. Te anāmasitvā yesaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena te tikādayo vibhattā, te paccaye eva tāva iminā mātikānikkhepapaccayavibhaṅgasaṅkhātena vārena uddesato ca niddesato ca dassetvā, idāni ye tikādayo nissāya niddiṭṭhattā etaṃ tikapaṭṭhānaṃ, dukapaṭṭhānaṃ…pe… dukadukapaṭṭhānanti vuttaṃ. Te [M 0.0395] tikādayo imesaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena vitthāretvā dassetuṃ ekekaṃ tikadukaṃ nissāya sattahi mahāvārehi desanā katā. Tesaṃ imāni nāmāni – paṭiccavāro, sahajātavāro, paccayavāro, nissayavāro, saṃsaṭṭhavāro, sampayuttavāro, pañhāvāroti.

Thus, in the Anuloma Paṭṭhāna and so forth, in the comprehensive presentation of the twenty-four universal relations by way of the Triad-Paṭṭhāna, etc., within the Great Treatise of Relations, it is called the Triad-Paṭṭhāna, the Dyad-Paṭṭhāna… and so forth… the Dyad-Dyad-Paṭṭhāna, because it is designated by relying on these triads and so forth. Having first, without touching upon them, shown the very conditions by which those triads and so forth are analyzed in this section called the Mātikānikkhepa Paccayavibhaṅga, both in summary and in detail, now, in order to explain them in detail by means of these conditions, a discourse is given in seven great sections, relying on each triad and dyad. These are their names: the Paṭiccavāra, the Sahajātavāra, the Paccayavāra, the Nissayavāra, the Saṃsaṭṭhavāra, the Sampayuttavāra, and the Pañhāvāra.

Tattha “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo”ti evaṃ paṭiccābhidhānavasena vutto paṭiccavāro nāma. Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ sahajāto kusalo dhammo”ti evaṃ sahajātābhidhānavasena vutto sahajātavāro nāma. So purimena paṭiccavārena atthato ninnānākaraṇo. Paṭiccābhidhānavasena bujjhanakānaṃ vasena pana paṭhamo vutto, sahajātābhidhānavasena bujjhanakānaṃ vasena dutiyo. Dvīsupi cetesu rūpārūpadhammavasena paccayā ceva paccayuppannadhammā ca veditabbā. Te ca kho sahajātāva, na purejātapacchājātā labbhanti. “Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā kusalo dhammo”ti evaṃ paccayābhidhānavasena vutto pana paccayavāro nāma. Sopi purimavāradvayaṃ viya rūpārūpadhammavaseneva veditabbo. Paccayo panettha purejātopi labbhati. Ayamassa purimavāradvayato viseso. Tadanantaro “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ nissāya kusalo dhammo”ti evaṃ nissayābhidhānavasena vutto nissayavāro nāma. So purimena paccayavārena atthato ninnānākaraṇo. Paccayābhidhānavasena bujjhanakānaṃ vasena pana paṭhamo vutto, nissayābhidhānavasena bujjhanakānaṃ vasena dutiyo. Tato paraṃ “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ saṃsaṭṭho kusalo dhammo”ti evaṃ saṃsaṭṭhābhidhānavasena vutto saṃsaṭṭhavāro nāma. “Kusalaṃ dhammaṃ sampayutto kusalo dhammo”ti evaṃ sampayuttābhidhānavasena vutto sampayuttavāro nāma. So purimena saṃsaṭṭhavārena atthato ninnānākaraṇo. Saṃsaṭṭhābhidhānavasena bujjhanakānaṃ vasena pana paṭhamo vutto, sampayuttābhidhānavasena [V 0.0393] dutiyo. Dvīsupi cetesu arūpadhammavaseneva paccayā paccayuppannā ca veditabbā. Sattamavāre pana yasmā “kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo”tiādinā nayena te te pañhe uddharitvā puna “kusalā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhāna”ntiādinā nayena sabbepi te pañhā nijjaṭā niggumbā ca katvā vibhattā, tasmā so vāro pañhānaṃ sādhukaṃ vibhattattā pañhāvārotveva saṅkhyaṃ gato. Rūpārūpadhammavaseneva panettha paccayāpi paccayuppannāpi veditabbā.

Here, the division called the Paṭiccavāra is stated by way of the designation 'dependence' as follows: 'A wholesome phenomenon depends on a wholesome phenomenon.' The division called the Sahajātavāra is stated by way of the designation 'co-nascence' as follows: 'A wholesome phenomenon is co-nascent with a wholesome phenomenon.' This does not differ in meaning from the preceding Paṭiccavāra. However, the first is stated for the sake of those who understand by way of the designation 'dependence,' and the second for the sake of those who understand by way of the designation 'co-nascence.' In both these cases, conditions and condition-arisen phenomena should be understood in terms of material and immaterial phenomena. These are only co-nascent; prior-arisen or later-arisen are not obtained. The division called the Paccayavāra, however, is stated by way of the designation 'condition' as follows: 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon.' This too, like the preceding two divisions, should be understood in terms of material and immaterial phenomena. Here, however, a prior-arisen condition is also obtained. This is its distinction from the preceding two divisions. Following that, the division called the Nissayavāra is stated by way of the designation 'support' as follows: 'A wholesome phenomenon relies on a wholesome phenomenon.' This does not differ in meaning from the preceding Paccayavāra. However, the first is stated for the sake of those who understand by way of the designation 'condition,' and the second for the sake of those who understand by way of the designation 'support.' Next, the division called the Saṃsaṭṭhavāra is stated by way of the designation 'association' as follows: 'A wholesome phenomenon is associated with a wholesome phenomenon.' The division called the Sampayuttavāra is stated by way of the designation 'conjunction' as follows: 'A wholesome phenomenon is conjoined with a wholesome phenomenon.' This does not differ in meaning from the preceding Saṃsaṭṭhavāra. However, the first is stated for the sake of those who understand by way of the designation 'association,' and the second by way of the designation 'conjunction.' In both these cases, conditions and condition-arisen phenomena should be understood only in terms of immaterial phenomena. In the seventh division, however, since those various questions are extracted by such a method as 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition,' and then all those questions are made clear and disentangled by such a method as 'Wholesome roots are conditions for the associated aggregates,' therefore that division is reckoned as the Pañhāvāra due to the questions being thoroughly analyzed. Here too, conditions and condition-arisen phenomena should be understood in terms of material and immaterial phenomena.

Tattha [M 0.0396] yo tāva esa sabbapaṭhamo paṭiccavāro nāma, so uddesato niddesato ca duvidho hoti. Tattha uddesavāro paṭhamo, pucchāvārotipi vuccati. Paṇṇattivārotipi tasseva nāmaṃ. So hi kusalādayo paṭicca kusalādīnaṃ hetupaccayādīnaṃ vasena uddiṭṭhattā uddesavāro, kusalādayo paṭicca hetupaccayādivasena kusalādīnaṃ uppattiyā pucchitattā pucchāvāro, kusalādayo paṭicca hetupaccayādivasena kusalādīnaṃ uppattiyā paññāpitattā paṇṇattivārotipi vutto.

Here, that very first division called the Paṭiccavāra is twofold: by way of brief statement and by way of detailed explanation. Among them, the brief statement division is first; it is also called the Question Division. The Designation Division is also a name for it. For it is called the brief statement division because wholesome states and so forth are briefly stated by way of root condition and other conditions, dependent on wholesome states and so forth. It is called the Question Division because the arising of wholesome states and so forth by way of root condition and other conditions, dependent on wholesome states and so forth, is questioned. And it is called the Designation Division because the arising of wholesome states and so forth by way of root condition and other conditions, dependent on wholesome states and so forth, is designated.

25-34. Tattha siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayāti parikappapucchā. Ayañhettha attho – yo kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayā, kiṃ so kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca siyāti atha vā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca yo kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya, so hetupaccayā siyāti ayamettha attho. Tattha paṭīti sadisatthe vattati. Sadisapuggalo hi paṭipuggalo, sadisabhāgo ca paṭibhāgoti vuccati. Iccāti gamanussukkavacanametaṃ. Ubhayaṃ ekato katvā paṭiccāti paṭigantvā sahuppattisaṅkhātena sadisabhāvena patvā, tena saddhiṃ ekato uppattibhāvaṃ upagantvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Kusalo dhammoti evaṃ sahuppattibhāvena kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo dhammo uppajjeyya hetupaccayāti pucchati. Atha vā paṭiccāti paccayaṃ katvā. Taṃ pana paccayakaraṇaṃ purejātepi paccaye labbhati sahajātepi. Idha sahajātaṃ adhippetaṃ. Siyā kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalotiādīsupi eseva nayo. Tattha kiñcāpi sahajātavasena kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo natthi, imasmiṃ pana pucchāvāre yampi vissajjiyamānaṃ atthato labbhati, yampi na labbhati, taṃ sabbaṃ pucchāvasena uddhaṭaṃ. Parato pana vissajjane yaṃ na labbhati, taṃ pahāya yaṃ labbhati, tadeva vissajjitaṃ.

Herein, 'Might a wholesome phenomenon arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition?' is a hypothetical question. The meaning here is this: 'If a wholesome phenomenon were to arise by way of root condition, might it be dependent on a wholesome phenomenon?' Or, 'If a wholesome phenomenon were to arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, might it be by way of root condition?' This is the meaning here. Here, 'paṭi' operates in the sense of 'similar.' For a similar person is indeed called a counterpart, and a similar portion is called a counterpart portion. The word 'icca' is an expression indicating going. Taking both together, 'paṭicca' means having gone towards, having reached by way of similarity, which is co-arising, and thus having entered into the state of arising together with it. Thus, by way of the nature of co-arising, it asks: 'Might a wholesome phenomenon arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition?' Alternatively, 'paṭicca' means making it a condition. That making-of-a-condition is obtained both in a prior-arisen condition and in a co-arisen condition. Here, the co-arisen is intended. The same method applies to 'Might an unwholesome phenomenon arise dependent on a wholesome phenomenon?' and so forth. Herein, although in terms of co-arising there is no unwholesome phenomenon dependent on a wholesome phenomenon, in this Question Section, whatever is obtained in terms of meaning when being answered, and whatever is not obtained, all that is set forth by way of a question. Later, however, in the answering, what is not obtained is abandoned, and only what is obtained is answered.

Evamettha pucchānaṃ atthañceva pucchāgatiñca ñatvā idāni gaṇanavasena pucchāparicchedo veditabbo[V 0.0394]. Ettha hi “kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccā”ti kusalapadaṃ ādiṃ katvā kusalākusalābyākatantā tisso pucchā, puna tadevādiṃ katvā kusalābyākatādivasena dukappabhedantā tisso, puna tadevādiṃ katvā tikantā ca ekā, evaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccāti kusalādikā [M 0.0397] satta pucchā, tathā akusalādikā, tathā abyākatādikā, tathā kusalābyākatādikā, akusalābyākatādikā, kusalākusalādikā, kusalākusalābyākatādikāti sabbāpi sattannaṃ sattakānaṃ vasena kusalattikaṃ nissāya hetupaccaye ekūnapaññāsaṃ pucchā.

Thus, having understood both the meaning of the questions and their course, the delimitation of questions should now be understood by way of enumeration. Herein, taking the term 'wholesome' as the beginning in 'dependent on a wholesome phenomenon,' there are three questions ending with wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. Again, taking that same term as the beginning, there are three questions ending with the dyad-divisions, by way of wholesome-indeterminate and so forth. Again, taking that same term as the beginning, there is one question ending with the triad. Thus, taking 'dependent on a wholesome phenomenon' as the beginning, there are seven questions beginning with the wholesome. Similarly, there are seven beginning with the unwholesome, seven beginning with the indeterminate, seven beginning with the wholesome-indeterminate, seven beginning with the unwholesome-indeterminate, seven beginning with the wholesome-unwholesome, and seven beginning with the wholesome-unwholesome-indeterminate. In all, relying on the wholesome triad, there are forty-nine questions in the root condition, by way of seven sets of seven.

Tattha ekamūlakāvasānā nava, ekamūladukāvasānā nava, ekamūlatikāvasānā tisso, dukamūlaekāvasānā nava, dukamūladukāvasānā nava, dukamūlatikāvasānā tisso, tikamūlaekāvasānā tisso, tikamūladukāvasānā tisso, tikamūlatikāvasānā ekāti evametā mūlavasenāpi veditabbā. Yathā ca hetupaccaye ekūnapaññāsaṃ, ārammaṇapaccayādīsupi tathevāti sabbesupi catuvīsatiyā paccayesu –

Herein, there are nine [questions] with a single-term basis and a single-term ending; nine with a single-term basis and a dyad ending; three with a single-term basis and a triad ending; nine with a dyad basis and a single-term ending; nine with a dyad basis and a dyad ending; three with a dyad basis and a triad ending; three with a triad basis and a single-term ending; three with a triad basis and a dyad ending; and one with a triad basis and a triad ending. Thus, these should also be understood by way of their bases. And just as there are forty-nine in the root condition, so too in the object condition and so forth. Thus, in all twenty-four conditions—

Sahassamekañca sataṃ, chasattati punāparā;

Pucchā sampiṇḍitā honti, nayamhi ekamūlake.

One thousand, one hundred, and seventy-six more; the questions are thus summed up in the single-basis method.

35-36. Tato paraṃ hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayāti dumūlakanayo āraddho. Tattha hetārammaṇaduko…pe… hetuavigatadukoti hetupaccayena saddhiṃ tevīsati dukā honti. Tesu hetupaccaye viya hetārammaṇadukepi ekūnapaññāsaṃ pucchā, tāsu pāḷiyaṃ dveyeva dassitā. Yathā ca hetārammaṇaduke ekūnapaññāsaṃ tathā hetādhipatidukādīsupi. Tattha paṭhamapucchāvasena hetādhipatiduko, hetānantaraduko, hetusamanantaradukoti paṭipāṭiyā tayo duke dassetvā pariyosāne hetuavigataduko dassito, sesaṃ saṅkhittaṃ. Pucchāparicchedo panettha evaṃ veditabbo.

35-36. Thereafter, the two-basis method is commenced, [starting with] 'root condition, object condition.' Herein, the dyad of root-object… and so on… up to the dyad of root-non-disappearance—thus, there are twenty-three dyads together with the root condition. Among these, just as in the root condition, so also in the root-object dyad there are forty-nine questions, of which only two are shown in the Pāli. And just as there are forty-nine in the root-object dyad, so too in the root-dominance dyad and so forth. Herein, by way of the first question, three dyads are shown in sequence—namely, the root-dominance dyad, the root-proximity dyad, and the root-contiguity dyad—and at the end the root-non-disappearance dyad is shown; the rest is condensed. The delimitation of questions here should be understood thus:

Sahassamekañca sataṃ, sattavīsatimeva ca;

Dukesu tevīsatiyā, pucchā honti dumūlake.

One thousand, one hundred, and twenty-seven indeed; in the twenty-three dyads, such are the questions in the two-basis method.

37. Tato paraṃ hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayāti timūlakanayo āraddho. Tattha [V 0.0395] hetārammaṇadukena saddhiṃ adhipatipaccayādīsu bāvīsatiyā paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena bāvīsati tikā honti. Tesu paṭhamapucchāvasena paṭhamattikañca dutiyattikañca dassetvā pariyosānatiko dassito, sesaṃ saṅkhittaṃ. Yathā pana [M 0.0398] dukesu, evaṃ tikesupi ekamekasmiṃ tike ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā sabbesupi bāvīsatiyā tikesu –

37. Thereafter, the three-basis method is begun with 'root condition, object condition, dominance condition.' Herein, together with the root-object dyad, twenty-two triads are formed by combining each of the twenty-two conditions beginning with the dominance condition. Among these, the first and second triads are shown by way of the first question, and the final triad is shown; the rest is condensed. And just as in the dyads, so too in the triads: with forty-nine in each triad, in all twenty-two triads—

Sahassamekaṃ pucchānaṃ, aṭṭhasattatimeva ca;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, nayamhi tikamūlake.

One thousand and seventy-eight questions indeed; by calculation, such are the questions in the three-basis method.

38. Tato paraṃ hetupaccayā ārammaṇapaccayā adhipatipaccayā anantarapaccayāti catumūlakanayo āraddho. Tattha paṭhamattikena saddhiṃ anantarapaccayādīsu ekavīsatiyā paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena ekavīsati catukkā honti. Tesu dve catukke dassetvā sesaṃ saṅkhittaṃ. Idhāpi ekamekasmiṃ catukke ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā sabbesupi ekavīsatiyā catukkesu –

38. Thereafter, the four-basis method is begun with 'root condition, object condition, dominance condition, proximity condition.' Herein, together with the first triad, twenty-one tetrads are formed by combining each of the twenty-one conditions beginning with the proximity condition. Among these, two tetrads are shown, and the rest are condensed. Here too, with forty-nine in each tetrad, in all twenty-one tetrads—

Sahassamekaṃ pucchānaṃ, ekūnatiṃsa punāparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, nayamhi catumūlake.

One thousand and twenty-nine more; by calculation, such are the questions in the four-basis method.

Tato paraṃ pañcamūlakaṃ ādiṃ katvā yāva sabbamūlakā desanā katā, taṃ sabbaṃ saṅkhipitvā heṭṭhā vuttañca upari vattabbañca ekato katvā pāḷiyaṃ “ekamūlakaṃ, dumūlakaṃ, timūlakaṃ, catumūlakaṃ, pañcamūlakaṃ, sabbamūlakaṃ asammuyhantena vitthāretabba”nti nayo dassito. Tattha ekamūlakādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ vuttameva. Pañcamūlake pana paṭhamacatukkena saddhiṃ samanantarapaccayādīsu samavīsatiyā paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena samavīsati pañcakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

Thereafter, the teaching was given, beginning with the five-root method up to the all-root method. By condensing all that, and by combining what was said below with what is to be said above, the method is shown in the Pāli text thus: 'The one-root, two-root, three-root, four-root, five-root, and all-root methods should be expounded without confusion.' Therein, what was to be said about the one-root method, etc., has already been said. But in the five-root method, together with the first tetrad, twenty pentads are formed by combining each of the twenty conditions beginning with the contiguity condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni nava pucchānaṃ, asīti ca punāparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, nayamhi pañcamūlake.

Nine hundred questions, and eighty more besides; by calculation, these are the questions in the five-root method.

Chamūlake paṭhamapañcakena saddhiṃ sahajātapaccayādīsu ekūnavīsatiyā paccayesu ekamekassa [V 0.0396] yojanāvasena ekūnavīsati chakkā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the six-root method, together with the first pentad, nineteen sextads are formed by combining each of the nineteen conditions beginning with the conascence condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni nava pucchānaṃ, ekatiṃsa tatoparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, nayamhi chakkamūlake.

Nine hundred questions, and thirty-one beyond that; by calculation, these are the questions in the six-root method.

Sattamūlake [M 0.0399] paṭhamachakkena saddhiṃ aññamaññapaccayādīsu aṭṭhārasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena aṭṭhārasa sattakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the seven-root method, together with the first sextad, eighteen septads are formed by combining each of the eighteen conditions beginning with the mutuality condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni aṭṭha pucchānaṃ, dvāsīti ca tatoparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, nayamhi sattamūlake.

Eight hundred questions, and eighty-two beyond that; by calculation, these are the questions in the seven-root method.

Aṭṭhamūlake paṭhamasattakena saddhiṃ nissayapaccayādīsu sattarasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena sattarasa aṭṭhakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the eight-root method, together with the first septad, seventeen octads are formed by combining each of the seventeen conditions beginning with the dependence condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni aṭṭha pucchānaṃ, tettiṃsā ca tatoparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, nayamhi aṭṭhamūlake.

Eight hundred questions, and thirty-three beyond that; by calculation, these are the questions in the eight-root method.

Navamūlake paṭhamaaṭṭhakena saddhiṃ upanissayapaccayādīsu soḷasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena soḷasa navakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the nine-root method, together with the first octad, sixteen nonads are formed by combining each of the sixteen conditions beginning with the decisive support condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni [V 0.0397] satta pucchānaṃ, caturāsīti tatoparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, nayamhi navamūlake.

Seven hundred questions, and eighty-four beyond that; by calculation, these are the questions in the nine-root method.

Dasamūlake paṭhamanavakena saddhiṃ purejātapaccayādīsu pannarasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena pannarasa dasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the ten-root method, together with the first nonad, fifteen decads are formed by combining each of the fifteen conditions beginning with the prenascence condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni satta pucchānaṃ, pañcatiṃsa tatoparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, nayamhi dasamūlake.

Seven hundred questions, and thirty-five beyond that; by calculation, these are the questions in the ten-root method.

Ekādasamūlake paṭhamadasakena saddhiṃ pacchājātapaccayādīsu cuddasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena cuddasa ekādasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the eleven-root method, together with the first decad, fourteen hendecads are formed by combining each of the fourteen conditions beginning with the postnascence condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Cha satāni ca pucchānaṃ, chaḷāsīti tatoparā;

Nayamhi pucchā gaṇitā, ekādasakamūlake.

Six hundred questions, and eighty-six beyond that; in this method are the questions counted, in the eleven-root method.

Dvādasamūlake paṭhamaekādasakena saddhiṃ āsevanapaccayādīsu terasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena terasa dvādasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the twelve-root method, together with the first hendecad, thirteen duodecads are formed by combining each of the thirteen conditions beginning with the repetition condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Cha [M 0.0400] satāni ca pucchānaṃ, sattatiṃsa tatoparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, naye dvādasamūlake.

Six hundred questions, and thirty-seven beyond that; by calculation, these are the questions in the twelve-root method.

Terasamūlake paṭhamadvādasakena saddhiṃ kammapaccayādīsu dvādasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena dvādasa terasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the thirteen-root method, together with the first duodecad, twelve tredecads are formed by combining each of the twelve conditions beginning with the kamma condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni pañca pucchānaṃ, aṭṭhāsīti punāparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, naye terasamūlake.

Five hundred questions, and eighty-eight more besides; by calculation, these are the questions in the thirteen-root method.

Cuddasamūlake paṭhamaterasakena saddhiṃ vipākapaccayādīsu ekādasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena ekādasa cuddasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the fourteen-root method, together with the first tredecad, eleven quattuordecads are formed by combining each of the eleven conditions beginning with the result condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni pañca pucchānaṃ, tiṃsa cātha navāparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, naye cuddasamūlake.

Five hundred questions, and then thirty and nine more; by calculation, these are the questions in the fourteen-root method.

Pannarasamūlake [V 0.0398] paṭhamacuddasakena saddhiṃ āhārapaccayādīsu dasasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena dasa pannarasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the fifteen-root method, together with the first quattuordecad, ten quindecads are formed by combining each of the ten conditions beginning with the nutriment condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni cattāri pucchānaṃ, navuti ca tatoparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, naye pannarasamūlake.

Four hundred questions, and ninety beyond that; by calculation, these are the questions in the fifteen-root method.

Soḷasamūlake paṭhamapannarasakena saddhiṃ indriyapaccayādīsu navasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena nava soḷasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the sixteen-root method, together with the first quindecad, nine sexdecads are formed by combining each of the nine conditions beginning with the faculty condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni cattāri cattā-līsekā ceva punāparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, naye soḷasamūlake.

Four hundred questions, and forty-one more besides; by calculation, these are the questions in the sixteen-root method.

Sattarasamūlake paṭhamasoḷasakena saddhiṃ jhānapaccayādīsu aṭṭhasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena aṭṭha sattarasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the seventeen-root method, together with the first sexdecad, eight septendecads are formed by combining each of the eight conditions beginning with the jhāna condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni tīṇi pucchānaṃ, navuti dve punāparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, naye sattarasamūlake.

Three hundred questions, and ninety-two more besides; by calculation, these are the questions in the seventeen-root method.

Aṭṭhārasamūlake [M 0.0401] paṭhamasattarasakena saddhiṃ maggapaccayādīsu sattasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena satta aṭṭhārasakā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the eighteen-root method, together with the first septendecad, seven octodecads are formed by combining each of the seven conditions beginning with the path condition. In each of these, having made forty-nine—

Satāni tīṇi pucchānaṃ, tecattārīsameva ca;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, naye aṭṭhārasamūlake.

Three hundred questions, and forty-three as well; by calculation, these are the questions in the eighteen-root method.

Ekūnavīsatimūlake paṭhamaaṭṭhārasakena saddhiṃ sampayuttapaccayādīsu chasu paccayesu ekamekassa yojanāvasena cha ekūnavīsatikā honti. Tesu ekamekasmiṃ ekūnapaññāsaṃ katvā –

In the nineteen-root method, together with the first octodecuplet, six sets of nineteen are formed by combining each of the six conditions beginning with the association condition. In each of these, forty-nine are made—

Dve [V 0.0399] satā navuti ceva, catasso ca punāparā;

Pucchā gaṇanato honti, naye ekūnavīsatike.

Two hundred and ninety-four questions are counted in the nineteen-root method.
