Evaṃ kiriyābyākatassa ārammaṇapaccayaṃ dassetvā puna vipākābyākatassa dassetuṃ sekkhā vātiādimāha. Kusale niruddheti vipassanājavanavīthiyā pacchinnāya. Vipākoti kāmāvacaravipāko. Tadārammaṇatāti tadārammaṇatāya, taṃ kusalassa javanassa ārammaṇabhūtaṃ vipassitakusalaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā uppajjatīti attho. Na kevalañca tadārammaṇavaseneva, paṭisandhibhavaṅgacutivasenāpi. Vipāko hi kammaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā gahitapaṭisandhikassa kusalārammaṇo hotiyeva, so pana dubbiññeyyattā idha na dassito.

406. 'An Arahant, having emerged from the path' means having emerged by way of transcending the life-continuum that immediately follows fruition in the path process. His reviewing consciousnesses, however, are functional and indeterminate. Having thus shown the object condition for the functional indeterminate, to show it again for the resultant indeterminate, he says, 'or for trainees,' and so on. 'When the wholesome has ceased' means when the insight-javana process has been cut off. 'Resultant' means the sense-sphere resultant. 'By having that as its object' means that it arises by taking as its object that wholesome insight which was the object of the wholesome javana. And not only by way of having that as its object, but also by way of rebirth-linking, life-continuum, and death. For the resultant consciousness of one who has taken rebirth-linking by taking kamma as its object indeed has a wholesome object; however, because this is difficult to understand, it is not shown here.

Kusalaṃ assādetītiādi akusalajavanāvasāne kusalārammaṇavipākaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Viññāṇañcāyatanavipākassāti idaṃ dubbiññeyyampi samānaṃ mahaggatavipākassa tadārammaṇabhāvena anuppattito labbhamānakavasena vuttaṃ. Kiriyassāti arahattaṃ patvā asamāpannapubbe ākāsānañcāyatane paṭilomato vā ekantarikavasena vā samāpannakiriyāya. Cetopariyañāṇassātiādīni parato āvajjanāya yojetabbāni. Yā etesaṃ āvajjanā, tassā kusalā khandhā ārammaṇapaccayena paccayoti ayañhettha attho.

'Savoring the wholesome,' and so on, is stated to show the resultant with a wholesome object at the end of the unwholesome javanas. 'And of the resultant of the base of infinite consciousness': this, though difficult to understand, is stated by way of its being obtainable, since an exalted resultant is not attained by way of `tadārammaṇa`. 'Of the functional': this refers to the functional consciousness of one who, having attained Arahantship, attains the base of infinite space—which he had not attained before—either in reverse order or by skipping one jhāna. 'The knowledge of others' minds,' and so on, should be connected with the subsequent advertence. The meaning here is this: the wholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of object condition, for the advertence towards these.

407-409. Rāganti attano vā parassa vā rāgaṃ. Attano rāgavasena panettha vaṇṇanā pākaṭā hoti. Assādetītiādīni vuttatthāneva. Vicikicchādīsu pana tīsu assādetabbatāya abhāvena “assādetī”ti na vuttaṃ. Diṭṭhi panettha uppajjati, sā assādetīti padassa parihīnattā [M 0.0437] āgatapaṭipāṭiyā paṭhamaṃ na vuttā. Vicikicchādīsuyeva taṃ [V 0.0434] taṃ sabhāgaṃ paṭhamaṃ vatvā tassa tassa anantarā vuttā. Imesu ca pana rāgādīsu “kiṃ me pāpadhammā uppajjantī”ti akkhantivasena vā, “kataṃ pāpaṃ kataṃ luddha”nti vippaṭisārādivasena vā domanassuppatti veditabbā.

407-409. 'Lust' (`Rāga`) means one's own lust or another's lust. Here, the explanation is clear with reference to one's own lust. 'He savors' (`Assādetīti`), and so on, have the same meaning as stated before. However, in the case of the three beginning with doubt, 'he savors' is not stated because there is nothing to be savored. Here, a view arises; since the word 'he savors' is omitted, it is not stated first in the established order. In the case of doubt and the others, having first stated the corresponding factor for each, what immediately follows each is then stated. And in these cases of lust and so on, the arising of grief should be understood as occurring either by way of impatience, thinking, 'Why do evil states arise in me?' or by way of remorse and so on, thinking, 'An evil deed was done, a cruel deed was done.'

410. Cakkhuṃ aniccatoti vipassanānukkamena oḷārikāyatanāni vatthurūpañcāti ekādasa rūpāni pākaṭattā gahitāni. Puna rūpāyatanādīni cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ ārammaṇattā gahitāni. Yasmā panesā viññāṇakāyavasena desanā, na dhātuvasena, tasmā manodhātu na gahitā. Evaṃ sabbattha gahitāgahitaṃ veditabbaṃ.

410. 'The eye is impermanent,' and so on: in the sequence of insight, the eleven forms—the gross bases and the physical basis—are taken up because they are manifest. Furthermore, the visible-form base and the others are taken up because they are the objects of eye-consciousness and so on. But since this teaching is by way of the groups of consciousness, not by way of the elements, the mind-element is therefore not taken up. In this way, what is taken up and not taken up should be understood everywhere.

411. Phalaṃ paccavekkhanti nibbānaṃ paccavekkhantīti paccavekkhaṇakusalassa ārammaṇadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ.

411. 'They review the fruition, they review Nibbāna'—this is said for the purpose of showing the object of the wholesome reviewing consciousness.

413-416. Ārammaṇādhipatiniddese sekkhaputhujjanānaṃ vasena catubhūmakakusalaṃ dassitaṃ, tathā sahajātādhipatiniddese. Arahato uttamadhammaṃ adhigatattā lokiyakusalesu garukāro natthīti aggamaggova dassito.

413-416. In the exposition of object-predominance, the wholesome states of the four planes are shown with respect to trainees and worldlings; likewise in the exposition of conascence-predominance. For the Arahant, because the supreme Dhamma has been attained, there is no high regard for mundane wholesome states; thus, only the highest path is shown.

417. Anantarapaccaye purimā purimāti ekabhūmakāpi nānābhūmakāpi kusalā ekato katvā vuttā. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa, anulomaṃ vodānassāti nānārammaṇavasena. Gotrabhu maggassa, vodānaṃ maggassāti nānābhūmivasena. Kusalaṃ vuṭṭhānassāti ettha pana kusalanti tebhūmakakusalaṃ. Vuṭṭhānanti tebhūmakavipākaṃ. Tehi kusalajavanavīthito vuṭṭhahanti, tasmā vuṭṭhānanti vuccati. Taṃ duvidhaṃ hoti – tadārammaṇaṃ bhavaṅgañca. Tattha kāmāvacarakusalassa ubhayampi vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, mahaggatassa bhavaṅgameva. Maggo phalassāti idaṃ yasmā lokuttaravipākaṃ javanavīthipariyāpannattā vuṭṭhānaṃ nāma na hoti, tasmā visuṃ vuttaṃ. Anulomaṃ sekkhāyāti asekkhāya kusalaṃ anantaraṃ na hoti, tasmā vibhāgaṃ karoti. Phalasamāpattiyāti sotāpattiphalasakadāgāmiphalaanāgāmiphalasamāpattiyāpi. Phalasamāpattiyāti anāgāmiphalasamāpattiyā. Akusale duvidhampi vuṭṭhānaṃ labbhati. Vipākābyākatā kiriyābyākatāti ettha vipākābyākatā vipākābyākatānaṃyeva, kiriyābyākatā kiriyābyākatānaṃyeva [M 0.0438] veditabbā. Bhavaṅgaṃ āvajjanāyātiādi vomissakavasena vuttaṃ. Tattha kiriyāti kāmāvacarakiriyā. Sā duvidhassāpi [V 0.0435] vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayo hoti, mahaggatā bhavaṅgasseva. Iti ye heṭṭhā paccayavibhaṅganiddese “purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo”ti ārabhitvā kusalaṃ kusalassa, kusalaṃ abyākatassa, akusalaṃ akusalassa, akusalaṃ abyākatassa, abyākataṃ abyākatassa, abyākataṃ kusalassa, abyākataṃ akusalassāti satta vārā dassitā; tesaṃ vasena idha saṅkhepato anantarapaccayo vibhatto.

417. In the condition of immediacy, ‘each preceding’—whether belonging to a single plane or multiple planes—the wholesome states are spoken of together. The adaptation to the change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) and the adaptation to the purification (vodāna) are by way of different objects. Gotrabhū is for the path, and vodāna is for the path—by way of different planes. Here, ‘wholesome’ refers to the wholesome states of the three planes. ‘Emergence’ refers to the resultant states of the three planes. They emerge from the cognitive process of wholesome impulsion (javana); therefore, it is called ‘emergence.’ It is of two kinds: retention (tadārammaṇa) and life-continuum (bhavaṅga). In this regard, for sense-sphere wholesome states, both kinds of emergence occur; for sublime (mahaggata) states, only life-continuum. ‘The path is for the fruit’—this is stated separately because supramundane resultant states, being included within the impulsion cognitive process, are not called ‘emergence.’ The adaptation to the trainee (sekha) is explained, because wholesome states are not immediately proximate for the non-trainee (asekha); therefore, the distinction is made. ‘Fruition attainment’ refers to the attainments of stream-entry fruit, once-returner fruit, and non-returner fruit. ‘Fruition attainment’ also refers to the non-returner fruit attainment. For unwholesome states, both kinds of emergence are possible. Regarding resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate—here, resultant-indeterminate should be understood as being only for resultant-indeterminate states, and functional-indeterminate only for functional-indeterminate states. ‘Life-continuum for adverting’ and so on are mentioned in a mixed manner. Here, ‘functional’ refers to sense-sphere functional states. It is an immediately proximate condition for both kinds of emergence, while sublime functional states are a condition only for life-continuum. Thus, in the earlier exposition of the analysis of conditions, beginning with ‘the preceding, preceding wholesome states are a condition for the succeeding, succeeding wholesome states by way of the immediately proximate condition,’ seven instances are shown: wholesome for wholesome, wholesome for indeterminate, unwholesome for unwholesome, unwholesome for indeterminate, indeterminate for indeterminate, indeterminate for wholesome, indeterminate for unwholesome. Based on these, the immediately proximate condition is briefly analyzed here.

Vitthārato panettha –

Herein in detail:

Dasadhā sattarasadhā, samasaṭṭhividhena ca;

Bahudhāpi ca niddesaṃ, sādhukaṃ upalakkhaye.

In ten ways, in seventeen ways, and in sixty-six ways; and also in many other ways, one should carefully discern the exposition.

Ayañhi anantarapaccayo na kevalaṃ sattadhāva niddesaṃ labhati, kusalaṃ pana kusalassa vipākassa; akusalaṃ akusalassa vipākassa; vipākaṃ vipākassa kiriyassa; kiriyaṃ kusalassa akusalassa vipākassa kiriyassāti evaṃ dasadhāpi niddesaṃ labhati. Na kevalaṃ dasadhāyeva, kusalaṃ pana kusalassa kusalavipākassa akusalavipākassa; akusalaṃ akusalassa akusalavipākassa kusalavipākassa; kusalavipākaṃ kusalavipākassa akusalavipākassa kiriyassa; akusalavipākaṃ akusalavipākassa kusalavipākassa kiriyassa; kiriyaṃ kiriyassa kusalassa akusalassa kusalavipākassa akusalavipākassāti evaṃ sattarasadhā niddesaṃ labhati.

For this immediately proximate condition not only obtains a sevenfold exposition, but also: wholesome (states) for wholesome (states) and resultant (states); unwholesome (states) for unwholesome (states) and resultant (states); resultant (states) for resultant (states) and functional (states); functional (states) for wholesome, unwholesome, resultant, and functional (states)—thus obtaining a tenfold exposition. Not only a tenfold (exposition), but also: wholesome (states) for wholesome, wholesome-resultant, and unwholesome-resultant (states); unwholesome (states) for unwholesome, unwholesome-resultant, and wholesome-resultant (states); wholesome-resultant (states) for wholesome-resultant, unwholesome-resultant, and functional (states); unwholesome-resultant (states) for unwholesome-resultant, wholesome-resultant, and functional (states); functional (states) for functional, wholesome, unwholesome, wholesome-resultant, and unwholesome-resultant (states)—thus obtaining a seventeenfold exposition.

Na kevalañca sattarasadhāva samasaṭṭhividhenāpi niddesaṃ labhateva. Kathaṃ? Kāmāvacarakusalañhi bhūmibhedena catubbidhassa kusalassa anantarapaccayo hoti, rūpāvacarārūpāvacaraṃ sakasakabhūmikassevāti kusalaṃ kusalassa chabbidhena anantarapaccayo. Kāmāvacarakusalaṃ pana kāmāvacarakusalavipākassa akusalavipākassa rūpāvacaravipākassa arūpāvacaravipākassa lokuttaravipākassa; rūpāvacarakusalaṃ rūpāvacaravipākassa kāmāvacarakusalavipākassa; arūpāvacarakusalaṃ kāmāvacarakusalavipākassa rūpāvacaraarūpāvacaralokuttaravipākassa; lokuttarakusalaṃ lokuttaravipākassāti kusalaṃ vipākassa dvādasavidhena [V 0.0436] anantarapaccayo[M 0.0439]. Akusalaṃ akusalassa akusalavipākassa tebhūmakakusalavipākassāti pañcavidhena anantarapaccayo.

Not only does it receive the seventeenfold classification, but it also obtains a description in sixty-six ways. How? For instance, sense-sphere wholesome (states) serve as the immediately proximate condition for the fourfold wholesome states by way of different planes. Similarly, form-sphere and formless-sphere (wholesome states) for those of their respective planes only. Thus, wholesome acts as the immediately proximate condition for wholesome in six ways. Furthermore, sense-sphere wholesome (states) serve as the immediately proximate condition for the resultant of sense-sphere wholesome, the resultant of unwholesome, the resultant of form-sphere, the resultant of formless-sphere, and the supramundane resultant. Form-sphere wholesome (states) serve as the immediately proximate condition for the resultant of form-sphere and the resultant of sense-sphere wholesome. Formless-sphere wholesome (states) serve as the immediately proximate condition for the resultant of sense-sphere wholesome, the resultant of form-sphere, the resultant of formless-sphere, and the supramundane resultant. Supramundane wholesome (states) serve as the immediately proximate condition for the supramundane resultant. Thus, wholesome acts as the immediately proximate condition for resultant in twelve ways. Unwholesome (states) act as the immediately proximate condition for unwholesome, the resultant of unwholesome, and the wholesome resultant states of the three planes—thus in five ways.

Kāmāvacarakusalavipākaṃ kāmāvacarakusalavipākassa akusalavipākassa rūpāvacaravipākassa arūpāvacaravipākassāti kāmāvacarakusalavipākaṃ vipākassa catubbidhena anantarapaccayo. Rūpāvacaravipākaṃ tebhūmakakusalavipākassāti tividhena anantarapaccayo. Arūpāvacaravipākaṃ arūpāvacaravipākassa kāmāvacarakusalavipākassāti duvidhena anantarapaccayo. Lokuttaravipākaṃ catubhūmakakusalavipākassāti catubbidhena anantarapaccayo. Evaṃ kusalavipākaṃ vipākassa terasadhāpi anantarapaccayo. Akusalavipākaṃ akusalavipākassa kāmāvacarakusalavipākassāti duvidhena anantarapaccayo. Evaṃ sabbathāpi vipākaṃ vipākassa pañcadasavidhena anantarapaccayo. Kāmāvacarakusalavipākaṃ pana kāmāvacarakiriyassa, tathā akusalavipākaṃ, tathā rūpāvacaravipākaṃ, tathā arūpāvacaravipākañcāti vipākaṃ kiriyassa ca catubbidhena anantarapaccayo.

The sense-sphere wholesome resultant is an immediately proximate condition for resultant in four ways: for the sense-sphere wholesome resultant, the unwholesome resultant, the form-sphere resultant, and the formless-sphere resultant. The form-sphere resultant is an immediately proximate condition for the wholesome resultant of the three planes in three ways. The formless-sphere resultant is an immediately proximate condition in two ways: for the formless-sphere resultant and the sense-sphere wholesome resultant. The supramundane resultant is an immediately proximate condition for the wholesome resultant of the four planes in four ways. Thus, the wholesome resultant is an immediately proximate condition for resultant in thirteen ways. The unwholesome resultant is an immediately proximate condition in two ways: for the unwholesome resultant and the sense-sphere wholesome resultant. In this way, altogether, resultant is an immediately proximate condition for resultant in fifteen ways. Moreover, the sense-sphere wholesome resultant is an immediately proximate condition for the sense-sphere functional, and similarly the unwholesome resultant, the form-sphere resultant, and the formless-sphere resultant—thus, resultant is an immediately proximate condition for functional in four ways.

Kāmāvacarakiriyaṃ tebhūmakakiriyassa, rūpāvacarārūpāvacarakiriyaṃ rūpāvacarārūpāvacarānaññevāti kiriyaṃ kiriyassa pañcavidhena anantarapaccayo. Kāmāvacarakiriyaṃ akusalavipākassa ceva catubhūmakakusalavipākassa ca, rūpāvacarakiriyaṃ kāmāvacarakusalavipākarūpāvacaravipākānaṃ arūpāvacarakiriyaṃ catubhūmakakusalavipākassāpīti kiriyaṃ vipākassa ekādasavidhena anantarapaccayo. Kāmāvacarakiriyaṃ pana kāmāvacarakusalassa akusalassāti kusalākusalānaṃ duvidhena anantarapaccayo hoti. Evaṃ samasaṭṭhividhenāpi niddesaṃ labhati.

The sense-sphere functional states are an immediately proximate condition for the functional states of the three planes; the form-sphere and formless-sphere functional states for those of the form-sphere and formless-sphere only—thus, functional for functional in five ways. The sense-sphere functional states are an immediately proximate condition for both unwholesome resultant and wholesome resultant of the four planes; the form-sphere functional states for sense-sphere wholesome resultant and form-sphere resultant; the formless-sphere functional states for wholesome resultant of the four planes as well. Thus, functional is an immediately proximate condition for resultant in eleven ways. Moreover, the sense-sphere functional states are an immediately proximate condition for sense-sphere wholesome and unwholesome states in two ways. In this manner, the exposition is obtained in sixty-six ways as well.

Na kevalañca samasaṭṭhividheneva, bahuvidhenāpi labhateva. Kathaṃ? Kāmāvacarapaṭhamamahākusalacittaṃ tāva attano, catunnañca rūpāvacarakusalānaṃ pādakayogena soḷasannaṃ somanassalokuttarānanti ekavīsatiyā ca kusalānaṃ, javanapariyosāne tadārammaṇabhavaṅgavasena uppajjamānānaṃ ekādasannaṃ kāmāvacaravipākānaṃ, bhavaṅgavaseneva pavattānaṃ rūpāvacarārūpāvacaravipākānaṃ, phalasamāpattivasena pavattānaṃ dvādasannaṃ lokuttaravipākānanti [M 0.0440] evaṃ ekavīsatiyā kusalānaṃ; dvattiṃsāya vipākānanti tepaññāsāya cittānaṃ anantarapaccayo hoti[V 0.0437]. Tathā dutiyakusalacittaṃ. Tatiyacatutthāni pana ṭhapetvā uparibhūmakakusalāni ca lokuttaravipākāni ca sesaekavīsaticittānaṃ. Pañcamachaṭṭhāni attano ca, navannañca uparibhūmakaupekkhākusalānaṃ, tevīsatiyā ca vipākānanti tettiṃsāya. Sattamaaṭṭhamāni ekavīsatiyāva.

Not only in sixty-six ways, but also in many ways it is obtained. How? First, the first great sense-sphere wholesome consciousness is an immediately proximate condition for twenty-one wholesome states: itself, the four form-sphere wholesome states by way of foundational association, and the sixteen supramundane states accompanied by joy. At the conclusion of the impulsion phase, it is an immediately proximate condition for the eleven sense-sphere resultant states arising as retention and life-continuum. It is also a condition for the form-sphere and formless-sphere resultant states occurring only as life-continuum, and for the twelve supramundane resultant states occurring by way of fruition attainment. Thus, it is an immediately proximate condition for fifty-three consciousnesses: twenty-one wholesome states and thirty-two resultant states. Similarly, the second wholesome consciousness is a condition for fifty-three. The third and fourth, however, are a condition for the remaining twenty-one consciousnesses, as the wholesome states of the higher planes and the supramundane resultants are excluded. The fifth and sixth wholesome consciousnesses serve as conditions for thirty-three states: themselves, the nine wholesome states of the higher planes accompanied by equanimity, and twenty-three resultant states. The seventh and eighth wholesome consciousnesses serve as a condition for twenty-one states only.

Pañca rūpāvacarakusalāni attano attano pacchimānaṃ rūpāvacarakusalānaṃ, catunnampi ñāṇasampayuttamahāvipākānaṃ, pañcannaṃ rūpāvacaravipākānañcāti dasannaṃ. Eteneva ca nayena arūpāvacarakusalesu paṭhamaṃ attano vipākena saddhiṃ ekādasannaṃ, dutiyaṃ dvādasannaṃ, tatiyaṃ terasannaṃ, catutthaṃ cuddasannaṃ phalasamāpattiyā cāti pannarasannaṃ lokuttarakusalaṃ attano attano vipākasseva. Aṭṭhasu lobhasahagatesu ekekaṃ akusalaṃ ekādasannaṃ kāmāvacaravipākamanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ navannaṃ, mahaggatavipākānaṃ attano attano pacchimassa cāti ekavīsatiyā. Dve domanassasahagatāni upekkhāsahagatānaṃ channaṃ kāmāvacaravipākamanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ attano pacchimassa cāti sattannaṃ. Vicikicchuddhaccasahagatadvayaṃ somanassasahagatāhetukavipākena saddhiṃ ekādasannaṃ kāmāvacaravipākamanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ navannaṃ rūpāvacarārūpāvacaravipākānaṃ attano pacchimassa cāti ekavīsatiyā.

The five fine-material-sphere wholesome consciousnesses are a condition for ten states: their own respective subsequent fine-material-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, the four great resultant consciousnesses accompanied by knowledge, and the five fine-material-sphere resultant consciousnesses. And in the same way, among the immaterial-sphere wholesome consciousnesses, the first, together with its own resultant, is a condition for eleven; the second, for twelve; the third, for thirteen; the fourth, for fourteen, and with fruition attainment, for fifteen. The supramundane wholesome consciousnesses are a condition for their own respective resultants only. Among the eight unwholesome consciousnesses accompanied by greed, each is a condition for twenty-one: for the eleven sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses, for the nine exalted resultant consciousnesses, and for its own subsequent one. The two unwholesome consciousnesses accompanied by grief are a condition for seven: for the six sense-sphere resultant mind-consciousness-elements accompanied by equanimity and for its own subsequent one. The two unwholesome consciousnesses accompanied by doubt and restlessness are a condition for twenty-one: for the eleven sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses, for the nine fine-material-sphere and immaterial-sphere resultant consciousnesses, and for its own subsequent one.

Kusalavipākapañcaviññāṇā kusalavipākamanodhātuyā, manodhātu dvinnaṃ vipākamanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ. Tāsu dvīsu somanassasahagatā dasannaṃ vipākamanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ bhavaṅgabhūtānaṃ tadārammaṇakāle attano pacchimassa voṭṭhabbanakiriyassa cāti dvādasannaṃ. Upekkhāsahagatāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu pana āvajjanamanodhātuyā dviṭṭhānikāya āvajjanamanoviññāṇadhātuyā dasannañca vipākamanoviññāṇadhātūnanti dvādasannameva. Tihetukamahāvipākā somanassasahagatāhetukavajjānaṃ dasannampi kāmāvacaravipākamanoviññāṇadhātūnaṃ rūpāvacarārūpāvacaravipākānaṃ āvajjanadvayassa cāti ekavīsatiyā, duhetukavipākā ṭhapetvā mahaggatavipāke sesānaṃ dvādasannaṃ. Pañca rūpāvacaravipākā tebhūmakakusalavipākasahetukapaṭisandhicittānaṃ sattarasannaṃ [M 0.0441] āvajjanadvayassa cāti ekūnavīsatiyā. Arūpāvacaravipākesu paṭhamaṃ kāmāvacarakusalavipākatihetukapaṭisandhicittānaṃ, catunnaṃ arūpāvacaravipākacittānaṃ catunnaṃ manodvārāvajjanassa cāti navannaṃ. Dutiyaṃ heṭṭhimavipākaṃ vajjetvā aṭṭhannaṃ, tatiyaṃ dve heṭṭhimāni [V 0.0438] vajjetvā sattannaṃ, catutthaṃ tīṇi heṭṭhimāni vajjetvā channaṃ cattāri lokuttaravipākāni tihetukavipākānaṃ terasannaṃ attano attano pacchimassa cāti cuddasannaṃ.

The five wholesome-resultant sense consciousnesses are a condition for the wholesome-resultant mind-element. The mind-element is a condition for the two resultant mind-consciousness-elements. Among these two, the one accompanied by joy is a condition for twelve: for the ten resultant mind-consciousness-elements that function as life-continuum and as registering, and for the subsequent determining functional consciousness. The rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity, however, is a condition for twelve: for the advertence mind-element, for the advertence mind-consciousness-element, and for the ten resultant mind-consciousness-elements. The great resultant consciousnesses with three roots are a condition for twenty-one: the ten sense-sphere resultant mind-consciousness-elements (excluding the rootless one accompanied by joy), the nine fine-material-sphere and immaterial-sphere resultant consciousnesses, and the two advertence consciousnesses. The resultant consciousnesses with two roots are a condition for the remaining twelve, excluding the exalted resultant consciousnesses. The five fine-material-sphere resultant consciousnesses are a condition for nineteen: for the seventeen rooted wholesome-resultant rebirth-linking consciousnesses of the three realms, and for the two advertence consciousnesses. Among the immaterial-sphere resultant consciousnesses, the first is a condition for nine: for the four sense-sphere wholesome-resultant three-rooted rebirth-linking consciousnesses, for the four immaterial-sphere resultant consciousnesses, and for the mind-door advertence consciousness. The second, excluding the lowest resultant consciousness, is a condition for eight. The third, excluding the two lower ones, is a condition for seven. The fourth, excluding the three lower ones, is a condition for six. The four supramundane resultant consciousnesses are a condition for fourteen: for the thirteen three-rooted resultant consciousnesses, and for their own respective subsequent one.

Akusalavipākapañcaviññāṇā akusalavipākamanodhātuyā, manodhātu akusalavipākāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyā. Sā tadārammaṇakāle attano pacchimassa cutikāle paṭisandhivasena bhavaṅgavasena ca pavattānaṃ itaresampi navannaṃ kāmāvacaravipākānaṃ upekkhāsahagatānaṃ dvinnaṃ parittakiriyānañcāti dvādasannaṃ. Kiriyamanodhātu dasannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ hasituppādakiriyā pañcavokāre bhavaṅgavasena pavattānaṃ navannaṃ tihetukavipākānaṃ, tadārammaṇavasena pavattānaṃ pañcannaṃ somanassasahagatavipākānaṃ attano pacchimassa cāti aggahitaggahaṇena terasannaṃ. Voṭṭhabbanakiriyā ṭhapetvā kiriyamanodhātuṃ dasannaṃ kāmāvacarakiriyānaṃ, kāmāvacarakusalākusalānaṃ pañcavokāre bhavaṅgavasena pavattānaṃ pannarasannaṃ vipākacittānañcāti pañcacattālīsāya.

The five unwholesome-resultant sense consciousnesses are for the unwholesome-resultant mind-element; the mind-element is for the unwholesome-resultant rootless mind-consciousness-element. That (unwholesome-resultant rootless mind-consciousness-element) is for its own final moment at the time of registering and at the time of death, for the other nine sense-sphere resultant consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity which occur as rebirth-linking and as life-continuum, and for the two minor functional consciousnesses—thus for twelve. The functional mind-element is for ten consciousnesses. The functional consciousness producing laughter is for the nine triple-rooted resultant consciousnesses which occur as life-continuum in the five-constituent existence, for the five resultant consciousnesses accompanied by joy which occur as registering, and for its own final moment—thus for thirteen by the principle of including the unmentioned. The determining functional consciousness, excluding the functional mind-element, is for the ten sense-sphere functional consciousnesses, for the sense-sphere wholesome and unwholesome consciousnesses, and for the fifteen resultant consciousnesses which occur as life-continuum in the five-constituent existence—thus for forty-five.

Kāmāvacaratihetukasomanassasahagatakiriyadvayaṃ bhavaṅgavasena pavattānaṃ terasannaṃ tihetukavipākānaṃ tadārammaṇavasena pañcannaṃ somanassasahagatavipākānaṃ parikammavasena pavattamānānaṃ catunnaṃ rūpāvacarakiriyānaṃ arahattaphalasamāpattiyā attano pacchimassa cāti aggahitaggahaṇena dvāvīsatiyā duhetukasomanassasahagatakiriyadvayaṃ yathāvuttānaṃ terasannaṃ bhavaṅgacittānaṃ pañcannaṃ tadārammaṇānaṃ attano pacchimassa cāti aggahitaggahaṇena sattarasannaṃ. Kāmāvacaratihetukaupekkhāsahagatakiriyadvayaṃ tesaṃyeva terasannaṃ bhavaṅgānaṃ, tadārammaṇavasena pavattānaṃ channaṃ upekkhāsahagatavipākānaṃ, parikammavasena pavattānaṃ ekissā rūpāvacarakiriyāya catunnaṃ arūpāvacarakiriyānaṃ arahattaphalasamāpattiyā attano pacchimassa cāti aggahitaggahaṇena catuvīsatiyā. Duhetukaupekkhāsahagatakiriyadvayaṃ tesaṃyeva terasannaṃ bhavaṅgānaṃ [M 0.0442] channaṃ tadārammaṇānaṃ attano pacchimassa cāti aggahitaggahaṇena aṭṭhārasannaṃ. Rūpāvacarakiriyesu ekekaṃ navannaṃ pañcavokāre tihetukabhavaṅgānaṃ attano pacchimassa cāti dasannaṃ. Arūpāvacarakiriyesu paṭhamaṃ pañcavokāre navannaṃ bhavaṅgānaṃ, catuvokāre ekassa attano pacchimassa cāti ekādasannaṃ. Dutiyaṃ catuvokāre dve bhavaṅgāni labhati. Tatiyaṃ tīṇi, catutthaṃ cattāri phalasamāpattiñcāti tesu ekekaṃ yathāpaṭipāṭiyā ekādasannaṃ dvādasannaṃ terasannaṃ pañcadasannañca anantarapaccayo hoti. Evaṃ bahuvidhenāpi niddesaṃ labhati. Tena vuttaṃ –

The two sense-sphere three-rooted functional consciousnesses accompanied by joy are for the thirteen three-rooted resultant consciousnesses which occur as life-continuum, for the five resultant consciousnesses accompanied by joy which occur as registering, for the four fine-material-sphere functional consciousnesses which occur as preliminary act, for the attainment of Arahantship fruition, and for its own final moment—thus for twenty-two by the principle of including the unmentioned. The two two-rooted functional consciousnesses accompanied by joy are for the aforementioned thirteen life-continuum consciousnesses, for the five registering consciousnesses, and for its own final moment—thus for seventeen by the principle of including the unmentioned. The two sense-sphere three-rooted functional consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity are for those same thirteen life-continuum consciousnesses, for the six resultant consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity which occur as registering, for the one fine-material-sphere functional consciousness and the four immaterial-sphere functional consciousnesses which occur as preliminary act, for the attainment of Arahantship fruition, and for its own final moment—thus for twenty-four by the principle of including the unmentioned. The two two-rooted functional consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity are for those same thirteen life-continuum consciousnesses, for the six registering consciousnesses, and for its own final moment—thus for eighteen by the principle of including the unmentioned. Among the fine-material-sphere functional consciousnesses, each one is for the nine three-rooted life-continuum consciousnesses in the five-constituent existence, and for its own final moment—thus for ten. Among the immaterial-sphere functional consciousnesses, the first is for the nine life-continuum consciousnesses in the five-constituent existence, for the one (life-continuum consciousness) in the four-constituent existence, and for its own final moment—thus for eleven. The second obtains two life-continuum consciousnesses in the four-constituent existence. The third obtains three, and the fourth obtains four, including fruition attainment; among these, each one, in due order, is an immediate condition for eleven, twelve, thirteen, and fifteen respectively. Thus, the explanation is obtained in many ways. Therefore, it is said—

“Dasadhā [V 0.0439] sattarasadhā, samasaṭṭhividhena ca;

Bahudhāpi ca niddesaṃ, sādhukaṃ upalakkhaye”ti.

"Tenfold, seventeenfold, and in sixty-two ways as a summation; and also a manifold explanation, one should carefully note well."

Samanantarapaccayādayo uttānatthāyeva.

The conditions beginning with contiguity are of obvious meaning.

423. Upanissaye saddhaṃ upanissāyāti kammakammaphalaidhalokaparalokādīsu saddhaṃ upanissayaṃ katvā. Yathā hi puriso heṭṭhāpathaviyaṃ udakaṃ atthīti saddahitvā pathaviṃ khanati, evaṃ saddho kulaputto dānādīnaṃ phalañca ānisaṃsañca saddahitvā dānādīni pavatteti. Tasmā “saddhaṃ upanissāyā”ti vuttaṃ.

423. Regarding the condition of strong reliance: 'relying on faith' means establishing faith as the basis regarding kamma, the fruits of kamma, this world, the next world, and so on. Just as a man, believing there is water beneath the ground, digs the earth, so a faithful son of good family, believing in the fruits and benefits of giving and so forth, engages in acts of giving. Therefore, it is said, 'relying on faith.'

Sīlaṃ upanissāyātiādīsupi ime sīlādayo dhamme upanissayaṃ katvāti attho. Sīlavā hi sīlānubhāvesu sīlānisaṃsesu ca kusalo sīlaṃ upanissāya sīlavantānaṃ dānaṃ deti, uparūpari sīlaṃ samādiyati suparisuddhaṃ akhaṇḍaṃ, cātuddasīādīsu pakkhadivasesu uposathakammaṃ karoti, sīlasampadaṃ nissāya jhānādīni uppādeti. Bahussutopi dānādipuññakiriyāyattā sabbasampattiyo dānādīnañca saṅkilesavodānādibhedaṃ sutamayāya paññāya paṭivijjhitvā ṭhito sutaṃ upanissāya dānādīni pavatteti. Cāgavāpi cāgādhimutto attano cāgasampadaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlavanto hutvā dinnaṃ mahapphalanti sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti, tāya paṭipattiyā parisuddhacitto jhānādīni uppādeti. Paññavāpi idhalokaparalokahitañceva lokasamatikkamanupāyañca upaparikkhanto “sakkā imāya paṭipattiyā idhalokahitampi paralokahitampi lokasamatikkamanūpāyañca sampādetu”nti paññaṃ upanissāya dānādīni pavatteti. Yasmā pana na kevalaṃ [M 0.0443] saddhādayo dānādīnaṃyeva upanissayā, attano aparabhāge uppajjamānānaṃ saddhādīnampi upanissayā eva, tasmā saddhā sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgo paññā saddhāya sīlassa sutassa cāgassa paññāyāti vuttaṃ.

'Relying on virtue' and so on: the meaning here is that these qualities like virtue are made a foundation. For a virtuous person, skilled in the benefits and advantages of virtue, relying on virtue, gives gifts to the virtuous, undertakes higher and higher virtue, perfectly pure and unbroken, performs the Uposatha observance on the fourteenth and other fortnightly days, and, depending on the perfection of virtue, gives rise to jhāna and other attainments. Likewise, the learned one, because all kinds of prosperity depend on meritorious deeds like giving, having discerned through wisdom derived from learning the distinctions between defilement and purification in giving and other deeds, remains steadfast and, relying on learning, engages in giving and other acts. The generous one, devoted to generosity, relying on their own perfection in generosity, gives gifts, undertakes virtue thinking, 'What is given by one who is virtuous is of great fruit,' performs the Uposatha observance, and with that practice, having purified the mind, gives rise to jhāna and other attainments. The wise one, examining what is beneficial in this world and the next as well as the means to transcend the world, reflects, 'Through this practice, one can accomplish what is beneficial in this world and the next, as well as the means to transcend the world,' and relying on wisdom, engages in giving and other deeds. Moreover, not only are faith and the others a foundation for giving and the like, but they also are a foundation for faith and the others that arise in one’s future existence. Therefore, it is said: 'Faith is for faith, virtue for virtue, learning for learning, generosity for generosity, wisdom for wisdom.'

Parikammanti anantaraṃ aggahetvā pubbabhāge parikammaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Yathākammūpagañāṇassa anāgataṃsañāṇassāti imesaṃ dvinnaṃ dibbacakkhuparikammameva, parikammaṃ visuṃ natthi. Dibbacakkhusseva paribhaṇḍañāṇāni etāni, tasmiṃ ijjhamāne ijjhanti evaṃ santepi tadadhimuttatāya sahitaṃ dibbacakkhuparikammaṃ tesaṃ parikammanti veditabbaṃ. Na hi etāni sabbesaṃ [V 0.0440] dibbacakkhukānaṃ samagatikāni honti. Tasmā bhavitabbamettha parikammavisesenāti. Dibbacakkhu dibbāya sotadhātuyāti dūre rūpāni disvā tesaṃ saddaṃ sotukāmassa dibbacakkhu sotadhātuvisuddhiyā upanissayo hoti. Tesaṃ pana saddaṃ sutvā tattha gantukāmatādivasena dibbasotadhātu iddhividhañāṇassa upanissayo hoti. Evaṃ sabbattha tassa tassa upakārakabhāvavasena upanissayapaccayatā veditabbā.

Preparation should be undertaken in the preliminary stage, not immediately after. For the knowledge of beings’ faring according to their deeds and the knowledge of the future, these two have only the preparation for the divine eye; there is no separate preparation. These are merely the accessory knowledges of the divine eye itself; when that succeeds, these succeed as well. Even so, because of their inclination towards it, the preparation for the divine eye together with that inclination should be understood as their preparation. For these are not common to all who possess the divine eye. Therefore, there must be a special preparation in this case. The divine eye for the divine ear-element: for one who sees forms from afar and wishes to hear their sound, the divine eye becomes a decisive support for the purification of the ear-element. Then, having heard their sound, by way of the desire to go there and so on, the divine ear-element becomes a decisive support for the knowledge of the kinds of psychic power. Thus, in every case, the conditionality of decisive support should be understood by way of its helpfulness in each case.

Maggaṃ upanissāya anuppannaṃ samāpattinti tena tena maggena sithilīkatapāripanthakattā pahīnapāripanthakattā ca taṃ taṃ samāpattiṃ uppādentīti tesaṃ maggo samāpattiyā upanissayo hoti. Vipassantīti uparūparimaggatthāya vipassanti. Atthapaṭisambhidāyātiādi paṭisambhidānaṃ maggapaṭilābheneva ijjhanato vuttaṃ. Evaṃiddhānañca panetāsaṃ pacchā tesu tesu ārammaṇesu pavattiyā maggova upanissayo nāma hoti.

By relying on the path, an unarisen attainment: because through this or that path obstacles are loosened and abandoned, they bring forth this or that attainment. Thus, for them, the path is a decisive support for the attainment. They practice insight: for the sake of progressively higher paths. With discrimination of meaning, and so on: this is stated because the analytical knowledges are accomplished simply by gaining the path. And for these that are thus accomplished, the path itself is indeed the decisive support for their subsequent occurrence in regard to various objects.

Saddhaṃ upanissāya mānaṃ jappetīti ahamasmi saddho pasannoti mānaṃ pavatteti. Diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhātīti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vacane saddhāvaseneva gantvā paññāya atthaṃ anupaparikkhanto “atthi puggalo”tiādivasena diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Sīlaṃ sutaṃ cāgaṃ paññanti ahamasmi sīlavā sutavā cāgī paññāsampannoti mānaṃ jappeti. Sīlasutacāgapaññāsu pana mānamaññanaṃ viya diṭṭhimaññanaṃ uppādento diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Rāgassātiādīsu saddhādisampadaṃ upanissāya attukkaṃsanakāle tesu ekeko dhammo rāgassa, paravambhanakāle dosassa, ubhayena sampayuttassa mohassa, vuttappakārānaṃ mānadiṭṭhīnaṃ, saddhādisampadaṃ upanissāya bhavabhogasampattipatthanāya upanissayo hoti. Evamettha [M 0.0444] lokiyakusalaññeva dassitaṃ. Lokuttaraṃ pana santaṃ paṇītaṃ uttamaṃ akusalaviddhaṃsanaṃ. Tasmā cando viya andhakāratamānaṃ na akusalassa upanissayo hotīti na gahitaṃ.

Relying on faith, one generates conceit: thinking, 'I am faithful and confident,' one gives rise to conceit. One grasps a view: going by the power of faith alone in this or that statement, without investigating the meaning with wisdom, one grasps a view such as 'there is a person.' Virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom: thinking, 'I am virtuous, learned, generous, and endowed with wisdom,' one generates conceit. But regarding virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, generating the delusion of views just as one does the delusion of conceit, one grasps views. In the case of passion and so on: relying on the accomplishment of faith and so on, at the time of exalting oneself, each of these states becomes a decisive support for passion; at the time of disparaging others, for hatred; for delusion when associated with both; for conceit and views of the kinds mentioned; and, relying on the accomplishment of faith and so on, it becomes a decisive support for the aspiration for attainments of existence and wealth. Thus, only the mundane wholesome is shown here. The supramundane, however, is peaceful, sublime, supreme, and a destroyer of the unwholesome. Therefore, like the moon dispelling the deepest darkness, it is not a decisive support for the unwholesome—hence, it is not included.

Ātāpetītiādi kāyikadukkhavasena abyākatadhammadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Saddho hi saddhaṃ nissāya atisītaṃ atiuṇhanti anosakkitvā nānappakārāni navakammaveyyāvaccādīni karonto attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, bhogaṃ uppādetvā puññāni karissāmīti pariyeṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti. Sīlavāpi sīlānurakkhaṇatthaṃ abbhokāsikattādivasena attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, piṇḍacārikattādivasena pariyeṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti. Sutavāpi [V 0.0441] bāhussaccānurūpaṃ paṭipattiṃ paṭipajjissāmīti vuttanayeneva paṭipajjanto attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, pariyeṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti. Cāgavāpi cāgādhimuttatāya attano yāpanamattepi paccaye anavasesetvā pariccajanto, aṅgādipariccāgaṃ vā pana karonto attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, pariccajitabbassa vatthuno uppādanatthaṃ pariyeṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti. Paññavāpi uparūpari paññaṃ vaḍḍhessāmīti sappaññataṃ nissāya sītuṇhādīni agaṇetvā sajjhāyamanasikāresu yogaṃ karonto attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti, micchājīve ādīnavaṃ sammājīve ca ānisaṃsaṃ disvā micchājīvaṃ pahāya parisuddhena ājīvena jīvitavuttiṃ pariyesanto pariyeṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti.

'He torments himself,' and so on, is stated to show indeterminate states by way of bodily suffering. For a faithful person, relying on faith, not shrinking back from extreme cold and heat, engages in various tasks like new construction and service, and torments and exhausts himself; thinking, 'Having generated wealth, I will perform meritorious deeds,' he experiences suffering rooted in seeking. A virtuous person, too, for the sake of protecting virtue, torments and exhausts himself by way of practices such as dwelling in the open air, and by way of practices such as going on alms-round, he experiences suffering rooted in seeking. A learned person, too, thinking, 'I will undertake a practice befitting my great learning,' and practicing in the way already described, torments and exhausts himself and experiences suffering rooted in seeking. A generous person, too, due to being intent on generosity, torments and exhausts himself by giving away without reserve even the requisites for his own sustenance, or by making a sacrifice of his limbs and so on; for the purpose of producing an item to be given away, he experiences suffering rooted in seeking. A wise person, too, relying on his wisdom, thinking, 'I will increase wisdom higher and higher,' disregarding cold, heat, and so on, and making an effort in recitation and attention, torments and exhausts himself; and seeing the danger in wrong livelihood and the benefit in right livelihood, having abandoned wrong livelihood, while seeking a living with a pure livelihood, he experiences suffering rooted in seeking.

Kāyikassa sukhassāti saddhādisampattiṃ upanissāya uppannāni sukhopakaraṇāni paribhuñjanakāle saddhādisamuṭṭhānapaṇītarūpaphuṭakāyassa ca tesaṃ vasena avippaṭisāramūlakapāmojjapītisamuṭṭhānarūpaphuṭakāyassa ca sukhuppattikāle tesaṃ kaṭattā uppannavipākasukhakāle ca kāyikassa sukhassa, vuttanayeneva dukkhuppattikāle saddhādiguṇasampattiṃ asahamānehi payuttavadhabandhanādikāle ca kāyikassa dukkhassa, saddhādayo upanissāya pavattitaphalasamāpattikāle pana phalasamāpattiyā etesu ekeko upanissayapaccayena paccayo hotīti veditabbo. Kusalaṃ kammanti kusalacetanā attano vipākassa upanissayapaccayo, sā pana balavacetanāva labbhati, na dubbalā. Tatridaṃ vatthu – ekā kira itthī ubbandhitukāmā rukkhe rajjuṃ laggetvā saṃvidhātabbaṃ saṃvidahati. Atheko coro [M 0.0445] rattibhāge taṃ gehaṃ upasaṅkamitvā “imāya rajjuyā kiñcideva bandhitvā harissāmī”ti satthena chindituṃ upagato. Atha sā rajju āsīviso hutvā susūti akāsi. Coro bhīto apasakki. Itthī attano nivesanā nikkhamitvā rajjupāse gīvaṃ paṭimuñcitvā ubbandhā kālamakāsi. Evaṃ balavacetanā antarāye nivāretvā attano vipākassa upanissayo hoti. Na panetaṃ ekantato gahetabbaṃ. Katokāsañhi kammaṃ eva vipākassa antarāyaṃ paṭibāhitvā vipaccati, vipākajanakaṃ pana kammaṃ vipākassa upanissayapaccayo na hotīti na vattabbaṃ. Kammanti ettha catubhūmakampi veditabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana parato “maggo phalasamāpattiyā”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ acetanāvasena. Tenetaṃ dīpeti – yo koci vipākajanako dhammo, so attano vipākassa upanissayapaccayo hotīti.

Of bodily pleasure: this is at the time of enjoying the instruments of pleasure that have arisen in dependence on the accomplishment of faith and other virtues; and at the time of the arising of pleasure for the body touched by refined matter arisen from faith and so forth, and for the body touched by matter arisen from joy and delight rooted in non-remorse on account of them; and at the time of the pleasure of resultant-consciousness that has arisen because of those actions having been done. In the same way, of bodily suffering: at the time of the arising of suffering, and at the time of slaughter, imprisonment, and the like, inflicted by those who cannot tolerate the accomplishment of virtues like faith. However, at the time of the attainment of fruition that occurs in dependence on faith and so forth, it should be understood that each of these is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition. Wholesome kamma means wholesome volition, a decisive support condition for its own result. But only strong volition is obtained, not weak. Here is a story: It is said that a certain woman, wishing to hang herself, attached a rope to a tree and was making arrangements. Then, a thief came to her house at night, thinking, 'I will tie something with this rope and steal it,' and approached to cut it with a knife. Then that rope, having become a venomous snake, hissed. The thief, frightened, retreated. The woman then left her house, put her neck in the noose, hanged herself, and died. Thus, strong volition, having prevented an obstacle, becomes a decisive support for its own result. However, this should not be taken as an absolute rule. For kamma that has been given an opportunity indeed ripens, having warded off an obstacle to its result; but it should not be said that kamma that generates a result is not a decisive support condition for the result. Here, 'kamma' should be understood as pertaining to the four planes. But what is said later, 'the path for the attainment of fruition,' that is in the sense of non-volition. By this it is shown: whatever phenomenon produces a result, that is a decisive support condition for its own result.

Rāgaṃ [V 0.0442] upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanatīti yasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ sāratto hoti, tasmiṃ vā viruddhaṃ, tassa vā atthāya pāṇaṃ hanati. Adinnādānādīsupi etenevupāyena attho veditabbo. Sandhiṃ chindatīti adinnādānavasena vuttaṃ. Tattha sandhinti gehasandhiṃ. Nillopaṃ haratīti nilīyitvā harati. Ekāgārikaṃ karotīti bahūhi saddhiṃ ekameva gehaṃ parivāretvā vilumpati. Paripanthe tiṭṭhatīti panthadūhanakammaṃ karoti. Dosaṃ upanissāyātiādīsu “anatthaṃ me acarī”tiādivasena uppannaṃ dosaṃ upanissayaṃ katvā. Mohaṃ upanissāyāti pāṇātipātādīsu ādīnavapaṭicchādakaṃ mohaṃ upanissayaṃ katvā. Mānaṃ upanissāyāti ahaṃ kiṃ hanituṃ na sakkomi, ādātuṃ na sakkomīti mānaṃ upanissayaṃ katvā. Kenaci vā pana avaññāto hoti paribhūto hīḷito, taṃ omānaṃ upanissayaṃ katvātipi attho. Diṭṭhiṃ upanissāyāti yaññādīsu brāhmaṇādayo viya pādasikamilakkhuādayo viya ca diṭṭhiṃ upanissayaṃ katvā. Patthanaṃ upanissāyāti “sace me idaṃ nāma ijjhissati, evarūpaṃ te balikammaṃ karissāmīti evaṃ devatāyācanasaṅkhataṃ vā, asukaṃ nāma me ghātetvā dehi, asukassa santakaṃ āhara, ehi vā me etāni kammāni karontassa sahāyo hohī”ti evamādiṃ vā patthanaṃ upanissayaṃ katvā. Rāgo doso moho māno diṭṭhi patthanā rāgassāti. Ettha [M 0.0446] rāgo rāgassāpi upanissayo hoti dosādīnampi. Dosādīsupi eseva nayo.

Relying on lust, one kills a living being—this refers to being attached to an object, and killing another who is opposed to it, or killing for its sake. The same method should be understood for theft and other offenses. 'Breaking a joint' is said in the sense of taking what was not given. Here, 'joint' means a house-joint. 'Robbing by stealth' means taking after hiding. 'Committing a single-house-robbery' means surrounding a single house with many people and plundering it. 'Standing on the highway' refers to the act of highway robbery. 'Relying on hatred' and so on means making hatred the decisive support, hatred that has arisen from thinking, 'They have done me wrong,' and so on. 'Relying on delusion' means making delusion the decisive support, delusion which conceals the dangers in actions such as killing living beings. 'Relying on conceit' means making conceit the decisive support, thinking, 'Am I not capable of killing? Am I not capable of taking?' Alternatively, it also means making that disrespect the decisive support because one has been despised, insulted, or humiliated by someone. 'Relying on wrong view' means making wrong view the decisive support, like brahmins and others in sacrifices, or like foot-licking barbarians and others. 'Relying on aspiration' means making aspiration the decisive support, such as 'If such-and-such succeeds for me, I will perform such-and-such an offering for you,' thus in the manner of requesting from deities, or saying 'Kill such-and-such for me,' or 'Bring me what belongs to such-and-such person,' or 'Come, be my helper as I do these deeds,' and so on. Lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, and aspiration for lust, and so on. Here, lust can be a decisive support even for lust itself, as it can be for hatred and the others. The same principle applies to hatred and the rest.

Pāṇātipāto pāṇātipātassāti pāṇātipātī asaṃvare ṭhitattā aññampi pāṇaṃ hanati. Yo vā etena hato, tassa ñātimittehi upadduto tesu aññampi hanati. Evaṃ pāṇātipāto pāṇātipātassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Bhaṇḍasāmikaṃ pana gopakaṃ vā ghātetvā parabhaṇḍaharaṇe, sāmikaṃ ghātetvā tassa dārātikkame, nāhaṃ hanāmīti musābhaṇane, katassa paṭicchādanatthāya akatassa vā karaṇatthāya pesuññaṃ upasaṃhāre, teneva nayena pharusavācānicchāraṇe, samphappalāpabhaṇane, paraṃ hanitvā abhijjhāyitabbaparavittūpakaraṇābhijjhāyane, yo tena ghātito hoti; tassa mittāmaccā ucchijjantūtiādicintane “evaṃ me pāṇātipāto nijjiṇṇo bhavissatī”ti dukkarakārikādivasena diṭṭhiggahaṇakāle pāṇātipāto adinnādānādīnampi upanissayo hoti. Iminā upāyena adinnādānādimūlakesupi cakkesu attho veditabbo.

Killing living beings is a condition for killing living beings, in that one who kills, being unrestrained, kills another living being. Or, the killer, being harassed by the relatives and friends of the one he killed, kills another among them. Thus, killing living beings serves as a decisive support condition for further killing of living beings. Furthermore, in stealing another's goods after killing the owner of the goods or a guard; in committing adultery with a master's wife after killing him; in speaking falsely, 'I did not kill'; in employing slander to conceal what was done or to make what was not done appear as done; in uttering harsh speech in the same manner; in speaking frivolous talk; in coveting the wealth and property of another after killing them; in thinking, 'Let the friends and associates of the one killed be destroyed,' and so on; or at the time of grasping a wrong view through ascetic practices, thinking, 'Thus, my killing will be exhausted'—in such cases, killing becomes a decisive support for theft and other evils. In this way, the meaning should be understood in the cycles rooted in theft and other evils as well.

Mātughātikammaṃ mātughātikammassāti aññaṃ mātaraṃ hanantaṃ disvā “vaṭṭati evaṃ kātu”nti [V 0.0443] attano mātaraṃ hanantassa vā, ekasmiṃ bhave hantvā aparasmimpi hananavasena vā, ekasmiṃyeva bhave “gaccha, me mātaraṃ hanāhī”ti punappunaṃ āṇāpanavasena vā, dvīhi pahārehi niyatamaraṇāya dutiyapahāradānavasena vā mātughātikammaṃ mātughātikammassa upanissayo hoti. Sesānipi yathāyogaṃ imināva nayena veditabbāni. Yasmā pana balavākusalaṃ dubbalākusalassa upanissayo na hoti, tasmā kammapathānantariyakammavaseneva desanā katāti vadanti. Taṃ na ekantato gahetabbaṃ. Pāṇātipātādīni hi katvā “kasmā evamakāsī”ti codiyamāno kopamattakampi karoti. Vippaṭisārīpi hoti. Appamattakepi ca kilese uppanne taṃ vaḍḍhetvā vītikkamaṃ karoti. Tasmā balavaṃ dubbalassa dubbalañca balavassāpi upanissayo hotiyeva. Yaṃ pana paccayavibhaṅgassa uddesavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttaṃ “balavakāraṇaṭṭhena upanissayo hotī”ti, taṃ kāraṇabhāvasseva balavatāya vuttaṃ, na upanissayapaccayadhammānaṃ. Kammakilesā hi balavantopi dubbalāpi balavakāraṇaṃ hontiyeva.

The act of matricide is a supporting condition for the act of matricide in the following ways: seeing another person killing their mother and thinking, “It is fitting to do so,” then killing one's own mother; or killing one's mother in one existence and then again in another existence; or repeatedly commanding someone, “Go, kill my mother,” in the same existence; or delivering a second blow to ensure certain death. In these ways, the act of matricide serves as a supporting condition for the act of matricide. The remaining cases should be understood in the same manner, as is appropriate. However, since a strong unwholesome state is not a supporting condition for a weak unwholesome one, some say that the teaching is given only with reference to the course of action that is an immediately effective kamma. But this should not be taken as absolute. For having committed acts like killing living beings, when questioned, “Why did you do this?” one may react with even slight anger or experience remorse. And when even minor defilements arise, they can grow and lead to transgression. Therefore, a strong state can indeed be a supporting condition for a weak one, and a weak state for a strong one. As for what was stated in the commentary on the summary of the Analysis of Conditions—'it is a supporting condition in the sense of a strong cause'—that was said concerning the strength of the causal state itself, not of the phenomena that are the supporting condition. For kamma and defilements, whether strong or weak, can indeed be a strong cause.

Rāgaṃ [M 0.0447] upanissāya dānaṃ detītiādīsu aho vatāhaṃ cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyyanti upapattibhave vā bhogesu vā rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti. Sīlasamādānauposathakammesupi eseva nayo. Jhānaṃ pana rāgavikkhambhanatthāya, vipassanaṃ rāgassa pahānatthāya, maggaṃ samucchedanatthāya uppādento rāgaṃ upanissāya uppādeti nāma. Vītarāgabhāvatthāya pana abhiññaṃ samāpattiñca uppādento rāgaṃ upanissāya uppādeti nāma. Ettāvatā hi vītarāgo nāma hoti.

In cases such as giving gifts based on attachment, one thinks, “Oh, if only I could be reborn into the fellowship of the Four Great Kings!”—thus, one gives gifts based on attachment either for rebirth or for enjoyments. The same principle applies to undertaking precepts and Uposatha observances. However, when one generates jhāna for the purpose of suppressing attachment, develops insight for the purpose of abandoning attachment, or brings forth the path for the purpose of eradicating attachment, one is said to generate these states based on attachment. Moreover, when one generates higher knowledge and meditative attainments for the sake of becoming free from attachment, one is said to generate these states based on attachment. For by this much, one is called free from attachment.

Saddhāyāti dānādivasena pavattasaddhāya sīlādīsupi eseva nayo. Yatheva hi dānādivasena saddhādayo uppādento rāgaṃ upanissāya uppādeti nāma, evaṃ rāgādayopi saddhādīnaṃ upanissayapaccayā nāma hontīti veditabbā. Tassa paṭighātatthāyāti tassa paṭibāhanatthāya, vipākokāsassa anuppadānatthāyāti attho. Sappaṭighātesu tāva evaṃ hotu, yāni pana appaṭighātāni ānantariyakammāni, tesu “tassa paṭighātatthāyā”ti kasmā vuttanti? Tassa ajjhāsayavasena. Tappaṭighātatthāya pavattemīti hissa ajjhāsayo, taṃ gahetvā evaṃ vuttaṃ.

By faith: The same principle applies to faith that proceeds by way of generosity and so on, and to morality and so on. Just as one who generates faith and the like by way of generosity and so on is said to generate it based on attachment, so too should it be understood that attachment and other defilements are called the decisive-support condition for faith and the like. “For the purpose of obstructing it” means for the purpose of repelling it, that is, to prevent the arising of its resultant opportunity. This may be so in the case of kamma subject to obstruction. But why is it said, “for the purpose of obstructing it,” in the case of non-obstructive kamma, such as deeds with immediate result? It is due to the underlying intention. For the intention is, “I act to repel it,” and thus it is stated accordingly.

Rāgaṃ upanissāya attānaṃ ātāpetīti yattha ratto, tassa dukkarena pattiṃ sampassanto evaṃ [V 0.0444] karotīti sabbaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Kāyikassa sukhassāti rāgādisamatikkamavasena kusalaṃ katvā paṭiladdhasukhassa vā rāgādivasena anādīnavadassāvino kāme paribhuñjanavasena uppannasukhassa vā. Dukkhassāti ātāpanādivasena uppannasukhassa vā rāgādihetu pavattavadhabandhanādivasena uppannadukkhassa vā. Phalasamāpattiyāti rāgādayo samucchinditvā vā uppāditāya tehi vā aṭṭīyamānena samāpannāya.

“One torments oneself by relying on lust” means that where one is attached, seeing the attainment of that with difficulty, one acts thus—this should be understood in the same way as before. “Bodily happiness” refers to the happiness obtained by doing good through overcoming lust and the like, or to the happiness arising from enjoying sensual pleasures while not seeing the dangers of lust and the like. “Suffering” refers to the happiness arisen by way of self-torment and so on, or to the suffering arisen by way of destruction, bondage, and the like, caused by lust and the like. “Fruition attainment” refers to the fruition attained either by eradicating lust and the like, or by one who is distressed by them.

Kāyikaṃ sukhantiādīsu sukhe uppanne taṃ assādetvā punappunaṃ tathārūpeheva paccayehi taṃ uppādentassa purimaṃ pacchimassa upanissayo hoti. Sītādīsu pana aggisantāpanādīni atisevantassa pubbabhāge sukhaṃ aparabhāge dukkhassa, “sukho vati missā paribbājikāya taruṇāya lomasāya bāhāya samphasso”ti kāmesu pātabyataṃ āpajjantassa idha kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ nerayikassa kāyikadukkhassa, arogabhāvena pana sukhino phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjantassa kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayo [M 0.0448] hoti. Dukkhapaṭighātāya pana sukhaṃ sevantassa dukkhapaṭighātāya ca bhagavato viya ābādhaṃ vikkhambhetvā phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjantassa kāyikadukkhaṃ kāyikasukhassa ceva phalasamāpattiyā ca, upanissayapaccayo hoti. Utusappāyo sukhassa ceva phalasamāpattiyā ca, asappāyo dukkhassa. Utuasappāyaṃ vā abhibhavitvā samāpattisamuṭṭhitarūpavasena uppannaṃ sukhaṃ anubhavitukāmassa asappāyopi utu phalasamāpattiyā paccayova. Bhojanasenāsanesupi eseva nayo. Puna kāyikaṃ sukhantiādīni kevalaṃ ekato dassitāni. Heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva panesaṃ paccayabhāvo veditabbo. Phalasamāpatti kāyikassa sukhassāti samāpattisamuṭṭhānarūpavasena uppannassa sukhassa. Taṃ hesa samāpattito vuṭṭhāya anubhavati.

In the case of bodily pleasure, etc., when pleasure arises, by delighting in it and repeatedly arousing it through similar conditions, the former becomes a decisive support condition for the latter. However, for one who excessively indulges in cold or heat, or warming oneself by fire and so on, pleasure arises in the initial stage, but suffering in the later stage. For one who engages in sensual misconduct, thinking, “How pleasant is the touch of the young, soft-haired arms of the wandering ascetic woman,” the bodily pleasure here becomes a condition for the bodily suffering of a hell-being. Yet, for one who is healthy and attains fruition attainment, bodily pleasure serves as a decisive support condition for fruition attainment. For one who cultivates pleasure to counteract suffering, and for one who, like the Blessed One warding off illness, attains fruition attainment to counteract suffering, bodily suffering becomes a decisive support condition for both bodily pleasure and fruition attainment. A suitable climate is a condition for pleasure and fruition attainment, while an unsuitable climate is a condition for suffering. Even if one overcomes an unsuitable climate and wishes to experience pleasure arisen through absorption-produced material form, the unsuitable climate still serves as a condition for fruition attainment. The same principle applies to food and lodging. Again, “bodily pleasure,” etc., are shown here only together. However, their conditionality should be understood according to the method explained above. “Fruition attainment for bodily pleasure” refers to the pleasure arisen through absorption-produced material form. After emerging from attainment, one experiences that pleasure.

Kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya dānantiādīsu “aho vata me idaṃ sukhaṃ na parihāyeyyā”ti pattassa vā aparihāyanavasena; “aho vatāhaṃ āyatiṃ evarūpaṃ sukhaṃ pāpuṇeyya”nti appattassa vā pattivasena; dukkhepi “aho vata me dukkhaṃ parihāyeyyā”ti pattassa parihāyanavasena vā; “āyatiṃ evarūpaṃ nuppajjeyyā”ti anuppādapatthanāvasena vā sukhadukkhānaṃ upanissayatā veditabbā. Utubhojanasenāsanāni vuttanayāneva. Puna kāyikaṃ sukhantiādīsu yasmā “sādhu kho, mārisa, moggallāna, buddhasaraṇagamanaṃ hotī”ti sukhappattānampi, “sammāsambuddho vata, so bhagavā, yo evarūpassa dukkhassa pariññāya dhammaṃ desetī”ti [V 0.0445] (udā. 18) dukkhappattānampi saddhā uppajjati. Sukhadukkhehi ca saṃyogaviyogatthāya sīlādiparipūraṇaṃ kareyya, tasmā sukhadukkhāni saddhādīnaṃ upanissayabhāvena dassitāni. Utuādīnipi yathāyogaṃ yojetabbāni. Kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanatītiādīsupi vuttanayānusāreneva sukhādīnaṃ upanissayatā veditabbā.

Relying on bodily happiness, in cases such as giving and so forth, one thinks, “Oh, may this happiness of mine not decline!”—by way of the non-decline of what has been attained. Or one thinks, “Oh, may I attain such happiness in the future!”—by way of the attainment of what has not yet been attained. Even in suffering, one thinks, “Oh, may this suffering of mine decline!”—by way of the decline of what has been attained. Or one thinks, “May such suffering not arise in the future!”—by way of the aspiration for non-arising. Thus, the nature of happiness and suffering as decisive support conditions should be understood. Seasons, food, and lodging are just as was stated. Furthermore, regarding bodily happiness and so forth, since faith arises even in those who have attained happiness, as in the statement, “Good indeed, friend Moggallāna, is going for refuge to the Buddha,” and even in those who have attained suffering, as in the statement, “Truly, the Blessed One is the perfectly enlightened one, who teaches the Dhamma for the full understanding of such suffering” (Udāna 18), and one would fulfill virtue and other practices for the sake of union with happiness and separation from suffering, therefore, happiness and suffering are shown as being decisive support conditions for faith and other qualities. Seasons and the like should be connected accordingly. Even in cases such as killing a living being relying on bodily happiness, the nature of happiness and so forth as decisive support conditions should be understood in the same way as explained.

Imasmiṃ pana upanissayabhājanīye kusalo kusalassa tividhenāpi upanissayo, akusalassa duvidhena, abyākatassa tividhena. Akusalo akusalassa tividhena, kusalassa ekavidhena, abyākatassa duvidhena. Abyākatopi abyākatassa tividhena, tathā kusalassa, tathā [M 0.0449] akusalassāti. Evaṃ kusalo aṭṭhavidhena, akusalo chabbidhena, abyākato navavidhenāti tevīsatividhena upanissayo bhājitoti veditabbo.

In this analysis of decisive support, the wholesome is a decisive support for the wholesome in three ways, for the unwholesome in two ways, and for the indeterminate in three ways. The unwholesome is a decisive support for the unwholesome in three ways, for the wholesome in one way, and for the indeterminate in two ways. The indeterminate is also a decisive support for the indeterminate in three ways, likewise for the wholesome, and likewise for the unwholesome. Thus, the wholesome is a decisive support in eight ways, the unwholesome in six ways, and the indeterminate in nine ways—in this way decisive support is analyzed into twenty-three types, it should be understood.

424. Purejāte cakkhādīni oḷārikavasena vuttāni. Āpodhātuādīnipi pana purejātārammaṇāni hontiyeva. Vatthu purejātaṃ cakkhāyatanantiādi yaṃ vatthu hutvā purejātaṃ hoti, taṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Vatthu vipākābyākatānanti pavattiyaṃ purejātapaccayaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

424. In the case of the pre-nascent condition, the eye and so forth are stated by way of being gross. But the water element and others are indeed pre-nascent objects. The statement, “The base is pre-nascent, like the eye-base,” and so forth, is said to show that which, having become a base, is pre-nascent. The statement, “The base is resultant and indeterminate,” is said with reference to the pre-nascent condition in the course of existence.

425. Pacchājāte imassa kāyassāti cātumahābhūtikakāyassa. Pacchājātapaccayena paccayoti upatthambhanavasena pacchājāto hutvā paccayo. Upatthambhakaṭṭhena paccayattāyeva hesa pacchājātapaccayoti imasmiṃ pañhāvāre anulomato āgato.

425. In the post-nascent condition, 'for this body' means for the body composed of the four great elements. 'A condition by way of post-nascent condition' means that, having arisen afterward, it is a condition by way of support. Because it is a condition in the sense of supporting, it is called the post-nascent condition—this is presented in this question section in the forward order.

426. Āsevanapaccaye anulomaṃ gotrabhussātiādīnaṃ visuṃ gahaṇe heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva kāraṇaṃ veditabbaṃ.

426. In the repetition condition, regarding the separate mention of adaptation, change-of-lineage, and so forth, the reason should be understood in the same way as stated before.

427. Kammapaccaye kusalā cetanā sampayuttakānanti ettha sahajātanānākkhaṇikavibhāgassa abhāvato sahajātāti na vuttā. Abyākatavissajjane pana so vibhāgo atthi, tasmā tattha vuttā. Paṭisandhiggahaṇaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ vasena kataṃ. Cetanā vatthussāti kiñcāpi paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthupatiṭṭhitā arūpadhammā vatthupaccayā vattanti, cetanā pana vatthussāpi paccayoti dassetuṃ vuttaṃ.

427. In the kamma condition, regarding 'wholesome volition for associated states,' here, because there is no division into co-nascent and different-moment, 'co-nascent' is not stated. However, in the answer concerning the indeterminate, that division exists, so it is stated there. The taking of rebirth-linking is done by way of kamma-produced matter. The statement, 'Volition is a condition for the base,' is said to show that although at the moment of rebirth-linking immaterial phenomena established on a base proceed by way of the base condition, volition, however, is also a condition for the base.

428. Vipākapaccaye [V 0.0446] paṭisandhivāre imināva nayena attho veditabbo.

428. In the resultant condition, in the section on rebirth-linking, the meaning should be understood in this same way.

429-438. Āhārapaccaye imassa kāyassāti imasmiṃ catusantativasena pavatte cātumahābhūtikakāye āhārasamuṭṭhānassa janakavasena, sesassa upatthambhakavasena āhārapaccayena paccayo. Indriyapaccayādīsupi paṭisandhivāro vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

429-438. In the nutriment condition, 'for this body' means: in this body composed of the four great elements, which proceeds by way of the fourfold continuity, it is a condition by way of nutriment condition by generating nutriment-originated matter and, for the remainder, by way of supporting. In the faculty condition and so forth, too, the section on rebirth-linking should be understood in the same way as stated. The rest is everywhere of obvious meaning.

Pañhāvāravibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Analysis of the Question Section is concluded.

Pañhāvārassa ghaṭane anulomagaṇanā

Enumeration of the Forward Order in the Combination of the Question Section

439. Idānettha [M 0.0450] yathāladdhāni vissajjanāni gaṇanāvasena dassetuṃ hetuyā sattātiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sattāti kusalena kusalaṃ, abyākataṃ, kusalābyākatanti tīṇi. Tathā akusalena; abyākatena abyākatamevāti evaṃ satta. Ārammaṇe navāti ekamūlakaekāvasānāni nava. Adhipatiyā dasāti kusalaṃ kusalassa sahajātato ceva ārammaṇato ca; akusalassa ārammaṇatova abyākatassa sahajātato ceva ārammaṇato ca; kusalābyākatassa sahajātatovāti kusalamūlakāni cattāri. Akusalaṃ akusalassa sahajātato ceva ārammaṇato ca; abyākatassa sahajātatova tathā akusalābyākatassāti akusalamūlakāni tīṇi. Abyākato abyākatassa sahajātato ceva ārammaṇato ca; kusalassa ārammaṇatova tathā akusalassāti abyākatamūlakāni tīṇīti evaṃ dasa. Ettha pana ārammaṇādhipatipi sattadhā, sahajātādhipatipi sattadhāva labbhati.

439. Now here, to present the answers as they have been obtained by way of enumeration, the passage beginning, 'In the root condition, seven,' is stated. Therein, 'seven' means: by the wholesome, for the wholesome, for the indeterminate, and for the wholesome-and-indeterminate—three; similarly by the unwholesome—three; by the indeterminate, for the indeterminate only—one; thus there are seven. In the object condition, there are nine: the nine that are single-rooted and single-ended. In the predominance condition, there are ten: wholesome is a condition for wholesome by way of both co-nascence and object; for unwholesome by way of object only; for indeterminate by way of both co-nascence and object; for wholesome-and-indeterminate by way of co-nascence only—thus there are four rooted in the wholesome. Unwholesome is a condition for unwholesome by way of both co-nascence and object; for indeterminate by way of co-nascence only; similarly for unwholesome-and-indeterminate—thus there are three rooted in the unwholesome. Indeterminate is a condition for indeterminate by way of both co-nascence and object; for wholesome by way of object only; similarly for unwholesome—thus there are three rooted in the indeterminate. In this way, there are ten. Here, however, object-predominance is obtained in seven ways, and co-nascent-predominance is also obtained in seven ways.

Anantare sattāti kusalamūlakāni dve, tathā akusalamūlakāni, abyākatamūlakāni tīṇīti evaṃ satta. Samanantarepi etāneva. Sahajāte navāti kusalamūlakāni tīṇi, akusalamūlakāni tīṇi, abyākatamūlakaṃ ekaṃ, tathā kusalābyākatamūlakaṃ, akusalābyākatamūlakañcāti evaṃ nava. Aññamaññe tīṇīti kusalena kusalaṃ, akusalena akusalaṃ[V 0.0447], abyākatena abyākatanti evaṃ tīṇi. Nissaye terasāti sahajātatova kusalamūlakāni tīṇi, tathā akusalamūlakāni, tathā abyākatamūlakāni. Ettha pana purejātampi labbhati. Abyākatañhi abyākatassa sahajātampi hoti purejātampi; kusalassa purejātameva tathā akusalassa. Puna kusalābyākato sahajātapurejātato kusalassa, sahajātatova abyākatassa, tathā akusalābyākatoti evaṃ terasa. Upanissaye navāti ekamūlakekāvasānā nava. Tesaṃ vibhaṅge tevīsati bhedā dassitā. Tesu ārammaṇūpanissaye satta, anantarūpanissaye satta, pakatūpanissaye nava honti. Purejāte tīṇīti abyākato abyākatassa, kusalassa, akusalassāti evaṃ tīṇi.

In immediate contiguity, there are seven: two wholesome roots, similarly two unwholesome roots, and three indeterminate roots—thus seven. In proximity, these same. In co-nascence, there are nine: three wholesome roots, three unwholesome roots, one indeterminate root, and also a wholesome-indeterminate root and an unwholesome-indeterminate root—thus nine. In mutuality, there are three: wholesome with wholesome, unwholesome with unwholesome, indeterminate with indeterminate—thus three. In dependence, there are thirteen: from co-nascence, three wholesome roots, similarly three unwholesome roots, and similarly three indeterminate roots. Here, however, pre-nascence is also found. For the indeterminate is related to the indeterminate by both co-nascence and pre-nascence; to the wholesome by pre-nascence only, and similarly for the unwholesome. Again, the wholesome-indeterminate is related to the wholesome by co-nascence and pre-nascence, and to the indeterminate by co-nascence alone; similarly for the unwholesome-indeterminate—thus thirteen. In decisive support, there are nine: nine with a single root and a single conclusion. In their analysis, twenty-three distinctions are shown. Among them, there are seven in object-decisive support, seven in immediate-decisive support, and nine in natural-decisive support. In pre-nascence, there are three: the indeterminate is related to the indeterminate, to the wholesome, and to the unwholesome—thus three.

Pacchājāte [M 0.0451] tīṇīti kusalo abyākatassa, akusalo abyākatassa, abyākato abyākatassāti evaṃ tīṇi. Āsevane tīṇi aññamaññasadisāni. Kamme satta hetusadisāni. Tattha dvīsu vissajjanesu nānākkhaṇikakammampi āgataṃ, pañcasu sahajātameva. Vipāke ekaṃ abyākatena abyākataṃ. Āhāraindriyajhānamaggesu satta hetusadisāneva. Indriyaṃ panettha sahajātapurejātavasena āgataṃ. Sampayutte tīṇi aññamaññasadisāni. Vippayutte pañcāti sahajātapacchājātato kusalena abyākataṃ, akusalena abyākataṃ, sahajātapurejātapacchājātato abyākatena abyākataṃ, vatthupurejātato abyākatena kusalaṃ, tathā akusalanti ekaṃ kusalamūlaṃ, ekaṃ akusalamūlaṃ, tīṇi abyākatamūlānīti evaṃ pañca.

In post-nascence, there are three: the wholesome conditioning the indeterminate, the unwholesome conditioning the indeterminate, and the indeterminate conditioning the indeterminate—thus three. In repetition, there are three, similar to mutuality. In kamma, there are seven, similar to the root condition. Here, in two expositions, kamma occurring at different moments is also included; in the five, only that which is co-nascent. In result, there is one: the indeterminate conditioning the indeterminate. In nutriment, faculty, jhāna, and path, there are seven, similar to the root condition. Here, faculty is included by way of co-nascence and pre-nascence. In association, there are three, similar to mutuality. In dissociation, there are five: from co-nascence and post-nascence, the wholesome conditioning the indeterminate, and the unwholesome conditioning the indeterminate; from co-nascence, pre-nascence, and post-nascence, the indeterminate conditioning the indeterminate; from the pre-nascent base, the indeterminate conditioning the wholesome, and similarly the unwholesome—thus, one wholesome-rooted, one unwholesome-rooted, and three indeterminate-rooted—thus five.

Atthiyā terasāti sahajātato kusalena kusalaṃ, sahajātapacchājātato kusalena abyākataṃ, sahajātatova kusalena kusalābyākatanti kusalamūlāni tīṇi, tathā akusalamūlāni, sahajātapurejātapacchājātāhārindriyato pana abyākatena abyākataṃ, vatthārammaṇapurejātato abyākatena kusalaṃ, tathā akusalaṃ, sahajātapurejātato kusalo ca abyākato ca akusalassa; sveva abyākatassa sahajātapacchājātaāhārindriyato sahajātapurejātato ca kusalo ca abyākato ca kusalassa; sveva abyākatassa sahajātapacchājātaāhārindriyatoti evaṃ terasa. Natthivigatesu satta anantarasadisāni. Avigate terasa atthisadisānīti. Evamettha satta gaṇanaparicchedā ekaṃ tīṇi pañca satta nava dasa terasāti. Tesu vipākavasena ekameva ekakaṃ, aññamaññapurejātapacchājātāsevanasampayuttavasena pañca tikā, vippayuttavasena ekameva pañcakaṃ, hetuanantarasamanantarakammaāhārindriyajhānamagganatthivigatavasena [V 0.0448] dasa sattakā, ārammaṇasahajātaupanissayavasena tayo navakā, adhipativasena ekaṃ dasakaṃ, nissayaatthiavigatavasena tayo terasakāti evaṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ paccaye niddiṭṭhavāre gaṇanavasena sādhukaṃ sallakkhetvā tesaṃ vasena dukatikādīsu paccayasaṃsandane gaṇanā veditabbā.

In presence, there are thirteen: from co-nascence, the wholesome with the wholesome; from co-nascence and post-nascence, the wholesome with the indeterminate; from co-nascence alone, the wholesome with the wholesome-and-indeterminate—thus, three wholesome-rooted. Similarly, three unwholesome-rooted. Further, from co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty, the indeterminate with the indeterminate. From the base, object, and pre-nascence, the indeterminate with the wholesome, and similarly with the unwholesome. From co-nascence and pre-nascence, the wholesome and the indeterminate are conditions for the unwholesome; these same two are also conditions for the indeterminate by way of co-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. And from co-nascence and pre-nascence, the wholesome and the indeterminate are conditions for the wholesome; these same two are also conditions for the indeterminate by way of co-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty—thus thirteen. In absence and disappearance, there are seven, similar to immediate contiguity. In non-disappearance, there are thirteen, similar to presence. Thus, here, there are seven numerical enumerations: one, three, five, seven, nine, ten, and thirteen. Among them: by way of result, there is only one single item; by way of mutuality, pre-nascence, post-nascence, repetition, and association, there are five triads; by way of dissociation, only one pentad; by way of root, immediate contiguity, proximity, kamma, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, absence, and disappearance, there are ten heptads; by way of object, co-nascence, and decisive support, there are three nonads; by way of dominance, one decad; by way of dependence, presence, and non-disappearance, there are three groups of thirteen. Thus, for each condition, having carefully considered the numerical arrangements in the specified sections, the calculation for the combination of conditions in dyads, triads, etc., should be understood.

440. Ye pana paccayā yesaṃ paccayānaṃ visabhāgā vā viruddhā vā honti, te tehi saddhiṃ na yojetabbā. Seyyathidaṃ – hetupaccayassa tāva ārammaṇānantarasamanantarūpanissayapurejātapacchājātakammāsevanāhārajhānanatthivigatā [M 0.0452] adhipatipaccaye ca ṭhapetvā vīmaṃsaṃ sesādhipatino visabhāgā, sahajātādayo sabhāgā. Kasmā? Tathā bhāvābhāvato. Hetupaccayo hi yesaṃ hetupaccayo hoti, tesaṃ sahajātādipaccayopi hoti, ārammaṇādipaccayo pana na hotīti ārammaṇādayo tassa visabhāgā nāma. Tasmā so tehi, te vā tena saddhiṃ, na yojetabbā. Purejātapacchājātasampayuttavippayuttaatthinatthivigatāvigatā ca aññamaññaviruddhā, tepi aññamaññaṃ na yojetabbā. Tattha ayojanīye vajjetvā yojanīyehi yoge ye vārā labbhanti, te saṅkhepato dassetuṃ hetupaccayā adhipatiyā cattārītiādi vuttaṃ.

440. Those conditions which are incompatible or contradictory to other conditions should not be combined with them. For example: with the root condition, the following are incompatible: the object, immediate contiguity, proximity, decisive support, pre-nascence, post-nascence, kamma, repetition, nutriment, jhāna, absence, and disappearance conditions; and in the dominance condition, excepting investigation, the remaining dominances are also incompatible. The co-nascence and other similar conditions are compatible. Why? Because of the presence and absence of such a nature. For those phenomena for which the root condition applies, the co-nascence condition and similar conditions also apply, but the object condition and others do not. Thus, the object condition and others are called incompatible with it. Therefore, it should not be combined with them, nor they with it. Pre-nascence, post-nascence, association, dissociation, presence, absence, disappearance, and non-disappearance are mutually contradictory; they too should not be combined with each other. Here, excluding the non-combinable and combining the combinable, the permutations that are obtained are shown in brief, as when it is said, 'With the root condition and dominance, there are four,' and so on.

Tattha kiñcāpi hetupaccayassa adhipatinā saṃsandane ūnataragaṇanavasena sattahi vārehi bhavitabbaṃ, yasmā pana adhipatīsu vīmaṃsāva hetupaccayo, na itare, tasmā visabhāge vajjetvā sabhāgavasena “cattārī”ti vuttaṃ.
