Tāni evaṃ veditabbāni – kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo adhipatipaccayena paccayo; kusalā vīmaṃsā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ, kusalo dhammo abyākatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo adhipatipaccayena paccayo; kusalā vīmaṃsā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ, kusalo dhammo kusalassa ca abyākatassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo adhipatipaccayena paccayo; kusalā vīmaṃsā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ, abyākato dhammo abyākatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo adhipatipaccayena paccayo; vipākābyākatā kiriyābyākatā vīmaṃsā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānanti. Ettha ca vipākābyākatā lokuttaratova gahetabbā. Ārammaṇapaccayaanantarapaccayādayo pana visabhāgattā na yojitā. Iminā upāyena sabbattha labbhamānañca alabbhamānañca ñatvā labbhamānavasena vārā uddharitabbā.

Here, although in the combination of the root condition with the dominance condition, there should be seven instances by way of the lesser count, since among the dominance conditions, only investigation is a root condition, not the others, therefore, excluding the dissimilar, it is said 'four' by way of the similar. These should be understood thus: A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of the root condition and dominance condition; wholesome investigation for the associated aggregates. A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of the root condition and dominance condition; wholesome investigation for mind-originated material phenomena. A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for both wholesome and indeterminate phenomena by way of the root condition and dominance condition; wholesome investigation for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of the root condition and dominance condition; investigation that is resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena. And here, the resultant-indeterminate should be taken as only the supramundane. The object condition, contiguity condition, and others are not applied due to dissimilarity. By this method, knowing what is obtainable and unobtainable in all cases, the instances should be extracted according to what is obtainable.

Sahajāte [V 0.0449] sattāti hetuyā laddhāneva. Aññamaññe tīṇīti suddhikaaññamaññe laddhāneva. Nissaye sattāti hetuyā laddhāneva. Vipāke ekanti suddhikavipāke laddhameva. Indriyamaggesu cattārīti heṭṭhā vuttanayāneva[M 0.0453]. Sampayutte tīṇīti suddhikasampayutte laddhāneva. Vippayutte tīṇīti kusalādicittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ paccayuppannaṃ katvā veditabbāni. Atthiavigatesu sattāti hetuyā laddhāneva.

In the co-arisen, seven [instances] are obtained, just as in the root condition. In mutuality, three [instances] are obtained, just as in pure mutuality. In dependence, seven [instances] are obtained, just as in the root condition. In result, one [instance] is obtained, just as in pure result. In the faculties and paths, four [instances] are just as stated below. In association, three [instances] are obtained, just as in pure association. In dissociation, three [instances] should be understood by taking material phenomenon arising from wholesome consciousness and so on as conditionally produced. In presence and non-disappearance, seven [instances] are obtained, just as in the root condition.

441-443. Evaṃ yehi adhipatipaccayādīhi ekādasahi paccayehi saddhiṃ hetupaccayo yojanaṃ labhati, tesaṃ vasena dumūlakanaye gaṇanaṃ dassetvā idāni timūlakādīsu tassa dassanatthaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ ṭhapento hetusahajātanissayaatthiavigatanti sattātiādimāha. Potthakesu pana nissaupanissaadhipāti evaṃ parihīnakkharāni paccayanāmāni likhanti, taṃ saññākaraṇamattavasena likhitaṃ. Tasmā tādisesu ṭhānesu paripuṇṇā pāḷi kātabbā. Yaṃ panidaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ ṭhapitaṃ, tena idaṃ dīpeti – ayaṃ hetupaccayo sahajātādīhi catūhi saddhiṃ saṃsandane attano vibhaṅge laddhāni satteva vissajjanāni labhati. Sace panettha aññamaññapaccayo pavisati, aññamaññe laddhāni tīṇi labhati. Sace sampayuttapaccayo pavisati, tāneva tīṇi labhati. Sace vippayuttapaccayo pavisati, hetuvippayuttaduke laddhāni tīṇi labhati. Sace vipākapaccayo pavisati, sabbehi vipākasabhāgehi saddhiṃ saṃsandane evameva vissajjanaṃ labhati. Sace panettha indriyamaggapaccayā pavisanti, tehi saddhiṃ dumūlake laddhāni cattāriyeva labhati. Sace tehi saddhiṃ aññamaññapaccayo pavisati, hetādhipatiduke dassitesu catūsu vissajjanesu “kusalo dhammo abyākatassa, kusalo dhammo kusalassa ca abyākatassa cā”ti dve apanetvā sesāni dve labhati. Sacepi tattha sampayuttapaccayo pavisati, tāneva dve labhati. Sace pana vippayuttapaccayo pavisati, itarāni dve labhati. Sace pana tesu vipākapaccayo pavisati, sabbattha ekameva labhati. Adhipatinā pana saddhiṃ hetādhipatidukato ūnataragaṇanesu appavisantesu cattāriyeva labhati. Ūnataragaṇanesu pavisantesu tesaṃ vasena dve ekanti labhati. Evaṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ paccayānaṃ samāyoge labbhamānaṃ gaṇanaṃ viditvā timūlakādīsu gaṇanā uddharitabbāti.

441-443. Thus, having shown the calculation in the two-rooted method by way of the eleven conditions, such as the dominance condition, with which the root condition obtains combination, now, to illustrate its application in the three-rooted and other methods, the characteristic is established, saying: 'hetusahajātanissayaatthiavigatanti sattātiādimāha.' In the texts, however, condition names are sometimes written incompletely, such as 'nissaupanissaadhipāti,' with missing letters. This is written merely for the sake of recognition. Therefore, in such places, the full Pāli should be supplied. Now, this established characteristic clarifies this: This root condition, when combined with the four conditions like co-arisen and so on, obtains the seven answers found in its own analysis. If the mutuality condition is also involved here, it obtains three answers as found in mutuality. If the association condition is involved, it obtains those same three. If the dissociation condition is involved, it obtains three answers as found in the root-dissociation pair. If the result condition is involved, it similarly obtains an answer when combined with all states sharing the nature of result. If the faculty and path conditions are involved here, when combined with them, it obtains only four answers as found in the two-rooted method. If the mutuality condition is also involved with them, then, after excluding the two answers—'a wholesome phenomenon for an indeterminate one' and 'a wholesome phenomenon for both a wholesome and an indeterminate one'—from the four answers shown in the root-dominance pair, the remaining two are obtained. If the association condition is also involved there, those same two are obtained. If the dissociation condition is involved, the other two are obtained. If the result condition is involved within these, only one is obtained in all cases. When combined with the dominance condition, if these other conditions do not enter the groups with fewer counts, only four answers are obtained. If they enter the groups with fewer counts, then, depending on them, either two or one is obtained. Thus, having understood the calculation arising from the combination of these various conditions, the calculation should be extracted in the three-rooted and other methods.

Etesu [M 0.0454] pana ghaṭanesu sabbapaṭhamāni cattāri ghaṭanāni sāmaññato navannampi hetūnaṃ vasena vuttāni avipākāni. Abyākatena abyākatavissajjane panettha vipākahetupi labbhati.

Among these combinations, the very first four combinations are stated generally as non-resultant by way of all nine roots. However, in the answer of an indeterminate phenomenon for an indeterminate phenomenon, resultant roots are also obtained here.

Tato [V 0.0450] parāni pañca ghaṭanāni vipākahetuvasena vuttāni. Tattha sabbepi sahajātavipākā ceva vipākasahajātarūpā ca. Tesu paṭhame ghaṭane vipākā ceva taṃsamuṭṭhānarūpā ca labbhanti, dutiye vipākā ceva paṭisandhiyañca vatthurūpaṃ. Tatiye arūpadhammāva. Catutthe vipākacittasamuṭṭhānarūpameva labbhati. Pañcame vatthurūpameva.

Then, the remaining five combinations are stated by way of resultant roots. Herein, all are both co-arisen results and material phenomena co-arisen with result. Among these, in the first combination, both results and material phenomena arisen from them are obtained. In the second, both results and the base material phenomenon at rebirth-linking are obtained. In the third, only immaterial phenomena are obtained. In the fourth, only the material phenomenon produced by resultant consciousness is obtained. In the fifth, only the base material phenomenon is obtained.

Tato parāni pañcadasa ghaṭanāni indriyamaggayuttāni amohahetuvasena vuttāni. Tattha paṭhamāni nava nirādhipatīni, pacchimāni cha sādhipatīni. Nirādhipatikesupi paṭhamāni cattāri sāmaññato sabbattha amohavasena vuttāni, pacchimāni pañca vipākāmohavasena. Tattha nirādhipatikesu paṭhame cattārīti heṭṭhā hetādhipatiduke dassitāneva. Dutiye cittasamuṭṭhānarūpaṃ parihāyati. Tatiye vatthurūpaṃ parihāyati. Catutthe kusalo dhammo cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ, abyākato taṃsamuṭṭhānānanti rūpameva labbhati. Tato parāni vipākayuttāni pañca heṭṭhā vuttanayāneva. Sādhipatikesu paṭhamāni tīṇi ghaṭanāni sāmaññato vipākāvipākahetuvasena vuttāni. Tesu paṭhame cattāri vuttanayāneva. Dutiye rūpaṃ parihāyati, tatiye arūpaṃ parihāyati. Tato parāni tīṇi vipākahetuvasena vuttāni. Tesu paṭhame rūpārūpaṃ labbhati, dutiye arūpameva, tatiye rūpameva. Evampi tesaṃ tesaṃ paccayānaṃ samāyoge labbhamānaṃ gaṇanaṃ viditvā timūlakādīsu gaṇanā uddharitabbāti.

Then, the subsequent fifteen combinations, associated with the faculties and paths, are stated by way of the root of non-delusion. Among them, the first nine are without a dominance factor, and the last six are with a dominance factor. Even among those without a dominance factor, the first four are stated generally as being everywhere by way of non-delusion, while the last five are by way of resultant non-delusion. Here, among those without a dominance factor, the first four are just as shown below in the root-dominance dyad. In the second, mind-originated matter is lost. In the third, base-matter is lost. In the fourth, a wholesome state for mind-originated phenomena, and an indeterminate state for phenomena arisen from that—only matter is obtained. After that, the subsequent five associated with resultant [roots] are just as stated below. Among those with a dominance factor, the first three combinations are stated generally by way of both resultant and non-resultant roots. Among them, in the first [combination], the four [items] are just as stated before. In the second, matter is lost; in the third, the immaterial is lost. Then, the subsequent three are stated by way of the resultant root. Among them, in the first, both matter and the immaterial are obtained; in the second, only the immaterial; in the third, only matter. Thus, having understood the calculation of what is obtained in the combination of these various conditions, the calculation should be extracted for the three-rooted and other groups.

Hetumūlakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Root-Based [Section] is concluded.

444. Ārammaṇamūlakepi adhipatipaccayādayo satta ārammaṇena sabhāgā, sesā soḷasa visabhāgāti te ayojetvā satteva yojitā. Tesu adhipatiyā sattāti kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa, akusalassa dhammassa, abyākatassāti evaṃ kusalamūlāni tīṇi, akusalamūlaṃ ekaṃ, abyākatamūlāni tīṇīti satta. Nissaye tīṇīti vatthuvasena abyākatamūlāneva. Upanissaye satta heṭṭhimāni eva. Purejāte tīṇīti vatthārammaṇavasena abyākatamūlāni. Vippayutte tīṇīti [M 0.0455] vatthuvaseneva. Atthiavigatesu tīṇīti vatthārammaṇavasena. Yathā pana hetumūlake lakkhaṇadassanatthaṃ ghaṭanāni ṭhapitāni, tathā ārammaṇamūlakādīsupi.

444. In the Object-Based [Section] too, the seven conditions beginning with the dominance condition are of a similar nature to the object condition, while the remaining sixteen are of a dissimilar nature. Thus, not applying them, only seven are applied. Among these, in dominance, there are seven: a wholesome state for a wholesome state, for an unwholesome state, and for an indeterminate state—thus, three rooted in the wholesome, one rooted in the unwholesome, and three rooted in the indeterminate, making seven. In dependence, there are three—only those rooted in the indeterminate by way of the base. In strong dependence, the seven are just as the preceding ones. In prenascence, there are three—those rooted in the indeterminate by way of base and object. In dissociation, there are three—only by way of the base. In presence and non-disappearance, there are three—by way of base and object. Just as, for the purpose of illustrating the characteristics in the Root-Based [Section], combinations were established, so too in the Object-Based and other sections.

445. Tattha [V 0.0451] yāni tāva imasmiṃ ārammaṇamūlake pañca ghaṭanāni ṭhapitāni. Tattha paṭhamaṃ ārammaṇādhipativasena sādhipatikaṃ. Tattha sattāti ārammaṇādhipatiduke laddhavissajjanāneva. Dutiyaṃ nirādhipatikaṃ. Tattha tīṇīti vatthārammaṇavasena ārammaṇavaseneva vā abyākatamūlāni. Tatiyaṃ nissayena vuttaṃ. Tattha tīṇīti vatthuvasena abyākatamūlāni. Catutthapañcamāni sādhipatikāni. Tesu catutthe ekanti vatthārammaṇavasena ārammaṇavaseneva vā abyākatamūlaṃ akusalaṃ. Pañcame ekanti nissayato abyākatamūlakaṃ akusalaṃ. Evamidhāpi labbhamānavasena tikādīsu gaṇanā veditabbā. Tathā adhipatimūlakādīsu. Ārammaṇaindriyavipākavasena vitthārayojanaṃ pana avatvā tattha tattha vattabbayuttakameva vadāmāti.

445. Herein, five combinations are established in this Object-Based [Section]. Among them, the first is with a dominance factor by way of object-dominance. There, the seven are just the answers obtained in the object-dominance dyad. The second is without a dominance factor. There, the three are those rooted in the indeterminate by way of base and object, or only by way of object. The third is stated by way of dependence. There, the three are those rooted in the indeterminate by way of the base. The fourth and fifth are with a dominance factor. Among them, in the fourth, there is one: an unwholesome state rooted in the indeterminate by way of base and object, or only by way of object. In the fifth, there is one: an unwholesome state rooted in the indeterminate by way of dependence. Thus, here too, the calculation in the triads and so on should be understood according to what is obtainable. Similarly, in the Dominance-Based and other sections. However, without stating the detailed application by way of object, faculty, and result, we shall state only what is appropriate to be said in each respective place.

446. Adhipatimūlake sahajāte sattāti sahajātādhipativasena kusalamūlāni tīṇi, akusalamūlāni tīṇi, abyākatamūlaṃ ekaṃ. Sahajātena pana saddhiṃ ārammaṇādhipati, ārammaṇādhipatinā ca saddhiṃ sahajātaṃ na labbhati. Aññamaññe tīṇīti sahajātādhipativaseneva. Nissaye aṭṭhāti kusalamūlāni tīṇi, akusalamūlāni tīṇi, abyākatamūlāni dve. Abyākato hi adhipati abyākatassa sahajātato ceva ārammaṇato ca nissayo hoti, akusalassa ārammaṇatova. Kusalassa pana ubhayathāpi na hotīti abyākatamūlāni dveyevāti evaṃ aṭṭha. Upanissaye satta ārammaṇasadisāneva. Purejāte ekanti abyākatādhipati ārammaṇavasena akusalassa. Vipāke ekaṃ abyākatena abyākataṃ lokuttaraṃ. Āhārādīsu satta heṭṭhā ekamūlake laddhāneva. Vippayutte cattārīti kusalena abyākataṃ, tathā akusalena, abyākatena abyākatañca kusalañca. Atthiavigatesu aṭṭha nissayasadisāneva.

446. In the Dominance-Based [Section], in conascence, there are seven: three rooted in the wholesome, three rooted in the unwholesome, and one rooted in the indeterminate, by way of conascence-dominance. However, object-dominance is not obtained together with conascence, nor is conascence obtained together with object-dominance. In mutuality, there are three, only by way of conascence-dominance. In dependence, there are eight: three rooted in the wholesome, three rooted in the unwholesome, and two rooted in the indeterminate. For an indeterminate dominant factor is a dependence for an indeterminate state by way of both conascence and object, but for an unwholesome state, only by way of object. For a wholesome state, however, it is not a dependence in either way—thus, there are only two rooted in the indeterminate; thus, eight. In strong dependence, there are seven, just as for the object condition. In prenascence, there is one: an indeterminate dominant factor for an unwholesome state by way of object. In result, there is one: an indeterminate state by an indeterminate root, a supramundane case. In nutriment and so forth, there are seven, just as those obtained below in the single-rooted section. In dissociation, there are four: a wholesome state for an indeterminate one; similarly, an unwholesome one; and an indeterminate state for both an indeterminate and a wholesome one. In presence and non-disappearance, there are eight, just as for dependence.

447-452. Ghaṭanāni panettha paṭipāṭiyā ārammaṇādīhi ayojetvā paṭhamaṃ atthiavigatehi yojitāni. Kiṃ kāraṇāti? Ubhayādhipatimissakattā. Tattha paṭhame ghaṭane ārammaṇādhipativasena vatthārammaṇaṃ labbhati[M 0.0456], dutiye nissayavasena garuṃ katvā assādentassa vatthumeva, tatiye sahajātādhipativasena kusalādayo rūpānaṃ, ārammaṇādhipativasena vatthu akusalassa. Tato parāni tīṇi ghaṭanāni ārammaṇādhipativasena vuttāni. Tattha paṭhame sattāti heṭṭhā vuttāneva. Dutiye ekanti purejātāni vatthārammaṇāni akusalassa. Tatiye vatthumeva [V 0.0452] akusalassa. Tato parāni tīṇi ghaṭanāni vipākāvipākasādhāraṇāni sahajātādhipativasena vuttāni. Tattha paṭhame rūpārūpaṃ labbhati, dutiye arūpameva, tatiye rūpameva. Tato parāni tīṇi vipākādhipativasena vuttāni. Tesupi paṭhame rūpārūpaṃ labbhati, dutiye arūpaṃ, tatiye rūpameva. Tato parāni cha ghaṭanāni āhārindriyayuttāni cittādhipativasena vuttāni. Tattha tīṇi avipākāni, tīṇi savipākāni. Tesu gaṇanā pākaṭāyeva. Tato parāni cha ghaṭanāni tatheva viriyādhipativasena vuttāni. Nanu ca adhipatipaṭipāṭiyā paṭhamaṃ viriyādhipativasena vattabbāni siyuṃ, kasmā tathā na vuttānīti? Parato hetuvasena vuttaghaṭanehi sadisattā. Parato hi hetuvasena ghaṭanāni amohassa vīmaṃsādhipatittā vīmaṃsāya ca sammādiṭṭhibhāvato maggasampayuttāni. Viriyampi ca sammāvāyāmamicchāvāyāmabhāvena maggoti tena saddhiṃ ghaṭanāni parato hetuvasena vuttaghaṭanehi sadisānīti parivattetvā vuttāni. Tesupi gaṇanā pākaṭāyeva.

447-452. Here, the combinations are arranged in sequence, not associating them initially with object and so forth, but associating them initially with presence and non-disappearance. Why is this? Because they are mixed with both dominances. In the first combination, the physical base as object is obtained by way of object dominance; in the second, only the physical base for one who delights in it, by way of dependence, making it weighty; in the third, wholesome and other states are obtained as regards material forms by way of co-arisen dominance, while as regards the unwholesome, the physical base is obtained by way of object dominance. The next three combinations are stated by way of object dominance. Among them, in the first, 'seven' is as stated above. In the second, there is one: the pre-arisen physical bases as objects for the unwholesome. In the third, only the physical base for the unwholesome. The next three combinations are common to both resultants and non-resultants, and are stated by way of co-arisen dominance. Among them, in the first, material and immaterial are obtained; in the second, only the immaterial; in the third, only the material. The next three are stated by way of resultant dominance. Among these too, in the first, material and immaterial are obtained; in the second, only the immaterial; in the third, only the material. The next six combinations are connected with nutriment and faculties, and are stated by way of consciousness dominance. Among them, three are non-resultant, and three are resultant. Their enumeration is evident. The next six combinations are similarly stated by way of energy dominance. Now, should they not first be stated by way of energy dominance according to the sequence of dominance? Why are they not stated thus? Because they are similar to the combinations stated later by way of root condition. For later, by way of root condition, the combinations are associated with the path due to the dominance of investigation because of non-delusion, and because investigation is right view. And energy, being right effort and wrong effort, is the path. Therefore, the combinations are stated after reversing their order, as they are similar to the combinations stated later by way of root condition. Their enumeration is also evident.

453-456. Anantarasamanantaramūlakesu sattāti kusalo kusalassa abyākatassa ca, tathā akusalo, abyākato tiṇṇannampīti evaṃ satta. Kamme ekanti kusalā maggacetanā attano vipākābyākatassa. Ghaṭanāni panetesu tīṇi tīṇiyeva. Tāni bahutarapaṭipāṭiyā vuttāni.

453-456. In the root conditions of immediacy and proximity, there are seven: the wholesome for the wholesome and the indeterminate, similarly the unwholesome, and the indeterminate for all three—thus seven. In kamma, there is one: the wholesome path-volition for its own indeterminate result. However, in these, there are just three combinations each. These have been stated in a more extensive sequence.

457-460. Sahajātaaññamaññanissayamūlakesu ye ye dukamūlake paccayā vuttā te teyeva ādito ṭhitena sabhāgā. Tasmā dukamūlake gaṇanaṃ ñatvā ye upari paccayā ghaṭitā, tesu ūnataragaṇanassa vasena sabbaghaṭanesu gaṇanā veditabbā. Tattha sahajātamūlake dasa ghaṭanāni. Tesu pañca avipākāni, pañca savipākāni. Tattha avipākesu tāva paṭhame kusalo kusalassa abyākatassa[M 0.0457], kusalābyākatassa, kusalābyākato abyākatassāti cattāri, tathā akusalo, abyākato abyākatassevāti evaṃ nava. Tattha kusalākusalādikesu aṭṭhasu vissajjanesu arūpañceva cittasamuṭṭhānarūpañca labbhati. Abyākate vatthurūpampi. Dutiye ghaṭane abyākatavissajjane rūpesu vatthumeva labbhati, tatiye tīsupi arūpameva, catutthe cittasamuṭṭhānarūpameva, pañcame paṭisandhiyaṃ vatthunā saddhiṃ arūpadhammā. Savipākesu paṭhame vipākā ceva vipākacittasamuṭṭhānarūpañca, dutiye vipākā ceva vatthurūpañca, tatiye vipākameva, catutthe vipākacittasamuṭṭhānameva, pañcame vatthurūpameva labbhati.

457-460. In the root conditions of co-arisen, mutual, and dependence, whatever conditions are stated in the dual-root, those very conditions are similar to those established from the beginning. Therefore, knowing the enumeration in the dual-root, the enumeration in all combinations should be understood by way of the lesser enumeration among the conditions connected above. Herein, in the co-arisen root condition, there are ten combinations. Among them, five are non-resultant and five are resultant. First, among the non-resultants, in the first combination: wholesome for wholesome, for indeterminate, and for wholesome-and-indeterminate; and wholesome-and-indeterminate for indeterminate—thus four. Similarly for the unwholesome; and indeterminate for indeterminate only—thus nine. Herein, in the eight instances of the wholesome, unwholesome, and so forth, both immaterial phenomena and mind-produced material phenomena are obtained. In the indeterminate, the physical base is also obtained. In the second combination, in the indeterminate instance, only the physical base is obtained among material phenomena. In the third, only immaterial phenomena in all three instances. In the fourth, only mind-produced material phenomena. In the fifth, at rebirth-linking, immaterial phenomena together with the physical base. Among the resultants: in the first, both resultant and resultant-mind-produced material phenomena are obtained. In the second, both resultant and the physical base. In the third, only the resultant. In the fourth, only resultant-mind-produced material phenomena. In the fifth, only the physical base is obtained.

Aññamaññamūlake [V 0.0453] cha ghaṭanāni. Tesu paṭhamāni tīṇi avipākāni, pacchimāni tīṇi savipākāni. Tesu gaṇanā pākaṭāyeva.

In the mutual root condition, there are six combinations. Of these, the first three are non-resultant, the last three are resultant. Their enumeration is evident.

461. Nissayamūlake nissayapaccayā ārammaṇe tīṇīti vatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā pavattakusalādivasena veditabbāni. Upanissaye ekanti vatthuṃ ārammaṇūpanissayaṃ katvā uppannākusalaṃ. Sesaṃ dumūlake heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

461. In the root condition of dependence, the three dependence conditions in object should be understood by way of wholesome qualities and so forth that arise by making the physical base an object. In decisive support, there is one: the unwholesome that has arisen by making the physical base an object-decisive support. The rest, in the dual root condition, should be understood in the same way as stated above.

462-464. Imasmiṃ pana nissayapaccaye vīsati ghaṭanāni. Tesu purimāni cha ghaṭanāni purejātasahajātavasena vuttāni, tato cattāri purejātavaseneva, tato dasa sahajātavaseneva. Tattha paṭhame ghaṭane terasāti nissayapaccayavibhaṅge vuttāneva. Dutiye aṭṭhāti sahajātādhipativasena satta, vatthuṃ garuṃ katvā akusalañcāti aṭṭha. Tatiye satta indriyapaccaye laddhāneva. Catutthe pañca vippayutte laddhāni. Pañcame cattārīti kusalādīni cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ, vatthu ca akusalassa. Chaṭṭhe tīṇīti kusalādīni cittasamuṭṭhānassa. Purejātavasena catūsu paṭhame tīṇīti vatthu kusalādīnaṃ, cakkhādīni ca abyākatassa. Dutiye vatthumeva kusalādīnaṃ. Tatiye ekanti vatthu akusalassa. Catutthe cakkhādīni viññāṇapañcakassa. Sahajātavasena dasa savipākāvipākavasena dvidhā bhinditvā sahajātamūlake vuttanayeneva veditabbāni.

462-464. However, in this dependence condition, there are twenty combinations. Among them, the first six combinations are stated by way of pre-arisen and co-arisen, then four solely by way of pre-arisen, then ten solely by way of co-arisen. Among these, in the first combination, the thirteen are exactly as stated in the analysis of the dependence condition. In the second, there are eight: seven by way of co-arisen dominance, and the unwholesome by making the physical base weighty—thus eight. In the third, the seven are obtained in the faculty condition. In the fourth, the five are obtained in dissociation. In the fifth, there are four: the wholesome and so forth for mind-produced phenomena, and the physical base for the unwholesome. In the sixth, there are three: the wholesome and so forth for mind-produced phenomena. In the four by way of pre-arisen, in the first, there are three: the physical base for the wholesome and so forth, and the eye and so forth for the indeterminate. In the second, only the physical base for the wholesome and so forth. In the third, there is one: the physical base for the unwholesome. In the fourth, the eye and so forth for the fivefold consciousness. The ten co-arisen combinations should be understood by dividing them into two by way of resultant and non-resultant, following the method stated in the co-arisen root condition.

465. Upanissayamūlake ārammaṇe sattāti ārammaṇūpanissaye laddhāneva. Adhipatiyā sattāti tāneva. Anantarasamanantaresu anantarūpanissaye laddhāneva. Nissaye ekanti vatthu akusalassa. Purejāte ekanti [M 0.0458] tasseva vatthuṃ vā ārammaṇaṃ vā. Āsevane tīṇi anantarūpanissayavasena. Kamme dve pakatūpanissayavasena. Lokuttarakusalacetanā pana anantarūpanissayopi hoti. Vippayutte ekaṃ ārammaṇūpanissayavasena, tathā atthiavigatesu. Natthivigatesu satta anantarasamāneva.

465. In the decisive support root-condition, in object condition there are seven, as they are obtained in object-decisive support. In dominance, there are seven, those very same. In immediacy and proximity, they are as obtained in immediacy-decisive support. In dependence, there is one: the physical base for the unwholesome. In pre-arisen, there is one: its own physical base or object. In repetition, there are three by way of immediacy-decisive support. In kamma, there are two by way of natural decisive support. Supramundane wholesome volition, however, is also an immediacy-decisive support. In dissociation, there is one by way of object-decisive support, and similarly in presence and non-disappearance. In absence and disappearance, there are seven, the very same as in immediacy.

466. Upanissayamūlakāni pana satta ghaṭanāni honti. Tattha purimāni tīṇi ārammaṇūpanissayavasena vuttāni. Tattha paṭhame sattāti kusalo kusalādīnaṃ, tathā abyākato, akusalo akusalassevāti evaṃ satta. Dutiye ekanti cakkhādiabyākataṃ akusalassa. Tatiye [V 0.0454] vatthu akusalassa. Tato parāni dve anantarūpanissayavasena vuttāni. Tesu gaṇanā pākaṭāyeva. Tato dve anantarapakatūpanissayavasena vuttāni. Tattha paṭhame lokiyakusalākusalacetanāpaccayabhāvato gahetabbā, dutiye lokuttarakusalāva.

466. There are, however, seven combinations in the decisive support root-condition. Among them, the first three are stated by way of object-decisive support. Therein, in the first, there are seven: the wholesome for the wholesome and so forth, similarly the indeterminate, and the unwholesome only for the unwholesome—thus seven. In the second, there is one: the indeterminate eye, etc., for the unwholesome. In the third, the physical base for the unwholesome. Thereafter, two are stated by way of immediacy-decisive support. Their enumeration is quite evident. Then two are stated by way of immediacy- and natural-decisive support. Therein, in the first, mundane wholesome and unwholesome volitions are to be taken as the condition; in the second, only the supramundane wholesome.

467-468. Purejātamūlake ārammaṇe tīṇīti abyākato kusalādīnaṃ. Adhipatiyā ekanti abyākato akusalassa. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Ettha pana satta ghaṭanāni. Tesu paṭhamaṃ vatthārammaṇavasena vuttaṃ, dutiyaṃ vatthuvaseneva, tatiyaṃ ārammaṇavasena, catutthaṃ vatthussa ārammaṇakālavasena, pañcamaṃ ārammaṇādhipativasena, chaṭṭhaṃ vatthuno ārammaṇādhipatikālavasena, sattamaṃ cakkhādivasena.

In the pre-arisen root-condition, in object condition there are three: the indeterminate for the wholesome, etc. In dominance, there is one: the indeterminate for the unwholesome. In the remaining conditions, this is the method. Here, however, there are seven combinations. Of these, the first is stated by way of physical base as object; the second, solely by way of physical base; the third, by way of object; the fourth, by way of the time of the physical base as object; the fifth, by way of object-dominance; the sixth, by way of the time of the physical base's object-dominance; and the seventh, by way of the eye, etc.

469-472. Pacchājātamūlake vīsati paccayā na yujjanti, tayova yojanaṃ labhanti. Ekamevettha ghaṭanaṃ, taṃ kāyassa kusalādīnaṃ vasena veditabbaṃ. Āsevanamūlakepi ekameva ghaṭanaṃ.

In the post-arisen root-condition, twenty conditions are not applicable; only three find application. Here, there is only one combination; it should be understood by way of the wholesome, etc., for the body. In the repetition root-condition also, there is only one combination.

473-477. Kammamūlake anantare ekanti maggacetanāvasena vuttaṃ. Aññamaññe tīṇīti ettha paṭisandhiyaṃ vatthupi gahetabbaṃ. Upanissaye dveti anantarapakatūpanissayavasena heṭṭhā vuttāneva. Evaṃ sesānipi heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbāni. Ettha pana ekādasa ghaṭanāni. Tattha paṭhamāni dve pakatūpanissayānantarūpanissayavibhāgato nānākkhaṇikakammavasena vuttāni. Tato parāni cattāri vipākāvipākato ekakkhaṇikakammavasena vuttāni. Tattha paṭhame arūpena saddhiṃ cittasamuṭṭhānarūpaṃ labbhati, dutiye [M 0.0459] arūpena saddhiṃ vatthu, tatiye arūpameva, catutthe cittasamuṭṭhānarūpameva. Paṭisandhiyaṃ pana kaṭattārūpampi labbhati. Tato parāni pañca savipākāni, tāni heṭṭhā vuttanayāneva. Vipākamūlake pañca ghaṭānāni uttānatthāneva.

In the kamma root-condition, in immediacy condition there is one, stated by way of path-volition. In mutuality condition, there are three; here, the physical base should also be taken at rebirth-linking. In decisive support, there are two, by way of immediacy- and natural-decisive support, just as stated above. Similarly, the remaining conditions should also be understood by the method stated above. Here, however, there are eleven combinations. Among them, the first two are stated by way of kamma of different moments, according to the distinction between natural-decisive support and immediacy-decisive support. Thereafter, four are stated by way of kamma of a single moment, as resultant and non-resultant. Among them, in the first, mind-originated matter is obtained together with the immaterial; in the second, the physical base together with the immaterial; in the third, only the immaterial; in the fourth, only mind-originated matter. At rebirth-linking, however, kamma-produced matter is also obtained. Thereafter, there are five with resultant; these are just as stated above. In the resultant root-condition, the five combinations are of obvious meaning.

478-483. Āhāramūlake sattātiādīni vuttanayāneva. Ghaṭanāni panettha catuttiṃsa. Tesu paṭhamāni pañca vipākāvipākasāmaññato vuttāni. Tattha paṭhame cattāropi āhārā labbhanti; dutiye tayo arūpāhārāva. Tatiye vatthupi paccayuppannaṃ hoti, catutthe taṃ parihāyati. Pañcame rūpameva paccayuppannaṃ. Tato parāni pañca savipākaghaṭanāni, tāni heṭṭhā vuttanayāneva. Tato parāni nava ghaṭanāni cetanāhāravasena vuttāni. Tato parāni nava nirādhipativiññāṇāhāravasena[V 0.0455]. Tato parāni sādhipativiññāṇāhāravasena cha ghaṭanāni vuttāni. Tattha tīṇi vipākāvipākasāmaññavasena vuttāni. Tīṇi vipākavaseneva. Tattha lokiyānaṃ vipākānaṃ abhāvato vatthu parihāyati.

In the nutriment root-condition, the seven, etc., are by the method already stated. Here there are thirty-four combinations. Among them, the first five are stated in terms of what is common to resultant and non-resultant. Therein, in the first, all four nutriments are obtained; in the second, only the three immaterial nutriments. In the third, the physical base is also conditionally arisen; in the fourth, that diminishes. In the fifth, only matter is conditionally arisen. Thereafter, there are five combinations with resultant; these are by the method stated above. Thereafter, nine combinations are stated by way of volition-as-nutriment. Thereafter, nine by way of consciousness-as-nutriment without dominance. Thereafter, six combinations are stated by way of consciousness-as-nutriment with dominance. Among these, three are stated by way of what is common to resultant and non-resultant. Three are stated solely by way of resultant. Here, due to the absence of mundane resultants, the physical base diminishes.

484-495. Indriyamūlake purejāte ekanti cakkhundriyādīnaṃ vasena abyākatena abyākataṃ. Sesaṃ dumūlakaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ghaṭanāni panettha cha sattati. Tattha paṭhame sabbānipi indriyāni paccayaṭṭhena labbhanti. Dutiye rūpajīvitindriyaṃ hāyati. Na hi taṃ nissayo hoti. Tatiye arūpindriyāni rūpānaṃ. Catutthe cakkhādīni cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ. Tato parāni nava ghaṭanāni sahajātaarūpindriyavasena vuttāni, tato nava maggabhūtānaṃ indriyānaṃ vasena, tato nava jhānaṅgabhūtānaṃ, tato nava jhānamaggabhūtānaṃ, tato nava manindriyavaseneva, tato sādhipatīni cha, tato vīriyavasena maggasampayuttāni cha, tato amohahetuvasena nirādhipatīni nava, sādhipatīni cha. Tesu sabbesu vipākapaccayena ayuttāni ca yuttāni ca heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbāni.

In the faculty root-condition, in pre-arisen there is one: the indeterminate by the indeterminate, by way of the eye faculty, etc. The rest, being two-rooted, should be understood by the method stated above. Here there are seventy-six combinations. In the first, all the faculties are obtained in the sense of a condition. In the second, the material life faculty is omitted, for it is not a support. In the third, the immaterial faculties are for material phenomena. In the fourth, the eye, etc., are for eye-consciousness, etc. Thereafter, nine combinations are stated by way of co-arisen immaterial faculties; then nine by way of faculties that are path factors; then nine by way of those that are jhāna factors; then nine by way of those that are jhāna and path factors; then nine solely by way of the mind faculty; then six with dominance; then six associated with the path by way of energy; then nine without dominance by way of the non-delusion root, and six with dominance. In all these, those not connected and those connected by way of resultant condition should be understood by the method stated above.

496-500. Jhānamūlakepi dumūlakaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ghaṭanāni panettha chattiṃsa. Tesu paṭhamāni nava indriyamaggabhāvaṃ anāmasitvā sādhāraṇajhānaṅgavaseneva [M 0.0460] vuttāni. Tato parāni nava indriyabhūtajhānaṅgavasena, tato nava maggabhūtajhānaṅgavasena, tato nava indriyamaggabhūtajhānaṅgavasena. Catūsupi cetesu navakesu ādito cattāri cattāri vipākāvipākasādhāraṇāni. Avasāne pañca pañca vipākāneva, tāni heṭṭhā vuttanayāneva.

496-500. Even in the jhāna-root, the two-rooted should be understood by the method stated previously. Here, there are thirty-six conjunctions. Among them, the first nine are stated solely by way of common jhāna-factors, without touching upon the state of being a faculty or a path. Thereafter, nine are stated by way of jhāna-factors that have become faculties; then nine by way of jhāna-factors that have become path-factors; then nine by way of jhāna-factors that have become both faculties and path-factors. In each of these four sets of nine, the first four are common to resultant and non-resultant. At the end, five each are resultants only; these are just as stated previously.

501-508. Maggamūlakepi dumūlakaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ghaṭanāni panettha sattapaññāsa. Tesu paṭhamāni nava indriyajhānabhāvaṃ anāmasitvā suddhikamaggavaseneva vuttāni. Tato nava indriyabhūtamaggavasena, tato nava jhānabhūtamaggavasena, tato nava indriyajhānabhūtamaggavasena, tato cha adhipatibhūtamaggavasena, tato nava nirādhipatimaggahetuvasena, tato cha sādhipatimaggahetuvasena, tattha navakesu pañca pañca chakkesu tīṇi tīṇi vipākāni. Sesāni sādhāraṇāni, tāni heṭṭhā vuttanayāneva.

501-508. Even in the path-root, the two-rooted should be understood by the method previously stated. Here, there are fifty-seven conjunctions. Among these, the first nine are stated solely by way of the simple path, without touching upon the state of being a faculty or jhāna. Then nine by way of the path that has become faculties; then nine by way of the path that has become jhāna; then nine by way of the path that has become both faculties and jhāna; then six by way of the path that has become a dominance; then nine by way of path-causes without dominance; then six by way of path-causes with dominance. Therein, in the sets of nine, five each are resultants; in the sets of six, three each are resultants. The rest are common; these are just as stated previously.

509-510. Sampayuttamūlake [V 0.0456] dumūlakaṃ uttānatthameva. Ettha pana dveyeva ghaṭanāni. Tattha ekaṃ sādhāraṇavasena, ekaṃ vipākavasena vuttaṃ.

509-510. In the associated-root, the two-rooted is of obvious meaning. Here, however, there are only two conjunctions. Of these, one is stated by way of what is common, and one by way of resultant.

511-514. Vippayuttamūlakepi dumūlakaṃ uttānatthameva. Ghaṭanāni panettha terasa. Tattha paṭhame pañcāti kusalo abyākatassa, tathā akusalo, abyākato tiṇṇannampi. Ettha ca ime vippayuttādayo sahajātāpi honti, pacchājātapurejātāpi. Dutiye purejātasahajātāva tatiye teyeva adhipativasena. Tattha kusalo abyākatassa tathā akusalo, abyākato pana abyākatassa ca ārammaṇādhipativasena akusalassa cāti evaṃ cattāri. Catutthe tīṇīti kusalādīni abyākatassa. Indriyāni panettha rūpānipi arūpānipi. Pañcame paccayā arūpāva chaṭṭhe vatthuvasena rūpāva sattame kusalābyākatānaṃ vipassanāvasena, akusalassa assādanavasena vatthumeva. Aṭṭhame tadevākusalassa, navame cakkhādīni abyākatassa, dasame kusalādayo cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ, ekādasame paṭisandhiyaṃ vatthu khandhānaṃ, dvādasame paṭisandhiyaṃ khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ, terasame paṭisandhiyaṃ khandhā vatthussa.

511-514. Even in the dissociated-root, the two-rooted is of obvious meaning. Here, there are thirteen conjunctions. Among these, in the first, there are five: the wholesome for the indeterminate, likewise the unwholesome, and the indeterminate for all three. Here, these dissociated and other conditions are also co-nascent, and post-nascent and pre-nascent. In the second, they are only pre-nascent and co-nascent. In the third, those same ones by way of dominance. Here, the wholesome for the indeterminate, likewise the unwholesome; but the indeterminate is for the indeterminate and also for the unwholesome by way of object-dominance—thus there are four. In the fourth, there are three: the wholesome, etc., for the indeterminate. Here, the faculties are both material and immaterial. In the fifth, the conditions are only immaterial. In the sixth, by way of base, only material. In the seventh, for the wholesome and indeterminate by way of insight, and for the unwholesome by way of gratification, it is the base only. In the eighth, the same for the unwholesome. In the ninth, the eye, etc., for the indeterminate. In the tenth, the wholesome, etc., for mind-originated matter. In the eleventh, at rebirth-linking, the base for the aggregates. In the twelfth, at rebirth-linking, the aggregates for kamma-produced matter. In the thirteenth, at rebirth-linking, the aggregates for the base.

515-518. Atthipaccayamūlake [M 0.0461] upanissaye ekanti ārammaṇūpanissayavasena abyākataṃ akusalassa. Sesaṃ dumūlake uttānameva. Ghaṭanāni panettha ekūnatiṃsa. Tesu paṭhame arūpavatthārammaṇamahābhūtaindriyāhārānaṃ vasena sahajātapurejātapacchājātapaccayā labbhanti. Dutiye pacchājātakabaḷīkārāhārā na labbhanti. Paṭhamadutiyaghaṭanāneva adhipatinā saddhiṃ upari tatiyacatutthāni katāni. Puna paṭhamameva catūhi āhārehi saddhiṃ pañcamaṃ, rūpindriyehi saddhiṃ chaṭṭhaṃ, rūpārūpindriyehi saddhiṃ sattamaṃ kataṃ. Dutiyameva vā pana indriyehi saddhiṃ sattamaṃ kataṃ. Paṭhamadutiyāneva vippayuttapaccayena saddhiṃ aṭṭhamanavamāni. Tesu navamaṃ adhipatinā saddhiṃ dasamaṃ kataṃ. Tato ekādasame paccayavasena vatthu hāyati. Dvādasame arūpadhammāyeva paccayā, terasame vatthārammaṇā, cuddasame vatthumeva, pannarasame ārammaṇameva, soḷasame vatthumeva ārammaṇaṃ, sattarasame pana tadeva ārammaṇādhipatibhāvena, aṭṭhārasamepi tadeva ārammaṇūpanissayavasena, ekūnavīsatime cakkhādayova paccayā. Imāni ekūnavīsati pakiṇṇakaghaṭanāni nāma sahajātaṃ aggahetvā vuttāni. Tato parāni dasa sahajātavasena vuttāni.

515-518. In the presence-condition-root, in decisive support, there is one: the indeterminate for the unwholesome by way of object-decisive support. The rest in the two-rooted is of obvious meaning. Here, there are twenty-nine conjunctions. Among them, in the first, co-nascent, pre-nascent, and post-nascent conditions are obtained by way of immaterial phenomena, base, object, great elements, faculties, and nutriment. In the second, post-nascent physical nutriment is not obtained. The first and second conjunctions, together with dominance, are made into the third and fourth above. Again, the first alone, together with the four nutriments, is made into the fifth; together with the material faculties, the sixth; together with the material and immaterial faculties, the seventh. Or, the second alone, together with the faculties, is made into the seventh. The first and second, together with the dissociated condition, are made into the eighth and ninth. Among them, the ninth, together with dominance, is made into the tenth. Then, in the eleventh, the base is omitted by way of condition. In the twelfth, only immaterial phenomena are conditions. In the thirteenth, base and object. In the fourteenth, only the base. In the fifteenth, only the object. In the sixteenth, the base itself is the object. In the seventeenth, that same thing by way of being object-dominance. In the eighteenth, that same thing also by way of object-decisive support. In the nineteenth, only the eye, etc., are conditions. These nineteen are called miscellaneous conjunctions, stated without taking co-nascence. Thereafter, ten are stated by way of co-nascence.

519. Natthivigatamūlakesu [V 0.0457] anantarasamanantaramūlakesu viya upanissayāsevanakammavasena tīṇiyeva ghaṭanāni, avigatamūlakaṃ atthimūlakasadisamevāti.

519. In the absence-root and disappearance-root, just as in the contiguity-root and immediate-contiguity-root, there are only three conjunctions by way of decisive support, repetition, and kamma. The non-disappearance-root is just like the presence-root.

Yāni panetāni imasmiṃ pañhāvāre ghaṭanāni vuttāni, tāni sabbānipi duvidhāniyeva – pakiṇṇakato sahajātato ca. Tattha sabbesampi ārammaṇamūlakādīnaṃ ādito sahajātaṃ aggahetvā vuttāni pakiṇṇakāni nāma. Tāni ārammaṇamūlake pañcapi, adhipatimūlake cha, anantaramūlake tīṇipi, tathā samanantaramūlake, nissayamūlake dasa, upanissayamūlake satta, purejātamūlake satta, pacchājātamūlake ekameva, tathā āsevanamūlake, kammamūlake dve, āhāramūlake ekaṃ, indriyamūlake cattāri, vippayuttamūlake nava, atthimūlake ekūnavīsati, natthimūlake tīṇipi, tathāvigatamūlake. Avigatamūlake ekūnavīsatīti sabbānipi satañceva tīṇi ca honti. Sahajātanissayabhāvena panetāni pakiṇṇakānīti vuttāni.

Now, as for the conjunctions mentioned in this section of questions, they are all of two kinds—miscellaneous and co-nascent. Herein, of all the roots beginning with the object-root, those stated without initially taking co-nascence are called 'miscellaneous'. These are: five in the object-root, six in the dominance-root, three in the contiguity-root, and likewise in the immediate-contiguity-root, ten in the dependence-root, seven in the decisive-support-root, seven in the prenascent-root, one in the postnascent-root, and likewise in the repetition-root, two in the kamma-root, one in the nutriment-root, four in the faculty-root, nine in the dissociated-root, nineteen in the presence-root, three in the absence-root, and likewise in the disappearance-root. In the non-disappearance-root, there are nineteen—thus, all together they amount to one hundred and three. However, these are called 'miscellaneous' in relation to co-nascent dependence.

Yāni [M 0.0462] pana sahajātaṃ labbhanti, tāni sahajātaghaṭanāni nāmāti vuccanti. Tāni ārammaṇamūlake anantarasamanantarapurejātapacchājātaāsevananatthivigatamūlakesu na labbhanti. Na hi te paccayā sahajātānaṃ paccayā honti. Yathā ca sahajātānaṃ na honti, tathā hetusahajātaaññamaññavipākajhānamaggasampayuttapaccayā. Asahajātānanti hetumūlake sabbāni catuvīsatipi ghaṭanāni sahajātaghaṭanāneva. Tathā adhipatimūlake catuvīsati, sahajātamūlake dasapi, aññamaññamūlake chapi, nissayamūlake dasa, kammamūlake nava, vipākamūlake pañcapi, āhāramūlake tettiṃsa, indriyamūlake dvāsattati jhānamūlake chattiṃsāpi, maggamūlake sattapaññāsampi, sampayuttamūlake dvepi, vippayuttamūlake cattāri, atthimūlake dasa, avigatamūlake dasāti sabbānipi tīṇi satāni dvādasa ca honti. Iti purimāni sataṃ tīṇi ca imāni ca dvādasuttarāni tīṇi satānīti sabbānipi pañcadasādhikāni cattāri ghaṭanasatāni pañhāvāre āgatāni. Tesu ye ye paccayadhammā nāmavasena na pākaṭā hutvā paññāyanti, tepi hetumūlakādīnaṃ nayānaṃ ādito vipākāvipākasāmaññato vuttesu ghaṭanesu dassetabbā. Dvādaseva hi hetū cha ārammaṇā cattāro adhipatayo cattāro āhārā vīsati indriyāni satta jhānaṅgāni dvādasa maggaṅgānīti ete paccayadhammā nāma. Tesu ye ye dhammā ekantena kusalā, ekanteneva akusalā, ekantena kusalavipākā, ekantenevākusalavipākā, ekanteneva [V 0.0458] vipākā, ekanteneva avipākā te te sādhukaṃ sallakkhetvā ye tattha vipākā, te vipākaghaṭanesu, ye avipākā, te avipākaghaṭanesu yathāyogaṃ yojetabbāti.

Those connections which are obtained as co-nascent are called co-nascent connections. These are not obtained in the object-root, contiguity-root, immediate-contiguity-root, prenascent-root, postnascent-root, repetition-root, absence-root, or disappearance-root. For those conditions are not conditions for co-nascent states. And just as those are not conditions for co-nascent states, so too the root, co-nascent, mutuality, resultant, jhāna, path, and association conditions are not for non-co-nascent states. In the root-root, all twenty-four connections are co-nascent connections. Similarly, in the predominance-root, twenty-four; in the co-nascent-root, ten; in the mutuality-root, six; in the support-root, ten; in the kamma-root, nine; in the resultant-root, five; in the nutriment-root, thirty-three; in the faculty-root, seventy-two; in the jhāna-root, thirty-six; in the path-root, fifty-seven; in the association-root, two; in the dissociation-root, four; in the presence-root, ten; and in the non-disappearance-root, ten—all these amount to three hundred and twelve. Thus, the previous one hundred and three, and these three hundred and twelve, amount to all four hundred and fifteen connections, which have been presented in the question section. Among them, those conditioning states which are not clearly designated by name but are discernible should also be shown in the connections mentioned from the root-root onwards, according to the general distinction between resultant and non-resultant, as previously stated. For there are indeed twelve roots, six objects, four predominances, four nutriments, twenty faculties, seven jhāna factors, and twelve path factors—these are named conditioning states. Among them, those states which are entirely wholesome, entirely unwholesome, entirely wholesome-resultant, entirely unwholesome-resultant, entirely resultant, or entirely non-resultant should be carefully discerned. Those which are resultant there should be assigned to resultant connections, and those which are non-resultant to non-resultant connections, as is appropriate.

Pañhāvārassa ghaṭane anulomagaṇanā.

Direct Enumeration of the Connections in the Section of Questions.

Paccanīyuddhāravaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Negative Summary.

527. Idāni paccanīyaṃ hoti. Tattha yathā paṭicca vārādīsu “akusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā”tiādinā nayena labbhamānā [M 0.0463] pañhā labbhamānānaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena sarūpatova vitthāritā. Evaṃ avitthāretvā ekena lakkhaṇena saṅkhepato paccanīyaṃ dassetuṃ dhammasaṅgāhakehi kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayotiādinā nayena anulomato kusalādīnaṃ paccayā uddhaṭā. Te ca kho paccayā samūhavasena, no ekekapaccayavaseneva; tasmā ye yattha samūhato dassitā, te vibhajitvā veditabbā. Sabbepi hi ime catuvīsati paccayā aṭṭhasu paccayesu saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Kataresu aṭṭhasu? Ārammaṇe, sahajāte, upanissaye, purejāte, pacchājāte, kamme, āhāre, indriyeti. Kathaṃ? Ṭhapetvā hi ime aṭṭha paccaye sesesu soḷasasu hetupaccayo aññamaññavipākajhānamaggasampayuttapaccayoti ime cha paccayā ekantena sahajātā hutvā sahajātānaññeva paccayabhāvato sahajātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Anantarapaccayo samanantaraāsevananatthivigatapaccayoti ime pana pañca uppajjitvā niruddhā attano anantaraṃ uppajjamānānaññeva paccayabhāvato anantarūpanissayalakkhaṇena upanissaye saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Nissayapaccayo sahajātapurejātabhedato duvidho. Tattha sahajātanissayo sahajātānaññeva nissayapaccayabhāvato sahajātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati, purejātanissayo purejātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati.

527. Now comes the negative mode. Here, just as in the conditional mode regarding the sections beginning with "an unwholesome state arises dependent on an unwholesome state, not by way of root condition," and so on, the questions that arise are explained in detail according to their own nature based on the conditions that are obtained. Without elaborating in this way, the compilers of the Dhamma have briefly presented the negative mode with a single characteristic, such as "a wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of object condition," and so on, extracting the conditions for the wholesome, etc., in the affirmative mode. However, these conditions are presented as a group, not individually for each condition. Therefore, those that are shown as a group should be understood by analyzing them. Indeed, all these twenty-four conditions are included in eight conditions. Which eight? Object condition, co-nascent condition, decisive-support condition, prenascent condition, postnascent condition, kamma condition, nutriment condition, and faculty condition. How so? Excluding these eight conditions, among the remaining sixteen, the root condition, mutual condition, resultant condition, jhāna condition, path condition, and associated condition—these six conditions are invariably co-nascent and, because they function as conditions only for co-nascent states, are included under the co-nascent condition. The contiguity condition, immediate-contiguity condition, repetition condition, absence condition, and disappearance condition—these five, having arisen and ceased, function as conditions only for states that arise immediately after them. Due to their nature as contiguity decisive support, they are included under the decisive-support condition. The support condition is twofold: co-nascent and prenascent. Among these, the co-nascent support, because it functions as a support condition only for co-nascent states, is included under the co-nascent condition. The prenascent support is included under the prenascent condition.

Adhipatipaccayopi sahajātādhipatiārammaṇādhipativasena duvidho. Tattha sahajātādhipati sahajātānaṃyeva adhipatipaccayabhāvato sahajātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Ārammaṇādhipati ārammaṇūpanissayo [V 0.0459] hotiyevāti ārammaṇūpanissayalakkhaṇena upanissayapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Vippayuttapaccayo sahajātapurejātapacchājātabhedato tividho. Tattha sahajātavippayutto sahajātānaññeva vippayuttapaccayabhāvato sahajātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Purejātavippayutto pure uppajjitvā pacchā uppajjamānānaṃ paccayabhāvato purejāte saṅgahito. Pacchājātavippayutto pacchā uppajjitvā pure uppannānaṃ upatthambhanavasena paccayabhāvato pacchājātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Atthipaccayaavigatapaccayā sahajātapurejātapacchājātaāhārindriyānañceva atthiavigatesu ca ekekassa vasena chahi bhedehi ṭhitā. Tattha sahajātaatthiavigatā sahajātānaññeva atthiavigatapaccayabhāvato. Sahajātapaccaye [M 0.0464] saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Purejātā pure uppajjitvā pacchā uppajjamānānaṃ paccayabhāvato purejātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Pacchājātā pacchā uppajjitvā pure uppannānaṃ upatthambhanavasena paccayabhāvato pacchājātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Āhārabhūtā kabaḷīkārāhārapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Indriyabhūtā rūpajīvitindriyapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchantīti evaṃ ime soḷasa paccayā imesu aṭṭhasu paccayesu saṅgahaṃ gacchantīti veditabbā.

The dominance condition is twofold: as co-nascent dominance and object dominance. Herein, co-nascent dominance is included in the co-nascent condition because it is a dominance condition only for co-nascent states. Object dominance is indeed object-decisive-support; thus, it is included in the decisive-support condition by way of the characteristic of object-decisive-support. The dissociation condition is threefold: as co-nascent, prenascent, and postnascent dissociation. Herein, co-nascent dissociation is included in the co-nascent condition because it is a dissociation condition only for co-nascent states. Prenascent dissociation, having arisen previously, is included in the prenascent condition because it is a condition for states arising subsequently. Postnascent dissociation, having arisen subsequently, is included in the postnascent condition because it is a condition by way of supporting previously arisen states. The presence condition and the non-disappearance condition are established in six ways: by way of the co-nascent, prenascent, postnascent, nutriment, and faculty, and by way of each of the presence and non-disappearance conditions. Herein, co-nascent presence and non-disappearance are included in the co-nascent condition because they are presence and non-disappearance conditions only for co-nascent states. The prenascent, having arisen previously, are included in the prenascent condition because they are a condition for states arising subsequently. The postnascent, having arisen subsequently, are included in the postnascent condition because they are a condition by way of supporting previously arisen states. Those that are nutriment are included in the edible food condition. Those that are faculties are included in the material life-faculty condition. Thus, it should be understood that these sixteen conditions are included in these eight conditions.

Imesampi pana aṭṭhannaṃ paccayānaṃ aññamaññaṃ saṅgaho atthiyeva. Ādito niddiṭṭho hi ārammaṇapaccayo adhipatianadhipatibhedena duvidho. Tattha adhipatibhūto ārammaṇūpanissayalakkhaṇena upanissaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Anadhipatibhūto suddho ārammaṇapaccayova. Kammapaccayopi sahajātanānākkhaṇikavasena duvidho. Tattha sahajātakammaṃ attanā sahajātānaññeva kammapaccayabhāvato sahajāteyeva saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Nānākkhaṇikakammaṃ balavadubbalavasena duvidhaṃ. Tattha balavakammaṃ vipākadhammānaṃ upanissayova hutvā paccayo hotīti upanissaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Balavampi pana rūpānaṃ dubbalañca arūpānaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayeneva paccayo. Āhārapaccayopi rūpārūpato duvidho. Tattha arūpāhāro attanā sahajātānaññeva paccayo hotīti sahajātapaccaye saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Rūpāhāro sahajātapurejātapacchājātānaṃ paccayo na hoti. Attano pana uppādakkhaṇaṃ atikkamitvā ṭhitippatto āhārapaccayataṃ sādhetīti āhārapaccayova hoti. Indriyapaccayopi rūpārūpato duvidho. Tattha arūpindriyapaccayo attanā sahajātānaññeva indriyapaccayataṃ sādhetīti sahajāteyeva saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Rūpindriyapaccayo pana ajjhattabahiddhābhedato duvidho. Tattha ajjhattaṃ indriyapaccayo pure uppajjitvā pacchā uppajjamānānaṃ [V 0.0460] sasampayuttadhammānaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ indriyapaccayo hotīti purejāteyeva saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Bāhiro indriyapaccayo nāma rūpajīvitindriyaṃ, taṃ sahajātānaṃ paccayo hontampi anupālanamattavaseneva hoti, na janakavasenāti indriyapaccayova hoti. Evaṃ ime aṭṭha paccayā aññamaññampi saṅgahaṃ gacchantīti veditabbā. Ayaṃ tāva aṭṭhasu paccayesu avasesānaṃ soḷasannañceva tesaṃyeva ca aṭṭhannaṃ aññamaññavasena saṅgahanayo.

Moreover, there is indeed a mutual inclusion among these eight conditions. Indeed, the object condition, first stated, is twofold by way of dominant and non-dominant. Therein, the object condition that has become dominant is included in the decisive-support condition by the characteristic of object-decisive-support. The non-dominant one is purely the object condition. The kamma condition is also twofold by way of conascent and different-moment. Therein, conascent kamma, being a kamma condition only for those that are conascent with itself, is included in the conascent condition itself. Different-moment kamma is twofold by way of strong and weak. Therein, strong kamma, being a condition for resultant phenomena only as a decisive support, is included in the decisive-support condition. However, strong kamma for material phenomena and weak kamma for immaterial phenomena are conditions purely by way of the different-moment kamma condition. The nutriment condition is also twofold by way of material and immaterial. Therein, immaterial nutriment, being a condition only for those that are conascent with itself, is included in the conascent condition. Material nutriment is not a condition for conascent, prenascent, or postnascent phenomena. But having passed its own moment of arising and attained the moment of presence, it accomplishes the nutriment condition, and thus is purely the nutriment condition. The faculty condition is also twofold by way of material and immaterial. Therein, the immaterial faculty condition, by accomplishing the faculty condition only for those that are conascent with itself, is included in the conascent condition itself. However, the material faculty condition is twofold by way of internal and external. Therein, the internal faculty condition, having arisen earlier, is a faculty condition for subsequently arising associated phenomena such as eye-consciousness, and so on, and is thus included in the prenascent condition itself. The external faculty condition is the material life faculty; though it is a condition for conascent phenomena, it is so only by way of mere maintenance, not by way of generation, and thus it is purely the faculty condition. Thus, it should be understood that these eight conditions also undergo mutual inclusion. This, then, is the method of inclusion for the remaining sixteen conditions among the eight conditions, and also the mutual inclusion of these eight themselves.

Idāni [M 0.0465] imesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ paccayānaṃ ekekasmiṃ catuvīsatiyāpi paccayesu ye ye saṅgahaṃ gacchanti, te te veditabbā. Tattha aṭṭhannaṃ tāva sabbapaṭhame ārammaṇapaccaye ārammaṇapaccayova saṅgahaṃ gacchati, na sesā tevīsati. Dutiye sahajātapaccaye hetupaccayo sahajātādhipatipaccayo sahajātapaccayo aññamaññapaccayo sahajātanissayapaccayo sahajātakammapaccayo vipākapaccayo sahajātaāhārapaccayo sahajātaindriyapaccayo jhānapaccayo maggapaccayo sampayuttapaccayo sahajātavippayuttapaccayo sahajātatthipaccayo sahajātāvigatapaccayoti ime pannarasa paccayā saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Tatiye upanissayapaccaye adhipatibhūto ārammaṇapaccayo ārammaṇabhūto adhipatipaccayo anantarasamanantaraupanissayaāsevanapaccayā nānākkhaṇiko balavakammapaccayo natthipaccayo vigatapaccayoti ime nava paccayā saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Catutthe purejātapaccaye purejātanissayapaccayo purejātapaccayo purejātindriyapaccayo purejātavippayuttapaccayo purejātatthipaccayo purejātāvigatapaccayoti ime cha paccayā saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Pañcame pacchājātapaccaye pacchājātapaccayo pacchājātavippayuttapaccayo pacchājātatthipaccayo pacchājātāvigatapaccayoti ime cattāro paccayā saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Chaṭṭhe kammapaccaye nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayova saṅgahito. Sattame āhārapaccaye kabaḷīkārāhāravaseneva āhārapaccayo āhāratthipaccayo āhārāvigatapaccayoti ime tayo paccayā saṅgahitā. Aṭṭhame indriyapaccaye rūpajīvitindriyapaccayo indriyatthipaccayo indriyāvigatapaccayoti ime tayo paccayā saṅgahaṃ gacchanti. Evaṃ imesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ paccayānaṃ ekekasmiṃ ime cime ca paccayā saṅgahaṃ gatāti ñatvā ye yattha saṅgahaṃ gatā, te tassa gaṇanena gahitāva hontīti veditabbā.

Now, it should be understood which conditions are included in each of these eight conditions among the twenty-four conditions. Therein, first of all, in the object condition among the eight, only the object condition itself is included, not the remaining twenty-three. Second, in the conascence condition, these fifteen conditions are included: the root condition, the conascent dominance condition, the conascence condition, the mutuality condition, the conascent dependence condition, the conascent kamma condition, the resultant condition, the conascent nutriment condition, the conascent faculty condition, the jhāna condition, the path condition, the association condition, the conascent dissociation condition, the conascent presence condition, and the conascent non-disappearance condition. Third, in the decisive support condition, these nine conditions are included: the object condition that has become dominant, the dominant condition that has become object, the contiguity condition, the immediate contiguity condition, the decisive support condition, the repetition condition, the strong non-co-momentary kamma condition, the absence condition, and the disappearance condition. Fourth, in the pre-nascence condition, these six conditions are included: the pre-nascent dependence condition, the pre-nascence condition, the pre-nascent faculty condition, the pre-nascent dissociation condition, the pre-nascent presence condition, and the pre-nascent non-disappearance condition. Fifth, in the post-nascence condition, these four conditions are included: the post-nascence condition, the post-nascent dissociation condition, the post-nascent presence condition, and the post-nascent non-disappearance condition. Sixth, in the kamma condition, only the non-co-momentary kamma condition is included. Seventh, in the nutriment condition, these three conditions are included: the nutriment condition by way of physical nutriment, the nutriment-presence condition, and the nutriment-non-disappearance condition. Eighth, in the faculty condition, these three conditions are included: the material life faculty condition, the faculty-presence condition, and the faculty-non-disappearance condition. Thus, knowing that these various conditions are included in each of these eight conditions, it should be understood that those which are included in a particular condition are indeed taken into its reckoning.

Evaṃ sabbapaccayasaṅgāhakānaṃ imesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena ekūnapaññāsāya pañhesu imasmiṃ paccanīye “kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo”tiādayo ime [V 0.0461] pannarasa pañhā uddharitvā vissajjitā. Tattha kusalo kusalassa, kusalo akusalassa, kusalo abyākatassa, kusalo kusalābyākatassāti kusalādikā cattāro pañhā; tathā akusalādikā; abyākato pana abyākatassa, abyākato [M 0.0466] kusalassa, abyākato akusalassāti abyākatādikā tayo; kusalo ca abyākato ca kusalassa; tathā abyākatassa; akusalo ca abyākato ca akusalassa; tathā abyākatassāti dumūlakekāvasānā cattāro honti. Tesu paṭhame pañhe yehi bhavitabbaṃ, te sabbe saṅgahetvā tayo paccayā vuttā. Dutiye dve, tatiye pañca, catutthe ekova pañcame tayo, chaṭṭhe dve, sattame pañca, aṭṭhame ekova navame satta, dasame tayo, ekādasame tayo, dvādasame dve, terasame cattāro, cuddasame dve, pannarasamepi cattārova. Te “sahajātapaccayenā”ti avatvā “sahajātaṃ pacchājāta”nti vuttā. Tattha kāraṇaṃ parato vakkhāma.

Thus, by way of these eight conditions, which are inclusive of all conditions, these fifteen questions, beginning with 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of object condition,' have been extracted and answered among the forty-nine questions in this antithetical section. Therein, there are four questions beginning with the wholesome: wholesome for wholesome, wholesome for unwholesome, wholesome for indeterminate, and wholesome for wholesome and indeterminate. Similarly, four beginning with the unwholesome. However, for those beginning with the indeterminate, there are three: indeterminate for indeterminate, indeterminate for wholesome, and indeterminate for unwholesome. And there are four dual-rooted questions ending in one: wholesome and indeterminate for wholesome; similarly for indeterminate; unwholesome and indeterminate for unwholesome; similarly for indeterminate. In the first of these questions, all that should be are gathered, and three conditions are stated. In the second, two; in the third, five; in the fourth, one; in the fifth, three; in the sixth, two; in the seventh, five; in the eighth, one; in the ninth, seven; in the tenth, three; in the eleventh, three; in the twelfth, two; in the thirteenth, four; in the fourteenth, two; and in the fifteenth, also four. These are stated as 'conascence and post-nascence,' not as 'by way of the conascence condition.' The reason for this we shall explain later.

Samāsato panettha eko dve tayo cattāro pañca sattāti chaḷeva paccayaparicchedā honti. Ayaṃ pañhāvārassa paccanīye ukkaṭṭhavasena pañhāparicchedo ceva te te paccaye saṅgahetvā dassitapaccayaparicchedo ca. “Na hetupaccayo”tiādīsu hi catuvīsatiyāpi paccayapaccanīyesu ekapaccanīyepi ito uddhaṃ pañhā vā paccayā vā na labbhanti, heṭṭhā labbhanti. Tasmā yesu pañhesu “kusalo dhammo kusalassa ca abyākatassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ ekova paccayo āgato, tasmiṃ paccaye paṭikkhitte te pañhā parihāyanti. Yasmiṃ pana pañhe “kusalo dhammo akusalassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo upanissayapaccayena paccayo”ti evaṃ dve paccayā āgatā. Tattha nārammaṇapaccayāti evaṃ ekasmiṃ paccaye paṭikkhittepi itarassa paccayassa vasena so pañho labbhateva. Tesu pana dvīsupi paccayesu paṭikkhittesu so vāro pacchijjati. Evameva yesu pañhesu tayo cattāro pañca satta vā labbhanti, tesu ṭhapetvā paṭikkhitte paccaye avasesānaṃ vasena te pañhā labbhantiyeva. Sabbesu pana paccayesu paṭikkhittesu sabbepi te vārā pacchijjantīti idameva cettha lakkhaṇaṃ. Iminā lakkhaṇena ādito paṭṭhāya tesu tesu pañhesu saṅkhipitvā vuttapaccayānaṃ pabhedo ca tasmiṃ tasmiṃ paccanīye tesaṃ tesaṃ pañhānaṃ parihāni ca veditabbā.

In brief, here there are only six divisions of conditions: one, two, three, four, five, and seven. This is both the division of questions in the antithetical section of the question-section, in terms of their maximum number, and the division of conditions shown by including those very conditions. For in the twenty-four antithetical sections of conditions, such as 'not a root condition,' no questions or conditions are found above this point, but they are found below. Therefore, in those questions where only one condition occurs, such as 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome and indeterminate phenomenon by way of the conascence condition,' when that condition is rejected, those questions are eliminated. However, in a question where two conditions occur, such as 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for an unwholesome phenomenon by way of the object condition and by way of decisive support condition,' if one condition, such as 'not an object condition,' is rejected, the question still obtains by virtue of the other condition. However, if both conditions are rejected, that section is cut off. Similarly, in those questions where three, four, five, or seven conditions obtain, when the rejected condition is set aside, those questions still obtain by virtue of the remaining ones. But if all conditions are rejected, all those sections are cut off—this indeed is the characteristic here. By this characteristic, from the beginning onwards, the distinctions of the conditions stated concisely in those various questions, and the elimination of those very questions in each antithetical section, should be understood.

Tatrāyaṃ [M 0.0467] vitthārakathā – paṭhamapañhe tāva tīhi paccayehi ekūnavīsati paccayā dassitā. Kathaṃ? Kusalo hi kusalassa purejātapacchājātavipākavippayutteheva paccayo na hoti[V 0.0462], sesehi vīsatiyā hoti, tesu ārammaṇapaccayo ekova sahajāte pana sabbasaṅgāhikavasena pannarasa paccayā saṅgahaṃ gacchantīti vuttā. Tesu hetupaccaye paṭikkhitte cuddasa honti. Kusalo pana kusalassa neva vipākapaccayo na, vippayuttapaccayoti te dve apanetvā sese dvādasa sandhāya sahajātapaccayena paccayoti vuttaṃ. Upanissayapaccayepi sabbasaṅgāhikavasena nava paccayā saṅgahaṃ gacchantīti vuttā. Tesu adhipatibhūto ārammaṇapaccayo ārammaṇabhūto ca adhipatipaccayo ārammaṇūpanissayavasena upanissayameva anupaviṭṭho. Kusalo pana kusalassa nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayo na hotīti taṃ apanetvā sese cha sandhāya upanissayapaccayena paccayoti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ paṭhamapañhe tīhi paccayehi ekūnavīsatipaccayā dassitāti veditabbā. Tesu imasmiṃ hetupaccanīye “kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa nahetupaccayena paccayoti dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhatī”ti evamādinā ārammaṇapaccayādīsu vuttanayeneva uddharitvā pāḷi dassetabbā.

Here is the detailed exposition: In the first question, nineteen conditions are shown by means of three conditions. How? A wholesome state is not a condition for another wholesome state by way of pre-nascence, post-nascence, resultant, or dissociation conditions. However, it is a condition by way of the remaining twenty. Among these, the object condition is only one. But by way of the co-nascence condition, fifteen conditions are included by encompassing all, so it is said. When the root condition is excluded from these, fourteen remain. A wholesome state is neither a resultant condition nor a dissociation condition for another wholesome state. Excluding these two, the remaining twelve are referred to as conditions by way of the co-nascence condition. Similarly, by way of the decisive-support condition, nine conditions are included by encompassing all, so it is said. Among these, the object condition, which functions as predominance, and the predominance condition, which functions as an object, are absorbed into the decisive-support condition by way of object-decisive-support. A wholesome state is not a condition for another wholesome state by way of the karma condition occurring at different moments. Excluding this, the remaining six are referred to as conditions by way of the decisive-support condition. Thus, in the first question, nineteen conditions are shown by means of three conditions; this should be understood. Among these, in this section on the non-root condition, the Pāli should be cited, having extracted it in the manner stated in the object condition and others, as in: 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of the non-root condition,' for example, 'having given a gift, undertaken precepts, performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews that action, one reviews previously well-performed actions.'

Ārammaṇapaccaye pana paṭikkhitte tassa vitthāraṃ apanetvā hetupaccayavitthāraṃ pakkhipitvā sāyeva pāḷi dassetabbā, sesapaccayapaṭikkhepesupi eseva nayo. Tasmiṃ pana paccaye paṭikkhitte ye vārā parihāyanti, te parato vakkhāma.

When the object condition is excluded, however, having removed its detailed exposition and inserted the detailed exposition of the root condition, that same Pāli text should be shown. This same method applies also in excluding the remaining conditions. But when a condition is excluded, the cases that are lost, those we will explain later.

Dutiyapañhe pana dvīhi paccayehi tayo paccayā dassitā. Kathaṃ? Kusalo hi akusalassa anantarādivasena paccayo na hoti. Tasmā te apanetvā ārammaṇūpanissayavasena saṅgahitaṃ ārammaṇādhipatiñceva pakatūpanissayañca sandhāya upanissayapaccayena paccayoti vuttaṃ. Tasmā suddho ārammaṇapaccayo ārammaṇādhipativasena adhipatipaccayo upanissayapaccayoti dutiyapañhe dvīhi paccayehi ime tayo paccayā dassitāti veditabbā.

In the second question, however, three conditions are shown by means of two conditions. How? A wholesome state is not a condition for an unwholesome state by way of contiguity, etc. Therefore, having excluded those, it is stated that it is a condition by way of the decisive-support condition, referring to object-predominance and natural decisive-support. Thus, the pure object condition, the predominance condition by way of object-predominance, and the decisive-support condition—these are the three conditions shown in the second question by means of two conditions; this should be understood.

Tatiyapañhe [M 0.0468] pana pañcahi paccayehi aṭṭhārasa paccayā dassitā. Kathaṃ? Kusalo hi abyākatassa aññamaññapurejātāsevanavipākasampayuttehiyeva paccayo na hoti, sesehi ekūnavīsatiyā hoti. Tesu ārammaṇapaccayo eko. Yasmā pana kusalo abyākatassa aññamaññavipākasampayuttavasena paccayo na hoti, hetupaccayo paṭikkhitto, kammapaccayo visuṃ gahito, tasmā ime pañca apanetvā sahajātena dasa paccayā dassitā. Upanissayena heṭṭhā [V 0.0463] vuttesu chasu ṭhapetvā āsevanaṃ sesā pañca. Pacchājāto ekova tathā sahajātanānākkhaṇikavasena duvidhopi kammapaccayoti evaṃ tatiyapañhe pañcahi paccayehi ime aṭṭhārasa paccayā dassitāti veditabbā.

In the third question, however, eighteen conditions are shown by means of five conditions. How? A wholesome state is not a condition for an indeterminate state by way of mutuality, pre-nascence, repetition, resultant, or association conditions. It is a condition by way of the remaining nineteen. Among these, the object condition is one. Since a wholesome state is not a condition for an indeterminate state by way of mutuality, resultant, or association, the root condition is excluded, and the kamma condition is taken separately. Thus, excluding these five, ten conditions are shown by way of the co-nascence condition. By way of the decisive-support condition, excluding repetition from the six stated below, the remaining five are shown. Post-nascence is one, and the kamma condition is twofold – co-nascent and occurring at different moments. Thus, in the third question, these eighteen conditions are shown by means of five conditions; this should be understood.

Catutthapañhe pana ekena paccayena dasa. Kathaṃ? Kusalo hi kusalābyākatassa sahajāte vuttesu pannarasasu aññamaññavipākasampayuttavippayuttehi paccayo na hoti, hetupaccayo paṭikkhitto. Iti ime pañca apanetvā sesā dasa paccayā ettha ekena paccayena dassitāti veditabbā.

In the fourth question, however, ten conditions are shown by means of one condition. How? A wholesome state is not a condition for a wholesome-and-indeterminate state by way of mutuality, resultant, association, and dissociation among the fifteen conditions stated for co-nascence; and the root condition is excluded. Thus, having eliminated these five, it should be understood that the remaining ten conditions are shown here by means of one condition.

528. Yathā ca imesu kusalādikesu catūsu, tathā akusalādikesupi catūsu pañhesu tehi tehi paccayehi te teyeva paccayā dassitāti veditabbā.

528. Just as in these four questions beginning with the wholesome, so too in the four questions beginning with the unwholesome, it should be understood that those very same conditions are shown by means of those very same conditions.

529. Tato parānaṃ abyākatādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pañhānaṃ paṭhamapañhe sattahi paccayehi tevīsati paccayā dassitā. Kathaṃ? Abyākato hi abyākatassa catuvīsatiyāpi paccayehi paccayo hoti. Hetupaccaye pana paṭikkhitte tevīsati honti. Tesu ārammaṇapaccayo ekova. Yasmā panettha asahajātānampi saṅgahaṇatthaṃ āhārindriyapaccayā visuṃ gahitā. Tasmā ime tayo apanetvā sahajātena dvādasa paccayā dassitā. Upanissayena heṭṭhā vuttā cha, purejāto ekova tathā pacchājātaāhārindriyapaccayāti evamettha sattahi paccayehi ime tevīsati paccayā dassitāti veditabbā. Dutiye tīhi paccayehi dvādasa dassitā. Kathaṃ? Ārammaṇapaccayo eko, upanissayena pana ārammaṇūpanissayavasena ārammaṇādhipatianantarasamanantaranatthivigataupanissayapaccayoti cha [M 0.0469] dassitā. Purejātena purejātanissayavippayuttaatthiavigatā pañcāti evamettha tīhi paccayehi ime dvādasa paccayā dassitāti veditabbā. Tatiyepi eseva nayo.

529. Thereafter, in the first of the three questions beginning with the indeterminate, twenty-three conditions are shown by means of seven conditions. How? An indeterminate state, indeed, becomes a condition for an indeterminate state by way of all twenty-four conditions. But when the root condition is excluded, there are twenty-three. Among these, the object condition is only one. Because here, to include even non-co-nascent conditions, the nutriment and faculty conditions are taken separately. Therefore, having eliminated these three, twelve conditions are shown by way of the co-nascence condition. By way of the decisive-support condition, six were stated below; the pre-nascence condition is only one; similarly, the post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty conditions—thus here, these twenty-three conditions are shown by means of seven conditions; this should be understood. In the second question, twelve conditions are shown by means of three conditions. How? The object condition is one; but by way of the decisive-support condition, six are shown as object-decisive-support, object-predominance, contiguity, immediate contiguity, absence, and disappearance decisive-support conditions. By way of the pre-nascence condition, five are shown: pre-nascence, dependence, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance—thus here, these twelve conditions are shown by means of these three conditions; this should be understood. The same method applies to the third question as well.
