530. Tato parānaṃ dukamūlakānaṃ catunnaṃ pañhānaṃ paṭhamapañhe “sahajātapaccayena purejātapaccayenā”ti avatvā “sahajātaṃ purejāta”nti vuttehi dvīhi nissayaatthiavigatavasena tayo paccayā dassitā. Kusalā hi khandhā vatthunā saddhiṃ ekato kusalassa paccayabhāvaṃ sādhayamānā kiñcāpi sahajātā, sahajātapaccayā pana na honti vatthumissakattā[V 0.0464]. Tasmā tesaṃ sahajātānaṃ nissayaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena sahajātanti vuttaṃ. Vatthumhipi eseva nayo. Tampi hi kiñcāpi purejātaṃ, khandhamissakattā pana purejātapaccayo na hoti. Kevalaṃ purejātānaṃ nissayādīnaṃ vasena purejātanti vuttaṃ.

530. Thereafter, in the first of the four questions concerning the two-rooted, without stating “by co-arisen condition and by pre-arisen condition,” three conditions are shown by way of dependence, presence, and non-disappearance through the two terms spoken: “co-arisen” and “pre-arisen.” For although the wholesome aggregates, together with the base, are co-arisen while establishing their nature as a condition for the wholesome, they are not co-arisen conditions because they are mixed with the base. Therefore, it is said “co-arisen” by way of the dependence, presence, and non-disappearance of those co-arisen factors. This same method applies to the base. For although it is pre-arisen, it is not a pre-arisen condition because it is mixed with the aggregates. It is called “pre-arisen” merely by way of the dependence, presence, and non-disappearance of pre-arisen factors.

Dutiyapañhe “sahajātaṃ pacchājātaṃ āhāraṃ indriya”nti vuttehi catūhipi sahajātanissayaatthiavigatavasena cattāro paccayā dassitā. Imasmiñhi vāre sahajātapaccayo labbhati, pacchājātapaccayādayo na labbhanti. Pacchājātānaṃ pana āhārindriyasaṅkhātānañca atthiavigatānaṃ vasenetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kusalā hi khandhā abyākatā ca mahābhūtā upādārūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena nissayapaccayena atthiavigatapaccayehīti catudhā paccayā honti. Pacchājātā pana kusalā tehiyeva bhūtehi saddhiṃ tesaññeva upādārūpānaṃ atthiavigatavasena paccayo. Kabaḷīkārāhāropi pacchājātehi kusalehi saddhiṃ purejātassa kāyassa atthiavigatavaseneva paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyampi pacchājātehi kusalehi saddhiṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthiavigatapaccayeneva paccayo. Iti imaṃ catudhā paccayabhāvaṃ sandhāya “sahajātaṃ pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ indriya”nti idaṃ vuttaṃ. Pacchājātāhārindriyapaccayā panettha na labbhantiyeva. Parato akusalamissakapañhādvayepi eseva nayoti. Evamettha tesu tesu pañhesu saṅkhipitvā vuttapaccayānaṃ pabhedo veditabbo. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ pana paccaye tesaṃ tesaṃ pañhānaṃ parihānāparihāniṃ parato āvikarissāmāti.

In the second question, by the four terms spoken—“co-arisen, post-arisen, nutriment, faculty”—four conditions are shown by way of co-arisen, dependence, presence, and non-disappearance. For in this instance, the co-arisen condition is obtained, but the post-arisen, nutriment, and faculty conditions are not. However, this is said with regard to the presence and non-disappearance of what are designated as post-arisen states, nutriment, and faculties. Wholesome aggregates and indeterminate great elements are conditions for derived material phenomena in four ways: by the co-arisen condition, the dependence condition, the presence condition, and the non-disappearance condition. Post-arisen wholesome states, however, together with those same elements, are a condition for those same derived material phenomena by way of presence and non-disappearance. Edible food, together with post-arisen wholesome states, is a condition for the previously arisen body only by way of presence and non-disappearance. The material life-faculty, together with post-arisen wholesome states, is a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena only by way of the presence and non-disappearance condition. Thus, with reference to this fourfold conditionality, it is said, “co-arisen, post-arisen, nutriment, faculty.” Here, however, the post-arisen, nutriment, and faculty conditions are not obtained at all. This same method applies to the two subsequent questions involving unwholesome mixed states. Thus, in each of these questions, the classification of the concisely stated conditions should be understood. We will later clarify the inclusion or exclusion of these questions for each respective condition.

Paccanīyuddhārassa atthavaṇṇanā.

Exposition of the Meaning of the Summary of the Negative

Paccanīyagaṇanavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Enumeration of the Negative

532. Idāni [M 0.0470] ete “kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassā”tiādayo anulomavasena pannarasa vārā dassitā. Yasmā paccanīyepi eteyeva, na ito uddhaṃ; heṭṭhā pana honti, tasmā yassa yassa paccayassa paccanīye ye ye vārā labbhanti, te te ādito paṭṭhāya gaṇanavasena dassetuṃ nahetuyā pannarasātiādi āraddhaṃ.

532. Now, these fifteen instances beginning with “a wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon” have been shown in the positive order. Since these same instances also apply in the negative section—and there are none more than this, but sometimes fewer—therefore, to show from the beginning by way of enumeration which instances are found for the negative of each condition, the section beginning with “In the non-root condition, fifteen” is commenced.

Tattha nahetuyā sabbesampi yathādassitānaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena pannarasa labbhanti. Nārammaṇe sahajāte [V 0.0465] hetupaccayo pavisati. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vāre suddho ārammaṇapaccayo parihāyati, sesapaccayavasena te vārā vissajjanaṃ labhanti. Yathā ca nārammaṇe, evaṃ sesesupi. Sahajāte hetupaccayo pavisati. Tasmiṃ tasmiñca vāre naupanissaye naanantareti evaṃ paccanīyato ṭhitā paccayā parihāyanti, avasesapaccayavasena te te vārā vissajjanaṃ labhanti. Nasahajāte pana “kusalo dhammo kusalassa ca abyākatassa ca, akusalo dhammo akusalassa ca abyākatassa ca, kusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā kusalassa, akusalo ca abyākato ca dhammā akusalassāti ime cattāro vārā parihāyanti. Etesañhi catunnaṃ purimesu dvīsu sahajātapaccayena paccayoti ekādasannaṃ paccayānaṃ vasena ekova paccayasaṅgaho vutto. Te tasmiṃ paṭikkhitte aññenākārena vissajjanaṃ na labhanti. Pacchimesu dvīsu nissayaatthiavigatapaccaye sandhāya “sahajātaṃ purejāta”nti vuttaṃ. Te sahajāte paṭikkhitte avasesānaṃ hetuādīnañca purejātānañceva nissayaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena vissajjanaṃ na labhanti, tasmā ime cattāropi vārā parihāyanti. Avasesānaṃ vasena “ekādasā”ti vuttaṃ.

Herein, in the non-root condition, fifteen instances are obtained by way of all the conditions as shown. In the non-object condition, the conascent root condition applies. In each such instance, the pure object condition is excluded, and those instances are resolved by way of the remaining conditions. Just as in the non-object condition, so too in the others. In the conascent condition, the root condition applies. In each such instance, the conditions standing in opposition, such as the non-decisive-support and non-immediacy conditions, are excluded, and those instances are resolved by way of the remaining conditions. However, in the non-conascent condition, these four instances are excluded: “A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for both wholesome and indeterminate phenomena; an unwholesome phenomenon is a condition for both unwholesome and indeterminate phenomena; wholesome and indeterminate phenomena are conditions for a wholesome phenomenon; and unwholesome and indeterminate phenomena are a condition for an unwholesome phenomenon.” For in the first two of these four, only one collection of conditions is stated—'is a condition by conascent condition'—which comprises a group of eleven conditions. When this is negated, they are not resolved in any other way. In the latter two, with reference to the dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions, it is said, “co-arisen, pre-arisen.” When the conascent condition is negated, they are not resolved by way of the remaining root conditions, etc., nor by way of the pre-arisen dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. Therefore, these four instances are also excluded. “Eleven” is stated by way of the remaining ones.

Tattha siyā – yathā hetumhi paṭikkhitte sesānaṃ adhipatiādīnaṃ vasena te vārā laddhā, evaṃ sahajāte paṭikkhitte avasesānaṃ hetuādīnaṃ vasena kasmā na labbhantīti? Nippadesattā. Hetuādayo hi sahajātānaṃ ekadesamattato sappadesā, tasmā tesu paṭikkhittesu aññesaṃ vasena te vārā labbhanti. Sahajāto pana nippadeso sabbepi hetuādayo gaṇhāti, tasmā tasmiṃ paṭikkhitte sabbepi te paṭikkhittā honti. Na hi asahajātā hetupaccayādayo nāma atthi[M 0.0471]. Iti sahajātassa nippadesattā tasmiṃ paṭikkhitte sabbepi te ubhopi vārā na labbhanti. “Sahajātaṃ purejāta”nti vissajjitavāresu pana kiñcāpi sahajātapaccayoyeva natthi, yasmā panettha sahajātāva arūpakkhandhā nissayaatthiavigatavasena paccayā, sahajāte ca paṭikkhitte ekantena sahajātanissayaatthiavigatā paṭikkhittā honti, tasmā tassa paṭikkhittattā tepi vārā na labbhantīti evaṃ sabbathāpettha ime cattāro vārā parihāyanti. Avasesānaññeva vasena ekādasāti vuttaṃ.

Here it may be asked: Just as when the root condition is excluded, those instances are obtained by way of the remaining dominant conditions, etc., why, when co-nascence is excluded, are they not obtained by way of the remaining root conditions, etc.? Because it is all-encompassing. Root conditions, etc., are indeed partial, being only a part of co-nascent phenomena; therefore, when they are excluded, those instances are obtained by way of others. However, co-nascence is all-encompassing and includes all root conditions, etc.; therefore, when it is excluded, all of them are also excluded. Indeed, there are no root conditions, etc., that are not co-nascent. Thus, because of the all-encompassing nature of co-nascence, when it is excluded, all of them, both instances, are not obtained. In the instances resolved as “conascent, prenascent,” although there is no co-nascent condition as such, since here the immaterial aggregates are conditions only by way of co-nascent dependence, presence, and non-disappearance, and when co-nascence is excluded, the co-nascent dependence, presence, and non-disappearance are entirely excluded, therefore, due to its exclusion, those instances are also not obtained. Thus, in every way, these four instances are excluded here. “Eleven” is stated by way of the remaining ones.

Naaññamaññananissayanasampayuttepi teyeva vārā parihāyanti. Kasmā? Sahajātagatikattā. Yatheva hi arūpadhammabhūto sahajātapaccayo nippadesena cattāro arūpakkhandhe gaṇhāti, tathā aññamaññanissayasampayuttāpīti sahajātagatikattā etesupi paṭikkhittesu te vārā [V 0.0466] na labbhantīti veditabbā. Tena vuttaṃ naaññamaññe ekādasa, nanissaye ekādasa, nasampayutte ekādasāti.

In the cases of non-reciprocity, non-dependence, and non-association also, those very same instances are excluded. Why? Because of their co-nascent nature. Just as the co-nascent condition, being an immaterial phenomenon, encompasses the four immaterial aggregates without remainder, so too do the reciprocal, dependence, and association conditions have a co-nascent nature; therefore, it should be understood that when these are excluded, those instances are not obtained. Hence it is said: “In non-reciprocity, eleven; in non-dependence, eleven; in non-association, eleven.”

Tattha siyā – kiñcāpi ime avisesena kusalādibhedānaṃ catunnaṃ khandhānaṃ saṅgāhakattā sahajātagatikā, kusalo pana kusalābyākatassa ṭhapetvā sahajātapaccayaṃ aññathā paccayova na hoti, tasmā tasmiṃ paṭikkhitte so vāro parihāyatu. Kusalo pana kusalābyākatānaṃ neva aññamaññapaccayo hoti, tasmiṃ paṭikkhitte so vāro kasmā parihāyatīti? Aññamaññapaccayadhammavasena pavattisabbhāvato. Yatheva hi kusalābyākatā kusalassa sahajātapaccayova na honti. Sahajātadhammavasena pana nissayapaccayādīhi pavattisabbhāvato tasmiṃ paṭikkhitte so vāro parihāyati, evamidhāpi aññamaññapaccayadhammavasena sahajātādīhi pavattisabbhāvato tasmiṃ paṭikkhitte so vāro parihāyati. Naaññamaññapaccayena paccayoti padassa hi ayamattho – ye dhammā aññamaññapaccayasaṅgahaṃ gatā, na tehi paccayo. Kusalo ca kusalābyākatānaṃ sahajātādivasena paccayo honto aññamaññapaccayadhammeheva paccayo hoti, tasmā tasmiṃ paṭikkhitte so vāro parihāyati. Yathā ca so vāro, tathā sesāpi tayoti cattāropi te vārā parihāyanti.

Here it may be asked: Although these conditions, being collectors of the four aggregates of the wholesome and other divisions without distinction, have a co-nascent nature, yet the wholesome is not a condition for the wholesome-and-indeterminate in any other way except as a co-nascent condition; therefore, when that is excluded, let that instance be excluded. But the wholesome is not a reciprocal condition for the wholesome-and-indeterminate; when that is excluded, why should that instance be excluded? Because of the existence of an occurrence by way of reciprocal condition phenomena. Just as the wholesome-and-indeterminate are not co-nascent conditions for the wholesome, yet because there is an occurrence by way of co-nascent phenomena through dependence condition, etc., when that is excluded, that instance is excluded—so too here, because there is an occurrence by way of reciprocal condition phenomena through co-nascent conditions, etc., when that is excluded, that instance is excluded. For the meaning of the phrase 'not a condition by way of reciprocal condition' is this: it is not a condition by means of those phenomena which are included under reciprocal condition. And the wholesome, in being a condition for the wholesome-and-indeterminate by way of co-nascent conditions, etc., is a condition precisely by way of reciprocal condition phenomena; therefore, when that is excluded, that instance is excluded. And just as that instance, so too the remaining three; thus, all four of those instances are excluded.

Nanissaye [M 0.0472] ekādasāti etthāpi yasmā tesaṃ vārānaṃ ekentena sahajātapaccayadhammāva nissayabhūtā, tasmā nissaye paṭikkhitte parihāyanti. Napurejāte terasāti sahajātaṃ purejātanti vuttavissajjane dvimūlake dve apanetvā terasa. Yathā hi te sahajāte paṭikkhitte purejātānaññeva nissayaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena vissajjanaṃ na labhanti, tathā purejātepi paṭikkhitte sahajātānaññeva nissayaatthiavigatānaṃ vasena vissajjanaṃ na labhanti, tasmā te apanetvā terasāti veditabbā.

In 'non-dependence, eleven': here too, because for those instances it is exclusively co-nascent condition phenomena that constitute the dependence, therefore, when dependence is excluded, they are excluded. In 'non-prenascent, thirteen': in the resolution stated as 'conascent, prenascent,' by removing the two two-rooted instances, there are thirteen. For just as when the co-nascent is excluded, they do not obtain a resolution by way of only the prenascent dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions, so too when the prenascent is excluded, they do not obtain a resolution by way of only the co-nascent dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions. Therefore, it should be understood that by removing those, there are thirteen.

Napacchājāte pannarasāti ettha “pacchājātapaccayena paccayo”ti vā “sahajātaṃ pacchājātaṃ āhāraṃ indriya”nti vā āgataṭṭhānesu ṭhapetvā pacchājātaṃ avasesavasenapi te pañhā labbhanti, tasmā pannaraseva vuttā. Nakammetiādīsu yasmā kammavipākāhārindriyajhānamaggāpi kusalādibhedānaṃ catunnaṃ khandhānaṃ ekadesova tasmā ṭhapetvā te dhamme avasesadhammavasena sahajātadhammā paccayā hontīti ekampi pañhāvissajjanaṃ na parihīnaṃ[V 0.0467]. Nasampayutte ekādasāti yasmā tesu catūsu vāresu sampayuttadhammā sahajātādipaccayena paccayā honti, tasmā sampayuttapaccayapaṭikkhepena teyeva vārā parihāyantīti veditabbā. Navippayutte navāti dumūlakaekāvasānā cattāro ekamūlakadukāvasānā dve cāti ime cha vārā ekantena vippayuttapaccayadhammehi yuttā. Tehi sahajātādivasena paccayā honti, tasmā vippayutte paṭikkhitte sabbepi te parihāyantīti naveva labbhanti. Tena vuttaṃ “navippayutte navā”ti. Noatthinoavigatesupi teyeva veditabbā. Ekantena hi te vārā atthiavigatapaccayadhammayuttā, tasmā te tesaṃ paṭikkhepe parihāyanti. Yepi labbhanti, tesu ārammaṇavasena anantarādivasena vā vissajjanāni kātabbāni. Sahajātapurejātapacchājātaāhārindriyabhedato pañcannaṃ atthiavigatānaṃ vippayuttadhammānaṃ vā vasena na kātabbānīti.

In 'non-postnascent, fifteen': here, in places where it is stated as “condition by postnascent condition” or “conascent, postnascent, nutriment, faculty,” even excluding the postnascent condition, those questions are obtained by way of the remaining conditions; therefore, fifteen are stated. In cases like “not by kamma,” since kamma, kamma-result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, and path factors are only a part of the four aggregates of wholesome, etc., therefore, excluding these phenomena, the remaining phenomena become conditions by way of co-nascent phenomena; thus, not even a single resolution of a question is excluded. In 'non-association, eleven': because in those four instances, associated phenomena are conditions by way of co-nascent and other conditions, therefore, by the exclusion of the association condition, those very instances are excluded—this should be understood. In 'non-dissociation, nine': four instances that are two-rooted and end in one, and two that are one-rooted and end in a dyad—these six instances are exclusively connected with dissociated condition phenomena. Through them, they are conditions by way of co-nascence and other conditions; therefore, when the dissociation condition is excluded, all of them are excluded, and only nine are obtained. Hence it is said, “in non-dissociation, nine.” In non-presence and non-non-disappearance, the same should be understood. For those instances are exclusively connected with presence and non-disappearance condition phenomena; therefore, when these are excluded, they are excluded. And for those that are obtained, resolutions should be made by way of object condition, proximity condition, etc. They should not be made by way of the five kinds of presence and non-disappearance (divided as co-nascent, prenascent, postnascent, nutriment, and faculty) or by way of dissociated phenomena.

533. Evaṃ paccanīye laddhavāre gaṇanato dassetvā idāni dumūlakādivasena paccayagaṇanaṃ dassetuṃ nahetupaccayā nārammaṇe pannarasātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha nahetumūlakadukesu atirekagaṇano ūnataragaṇanena saddhiṃ yojito ūnataragaṇanova hoti.

533. Having thus shown the enumeration of the obtained instances in the negative section, now, to show the enumeration of conditions by way of the two-rooted, etc., the section beginning with “in non-root condition, in non-object, fifteen” is commenced. Therein, in the dyads rooted in non-root, an enumeration with more, when combined with an enumeration with less, becomes only an enumeration with less.

Timūlake [M 0.0473] naupanissaye terasāti kusalo akusalassa, akusalo kusalassāti dve vārā parihāyanti. Kasmā? Nārammaṇena saddhiṃ naupanissayassa ghaṭitattā. Ārammaṇavasena hi upanissayavasena ca imesaṃ pavatti. Tañca ubhayaṃ paṭikkhittaṃ. Ārammaṇādhipati ca ārammaṇūpanissayaggahaṇena gahito hotiyeva.

In the three-rooted, in non-decisive-support, there are thirteen. The two instances, “wholesome for unwholesome” and “unwholesome for wholesome,” are excluded. Why? Because of the combination of non-decisive-support with non-object. For the occurrence of these is by way of object and by way of decisive support, and both of these are negated. Moreover, object-predominance is indeed included by the grasping of object-decisive-support.

Chamūlakepi naupanissaye terasāti teyeva terasa. Sattamūlake pana naupanissaye sattāti nasahajātena saddhiṃ ghaṭitattā tattha parihīnehi catūhi saddhiṃ “kusalo kusalassa, kusalo akusalassa, akusalo akusalassa, akusalo kusalassā”ti ime anantarūpanissayapakatūpanissayavasena pavattamānā cattāroti aṭṭha parihāyanti, tasmā avasesānaṃ vasena sattāti vuttaṃ. Napurejāte ekādasāti nasahajātena saddhiṃ ghaṭitattā ekādasa. Napacchājāte navāti tesu ekādasasu sahajātaṃ pacchājātaṃ āhāraṃ indriyanti laddhavissajjanesu dumūlake abyākatante dve vāre apanetvā. Te hi sahajāte paṭikkhittepi pacchājātavasena aparihīnā. Sahajātena pana saddhiṃ pacchājāte paṭikkhitte parihāyantīti sesānaṃ vasena navāti vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhamūlake nanissaye ekādasāti sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttasadisameva. Navamūlake [V 0.0468] naupanissaye pañcāti kusalādayo abyākatantā tayo dumūlakā abyākatantā dve cāti pañca. Tesu nānākkhaṇikakammakabaḷīkārāhārarūpajīvitindriyapacchājātadhammavasena vissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Even in the six-rooted, in non-decisive-support, there are thirteen; indeed, just those thirteen. But in the seven-rooted, in non-decisive-support, there are seven, because of the combination with non-co-nascent. For there, along with the four [co-nascent instances] that are excluded, these four instances which occur by way of contiguity-decisive-support and natural-decisive-support—namely, ‘wholesome for wholesome,’ ‘wholesome for unwholesome,’ ‘unwholesome for unwholesome,’ and ‘unwholesome for wholesome’—are also excluded; thus, eight are excluded. Therefore, it is said there are seven by way of the remainder. In non-pre-nascence, there are eleven, because of the combination with non-co-nascent. In non-post-nascence, there are nine; this is after excluding from those eleven the two instances of the two-rooted indeterminate states, in which the resolutions are obtained by way of co-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. For even when co-nascence is negated, they are not excluded by way of post-nascence. But when post-nascence is negated along with co-nascence, they are excluded. Thus, it is said there are nine by way of the remainder. In the eight-rooted, in non-dependence, there are eleven. All is just like what was stated above. In the nine-rooted, in non-decisive-support, there are five. That is, the three wholesome, etc., ending in indeterminate, and the two two-rooted ending in indeterminate, making five. Among these, the resolution should be understood by way of different-moment kamma, physical nutriment, material life faculty, and post-nascent phenomena.

Dasamūlake napurejāte pañcātiādīsupi teyeva. Napacchājāte tīṇīti pacchājātavasena labbhamāne dumūlake abyākatante dve apanetvā avasesā. Navippayuttepi teyeva tayo. Noatthiyā dveti nānākkhaṇikakammavasena kusalañca akusalañca kaṭattārūpassa. Vipākaṃ panettha naupanissayena saddhiṃ ghaṭitattā na labbhati. Ekādasamūlake heṭṭhā vuttasadisāva gaṇanā. Dvādasamūlake nakamme ekanti abyākatena abyākataṃ. Tattha ca āhārindriyavasena vissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Terasamūlakādīsupi sabbattha ekanti āgataṭṭhāne idameva gahetabbaṃ. Nāhāre pana indriyavasena vissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Naindriye āhāravasena. Cuddasamūlakādīsu nakammena saddhiṃ ghaṭitattā noatthinoavigatā na labbhantīti [M 0.0474] na vuttā. Nāhārapaccayā najhānapaccayāti naindriyaṃ apanetvā vuttaṃ. Tasmā tattha indriyavasena ekaṃ veditabbaṃ. Navipākapaccayā naindriyapaccayāti nāhāraṃ apanetvā vuttaṃ, tasmā tattha āhāravasena ekaṃ veditabbaṃ. Imesu pana dvīsu paccanīyato ṭhitesu gaṇanā nāma natthi, tasmā ekato na dassitāti.

In the ten-rooted, in non-pre-nascence, there are five, etc.; these are the same. In non-post-nascence, there are three; this is the remainder after excluding the two two-rooted indeterminate instances which are obtained by way of post-nascence. Even in non-dissociation, those same three. In non-presence, there are two: that is, wholesome and unwholesome by way of different-moment kamma for kamma-born materiality. Here, however, the resultant is not obtained because it is combined with non-decisive-support. In the eleven-rooted, the enumeration is just like what was stated above. In the twelve-rooted, in non-kamma, there is one: the indeterminate for the indeterminate. And there, a resolution should be understood by way of nutriment and faculty. Even in the thirteen-rooted, etc., wherever 'one' is mentioned, this same principle should be taken. But in non-nutriment, the resolution should be understood by way of faculty; in non-faculty, by way of nutriment. In the fourteen-rooted, etc., because they are combined with non-kamma, 'non-presence' and 'non-disappearance' are not obtained, thus they are not stated. 'Not by nutriment condition, not by jhāna condition'—this is stated having excluded non-faculty. Therefore, there, one should be understood by way of faculty. 'Not by resultant condition, not by faculty condition'—this is stated having excluded non-nutriment. Therefore, there, one should be understood by way of nutriment. But when these two stand in opposition, there is no enumeration as such; therefore, they are not shown together.

Nahetumūlakaṃ.

The Section Rooted in Non-Root.

534. Nārammaṇamūlakādīsupi pannarasaterasaekādasanavāti sabbadukesu cattārova mūlagaṇanaparicchedā. Tikādīsu pana bahupaccayasamāyoge itarānipi satta pañca tīṇi dve ekanti paricchinnagaṇanāni vissajjanāni labbhantiyeva. Tesu yesaṃ paccayānaṃ samāyoge yaṃ yaṃ labbhati, taṃ taṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayena sādhukaṃ sallakkhetvā uddharitabbaṃ. Sabbesu cetesu nārammaṇamūlakādīsu nārammaṇādīni padāni atikkantena hetupadena saddhiṃ paṭhamaṃ bandhitvāva cakkāni katāni. Yasmā pana tāni nahetumūlake vuttasadisāneva honti, tasmā vitthārena adassetvā saṅkhepaṃ katvā dassitāni. Tattha yathā nahetumūlake nārammaṇanaupanissayā visuṃ visuṃ pannarasa vāre labhantāpi samāyoge terasa labhiṃsu, evaṃ sabbattha teraseva labhanti. Yathā ca nārammaṇanasahajātehi saddhiṃ naupanissaye satta vārā honti, evaṃ naupanissayanārammaṇehi saddhiṃ nasahajātepi satta.

534. Even in the sections rooted in non-object, etc., there are fifteen, thirteen, eleven, and nine—these are the four divisions of the root-enumeration in all the dyads. But in the triads, etc., when many conditions are combined, other distinct enumerations of seven, five, three, two, or one are indeed obtained as resolutions. Among these, whatever is obtained by the combination of which conditions, that should be carefully noted and extracted according to the method stated above. And in all these sections rooted in non-object, etc., the terms 'non-object,' etc., are first combined with the positive `hetu` term to form the matrices. But since these are just like those stated in the section rooted in non-root, they have been shown briefly without detailing them. Here, just as in the section rooted in non-root, non-object and non-decisive-support, though separately obtaining fifteen instances, obtained thirteen when combined; so too everywhere, they obtain only thirteen. And just as there are seven instances for non-decisive-support when combined with non-object and non-co-nascent, so too there are seven for non-co-nascent when combined with non-decisive-support and non-object.

538. Nanissayapaccayā [V 0.0469] naupanissayapaccayā napacchājāte tīṇīti kusalādīni abyākatantāni. Tesu kaṭattārūpañca āhārasamuṭṭhānañca paccayuppannaṃ.

538. 'In non-dependence condition, non-decisive-support condition, non-post-nascence, there are three'—these are the wholesome, etc., ending in indeterminate. Among these, kamma-born materiality and nutriment-produced materiality are the conditionally arisen phenomena.

543-544. Nāhāranaindriyamūlakesu catukkesu nakammena saddhiṃ aghaṭitattā nahetumūlake viya ekentena labbhanti. Naindriyamūlake naupanissaye ca napurejāte ca ṭhapetvā nāhāre tīṇīti kātabbanti naindriyapaccayato paṭṭhāya ime dve paccaye ghaṭetvā naindriyapaccayā…pe… naupanissayapaccayā nāhāre tīṇī. Naindriyapaccayā…pe… napurejātapaccayā nāhāre tīṇīti evaṃ imehi paccayehi saddhiṃ nāhārapaccaye ca gaṇanā kātabbāti [M 0.0475] attho. Tattha tīṇīti kusalādīneva abyākatassa. Tattha kusalākusalā kaṭattārūpānaṃ purejātassa ca kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena, abyākatā pana cittacetasikā pacchājātapaccayenevāti imesaṃ vasena tīṇi vissajjanāni kātabbāni. Parato pana napacchājātena saddhiṃ ghaṭitattā nāhāre dveti vuttaṃ. Tattha kaṭattārūpavasena kusalaṃ abyākatassa, tathā akusalanti ettakameva labbhati. Āhārassa pana paṭikkhittattā kabaḷīkārāhāro atthiavigatavasenāpi paccayabhāvaṃ na labhati.

543-544. In the non-nutriment-rooted and non-faculty-rooted tetrads, since they are not combined with non-kamma, they are obtained singly, as in the non-root-rooted. In the non-faculty-rooted, having excluded non-decisive-support and non-pre-nascence, it should be stated that there are three in non-nutriment. This means that, starting from the non-faculty condition, combining these two conditions: ‘by non-faculty condition…pe… by non-decisive-support condition, there are three in non-nutriment’; and ‘by non-faculty condition…pe… by non-pre-nascence condition, there are three in non-nutriment’—thus, with these conditions, a calculation should also be made with the non-nutriment condition. Here, ‘three’ refers to the wholesome, etc., for the indeterminate. Therein, the wholesome and unwholesome are conditions for kamma-born materiality and the pre-nascent body by way of post-nascence condition; but the indeterminate consciousness and mental factors are conditions only by way of post-nascence condition. Thus, three answers should be given based on these. Further on, however, since it is combined with non-post-nascence, it is said there are two in non-nutriment. Therein, by way of kamma-born materiality, only the wholesome for the indeterminate, and similarly the unwholesome, are obtained. As for nutriment, since it is rejected, physical nutriment does not obtain conditionality even by way of presence and non-disappearance.

545. Navippayuttamūlakassa catumūlake naupanissaye pañcāti kusalo sahajātakusalassa, kusalo kaṭattārūpasaṅkhātassa abyākatassa, akusalo sahajātaakusalassa, tathā kaṭattārūpasaṅkhātassa abyākatassa, abyākato sahajātaabyākatassāti evaṃ pañca. Navippayuttapaccayā…pe… naupanissaye tīṇīti heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva kusalādayo tayo abyākatassa.

545. In the non-dissociated-rooted, in the four-rooted, in non-decisive-support, there are five: wholesome for co-nascent wholesome, wholesome for the indeterminate reckoned as kamma-born materiality, unwholesome for co-nascent unwholesome, likewise for the indeterminate reckoned as kamma-born materiality, and indeterminate for co-nascent indeterminate—thus five. By non-dissociation condition…pe… in non-decisive-support, there are three. That is, by the method stated previously, the three—wholesome, etc.—are for the indeterminate.

546. Noatthipaccayā nahetuyā navāti nahetupaccayā noatthiyā vuttā naveva. Sabbepi hi te ekamūlakekāvasānā anantarapakatūpanissayavasena labbhanti. Nārammaṇe navātipi teyeva nārammaṇe ṭhatvā naupanissaye dve kātabbā. Yāva nissayampīti noatthimūlake naye “noatthipaccayā nahetupaccayā nārammaṇapaccayā”ti evaṃ cakkabandhagamanena nārammaṇapaccaye ṭhatvā imehi vā tīhi, ito paresu nādhipatiādīsu aññataraññatarena vā saddhiṃ yāva nissayapaccayaṃ pāpuṇāti, tāva gantvā naupanissaye dve vissajjanāni kātabbānīti attho.

546. By non-presence condition, not by root condition—nine. That is, nine are stated as by non-root condition, not by presence condition. For all of them, having a single root and a single conclusion, are obtained by way of contiguity and natural decisive support. Not by object condition, there are also nine. Those same ones, being established in non-object, two are to be stated in non-decisive-support. Even up to dependence condition. This means that in the method of the non-presence-rooted, being established in the non-object condition by proceeding in a cyclical manner—‘by non-presence condition, by non-root condition, by non-object condition’—with these three, or with any one of the others among those further conditions beginning with non-dominance, one reaches up to the dependence condition; having gone thus far, two answers are to be given in non-decisive-support. This is the meaning.

Evaṃ [V 0.0470] lakkhaṇaṃ ṭhapetvā puna nārammaṇato paṭṭhāya yāva nissayā satta paccaye gahetvā naupanissaye dveti āha. Tattha noatthipaccayā nahetupaccayā nārammaṇapaccayā naupanissaye dve, noatthipaccayā nahetunārammaṇanādhipatipaccayā naupanissaye dveti evaṃ nārammaṇato purimapacchimehi nissayapariyosānehi sabbapadehi saddhiṃ yojanā kātabbā. Dveti panettha kusalo abyākatassa, akusalo abyākatassāti [M 0.0476] nānākkhaṇikakammavasena kaṭattārūpassa paccayavasena veditabbāni. Naupanissayapadena saddhiṃ napurejātādīsu sabbattha dve. Kammapaccayo panettha na gahito. Tasmiñhi gahite tepi dve vārā chijjanti, vissajjanameva na labbhati. Evaṃ yena yena saddhiṃ yassa yassa saṃsandane. Yaṃ labbhati, yañca parihāyati, taṃ sabbaṃ sādhukaṃ sallakkhetvā sabbapaccanīyesu gaṇanā uddharitabbāti.

Having thus established the characteristic, he says that again, starting from non-object up to dependence, taking seven conditions, there are two in non-decisive-support. Here, ‘by non-presence condition, by non-root condition, by non-object condition, there are two in non-decisive-support,’ and ‘by non-presence condition, by non-root, non-object, and non-dominance conditions, there are two in non-decisive-support’—thus, from non-object, the combination should be made with all terms, both preceding and succeeding, ending in dependence. Here, ‘two’ refers to the wholesome for the indeterminate, and the unwholesome for the indeterminate—these should be understood as conditions by way of different-moment kamma for kamma-born materiality. With the term ‘non-decisive-support,’ there are two in all cases, such as in non-pre-nascence, etc. The kamma condition, however, is not included here. For if it were included, those two instances would be cut off, and no answer would be obtainable. Thus, in the combination of whatever with whatever, whatever is obtained and whatever is lost—all that should be carefully noted, and the calculation should be carried out in all the negative conditions.

Paccanīyagaṇanavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Calculation of the Negative Conditions.

Anulomapaccanīyavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Positive and Negative Methods.

550. Anulomapaccanīye “hetuyā satta, ārammaṇe navā”ti evaṃ anulome “nahetuyā pannarasa, nārammaṇe pannarasā”ti evaṃ paccanīye ca laddhagaṇanesu paccayesu yo paccayo anulomato ṭhito, tassa anulome laddhavārehi saddhiṃ ye paccanīyato ṭhitassa paccanīye laddhavāresu sadisavārā, tesaṃ vasena gaṇanā veditabbā. Anulomasmiñhi hetupaccaye “hetuyā sattā”ti satta vārā laddhā, paccanīye nārammaṇapaccaye “nārammaṇe pannarasā”ti pannarasa laddhā. Tesu ye hetuyā satta vuttā, tehi saddhiṃ nārammaṇe vuttesu pannarasasu “kusalo kusalassa, abyākatassa, kusalābyākatassa, akusalo akusalassa, abyākatassa, akusalābyākatassa, abyākato abyākatassā”ti ime satta sadisā. Te sandhāya hetupaccayā naārammaṇe sattāti vuttaṃ. Naadhipatiyā sattātiādīsupi eseva nayo.

550. In the Positive and Negative Methods, 'by root condition, seven; by object condition, nine'—thus in the positive; and 'not by root condition, fifteen; not by object condition, fifteen'—thus in the negative. Among the conditions for which the counts have been obtained, for whichever condition belongs to the positive method, its calculation should be understood based on the similar instances among those obtained for it in the positive method and those obtained in the negative method for a condition belonging to the negative method. For in the positive method, for the root condition, 'by root condition, seven'—seven instances are obtained; in the negative method, for the non-object condition, 'not by object condition, fifteen'—fifteen are obtained. Among these, the seven stated 'by root condition,' when compared with the fifteen stated 'not by object condition'—namely, 'the wholesome for the wholesome, for the indeterminate, for the wholesome-and-indeterminate; the unwholesome for the unwholesome, for the indeterminate, for the unwholesome-and-indeterminate; the indeterminate for the indeterminate'—these seven are similar. With reference to these, it is said, 'by root condition, not by object condition, there are seven.' The same method applies to 'not by dominance condition, seven,' etc.

Nasahajātassa pana hetupaccayassa abhāvā nasahajāte ekopi na labbhati, tasmā tena saddhiṃ yojanā na katā. Naaññamaññe kusalādayo tayo rūpābyākatassa labbhanti, te sandhāya [V 0.0471] tīṇīti vuttaṃ. Tathā nasampayutte. Navippayutte pana kusalaṃ kusalassa, akusalaṃ akusalassa, abyākataṃ abyākatassāti arūpadhammavasena tīṇi veditabbāni. Nanissayanoatthinoavigatā nasahajāto viya [M 0.0477] na labbhantiyevāti tehipi saddhiṃ yojanā na katā. Evamettha satta tīṇīti dveyeva gaṇanaparicchedā, tesaṃ vasena ūnataragaṇanena saddhiṃ atirekagaṇanassapi gaṇanaṃ parihāpetvā paccayaghaṭanesu gaṇanā veditabbā.

However, since there is no root condition that is not co-nascent, not even one instance is obtained in the non-co-nascent; therefore, no combination is made with it. In non-mutuality, the three—wholesome, etc.—are obtained for indeterminate materiality; with reference to these, it is said, ‘three.’ Similarly in non-association. In non-dissociation, however, ‘the wholesome for the wholesome, the unwholesome for the unwholesome, the indeterminate for the indeterminate’—these three should be understood by way of immaterial phenomena. Just as the non-co-nascent is not obtained, so too non-dependence, non-presence, and non-disappearance are not obtained; therefore, no combination is made with them either. Thus, here, the seven and the three are only two numerical divisions. Based on these, the calculation in the combinations of conditions should be understood by reducing the count of the more numerous group in accordance with the less numerous one.

551. Tattha hetusahajātanissayaatthiavigatanti nārammaṇe sattāti kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo, sahajātanissayaatthiavigatapaccayena paccayo, nārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Kusalā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo, sahajātanissayaatthiavigatapaccayena paccayo, nārammaṇapaccayena paccayoti iminā nayena satta vārā uddharitabbā. Nādhipatiyā sattātiādīsupi eseva nayo. Dutiye ghaṭane aññamaññassa paviṭṭhattā ṭhapetvā nasampayuttaṃ sesesu tīṇīti vuttaṃ. Nasampayutte pana aññamaññavippayuttaṃ paṭisandhināmarūpaṃ sandhāya ekanti vuttaṃ. Aññamaññapaccayo cettha anulomaghaṭane paviṭṭhattā paccanīyato na labbhati, tasmā “naaññamaññe”ti na vuttaṃ. Yathā cettha, evaṃ sesaghaṭanesupi paviṭṭhapaccayā paccanīyato na labbhantīti na vuttā. Tatiyaghaṭane sampayuttassa paviṭṭhattā sabbattha tīṇiyeva. Catutthaghaṭane vippayuttassa paviṭṭhattā tīṇi kusalādīni cittasamuṭṭhānarūpassa. Pañcame vipākassa paviṭṭhattā sabbattha ekaṃ abyākatena abyākataṃ. Ito paresupi vipākasampayuttesu eseva nayo.

551. Herein, 'seven in not-object' means: a wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition, by way of co-nascence, dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions, and by way of not-object condition. Wholesome roots are conditions for the associated aggregates by way of root condition, by way of co-nascence, dependence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions, and by way of not-object condition. In this way, seven instances should be drawn out. The same method applies to 'seven in not-dominance,' and so on. In the second combination, due to the inclusion of mutuality, it is said that there are three in the remaining conditions, excluding not-association. However, in not-association, it is said 'one' with reference to the mutually dissociated rebirth-linking mentality-materiality. Here, the mutuality condition is not obtained from the negative side due to its inclusion in the positive combination; therefore, 'in not-mutuality' is not stated. Just as here, so too in the remaining combinations, the included conditions are not obtained from the negative side and are therefore not stated. In the third combination, due to the inclusion of association, there are only three everywhere. In the fourth combination, due to the inclusion of dissociation, there are three—wholesome, and so on—for mind-originated matter. In the fifth, due to the inclusion of resultant, there is one everywhere: the indeterminate by way of the indeterminate. The same method applies to the resultant-associated states beyond this.

552. Hetusahajātanissayaindriyamaggaatthiavigatanti nārammaṇe cattārīti kusalo kusalassa, abyākatassa, kusalābyākatassa; abyākato abyākatassāti imesaṃ vasena veditabbāni. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Naaññamaññe dveti kusalo abyākatassa, tathā abyākato. Paratopi dvīsu eseva nayo. Iminā upāyena sabbaghaṭanesu labbhamānavasena gaṇanā veditabbā. Sabbānipi cetāni imasmiṃ anulomapaccanīye sahajātavasena ceva pakiṇṇakavasena ca pannarasādhikāni cattāri ghaṭanasatāni vuttāni. Tesu tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ghaṭane ye anulomato ṭhitā paccayā, tesaṃ ekopi paccanīyato na labbhati. Hetumūlake cettha paṭhame ghaṭane anulomato pañcannaṃ paccayānaṃ ṭhitattā paccanīyato ekūnavīsati paccayā āgatā. Evaṃ sesesupi [M 0.0478] anulomato ṭhitāvasesā paccanīyato āgatā. Anulomato cettha bahūsupi ṭhitesu [V 0.0472] paccanīyato ekekova āgatoti veditabbo. Yathā ca hetumūlake, evaṃ ārammaṇādimūlakesupi sabbametaṃ vidhānaṃ yathānurūpato veditabbanti.

552. By way of root, co-nascence, dependence, faculty, path, presence, and non-disappearance, 'four in not-object' should be understood in terms of these cases: a wholesome phenomenon for a wholesome one, for an indeterminate one, and for a wholesome-and-indeterminate one; an indeterminate phenomenon for an indeterminate one. The same method applies to the remaining cases. In not-mutuality, 'two' means: the wholesome for the indeterminate, and likewise the indeterminate. The same method applies to the two beyond this. By this method, the enumeration should be understood based on what is obtained in all combinations. In this positive and negative analysis, all these are stated as four hundred and fifteen combinations, by way of co-nascence and by way of miscellaneous conditions. Among these, in each combination, not even one of the conditions that stand on the positive side is obtained from the negative side. Here, in the first combination rooted in root, since five conditions stand on the positive side, nineteen conditions come from the negative side. Similarly, in the remaining combinations, the conditions other than those standing on the positive side come from the negative side. Here, even when many conditions stand on the positive side, it should be understood that only a single one comes from the negative side. And just as in the root-based combinations, so too in the object-based and other combinations, this entire method should be understood accordingly.

Anulomapaccanīyavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Positive-Negative.

Paccanīyānulomavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Negative-Positive.

631. Paccanīyānulomepi “hetuyā satta, ārammaṇe navā”ti evaṃ anulome “nahetuyā pannarasa, nārammaṇe pannarasā”ti evaṃ paccanīye ca laddhagaṇanesu paccayesu yo paccanīyato ṭhito, tassa paccanīyato laddhavāresu ye anulomato ṭhitassa anulomato laddhavārehi sadisā vārā, tesaṃ vasena gaṇanā veditabbā. Paccanīyasmiñhi nahetupaccaye “nahetuyā pannarasā”ti pannarasa vārā laddhā, anulome ārammaṇapaccaye “ārammaṇe navā”ti nava vārā laddhā. Tattha ye nahetuyā pannarasa vuttā, tesu ye vārā ārammaṇe vuttehi navahi sadisā, tesaṃ vasena gaṇanā veditabbā. Tattha ye ārammaṇe nava vuttā, te nahetuyā vuttesu pannarasasu kusalo “kusalākusalābyākatānaṃ, akusalo akusalakusalābyākatānaṃ, abyākato abyākatakusalākusalāna”nti imehi navahi sadisā, te sandhāya nahetuyā ārammaṇe navāti vuttaṃ. Adhipatiyā dasātiādīsupi eseva nayo. Ārammaṇādīnañhi anulomagaṇanāya ye vārā vuttā nahetupaccayena saddhiṃ saṃsandanepi te sabbe labbhantīti veditabbā. “Kusalo dhammo kusalassa dhammassa nahetupaccayena paccayo ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo, dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhatī”ti iminā upāyena tesaṃ pāḷi uddharitabbā.

631. Also in the Negative-Positive method, with counts such as 'in root, seven; in object, nine' in the positive, and 'in not-root, fifteen; in not-object, fifteen' in the negative, the enumeration among the conditions thus obtained should be understood in this way: for a condition that stands on the negative side, the count is to be understood based on those of its instances obtained on the negative side that are similar to the instances obtained on the positive side for a condition that stands on the positive side. For, in the negative, for the not-root condition, fifteen instances are obtained, as in 'in not-root, fifteen.' In the positive, for the object condition, nine instances are obtained, as in 'in object, nine.' Therein, among the fifteen stated for not-root, the count should be understood based on those instances that are similar to the nine stated for object. Therein, the nine stated for object are similar to these nine among the fifteen stated for not-root: 'the wholesome for the wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate; the unwholesome for the unwholesome, wholesome, and indeterminate; the indeterminate for the indeterminate, wholesome, and unwholesome.' With reference to these, it is said: 'in not-root, nine by object.' The same method applies to 'in dominance, ten,' and so on. For it should be understood that all those instances stated in the positive enumeration for object, etc., are also obtained when correlated with the not-root condition. The Pāli text for these should be cited by this method: 'A wholesome phenomenon is a condition for a wholesome phenomenon by way of not-root condition and by way of object condition. Having given a gift, undertaken the precepts, or performed the observance day duty, one reflects upon it; one reflects upon previously well-done deeds.'

Nahetupaccayā adhipatiyā dasāti ettha ṭhapetvā vīmaṃsādhipatiṃ sesādhipativasena anulomavibhaṅge āgatavārā uddharitabbā. Evamettha nava [M 0.0479] dasasattatīṇiterasaekanti cha gaṇanaparicchedā, tesaṃ vasena ūnataragaṇanena saddhiṃ atirekagaṇanassāpi gaṇanaṃ parihāpetvā nahetumūlakādīnaṃ nayānaṃ timūlakādīsu sabbasaṃsandanesu gaṇanā veditabbā. Idaṃ tāva sādhāraṇalakkhaṇaṃ[V 0.0473]. Na panetaṃ sabbasaṃsandanesu gacchati, yehi pana paccayehi saddhiṃ yesaṃ paccayānaṃ saṃsandane ye vārā virujjhanti, te apanetvā avasesānaṃ vasenapettha gaṇanā veditabbā.

In 'by not-root condition, by dominance, ten,' the instances that occur in the positive analysis by way of the remaining dominances, excluding dominance by investigation, should be cited. Thus, there are here six numerical divisions: nine, ten, seven, three, thirteen, and one. By means of these, having disregarded the count of the lesser enumeration along with the excess enumeration, the enumeration of the methods beginning with the not-root-based, in all their correlations with the three-rooted, etc., should be understood. This, for now, is the general characteristic. This, however, does not apply in all correlations. In the correlation of certain conditions with certain other conditions, those instances that are in conflict should be removed, and the enumeration here should be understood by way of the remaining ones.

Nahetupaccayā naārammaṇapaccayā adhipatiyā sattāti ettha hi kusalo akusalassa; abyākato kusalassa, akusalassāti ime ārammaṇādhipativasena labbhamānā tayo vārā virujjhanti. Kasmā? Naārammaṇapaccayāti vuttattā. Tasmā te apanetvā sahajātādhipatinayenevettha “kusalo kusalassa, abyākatassa, kusalābyākatassa; akusalo akusalassa, abyākatassa, akusalābyākatassa; abyākato abyākatassā”ti satta vārā veditabbā. Tepi nahetupaccayāti vacanato ṭhapetvā vīmaṃsādhipatiṃ sesādhipatīnaṃ vasena. Evaṃ sabbattha ūnataragaṇanapaccayavasena avirujjhamānagaṇanavasena ca gaṇanā veditabbā.

By non-root condition and by non-object condition, in dominance there are seven instances. Here, 'wholesome for unwholesome,' 'indeterminate for wholesome,' and 'for unwholesome'—these three instances, being obtainable by way of object-dominance, are contradicted. Why? Because it is stated, 'by non-object condition.' Therefore, having excluded those, it should be understood that here, by the method of conascent dominance alone, there are seven instances: 'wholesome for wholesome, for indeterminate, and for wholesome-and-indeterminate; unwholesome for unwholesome, for indeterminate, and for unwholesome-and-indeterminate; indeterminate for indeterminate.' These too, because of the statement 'by non-root condition,' are by way of the remaining dominances, having excluded the dominance of investigation. Thus, everywhere, the calculation should be understood by way of conditions with a lesser count and by way of non-conflicting counts.

Yesu ca paccayesu paccanīyato ṭhitesu ye anulomato na tiṭṭhanti, tepi veditabbā. Seyyathidaṃ – anantare paccanīyato ṭhite samanantarāsevananatthivigatā anulomato na tiṭṭhanti, sahajāte paccanīyato ṭhite hetuaññamaññavipākajhānamaggasampayuttā anulomato na tiṭṭhanti, nissaye paccanīyato ṭhite vatthupurejāto anulomato na tiṭṭhati. Āhāre vā indriye vā paccanīyato ṭhite hetuaññamaññavipākajhānamaggasampayuttā anulomato na tiṭṭhanti. Ārammaṇe pana paccanīyato ṭhite adhipatiupanissayā anulomato na tiṭṭhanti, ārammaṇādhipatiārammaṇūpanissayā pana na labbhanti. Iminā upāyena sabbattha yaṃ labbhati, yañca na labbhati, taṃ jānitvā labbhamānavasena vārā uddharitabbā.

And in those conditions where the counteractive stands, those that do not stand in the forward order should also be understood. For example—when in the immediacy condition the counteractive stands, the contiguity, repetition, absence, and disappearance conditions do not stand in the forward order; when in conascence the counteractive stands, the root, mutuality, result, jhāna, path, and association conditions do not stand in the forward order; when in dependence the counteractive stands, the base-prenascence condition does not stand in the forward order. When in nutriment or faculty the counteractive stands, the root, mutuality, result, jhāna, path, and association conditions do not stand in the forward order. But when in the object condition the counteractive stands, dominance and decisive support do not stand in the forward order, and object-dominance and object-decisive support are not obtained. By this method, everywhere, what is obtained and what is not obtained should be known, and the instances should be extracted based on what is obtainable.

Tattha sabbesupi timūlakādīsu anantare sattātiādayo dumūlake laddhavārāyeva sattamūlakādīsu pana nasahajātapaccayā nissaye tīṇīti purejātavasena vatthunissaye tīṇi. Kamme dve nānākkhaṇikavaseneva. Āhāre [M 0.0480] ekaṃ kabaḷīkārāhāravasena. Indriye ekaṃ rūpindriyavasena. Kamena gantvā vippayutte tīṇīti kusalādīnaṃ abyākatantāni pacchājātavasena. Atthiavigatesu pañcāti tāni ceva tīṇi, kusalābyākatā abyākatassa, akusalābyākatā abyākatassāti imāni ca dve pacchājātāhārindriyavasenāti. Pacchājātapaccayassa paccanīkabhāvato paṭṭhāya pana atthiavigatesu ekanti abyākato abyākatassa [V 0.0474] āhārindriyavasena. Nāhāre gahite naindriyapaccayāti na gahetabbaṃ. Tathā naindriye gahite nāhārapaccayāti. Kasmā? Dvīsu ekato gahitesu gaṇetabbavārassa abhāvato. Jhānamaggādīsupi paccanīkato ṭhitesu āhārato vā indriyato vā ekaṃ anulomaṃ akatvāva avasāne indriye ekaṃ, atthiyā ekaṃ, avigate ekaṃ, āhāre ekaṃ, atthiyā ekaṃ, avigate ekanti vuttaṃ. Sesamettha uttānatthamevāti.

Therein, in all cases of the three-rooted, etc., the seven instances in the contiguity condition, etc., are just those whose turns were obtained in the two-rooted. However, in the seven-rooted, etc., by non-conascence condition, in the dependence condition there are three by way of pre-nascence, that is, three in base-dependence. In kamma, there are two by way of the different-moment condition. For nutriment, one by way of physical nutriment. For faculty, one by way of material faculty. Proceeding in order, in the disassociation condition there are three—the wholesome, etc., ending with the indeterminate—by way of post-nascence. In presence and non-disappearance, there are five: those same three, plus these two—the wholesome-and-indeterminate for the indeterminate, and the unwholesome-and-indeterminate for the indeterminate—by way of post-nascent nutriment and faculty. However, starting from the counteractive state of the post-nascence condition, in presence and non-disappearance there is one: the indeterminate for the indeterminate by way of nutriment and faculty. When the condition is 'non-nutriment', the condition 'non-faculty' should not be included; likewise, when the condition is 'non-faculty', the condition 'non-nutriment' should not be included. Why? Because when the two are taken together, there is no instance to be counted. Also in jhāna, path, etc., when they stand in the counteractive, without making a single one forward from either nutriment or faculty, at the end it is said: in faculty one, in presence one, in non-disappearance one; in nutriment one, in presence one, in non-disappearance one. The rest here has a plain meaning.

Nahetumūlakaṃ.

The Non-Root Basis.

636. Nārammaṇamūlakādīsu naaññamaññamūlake naaññamaññapaccayā hetuyā tīṇīti kusalādīni cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ. Adhipatiyā aṭṭhāti adhipatiyā vuttesu dasasu “kusalo kusalābyākatassa, akusalo akusalābyākatassā”ti dve apanetvā sesāni aṭṭha. Sahajāte pañcāti hetuyā vuttehi tīhi saddhiṃ “kusalo ca abyākato ca abyākatassa, akusalo ca abyākato ca abyākatassā”ti ime dve. Nissaye sattāti tehi pañcahi saddhiṃ “abyākato kusalassa, abyākato akusalassā”ti ime dve vatthuvasena. Kamme tīṇīti hetuyā vuttāneva. Sesatikesupi eseva nayo. Adhipatiyā tīṇīti heṭṭhā vuttāneva.

636. In the non-object basis, etc., in the non-mutuality basis, by non-mutuality condition, there are three instances by root, namely the wholesome, etc., for mind-originated phenomena. In the case of dominance, there are eight: among the ten mentioned under dominance, excluding 'the wholesome for the wholesome-and-indeterminate' and 'the unwholesome for the unwholesome-and-indeterminate,' the remaining eight. In the case of conascence, there are five: the three mentioned under the root condition, along with these two, 'the wholesome and indeterminate for the indeterminate' and 'the unwholesome and indeterminate for the indeterminate.' In the case of dependence, there are seven: the five mentioned above, plus these two, 'the indeterminate for the wholesome' and 'the indeterminate for the unwholesome,' in terms of the base. In the case of kamma, there are three: the very same as those mentioned under the root condition. This same method applies to the remaining triads as well. In the case of dominance, there are three: the very same as those mentioned below.

644. Nāhāramūlake aññamaññe tīṇīti ṭhapetvā āhāre sesacetasikavasena veditabbāni. Yathā ca heṭṭhā, tathā idhāpi nāhāranaindriyesu ekekameva gahitaṃ, na dve ekato.

644. In the non-nutriment basis, there are three in the mutuality condition, which should be understood by way of the remaining mental factors, excluding nutriment. And just as below, so here too: in the non-nutriment and non-faculty conditions, only one is taken at a time, not two together.

648. Nasampayuttapaccayā [M 0.0481] hetuyā tīṇīti heṭṭhā naaññamaññe vuttāneva. Adhipatiyā aṭṭhāti vuttāneva. Navippayuttamūlake kamme pañcāti kusalādicetanā sahajātakusalādīnaṃ, nānākkhaṇikā kusalākusalacetanā kammasamuṭṭhānarūpassāti evaṃ pañca. Āhārindriyesu tīṇi sahajātasadisāni. Jhānamaggādīsu tīṇi hetusadisāni.

648. By non-association condition, there are three by root, just as stated below in the non-mutuality condition. For the dominance condition, eight—just as previously stated. In the non-disassociation basis, in kamma, there are five: wholesome and other volitions for conascent wholesome states and so on, and wholesome and unwholesome volitions occurring at different moments for kamma-originated matter—thus, five. In the case of nutriment and faculties, three—similar to the conascent. In the case of jhāna and path, three—similar to the roots.

650. Noatthimūlake yasmā hetu noatthi nāma na hoti, niyamato atthiyeva, tasmā taṃ aggahetvā nārammaṇe navāti vuttaṃ. Yathā ca hetu, tathā aññepi atthipaccayalakkhaṇayuttā ettha anulomato na tiṭṭhanti. Kamme dveti idaṃ pana nānākkhaṇikakammavasena vuttaṃ. Paccanīyato sabbe labbhanti. Yaṃ pana anulomato labbhamānampi aggahetvā tato puretarā paccayā paccanīyato gayhanti, so pacchā yojanaṃ labhati. Tenevettha “noatthipaccayā nahetupaccayā…pe… noavigatapaccayā kamme dve”ti vuttaṃ. Kasmā panesa sakaṭṭhāneyeva na gahitoti[V 0.0475]? Yasmā avasesesupi paccanīyato ṭhitesu ekova anulomato labbhati. Idañhi imasmiṃ paccayānulome lakkhaṇaṃ – yo sabbesu paccanīyato ṭhitesu ekova anulomato labbhati, so pacchā vuccatīti. Noatthipaccayā nohetupaccayā…pe… noavigatapaccayā upanissaye navāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Idaṃ pana pakatūpanissayavasena vuttaṃ. Iminā upāyena sabbattha labbhamānaṃ alabbhamānaṃ purevuttaṃ pacchāvuttañca veditabbanti.

650. In the section based on non-presence, because a root is not called 'non-presence' (for it is invariably present), therefore, not taking that, it is said, 'in non-object, nine.' Just as with a root, so also other factors endowed with the characteristic of the presence condition do not stand here in the positive order. 'In kamma, two'—this, however, is stated with regard to kamma arising in different moments. All are obtainable in the negative order. However, without taking that which is obtainable in the positive order, the earlier conditions are taken in the negative order, and it obtains its connection later. Therefore, here it is said: 'By the non-presence condition, by the non-root condition…pe… by the non-disappearance condition, in kamma, two.' But why is this not taken in its own place? Because even when the remaining factors are established in the negative order, only one is obtainable in the positive order. For this is the characteristic in this positive order of conditions: that which is obtainable in the positive order alone when all are established in the negative order, is spoken of later. 'By the non-presence condition, by the non-root condition…pe… by the non-disappearance condition, in decisive support, nine'—here too, the same method applies. This, however, is stated with regard to natural decisive support. By this method, what is obtainable everywhere, what is unobtainable, what was stated earlier, and what was stated later should be understood.

Pañhāvārassa paccanīyānulomavaṇṇanā.

The explanation of the negative-positive order in the Pañhāvāra.

Niṭṭhitā ca kusalattikapaṭṭhānassa vaṇṇanāti.

Thus ends the explanation of the Paṭṭhāna on the wholesome triad.

2. Vedanāttikavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Triad of Feelings

1. Vedanāttike tisso vedanā rūpaṃ nibbānanti ime dhammā na labbhanti, tasmā ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca dve khandhātiādi vuttaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe sukhāya vedanāyāti sahetukapaṭisandhivasena vuttaṃ. Dukkhavedanā paṭisandhiyaṃ na labbhatīti [M 0.0482] dutiyavāre paṭisandhiggahaṇaṃ na kataṃ. Tatiyavāre paṭisandhikkhaṇeti sahetukapaṭisandhivasena vuttaṃ. Sesamettha ito paresu ca paccayesu yathāpāḷimeva niyyāti. Sabbattha tayo tayo vārā vuttā. Tena vuttaṃ hetuyā tīṇi…pe… avigate tīṇīti.

1. In the triad of feelings, the three feelings, form, and Nibbāna—these phenomena are not obtainable; therefore, it is said, 'one aggregate depending on two aggregates,' and so on. 'At the moment of rebirth-linking, with pleasant feeling'—this is stated by way of rebirth-linking with roots. Painful feeling is not obtainable at rebirth-linking—thus, in the second instance, the mention of rebirth-linking is not made. In the third instance, 'at the moment of rebirth-linking'—this is stated by way of rebirth-linking with roots. The remainder here and in the subsequent conditions proceeds exactly as in the Pāli text. Everywhere, three instances each are stated. Therefore it is said: 'By root condition, three... pe... by non-disappearance condition, three.'

6. Paccayasaṃsandane pana sahetukāya vipākadukkhavedanāya abhāvato hetumūlakanaye vipāke dveti vuttaṃ. Adhipatiādīhi saddhiṃ saṃsandanesupi vipāke dveyeva. Kasmā? Vipāke dukkhavedanāya adhipatijhānamaggānaṃ abhāvato. Yehi ca saddhiṃ saṃsandane vipāke dve vārā labbhanti, vipākena saddhiṃ saṃsandane tesupi dveyeva.

6. In the connection of conditions, however, due to the absence of resultant painful feeling with roots, it is said, 'in the resultant, two' in the method based on root condition. Even when connecting with dominance and other conditions, there are still only two in the resultant. Why? Because for resultant painful feeling there is an absence of dominance, absorption, and path. And for those conditions with which, in connection, two instances in the resultant are obtained, when they are connected with the resultant condition, there are also only two.

10. Paccanīye napurejāte āruppe ca paṭisandhiyañca dukkhavedanāya abhāvato dve vārā āgatā. Navippayuttepi āruppe dukkhābhāvato dveyeva. Sabbaarūpadhammapariggāhakā pana sahajātādayo paccayā imasmiṃ paccanīyavāre parihāyanti. Kasmā? Vedanāsampayuttassa dhammassa vedanāsampayuttaṃ [V 0.0476] paṭicca sahajātādīhi vinā anuppattito pacchājātapaccayañca vināva uppattito.

10. In the negative section, in non-prenascence, in the formless realm, and at rebirth-linking, due to the absence of painful feeling, two instances are given. Even in non-dissociation, in the formless realm, due to the absence of pain, there are only two. However, the co-nascent and other conditions that encompass all immaterial phenomena are omitted in this negative section. Why? Because a phenomenon associated with feeling, conditioned by that which is associated with feeling, does not arise without co-nascent and other such conditions, and it arises even without the post-nascent condition.

17. Paccayasaṃsandane pana napurejāte ekanti āruppe paṭisandhiyañca ahetukādukkhamasukhavedanāsampayuttaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Nakamme dveti ahetukakiriyasampayuttacetanāvasena vuttaṃ. Sukhāya hi adukkhamasukhāya ca vedanāya sampayutte dhamme paṭicca tāhi vedanāhi sampayuttā ahetukakiriyacetanā uppajjanti. Nahetupaccayā navipākepi eseva nayo. Navippayutte ekanti āruppe āvajjanavasena vuttaṃ. Iminā upāyena sabbasaṃsandanesu gaṇanā veditabbā.

17. However, in the connection of conditions, 'one in non-prenascence' is stated with reference to that which is associated with rootless neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling at rebirth-linking in the formless realm. 'Two in non-kamma' is stated by way of volition associated with rootless functional consciousness. For rootless functional volitions associated with pleasant or neutral feeling arise conditioned by states associated with those feelings. The same method applies to non-root condition and non-resultant. 'One in non-dissociation' is stated by way of advertence in the formless realm. By this method, the enumeration in all connections should be understood.

25-37. Anulomapaccanīye paccanīye laddhapaccayā eva paccanīyato tiṭṭhanti. Paccanīyānulome sabbā rūpadhammapariggāhakā sahajātādayo anulomatova tiṭṭhanti, na paccanīyato. Ahetukassa pana cittuppādassa adhipati natthīti adhipatipaccayo anulomato na tiṭṭhati. Paṭiccavārādīsu pana pacchājāto anulomato na labbhatiyevāti parihīno. Ye cettha anulomato labbhanti, te paccanīyato labbhamānehi saddhiṃ parivattetvāpi [M 0.0483] yojitāyeva. Tesu tīṇi dve ekanti tayova vāraparicchedā, te sabbattha yathānurūpaṃ sallakkhetabbā. Yo cāyaṃ paṭiccavāre vutto, sahajātavārādīsupi ayameva vaṇṇanānayo.

25-37. In the positive-negative, the conditions obtained in the negative stand only as negative conditions. In the negative-positive, all those that encompass material phenomena, such as the co-nascent, etc., stand only as positive conditions, not as negative conditions. However, for a rootless thought-moment, there is no dominance, so the dominance condition does not stand as a positive condition. In the sections beginning with the Dependent Origination order, however, the post-nascent is not obtained as a positive condition at all, hence it is excluded. And those here that are obtainable as positive conditions are connected even when combined by alternation with those obtainable as negative conditions. Among these, there are only three delimitations of instances: three, two, or one; these are to be carefully considered appropriately everywhere. And this method of description that has been stated in the Dependent Origination order is the same in the sections beginning with the co-nascent order.

38. Pañhāvāre pana sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānanti tena saddhiṃ sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ tehiyeva vā hetūhi sukhavedanādīhi vā.

38. In the Pañhāvāra, 'of the associated aggregates' means of the aggregates associated with it, or with those very roots, or with pleasant feeling, etc.

39. Vippaṭisārissāti dānādīsu tāva “kasmā mayā idaṃ kataṃ, duṭṭhu me kataṃ, akataṃ seyyo siyā”ti evaṃ vippaṭisārissa. Jhānaparihāniyaṃ pana “parihīnaṃ me jhānaṃ, mahājāniyo vatamhī”ti evaṃ vippaṭisārissa. Moho uppajjatīti dosasampayuttamoho. Tathā mohaṃ arabbhāti dosasampayuttamohameva.

39. 'Of one who regrets' means, firstly, of one who, concerning giving etc., regrets thus: 'Why did I do this? I have done it badly. It would have been better if I had not done it.' But concerning the decline of jhāna, one regrets thus: 'My jhāna has declined; alas, I am a great loser!' 'Delusion arises' means delusion associated with aversion. Similarly, 'in relation to delusion' refers only to delusion associated with aversion.

45. Sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa bhavaṅgassāti tadārammaṇasaṅkhātaṃ piṭṭhibhavaṅgaṃ mūlabhavaṅgassa. Vuṭṭhānassāti tadārammaṇassa bhavaṅgassa vā. Ubhayampi [V 0.0477] hetaṃ kusalākusalajavanato vuṭṭhitattā vuṭṭhānanti vuccati. Kiriyaṃ vuṭṭhānassāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Phalaṃ vuṭṭhānassāti phalacittaṃ bhavaṅgassa. Bhavaṅgena hi phalato vuṭṭhito nāma hoti. Parato “vuṭṭhāna”nti āgataṭṭhānesupi eseva nayo.

45. The life-continuum associated with pleasant feeling for the life-continuum associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling: this refers to the subsequent life-continuum, designated as tadārammaṇa, for the root life-continuum. 'For emergence' refers either to the tadārammaṇa or to the bhavaṅga. Both are called 'emergence' because they have emerged from wholesome or unwholesome impulsions. 'For emergence which is functional'—here too the same method applies. 'For emergence which is fruition' means the fruition consciousness for the life-continuum. For one is said to have emerged from fruition by means of the life-continuum. The same method applies to instances where 'emergence' is mentioned further on.

46. Dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā khandhāti domanassasampayuttā akusalā khandhā. Adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa vuṭṭhānassāti tadārammaṇasaṅkhātassa āgantukabhavaṅgassa vā upekkhāsampayuttamūlabhavaṅgassa vā. Sace pana somanassasahagataṃ mūlabhavaṅgaṃ hoti, tadārammaṇassa ca uppattikāraṇaṃ na hoti, javanassa ārammaṇato aññasmimpi ārammaṇe adukkhamasukhavedanaṃ akusalavipākaṃ uppajjateva. Tampi hi javanato vuṭṭhitattā vuṭṭhānanti vuccati. Sahajātapaccayādiniddesā uttānatthāyeva. Nahettha kiñci atthi, yaṃ na sakkā siyā heṭṭhā vuttanayena vedetuṃ, tasmā sādhukaṃ upalakkhetabbaṃ.

46. 'Aggregates associated with painful feeling' means the unwholesome aggregates associated with displeasure. 'For emergence associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling' refers either to the adventitious life-continuum designated as tadārammaṇa, or to the root life-continuum associated with equanimity. If, however, the root life-continuum is accompanied by joy, and there is no cause for the arising of tadārammaṇa, then an unwholesome resultant consciousness with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises even in an object different from the object of the impulsion. That too is called 'emergence' because it has emerged from the impulsion. The exposition of the co-nascent condition and so on is of clear meaning. There is nothing here that cannot be understood by the method stated above; therefore, it should be carefully noted.

62. Idāni yasmiṃ yasmiṃ paccaye ye ye vārā laddhā, sabbe te saṅkhipitvā gaṇanāya dassetuṃ hetuyā tīṇītiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sabbāni tīṇi [M 0.0484] suddhānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ padānaṃ vasena veditabbāni. Ārammaṇe nava ekamūlakekāvasānāni. Adhipatiyā pañca sahajātādhipativasena amissāni tīṇi, ārammaṇādhipativasena ca “sukhāya sampayutto sukhāya sampayuttassa, adukkhamasukhāya sampayutto adukkhamasukhāya sampayuttassā”ti dve, tāni na gaṇetabbāni. Sukhāya pana sampayutto adukkhamasukhāya, adukkhamasukhāya sampayutto sukhāyāti imāni dve gaṇetabbānīti evaṃ pañca. Anantarasamanantaresu sattāti sukhā dvinnaṃ, tathā dukkhā, adukkhamasukhā tiṇṇampīti evaṃ satta. Upanissaye navāti sukhasampayutto sukhasampayuttassa tīhipi upanissayehi, dukkhasampayuttassa pakatūpanissayeneva, upekkhāsampayuttassa tīhipi, dukkhasampayutto dukkhasampayuttassa anantarapakatūpanissayehi, sukhasampayuttassa pakatūpanissayena, adukkhamasukhasampayuttassa dvidhā, adukkhamasukhasampayutto adukkhamasukhasampayuttassa tidhāpi, tathā sukhasampayuttassa, dukkhasampayuttassa anantarapakatūpanissayehīti evaṃ nava. Paccayabhedato panettha pakatūpanissayā nava, anantarūpanissayā satta, ārammaṇūpanissayā cattāroti vīsati upanissayā. Purejātapacchājātā panettha chijjanti. Na hi purejātā pacchājātā vā arūpadhammā arūpadhammānaṃ paccayā honti.

62. Now, to show the count by summarizing all the permutations obtained in each condition, it is said: 'In the root condition, three,' and so on. Herein, all three are to be understood by way of the three pure terms. In the object condition, there are nine, with one as the root and one as the conclusion. In the predominance condition, there are five: three unmixed by way of co-nascent predominance, and by way of object predominance, the two—'associated with pleasure for what is associated with pleasure,' and 'associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure for what is associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure'—are not to be counted. However, 'associated with pleasure for what is associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure,' and 'associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure for what is associated with pleasure'—these two are to be counted; thus there are five. In the contiguous and immediately contiguous conditions, there are seven: pleasure for two, likewise pain for two, and neither-pain-nor-pleasure for all three—thus seven. In the decisive support condition, there are nine: a state associated with pleasure is a condition for a state associated with pleasure by all three decisive supports; for one associated with pain, only by natural decisive support; for one associated with equanimity, by all three. A state associated with pain is a condition for a state associated with pain by immediate and natural decisive support; for one associated with pleasure, by natural decisive support; for one associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure, in two ways. A state associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure is a condition for a state associated with neither-pain-nor-pleasure in three ways, and likewise for one associated with pleasure; for one associated with pain, by immediate and natural decisive support—thus there are nine. Here, by way of the distinction of conditions, there are nine natural decisive supports, seven immediate decisive supports, and four object decisive supports, making twenty decisive supports. Pre-nascence and post-nascence are excluded here, for pre-nascent or post-nascent immaterial phenomena are not conditions for immaterial phenomena.

Kamme [V 0.0478] aṭṭhāti sukhasampayutto sukhasampayuttassa dvidhāpi, dukkhasampayuttassa nānākkhaṇikatova tathā itarassa. Dukkhasampayutto dukkhasampayuttassa dvidhāpi, sukhasampayuttassa natthi, itarassa nānākkhaṇikatova adukkhamasukhasampayutto adukkhamasukhasampayuttassa dvidhāpi, itaresaṃ nānākkhaṇikatoti evaṃ aṭṭha. Paccayabhedato panettha nānākkhaṇikā aṭṭha, sahajātā tīṇīti ekādasa kammapaccayā. Yathā ca purejātapacchājātā, evaṃ vippayuttapaccayopettha chijjati. Arūpadhammā hi arūpadhammānaṃ vippayuttapaccayo na honti. Natthivigatesu satta anantarasadisāva. Evamettha tīṇi pañca satta aṭṭha navāti pañca gaṇanaparicchedā. Tesaṃ vasena paccayasaṃsandane ūnataragaṇanena saddhiṃ saṃsandanesu atirekañca alabbhamānañca apanetvā gaṇanā veditabbā.

In the kamma condition, there are eight: a state associated with pleasure for a state associated with pleasure, in both ways; for one associated with pain, only by way of different moments, and likewise for the other. A state associated with pain for a state associated with pain, in both ways; for one associated with pleasure, it does not occur; for the other, only by way of different moments. A state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling for a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, in both ways; for the others, only by way of different moments—thus, eight. By way of the distinction of conditions, there are eight different-moment and three co-nascent, thus eleven kamma conditions. And just as pre-nascence and post-nascence, so too the dissociation condition is excluded here. For immaterial phenomena are not a dissociation condition for immaterial phenomena. In the absence and disappearance conditions, the seven are just like in the contiguous condition. Thus, here there are three, five, seven, eight, and nine—five numerical divisions. Based on these, in the combination of conditions, the count should be understood by removing what is excessive and what is unobtainable in the combinations with a lesser number.

63-64. Hetuyā [M 0.0485] saddhiṃ ārammaṇaṃ na labbhati, tathā anantarādayo. Adhipatiyā dveti dukkhapadaṃ ṭhapetvā sesāni dve. Dukkhasampayutto hi hetu adhipati nāma natthi, tasmā so na labbhatīti apanīto. Sesadvayesupi eseva nayo. Iti hetumūlake dveyeva gaṇanaparicchedā, tesaṃ vasena cha ghaṭanāni vuttāni. Tesu paṭhamaṃ avipākabhūtānaṃ ñāṇavippayuttanirādhipatidhammānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ, dutiyaṃ tesaññeva vipākabhūtānaṃ, tatiyacatutthāni tesaññeva ñāṇasampayuttānaṃ, pañcamaṃ avipākabhūtasādhipatiamohavasena, chaṭṭhaṃ vipākabhūtasādhipatiamohavasena. Paṭhamaṃ vā sabbahetuvasena, dutiyaṃ sabbavipākahetuvasena, tatiyaṃ sabbāmohahetuvasena, catutthaṃ sabbavipākāmohahetuvasena. Pañcamaṃ sabbasādhipatiamohavasena, chaṭṭhaṃ sabbasādhipativipākāmohavasena.

63-64. With the root condition, the object condition is not obtained, and likewise the contiguous condition and others. In the predominance condition, there are two: setting aside the term associated with pain, there are the remaining two. For a root associated with pain is not a predominance factor; therefore, it is not obtained and is removed. The same method applies to the remaining two. Thus, in the section rooted in the hetu condition, there are only two numerical divisions, and based on these, six combinations are stated. Among them, the first is stated by way of non-resultant, knowledge-dissociated phenomena without predominance; the second, by way of those same resultant phenomena; the third and fourth, by way of those same knowledge-associated phenomena; the fifth, by way of non-resultant phenomena with predominance and non-delusion; the sixth, by way of resultant phenomena with predominance and non-delusion. Alternatively, the first is by way of all roots; the second, by way of all resultant roots; the third, by way of all non-delusion roots; the fourth, by way of all resultant non-delusion roots; the fifth, by way of all roots with predominance and non-delusion; the sixth, by way of all resultant roots with predominance and non-delusion.

66. Ārammaṇamūlake adhipatiyā cattārīti ārammaṇādhipativasena sukhaṃ sukhassa, adukkhamasukhassa, adukkhamasukhaṃ adukkhamasukhassa, sukhassāti evaṃ cattāri. Upanissayepi ārammaṇūpanissayavasena cattāro vuttā. Ghaṭanāni panettha ekameva. Adhipatimūlakādīsupi heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva yaṃ labbhati yañca na labbhati, taṃ sabbaṃ sādhukaṃ sallakkhetvā saṃsandanaghaṭanagaṇanā veditabbā.

66. In the object-based section, four are stated for the predominance condition by way of object predominance: pleasant feeling for pleasant feeling, pleasant feeling for neutral feeling, neutral feeling for neutral feeling, and neutral feeling for pleasant feeling—thus four. In the decisive support condition also, four are stated by way of object decisive support. Here, there is only one combination. In the sections based on the predominance condition and others, whatever is obtained and whatever is not obtained should be carefully noted according to the method stated earlier, and the calculation of combinations and connections should be understood accordingly.

83-87. Paccanīyamhi kusalattike vuttanayeneva anulomato paccaye uddharitvā tattha laddhānaṃ vārānaṃ vasena paccanīyato gaṇanavasena nahetuyā navāti sabbapaccayesu nava vārā dassitā[V 0.0479]. Te ekamūlakekāvasānānaṃ navannaṃ vissajjanānaṃ vasena “sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttassa dhammassa nahetupaccayena paccayo, sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttena cittena dānaṃ datvā”tiādinā nayena pāḷiṃ uddharitvā dassetabbā. Paccayasaṃsandane panettha nahetupaccayā…pe… naupanissaye aṭṭhāti nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayavasena veditabbā. Dubbalakammañhi vipākassa na upanissayo hoti. Kevalaṃ pana nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayeneva paccayo hoti. Sesamettha anulomapaccanīyapaccanīyānulomesu ca tesaṃ tesaṃ paccayānaṃ yoge laddhavāravasena sakkā heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva gaṇetuṃ, tasmā na vitthāritanti.

83-87. In the negative section, in accordance with the method stated in the triad of wholesome states, having extracted the conditions from the affirmative order, and based on the instances obtained therein, by way of negative enumeration, nine instances are shown for the non-root condition among all conditions. These should be demonstrated by way of the nine explanations for the single-root, single-ending questions, by extracting the Pāli in the manner of: “A phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling is a condition for a phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling by the non-root condition; having given a gift with a mind associated with pleasant feeling,” and so on. In the combination of conditions here, from the non-root condition… up to… non-decisive support, eight instances are to be understood by way of the kamma condition occurring at different moments. For feeble kamma is not a decisive support for its result; it is a condition only by way of the kamma condition occurring at different moments. The rest here, in the affirmative-negative and negative-affirmative, for the application of each of those conditions, it is possible to enumerate based on the instances obtained, according to the method stated earlier. Therefore, it is not elaborated.

Vedanāttikavaṇṇanā.

The Exposition on the Triad of Feeling.

3. Vipākattikavaṇṇanā

3. The Exposition on the Triad of Result.

1-23. Vipākattike [M 0.0486] vipākaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca vipāko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayāti ye hetupaccaye terasa vārā vuttā, te saṅkhipitvā gaṇanāya dassetuṃ hetuyā terasāti vuttaṃ. Ārammaṇe pañcātiādīsupi eseva nayo. Evamettha terasa pañca nava satta tīṇi dveti cha gaṇanaparicchedā, tesaṃ vasena paccayasaṃsandane heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva gaṇanā veditabbā.

1-23. In the triad of result, a resultant phenomenon arises dependent on a resultant phenomenon by the root condition—the thirteen instances stated for the root condition are summarized and stated as 'thirteen for the root condition' to show the enumeration. The same method applies to 'for the object condition, five,' and so on. Thus, in this case, there are six numerical sections: thirteen, five, nine, seven, three, and two. Based on these, the enumeration in the combination of conditions should be understood in the same way as stated earlier.

24-52. Paccanīyepi vipākaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca vipāko dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayāti ye nahetupaccaye dasa vārā vuttā, te saṅkhipitvā gaṇanāya dassetuṃ nahetuyā dasāti vuttaṃ. Na ārammaṇe pañcātiādīsupi eseva nayo.
