Evamettha dasa pañca terasa dvādasa dve ekaṃ nava tīṇīti aṭṭha gaṇanaparicchedā, tesaṃ vasena paccayasaṃsandane heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva vitthārato gaṇanā veditabbā. Pāḷi pana saṅkhittā, etesaññeva pana laddhagaṇanaraparicchedānaṃ vārānaṃ vasena saṃsanditvā anulomapaccanīyaṃ paccanīyānulomañca veditabbaṃ.

24-52. In the negative section also, a resultant phenomenon arises dependent on a resultant phenomenon by the non-root condition. The ten instances stated for the non-root condition are summarized and stated as 'ten for the non-root condition' to show the enumeration. The same method applies to 'for the non-object condition, five,' and so on. Thus, in this context, there are eight sections of enumeration: ten, five, thirteen, twelve, two, one, nine, and three. Based on these, the detailed enumeration in the combination of conditions should be understood in the manner explained earlier. The Pāli, however, is concise; but by combining these obtained numerical sections by way of instances, both the affirmative-negative and negative-affirmative should be understood.

Sahajātavāro [V 0.0480] imināva ekagatiko. Paccayanissayasaṃsaṭṭhasampayuttavārā yathāpāḷimeva niyyanti.

The co-nascence section proceeds in this very same way. The sections on condition, dependence, connection, and association proceed according to the Pāli itself.

92. Pañhāvāre kusalākusale niruddheti etasmiṃ vipassanāvasena pavatte kusale sārajjanādivasena pavatte akusale ca niruddhe. Vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjatīti kāmāvacaravipāko tadārammaṇatāya uppajjati. Ye pana “vipassanājavanānaṃ vicikicchuddhaccānañca pariyosāne tadārammaṇaṃ natthī”ti vadanti, te imāya tantiyā paṭisedhetabbā. Ākāsānañcāyatanakusalaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa kiriyassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayoti arahattaṃ patvā asamāpannapubbā samāpattiyo paṭilomato samāpajjantassa vasenetaṃ vuttaṃ. Iminā upāyena sabbavissajjanesu sādhukaṃ pāḷiṃ upaparikkhitvā attho veditabbo.

92. In the section on questions, 'when wholesome and unwholesome states have ceased' means when wholesome states occurring by way of insight have ceased, and when unwholesome states occurring by way of attachment and so forth have ceased. The resultant state arises as a 'taking that as its object'; thus, a sensual-sphere resultant state arises by way of taking that as its object. But those who say, “There is no tadārammaṇa at the conclusion of insight impulsion processes, or of doubt and agitation,” should be refuted by this text. The wholesome state of the base of infinite space is a condition for the functional consciousness of the base of infinite consciousness by way of the object condition; this is said with reference to one who, having attained arahantship, enters into the attainments in reverse order, not having previously entered them. By this method, one should carefully examine the Pāli in all the explanations and understand the meaning.

120. Hetuyā satta, ārammaṇe nava, adhipatiyā dasātiādīsupi sahajātādhipativasena ārammaṇādhipativasena sahajātanissayavasena purejātanissayavasena anantarūpanissayavasena ārammaṇūpanissayavasena [M 0.0487] pakatūpanissayavasena sahajātavippayuttavasena purejātapacchājātavippayuttavasenāti yattha yattha yathā yathā yattakāni vissajjanāni labbhanti, tattha tattha tathā tathā tāni sabbāni sallakkhetabbāni. Tathā paccanīyādīsu anulomavasena vāruddharaṇaṃ, anulomato laddhavārānaṃ paccanīyato gaṇanā, paccayasaṃsandanaṃ, anulomapaccanīye paccanīyānulome ca suddhikesu ceva saṃsandanavasena ca pavattesu hetumūlakādīsu labbhamānavāragaṇanā, alabbhamānānaṃ alabbhamānatāti sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

120. For the root condition, seven; for the object condition, nine; for the predominance condition, ten, and so forth—in all these cases, all the explanations should be carefully noted wherever and however many are obtainable, whether by way of co-nascence predominance, object predominance, co-nascence support, pre-nascence support, contiguity support, object decisive support, natural decisive support, co-nascence dissociation, or pre-nascence and post-nascence dissociation. Similarly, in the negative sections and so on, the extraction of instances in the affirmative order, the enumeration from the negative order of the instances obtained from the affirmative order, the combinations of conditions, the enumeration of instances obtainable in the root-based sections and so forth—occurring in the affirmative-negative and negative-affirmative, both in the pure cases and by way of combination—and the non-obtainability of what is not obtainable: all this should be understood in the manner explained earlier.

Yathā cettha, evaṃ ito paresupi tikadukesu. Paṭṭhānapakaraṇañhi pāḷitova anantaṃ aparimāṇaṃ. Tassa padapaṭipāṭiyā atthaṃ vaṇṇayissāmīti paṭipannassa atidīghāyukassāpi āyu nappahoti. Na cassa ekadesaṃ vaṇṇetvā sesamhi nayato dassiyamāne na sakkā attho jānituṃ, tasmā ito paraṃ ettakampi avatvā sesesu tikadukesu heṭṭhā avuttappakārattā yaṃ yaṃ avassaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ tadeva vakkhāma. Yaṃ pana avatvā gamissāma, taṃ pāḷinayeneva veditabbanti.

As it is here, so too in the remaining triads and dyads. For the Book of Conditional Relations in Pāli is indeed endless and immeasurable. For one who undertakes to explain its meaning following the sequence of the words, even a very long life would not suffice. Nor is it possible to understand its meaning by explaining a portion and indicating the method for the remainder. Therefore, from now on, without saying even this much, we will speak only of what is absolutely necessary in the remaining triads and dyads, because the manner has not been stated earlier. Whatever we pass over without saying should be understood according to the method of the Pāli.

Vipākattikavaṇṇanā.

The Exposition on the Triad of Result.

4. Upādinnattikavaṇṇanā

4. The Exposition on the Clung-to Triad.

51. Upādinnupādāniyattikassa [V 0.0481] pañhāvāre vatthu upādāniyānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayoti pavattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Paṭisandhiyaṃ pana taṃ purejātaṃ na hoti.

51. In the Question Section of the Triad of the Apprehended and Apprehendable, the statement that the physical basis is a condition for the apprehendable aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition is made with reference to the course of existence. At rebirth-linking, however, that is not pre-nascent.

72. Upādinnupādāniyo kabaḷīkāro āhāro upādinnupādāniyassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayoti ettha upādinnupādāniyo kabaḷīkārāhāro nāma kammasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ abbhantaragatā ojā. Upādinnupādāniyassa kāyassāti tasseva kammasamuṭṭhānarūpakāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ viya kaṭattārūpānaṃ anupālanaupatthambhanavasena paccayo, na janakavasena. Yaṃ pana maṇḍūkādayo gilitvā ṭhitānaṃ ahiādīnaṃ kāyassa jīvamānakamaṇḍūkādisarīre ojā āhārapaccayena [M 0.0488] paccayoti vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Na hi jīvamānakasarīre ojā aññassa sarīrassa āhārapaccayataṃ sādheti. Anupādinnupādāniyassa kāyassāti ettha pana janakavasenāpi labbhati. Upādinnupādāniyassa ca anupādinnupādāniyassa cāti ettha ekassa upatthambhakavasena, ekassa janakavasena, ubhinnampi vā upatthambhakavaseneva vutto. Dve pana āhārā ekato paccayā hontā upatthambhakāva honti, na janakā. Sesamettha pāḷimeva sādhukaṃ oloketvā veditabbaṃ.

72. The apprehended and apprehendable physical nutriment is a condition for the apprehended and apprehendable body by way of nutriment condition. Here, the apprehended and apprehendable physical nutriment refers to the nutritive essence contained within kamma-originated matter. The apprehended and apprehendable body means that same kamma-originated material body. It is a condition by way of nutriment condition in the sense of maintaining and supporting, like the life faculty of matter for kamma-born matter, not by way of generating. Some say that the nutritive essence in the bodies of living frogs, etc., that have been swallowed and remain in the bodies of snakes, etc., is a condition for the bodies of the snakes, etc., by way of nutriment condition; this should not be accepted. For the nutritive essence in a living body does not establish the state of being a nutriment condition for another body. But in the case of the non-apprehended and apprehendable body, it is also obtained by way of generating. In the case of both the apprehended and apprehendable and the non-apprehended and apprehendable, for one it is stated by way of supporting, for the other by way of generating, or for both only by way of supporting. But when two nutriments are conditions together, they are only supporting, not generating. The rest here should be understood by carefully examining the Pāli text itself.

Upādinnattikavaṇṇanā.

Exposition of the Triad of the Apprehended.

5-22. Saṅkiliṭṭhattikādivaṇṇanā

5-22. Exposition of the Triads Beginning with the Defiled.

Saṅkiliṭṭhasaṅkilesikattike sabbaṃ kusalattike vuttanayānusāreneva veditabbaṃ.

In the Triad of the Defiled and Defiling, everything should be understood in accordance with the method stated in the Triad of the Wholesome.

79. Vitakkattike yathākammūpagañāṇassa parikammanti dibbacakkhuparikammameva tassa uppādanatthāya [V 0.0482] parikammaṃ. Uppannassa pana vaḷañjanakāle parikammaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Sesamettha yathāpāḷimeva niyyāti.

79. In the Triad of Thought, the preparatory work for the knowledge of conformity with kamma is the preparatory work for the divine eye, which is for the purpose of its production. But this is stated with reference to the preparatory work at the time of its application once it has arisen. The rest here proceeds exactly as in the Pāli text.

82. Ti tadārammaṇabhavaṅgamūlabhavaṅgānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Sesamettha sabbaṃ pāḷivaseneva veditabbaṃ.

82. This is stated in terms of the registering life-continuum and the root life-continuum. The rest here should all be understood as in the Pāli text.

Dassanattike dassanena pahātabbo rāgo uppajjatītiādīsu dassanena pahātabbo puthujjanassa uppajjati. Bhāvanāya pahātabbo sotāpannassāpīti evaṃ uparimassa uparimassa heṭṭhimā heṭṭhimā nuppajjantīti veditabbā. Dassanena pahātabbo dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbassa dhammassa ekenapi paccayena paccayo na hoti. Sesamettha pāḷiṃ anugantvā kusalattike vuttalakkhaṇavaseneva veditabbaṃ.

In the Triad of Seeing, regarding 'the lust to be abandoned by seeing arises,' and so on—the lust to be abandoned by seeing arises in an ordinary person. That to be abandoned by development arises even in a stream-enterer. Thus, it should be understood that the lower defilements do not arise in the higher stages. A phenomenon to be abandoned by seeing is not a condition by even a single condition for a phenomenon to be abandoned by development. The rest here should be understood by following the Pāli text and in accordance with the characteristics stated in the Triad of the Wholesome.

Dassanenapahātabbahetukattike dassanenapahātabbahetukādīnaṃ vibhāgo aṭṭhakathākaṇḍe vuttanayeneva veditabbo. Vicikicchuddhaccasahagato moho ahetukattā tatiyapade paviṭṭho. Evamettha yesaṃ [M 0.0489] dassanabhāvanāhi pahātabbo hetu atthi, te pahātabbahetukā. Yesaṃ so natthi te nevadassanena nabhāvanāyapahātabbahetukāti imaṃ pahātabbahetukavibhāgaṃ ñatvā sesaṃ dassanenapahātabbattike ceva kusalattike ca dassitalakkhaṇānusāreneva veditabbaṃ.

In the Triad of Roots to be Abandoned by Seeing, the classification of roots to be abandoned by seeing, etc., should be understood in accordance with the method stated in the commentary section. The delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is included in the third category because it is rootless. Thus, here, those that have a root to be abandoned by seeing or development are 'those with a root to be abandoned.' Those that do not have that are 'those with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development.' Having understood this classification of roots to be abandoned, the rest should be understood in accordance with the characteristics indicated in the Triad of What is to be Abandoned by Seeing and in the Triad of the Wholesome.

Ācayagāmittike ca paṭiccavārasaṃsaṭṭhavāresu anulomaṃ kusalattikasadisameva. Sesaṃ vissajjanato gaṇanato ca yathāpāḷimeva niyyāti.

In the Triad of Leading to Accumulation, the Dependent Origination Section and the Association Section are similar to the Triad of the Wholesome in the forward order. The rest proceeds exactly as in the Pāli text, both in terms of explanation and enumeration.

Sekkhattike asekkho dhammo sekkhassa dhammassa na kenaci paccayena paccayo. Sekkho asekkhassa anantarapakatūpanissayo pana hoti. Sesamettha yathāpāḷimeva niyyāti, tathā parittattike.

In the Triad of the Trainee, the untrainee state is not a condition for the trainee state by any condition. The trainee state, however, can be an immediately proximate decisive support for the untrainee state. The remainder here follows the wording of the Pāli text, and so also in the Triad of the Limited.

Parittārammaṇattike appamāṇārammaṇācetanāti sekkhānaṃ gotrabhucetanā, paccavekkhaṇacetanātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Vipākānaṃ parittārammaṇānanti paṭisandhiyaṃ kammaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā, pavatte cakkhuviññāṇādivasenarūpādiārammaṇaṃ, tadārammaṇavasena javanena gahitaparittārammaṇañca [V 0.0483] ārammaṇaṃ katvā uppannānaṃ. Ye pana “gotrabhucittena natthi paṭisandhī”ti vadanti, te iminā suttena paṭisedhetabbā. Sesamettha pāḷinayeneva veditabbaṃ. Hīnattiko saṅkiliṭṭhattikasadiso.

In the Triad of Limited Object, 'volition with an immeasurable object' refers to the change-of-lineage volition of the trainees; it is also proper to say 'reviewing volition.' For resultant states with limited objects: at rebirth-linking, kamma is made the object; and in the course of existence, for those that have arisen, forms and other objects are objects by way of eye-consciousness, etc., and the limited object grasped by impulsion (javana) is also made an object by way of registering. Those who say, 'There is no rebirth-linking with change-of-lineage consciousness,' should be refuted by this discourse. The rest here should be understood according to the method of the Pāli text. The Triad of the Inferior is similar to the Triad of the Defiled.

Micchattattike micchattaniyato sammattaniyatassa, sammattaniyato vā micchattaniyatassa kenaci paccayena paccayo na hoti. Micchattaniyato vā sammattaniyato vā sahajātādhipatirahito nāma natthi. Sammattaniyate ekantato ārammaṇapurejātaṃ natthi, micchattaniyate siyā ārammaṇapurejātaṃ. Aniyataṃ cittaṃ ārabbha niyatā micchādiṭṭhi uppajjeyya. Sesā niyataṃ ārabbha niyataṃ nuppajjati, micchattaniyataṃ garuṃ katvā na koci dhammo uppajjati. Kusalo micchattassa upanissayapaccayo na hoti. Sesamettha pāḷiyaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

In the Triad of Wrongness, the fixed in wrongness is not a condition for the fixed in rightness, nor is the fixed in rightness a condition for the fixed in wrongness by any condition. There is no state fixed in wrongness or fixed in rightness that is devoid of co-nascent dominance. In the state fixed in rightness, there is absolutely no object-prenascence, but in the state fixed in wrongness, there may be object-prenascence. A fixed wrong view may arise with reference to an undetermined mind. Other fixed states do not arise with reference to fixed states; no state arises having made the fixed in wrongness weighty. The wholesome is not a decisive support condition for wrongness. The remainder should be understood here as stated in the Pāli text.

Maggārammaṇattike paṭiccavārassa anulome vipākapaccayo natthi. Kammapaccayepi imasmiṃ tike nānākkhaṇikaṃ na labbhati, tathā uppannattikaatītattikesu. Paccanīye ahetukaṃ maggārammaṇanti ahetukaṃ maggārammaṇaṃ, āvajjanaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Sesamettha pāḷianusāreneva veditabbaṃ.

In the Triad of Path-Object, in the forward order of the Dependent Origination Section, there is no resultant condition. Also, in this triad, kamma condition across different moments is not found, nor in the Triad of the Arisen and the Triad of the Past. In the reverse order, 'rootless path-object' refers to rootless adverting. The rest here should be understood according to the Pāli text.

Uppannattike [M 0.0490] ca atītattike ca paṭiccavārādayo natthi, pañhāvāramattameva labbhati. Kasmā? Paṭiccavārādayo hi sahajātapurejātānaññeva honti. Ime ca tikā atītānāgatamissakā. Uppannattike cettha anantarabhāgiyāpi paccayā na labbhanti. Kasmā? Uppannattike atītassa abhāvato. Uppanno ca anuppanno cāti ime cettha dve dhammā uppannassa ca anuppannassa cāti imesaṃ dvinnaṃ na kenaci paccayena paccayo. Anuppanno ca uppādī cāti ime pana dve uppannassa ārammaṇūpanissayavasena dvīhi paccayehi paccayo. Sesamettha pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

In the Triad of the Arisen and the Triad of the Past, the Dependent Section, etc., do not occur; only the Question Section is found. Why? Because the Dependent Section, etc., apply only to conascence and prenascence conditions. And these triads are a mixture of past and future. In the Triad of the Arisen, even contiguity-group conditions are not found. Why? Because in the Triad of the Arisen, the past is absent. Here, these two states—arisen and unarisen—are not a condition for these two by any condition. However, these two—the unarisen and the arising—are a condition for the arisen by two conditions: object and decisive support. The rest here should be understood according to the method stated in the Pāli text.

Atītattike paccuppannaṃ atītānāgatassa, atītānāgatañca atītānāgatassa na kenaci paccayena paccayo. Nibbānaṃ pana dvīsupi imesu tikesu neva paccayato na paccayuppannato labbhati. Sesamidhāpi pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

In the Triad of the Past, the present is not a condition for the past and future by any condition; and the past and future are not a condition for the past and future by any condition. Nibbāna, however, is not found as either a condition or a conditioned state in these two triads. The rest here should also be understood according to the method stated in the Pāli text.

Ajjhattattike [V 0.0484] ajjhattabahiddhāpadaṃ na gahitaṃ. Ajjhattabahiddhāsaṅkhātā hi ubho rāsayo neva ekato paccayā honti, na paccayuppannā; tasmā hatthatale ṭhapitassa sāsapassa vaṇṇopi hatthatalavaṇṇena saddhiṃ ekato ārammaṇaṃ na hotīti veditabbo. Yathā ca ajjhattabahiddhāpadaṃ, evamettha ajjhattārammaṇattikepi ajjhattabahiddhārammaṇapadaṃ na labbhati. Sesaṃ yathāpāḷimeva niyyāti.

In the Triad of the Internal, the category of 'internal and external' is not taken. For the two aggregates designated as internal and external are neither conditions together nor conditioned states; therefore, it should be understood that even the color of a mustard seed placed on the palm of the hand does not become a single object together with the color of the palm. Just as with the category of 'internal and external', so too in the Triad of Internal Objects, the category of 'internal and external objects' is not found. The rest follows as in the Pāli text.

Sanidassanattikepi pāḷivaseneva attho gahetabbo. Gaṇanāpettha pāḷiyaṃ āgatavāre saṅkhipitvā heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva saṃsandanesu saṃsanditvā veditabbāti.

In the Triad of the Visible also, the meaning should be taken as in the Pāli text itself. The enumeration here, too, should be understood by condensing the sections that occur in the Pāli and collating them with the comparisons according to the method stated below.

Dhammānulome tikapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

The Exposition of the Triad-Paṭṭhāna in the Dhammānuloma.

2. Dukapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

2. The Exposition of the Dyad-Paṭṭhāna

Dukapaṭṭhānepi sabbadukesu pañhāvissajjanāni ceva gaṇanā ca pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayeneva veditabbā. Apicettha sahetukahetusampayuttadukānaṃ vissajjanaṃ hetudukavissajjanasadisaṃ; tathā hetūcevasahetukahetūcevahetusampayuttadukānaṃ, tathā sappaccayasaṅkhatadukānaṃ. Idaṃ dukaṃ yathā sappaccayadukaṃ, evaṃ kātabbanti idaṃ yasmā sappaccayo viya appaccayena [M 0.0491] saṅkhatopi, asaṅkhatena saddhiṃ yojanaṃ na labbhati, tasmā vuttaṃ. Sārammaṇacittasampayuttasaṃsaṭṭhadukāpi sadisavissajjanāyeva; tathā āsavaoghayogagocchakā. Ete hi tayo aññamaññaṃ sadisavissajjanāyeva. Apica lokiyasāsavasaṃyojaniyaganthaniyanīvaraṇiyaparāmaṭṭhasaṅkilesikadukā āsavavippayuttasāsavasaṃyojanavippayuttasaṃyojaniyaganthavippayuttaganthaniyanīvaraṇavippayuttanīvaraṇiyaparāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhakilesavippayuttasaṅkilesikapariyāpannasauttaradukāta imepi dukā samānā.

In the Dyad-Paṭṭhāna, both the answers to the questions and the enumeration in all dyads should be understood according to the method given in the Pāli text. Moreover, here, the answers for the dyads of 'with root' (sahetuka) and 'conjoined with root' (hetusampayutta) are similar to the answers for the 'root dyad' (hetuduka); likewise for the dyads of 'root and with root' (hetūcevasahetuka) and 'root and conjoined with root' (hetūcevahetusampayutta), and similarly for the dyads of 'with condition' (sappaccaya) and 'conditioned' (saṅkhata). The 'conditioned' dyad is to be treated like the 'with condition' dyad; this is stated because for the 'conditioned' term, association with the 'unconditioned' term is not found. The dyads of 'with object' (sārammaṇa), 'conjoined with consciousness' (cittasampayutta), and 'associated' (saṃsaṭṭha) also have similar answers; likewise for the groups of taints (āsava), floods (ogha), and yokes (yoga). These three indeed have mutually similar answers. Furthermore, the worldly dyads of 'with taints' (sāsava), 'pertaining to fetters' (saṃyojaniya), 'pertaining to ties' (ganthaniya), 'pertaining to hindrances' (nīvaraṇiya), 'grasped at' (parāmaṭṭha), and 'defiling' (saṅkilesika) are similar to the dyads of 'disjoined from taints' (āsavavippayutta), 'disjoined from fetters' (saṃyojanavippayutta), 'disjoined from ties' (ganthavippayutta), 'disjoined from hindrances' (nīvaraṇavippayutta), 'disjoined from grasping' (parāmāsavippayutta), 'disjoined from defilements' (kilesavippayutta), 'included under the defiling' (saṅkilesikapariyāpanna), and 'with a superior' (sauttara). These dyads too are alike.

Kilesadukaṃ saṃyojanadukasadisaṃ. Saṅkiliṭṭhakilesasampayuttanīvaraṇasampayuttadassanenapahātabbasaraṇadukāpi samānā. Tathākilesā ceva saṅkiliṭṭhanīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttakilesā ceva kilesasampayuttadukā. Iminā nayena sabbesaṃ atthato sadisānaṃ dukānaṃ [V 0.0485] vissajjanāni sadisāneva hontīti veditabbāni. Sabbasmimpi pana paṭṭhāne kenaciviññeyyadukaṃ na labbhati. Āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca, saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca, ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca, nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca, kilesā ceva saṅkiliṭṭhā cāti evarūpesu dukesu vipākapaccayo ceva nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayo ca na labbhati. Nahetusahetukanahetuahetukesu hetupaccayo natthi. Hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca, āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca, ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā cāti imesu dukesu nahetunajhānanamaggā na labbhanti. Saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca, nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca, kilesā ceva kilesasampayuttā ca, kilesā ceva saṅkiliṭṭhā cāti imesu pana vicikicchuddhaccasahagatassa mohassa vasena nahetupaccayo labbhati; najhānanamaggapaccayā na labbhantīti evaṃ sabbadukesu labbhamānālabbhamānaṃ upaparikkhitvā pāḷivaseneva vāragaṇanā veditabbāti.

The 'defilement dyad' (kilesaduka) is similar to the 'fetter dyad' (saṃyojanaduka). The dyads of 'defiled' (saṅkiliṭṭha), 'conjoined with defilements' (kilesasampayutta), 'conjoined with hindrances' (nīvaraṇasampayutta), 'to be abandoned by vision' (dassanenapahātabba), and 'with a cause' (saraṇa) are also similar. Likewise, the dyads of 'defilements and defiled' (kilesā ceva saṅkiliṭṭhā ca), 'defiled and hindrances' (saṅkiliṭṭhanīvaraṇā), 'hindrances and conjoined with defilements' (nīvaraṇasampayuttakilesā), and 'conjoined with defilements' (kilesasampayutta) are also similar. In this way, it should be understood that the answers for all dyads that are similar in meaning are indeed similar. However, in the entire Paṭṭhāna, the dyad 'cognizable by some means' (kenaciviññeyya) is not found. In such dyads as 'taints and conjoined with taints' (āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca), 'fetters and conjoined with fetters' (saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca), 'ties and conjoined with ties' (ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca), 'hindrances and conjoined with hindrances' (nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca), and 'defilements and defiled' (kilesā ceva saṅkiliṭṭhā ca), the resultance condition (vipākapaccaya) and the different-moment kamma condition (nānākkhaṇikakammapaccaya) are not found. In the dyads of 'not-root and with root' (nahetusahetuka) and 'not-root and without root' (nahetuahetuka), the root condition (hetupaccaya) does not exist. In these dyads—'roots and conjoined with roots' (hetū ceva hetusampayuttā ca), 'taints and conjoined with taints' (āsavā ceva āsavasampayuttā ca), and 'ties and conjoined with ties' (ganthā ceva ganthasampayuttā ca)—the Not-Root, Not-Jhāna, and Not-Path conditions are not found. But in these dyads—'fetters and conjoined with fetters' (saṃyojanā ceva saṃyojanasampayuttā ca), 'hindrances and conjoined with hindrances' (nīvaraṇā ceva nīvaraṇasampayuttā ca), 'defilements and conjoined with defilements' (kilesā ceva kilesasampayuttā ca), and 'defilements and defiled' (kilesā ceva saṅkiliṭṭhā ca)—the Not-Root condition is found, on account of delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness; but the Not-Jhāna and Not-Path conditions are not found. Thus, having examined what is found and what is not found in all dyads, the enumeration of sections should be understood according to the Pāli text itself.

Dukapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

The Exposition of the Dyad-Paṭṭhāna.

3. Dukatikapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

3. The Exposition of the Dyad-Triad Paṭṭhāna

Dukatikapaṭṭhāne hetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetu kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayāti evaṃ pañhāmattuddhāravaseneva saṅkhepato desanā [M 0.0492] katā. “Kusalaṃ alobhaṃ paṭicca adoso amoho”tiādinā pana nayena vitthāro vattabbo siyā, so heṭṭhā dassitanayena sakkā avuttopi jānitunti ekapadepi ekapaccayo vā na vutto. Yā panesā saṅkhepato desanā katā, sā evaṃ katāti veditabbā. Hetudukena hi saddhiṃ kusalapadaṃ yojetvā paṭiccavāre anulomassa ceva paccanīyassa ca vasena sabbe labbhamānakapaccayā dassitā, anulomapaccanīyapaccanīyānulomanayā ceva sahajātavārādayo ca na dassitā, kevalaṃ “paṭiccavārasadisaṃyeva vitthāretabba”nti vuttaṃ. Pañhāvāre pañhampi avissajjetvā kevalaṃ pañhuddhāramattaṃ katvā anulomapaccanīyavaseneva labbhamānapaccayā dassitā. Yathā ca kusalapadaṃ, evaṃ akusalaabyākatapadānipi hetudukena saddhiṃ yojetvā hetukusaladukatikaṃ niddisitabbanti vuttaṃ.

In the Dyad-Triad Conditional Relations, the teaching is briefly given merely by raising the question: 'Dependent on a wholesome root-phenomenon, a wholesome root-phenomenon arises due to root condition.' However, the detailed explanation should be given in the manner beginning with 'Dependent on wholesome non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion,' and so on. Even if not explicitly stated, it can be understood by the method shown below; not a single term or a single condition is stated. The concise teaching given here should be understood as having been given in this way: Indeed, by combining the term 'wholesome' (kusala) with the root dyad (hetuduka), all obtainable conditions are shown in the Dependent Relation (paṭiccavāra) by way of the direct order (anuloma) and the reverse order (paccanīya). However, the methods of direct-reverse (anulomapaccanīya), reverse-direct (paccanīyānuloma), and the co-nascence relation (sahajātavāra) and others are not shown; it is merely stated that 'it should be elaborated similarly to the Dependent Relation.' In the Question Relation (pañhāvāra), without answering the question, only the raising of the questions is done, and the obtainable conditions are shown solely by way of the direct and reverse orders. It is stated that just as with the term 'wholesome' (kusala), so too the terms 'unwholesome' (akusala) and 'indeterminate' (abyākata) should be combined with the root dyad (hetuduka), and the root-wholesome dyad-triad (hetukusaladukatika) should be indicated.

Tato [V 0.0486] paraṃ hetuṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammantiādinā nayena hetuvedanādukatikādīni ekavīsati dukatikāni dassitāni. Yasmā pana hetu nāma sanidassanasappaṭigho anidassanasappaṭigho vā natthi, tasmā hetupadena saddhiṃ sanidassanasappaṭighaanidassanasappaṭighapadāni na yojitāni. Evaṃ hetudukena saddhiṃ labbhamānakavasena dvāvīsati tike yojetvā puna te sahetukadukādīhi saraṇadukapariyosānehi sabbadukehi saddhiṃ yojitā. Tattha yaṃ yaṃ padaṃ yena yena padena saddhiṃ yojanaṃ na gacchati, taṃ taṃ pāḷiyaṃyeva na labbhatīti vuttaṃ. Evamettha ekena dukena saddhiṃ bāvīsati tike yojetvā puna aparena bāvīsati, aparena bāvīsatīti paṭipāṭiyā dukasate labbhamānadukapadehi saddhiṃ dvāvīsati tikā yojitāti dvāvīsati tike gahetvā dukasate pakkhipitvā dukatikapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma desitaṃ. Tattha yesu yesu ṭhānesu nayaṃ dassetvā pāḷiyā saṅkhepo kato, tesu tesu ṭhānesu dassitanayānurūpena tassā vitthāro veditabboti.

Beyond that, twenty-one dyad-triads (dukatikāni), such as the root-feeling dyad-triad (hetuvedanādukatika), are shown by the method beginning with 'a root-phenomenon conjoined with pleasant feeling.' However, since there is no root that is 'visible and with impact' (sanidassanasappaṭigha) or 'invisible and with impact' (anidassanasappaṭigha), the terms 'visible and with impact' and 'invisible and with impact' are not combined with the term 'root' (hetu). Thus, by combining twenty-two triads (tika) with the root dyad (hetuduka) in the manner of what is obtainable, these are further combined with all dyads (sabbaduka), starting from the rooted dyad (sahetukaduka) up to the conclusion of the defilement dyad (saraṇaduka). Herein, it is stated that whatever term does not combine with another term is not found in the Pāḷi itself. In this way, by combining twenty-two triads with one dyad, then again twenty-two with another, and yet another twenty-two—thus, in sequence, twenty-two triads are combined with the obtainable dyad terms in a hundred dyads. Taking these twenty-two triads and inserting them into the hundred dyads, the exposition called the 'Dyad-Triad Conditional Relations' (Dukatikapaṭṭhāna) is taught. Wherever the method is shown and the Pāḷi text is summarized, in those very places, its detailed explanation should be understood in accordance with the method shown.

Dukatikapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

Exposition of the Dyad-Triad Conditional Relations.

4. Tikadukapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

4. Exposition of the Triad-Dyad Conditional Relations.

Tikadukapaṭṭhānepi [M 0.0493] kusalaṃ hetuṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayāti pañhāmattuddhāravaseneva desanā katā. Tattha yathā heṭṭhā hetudukena saddhiṃ kusalapadaṃ yojetvā sabbapaccayavasena sabbavāresu saṅkhepato desanā katā, evamidha kusalattikena saddhiṃ hetupadaṃ yojetvā sabbapaccayavasena sabbavāresu saṅkhepato desanā katā. Yathā ca hetupadaṃ, evaṃ nahetupadampi kusalattikena saddhiṃ yojetvā kusalattikahetudukaṃ niṭṭhāpitaṃ. Tato paraṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ hetuṃ dhammantiādinā nayena vedanāttikahetudukādīni ekavīsati tikadukāni dassitāni.

In the Triad-Dyad Conditional Relations, the teaching is given briefly by way of merely raising the question: 'Dependent on a wholesome root-phenomenon, a wholesome root-phenomenon arises due to root condition.' Here, just as below, the wholesome term was combined with the root dyad and briefly taught in all instances by way of all conditions, so here the root term is combined with the wholesome triad and briefly taught in all instances by way of all conditions. And just as the root term, so too the non-root term is combined with the wholesome triad, thus completing the wholesome triad-root dyad. Thereafter, by the method beginning 'a root-phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling,' twenty-one triad-dyads, such as the feeling triad-root dyad, are shown.

Evaṃ bāvīsatiyā tikehi saddhiṃ hetudukaṃ yojetvā puna tehiyeva saddhiṃ sahetukadukādayo saraṇadukapariyosānā labbhamānavasena sabbadukā yojitā. Idhāpi yaṃ yaṃ padaṃ yojanaṃ na gacchati, taṃ taṃ pāḷiyaṃyeva paṭikkhittaṃ. Evaṃ dukasataṃ gahetvā dvāvīsatiyā tikesu [V 0.0487] pakkhipitvā tikadukapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma desitaṃ. Tatrāpi yena yena nayena pāḷi saṅkhittā, so so nayo vitthārato veditabbo.

Thus, having combined the root dyad with the twenty-two triads, and then again having combined the dyads beginning with the rooted dyad up to the conclusion of the defilement dyad with those same triads, all the dyads are combined in an obtainable manner. Here too, whatever term does not go into combination is rejected in the Pāḷi itself. Thus, having taken a hundred dyads and inserted them into the twenty-two triads, the Triad-Dyad Conditional Relations is taught. In this too, by whatever method the Pāḷi is abbreviated, that method should be understood in detail.

Tikadukapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

Exposition of the Triad-Dyad Conditional Relations.

5. Tikatikapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

5. Exposition of the Triad-Triad Conditional Relations.

Tikatikapaṭṭhānepi kusalaṃ sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca kusalo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayāti pañhuddhāravaseneva saṅkhepato desanā katā. Ettha ca kusalattikaṃ vedanāttikādīhi, vedanāttikādayo ca kusalattikenāti evaṃ tikesuyeva tikā pakkhittā. Yena yena ca padena saddhiṃ yaṃ yaṃ padaṃ yojanaṃ na gacchati, taṃ taṃ hāpetvā labbhamānavaseneva sabbapaccayesu vārā ca gaṇananayā ca dassitā, tasmā te sādhukaṃ pāḷiṃ upaparikkhitvā veditabbā. Yathā ca kusalattikaṃ vedanāttikādīhi, vedanāttikādayo ca tena saddhiṃ yojetvā veditabbā; tathā ekekaṃ tikaṃ sesehi. Sesā ca tehi saddhiṃ yojetvā veditabbāti.

In the Triad-Triad Conditional Relations also, the teaching is given briefly by way of raising the question: 'Dependent on a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling, a wholesome phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling arises due to root condition.' Here, the wholesome triad is combined with the feeling triad and others, and the feeling triad and others are combined with the wholesome triad. Thus, triads are inserted into triads themselves. And whatever term does not go into combination with whatever other term, that is omitted, and the variations and methods of calculation are shown in all conditions only by way of what is obtainable. Therefore, these should be understood well by scrutinizing the Pāḷi. Just as the wholesome triad is to be understood as combined with the feeling triad and others, and the feeling triad and others with it; so too each triad with the remaining ones. And the remaining ones are to be understood as combined with them.

Tikatikapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

Exposition of the Triad-Triad Conditional Relations.

6. Dukadukapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

6. Exposition of the Dyad-Dyad Conditional Relations.

Dukadukapaṭṭhānepi [M 0.0494] hetusahetukaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca hetusahetuko dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayāti pañhuddhāravaseneva saṅkhepato desanā katā. Tattha hetudukaṃ sahetukadukādīhi, sahetukadukādīni ca tena saddhiṃ yojitāni. Ekekaṃ pana dukaṃ sesehi, sesā ca tehi saddhiṃ paṭipāṭiyā yojetabbā. Idañhi dukadukapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma ‘dukesuyeva duke pakkhipitvā’ desitaṃ. Tenettha sabbadukehi [V 0.0488] saddhiṃ sabbadukānaṃ yojanā veditabbā. Pāḷi pana saṅkhittā. Yena yena ca padena saddhiṃ yaṃ yaṃ padaṃ yojanaṃ na gacchati, taṃ taṃ hāpetvāva desanā katāti.

In the Dukadukapaṭṭhāna also, the teaching is given briefly by way of raising the question: 'A root-and-with-root phenomenon arises dependent on a root-and-with-root phenomenon by way of root condition.' Here, the root dyad is combined with the 'with-root dyad' and others, and the 'with-root dyad' and others are combined with it. Each dyad, however, is to be combined with the remaining ones, and the remaining ones with them, in due order. This Dukadukapaṭṭhāna is taught by 'inserting dyads into dyads themselves.' Therefore, here the combination of all dyads with all dyads is to be understood. The Pāḷi, however, is abbreviated. And the teaching is given by omitting whatever term does not go into combination with whatever other term.

Dukadukapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Dukadukapaṭṭhāna.

Ettāvatā –

Thus far:

Tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukaṃ tikañceva tikaṃ dukañca;

Tikaṃ tikañceva dukaṃ dukañca,

Cha anulomamhi nayā sugambhīrāti. –

The excellent triad and the supreme dyad,Dyad and triad, and triad and dyad;Triad and triad, and dyad and dyad—These six are exceedingly profound methods in the forward order.

Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttagāthāya dīpitā. Dhammānulomapaṭṭhāne cha nayā niddiṭṭhā honti. Paccayavasena panettha ekekasmiṃ paṭṭhāne anulomādayo cattāro cattāro nayāti ekena pariyāyena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ anulomapaṭṭhānaṃyeva veditabbaṃ.

As elucidated by the verse stated in the commentary, six methods are designated in the Dhammānuloma-Paṭṭhāna. Moreover, in each Paṭṭhāna here, by way of conditions, there are four methods each—the forward order and so on. Thus, by one reckoning, the forward Paṭṭhāna itself is to be understood as adorned with twenty-four methods.

7-12. Paccanīyapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

7-12. Explanation of the Paccanīya-Paṭṭhāna.

1. Idāni kusalādīnaṃ padānaṃ paṭikkhepavasena dhammānaṃ paccanīyatāya laddhanāmaṃ paccanīyapaṭṭhānaṃ dassetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nakusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccāti kusalassa paccayabhāvaṃ vāreti. Nakusalo dhammo uppajjatīti kusalassa uppattiṃ vāreti, tasmā “akusalābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca akusalābyākatā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpa”nti evamādinā nayenettha pañhaṃ vissajjitabbaṃ. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ paccaye laddhagaṇanā pana pāḷiyaṃ vuttāyeva. Yepi vārā sadisavissajjanā, tepi tattheva dassitā. Tasmā sabbamettha heṭṭhā vuttanayānusārena [M 0.0495] pāḷiṃ upaparikkhitvā veditabbaṃ. Yathā cettha, evaṃ dukapaṭṭhāne, dukatikapaṭṭhāne, tikadukapaṭṭhāne tikatikapaṭṭhāne, dukadukapaṭṭhāne ca.

1. Now, to show the Paccanīya-Paṭṭhāna, which has obtained its name by way of the opposition of phenomena through the rejection of terms such as 'wholesome,' etc., the passage beginning 'A non-wholesome phenomenon arises dependent on a non-wholesome phenomenon by way of root condition' has been commenced. Herein, 'dependent on a non-wholesome phenomenon' negates the conditionality of the wholesome. 'A non-wholesome phenomenon arises' negates the arising of the wholesome. Therefore, the question here is to be answered by the method beginning 'one aggregate that is unwholesome or indeterminate conditions three aggregates that are unwholesome or indeterminate, and mind-originated material form.' The numerical counts obtained for each condition, however, are stated in the Pāḷi itself. And those variations with similar answers are also shown there. Thus, all of this here is to be understood by scrutinizing the Pāḷi according to the method stated below. And as it is here, so it is in the Duka-Paṭṭhāna, Dukatika-Paṭṭhāna, Tikaduka-Paṭṭhāna, Tikatika-Paṭṭhāna, and Dukaduka-Paṭṭhāna.

Ettāvatā [V 0.0489] –

Thus far:

Tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukaṃ tikañceva tikaṃ dukañca;

Tikaṃ tikañceva, dukaṃ dukañca,

Cha paccanīyamhi nayā sugambhīrāti. –

The excellent triad and the supreme dyad,Dyad and triad, and triad and dyad;Triad and triad, and dyad and dyad—These six are exceedingly profound methods in the negative order.

Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ [M 0.0496] vuttagāthāya dīpitā. Dhammapaccanīyapaṭṭhāne cha nayā niddiṭṭhā honti. Paccayavasena panettha ekekasmiṃ paṭṭhāne anulomādayo cattāro cattāro nayāti ekena pariyāyena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ paccanīyapaṭṭhānaññeva veditabbaṃ.

As elucidated by the verse stated in the commentary, six methods are designated in the Dhammapaccanīya-Paṭṭhāna. Moreover, in each Paṭṭhāna here, by way of conditions, there are four methods each—the forward order and so on. Thus, by one reckoning, the Paccanīya-Paṭṭhāna itself is to be understood as adorned with twenty-four methods.

Paccanīyapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Paccanīya-Paṭṭhāna.

13-18. Anulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

13-18. Explanation of the Anulomapaccanīya-Paṭṭhāna

1. Idāni kusalādīsu dhammesu paccayadhammaṃ appaṭikkhipitvā paccayuppannassa kusalādibhāvapaṭikkhepavasena dhammānaṃ anulomapaccanīyatāya laddhanāmaṃ anulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhānaṃ dassetuṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca na kusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha kusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccāti kusalassa paccayabhāvaṃ anujānāti. Na kusalo dhammo uppajjatīti kusalasseva uppattiṃ vāreti. Tasmā “kusale khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpa”ntiādinā nayena vissajjanaṃ dassitaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ pāḷiṃ oloketvā sādhukaṃ sallakkhetabbaṃ. Yampi yena sadisaṃ, yañca yattha labbhati, yo ca yesaṃ vissajjanānaṃ yesu paccayesu gaṇanaparicchedo, so sabbo pāḷiyaṃ dassito, tasmā pāḷiyeva ettha attho. Yathā cettha, evaṃ dukapaṭṭhānādīsupīti.

1. Now, to demonstrate the Anulomapaccanīya-Paṭṭhāna, which has acquired its name by being direct-negative with respect to states—that is, by not rejecting the conditioning state among wholesome and other states, but by rejecting the wholesome and other nature of the conditioned state—it begins with the statement: 'A not-wholesome state arises dependent on a wholesome state by way of root condition,' and so on. Herein, 'dependent on a wholesome state' acknowledges the state of being a condition of the wholesome. 'A not-wholesome state arises' prevents the arising of a wholesome state itself. Therefore, the explanation is given in the manner of: 'mind-originated form dependent on wholesome aggregates,' and so on. All this should be carefully examined by looking at the Pāḷi text. Whatever is similar to what, whatever is found where, and whatever enumeration and limitation of conditions there is for which explanations, all that is shown in the Pāḷi text; therefore, the Pāḷi itself is the authority here. As it is here, so it is also in the Dukapaṭṭhāna and other sections.

Ettāvatā –

Thus far:

Tikañca [V 0.0490] paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukaṃ tikañceva tikaṃ dukañca;

Tikaṃ tikañceva dukaṃ dukañca,

Cha anulomapaccanīyamhi nayā sugambhīrāti. –

The excellent triad and the supreme dyad,Dyad and triad, and triad and dyad;Triad and triad, and dyad and dyad—These six are exceedingly profound methods in the direct-negative.

Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttagāthāya dīpitā dhammānulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhāne cha nayā niddiṭṭhā honti. Paccayavasena panettha ekekasmiṃ paṭṭhāne anulomādayo cattāro cattāro nayāti ekena pariyāyena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ anulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhānaññeva veditabbaṃ.

As elucidated by the verse stated in the commentary, six methods are designated in the Dhammānulomapaccanīya-Paṭṭhāna. Moreover, in each Paṭṭhāna here, by way of conditions, there are four methods each—the forward order and so on. Thus, by one reckoning, the Anulomapaccanīya-Paṭṭhāna itself is to be understood as adorned with twenty-four methods.

Anulomapaccanīyapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

Explanation of the Anulomapaccanīya-Paṭṭhāna.

19-24. Paccanīyānulomapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

19-24. Explanation of the Paccanīyānuloma-Paṭṭhāna

1. Idāni kusalādīsu dhammesu paccayadhammaṃ paṭikkhipitvā paccayuppannassa kusalādibhāvaṃ appaṭikkhepavasena dhammānaṃ paccanīyānulomatāya laddhanāmaṃ paccanīyānulomapaṭṭhānaṃ dassetuṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca akusalo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayātiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiccāti kusalassa paccayabhāvaṃ vāreti. Akusalo dhammo uppajjatīti akusalassa uppattiṃ anujānāti. Nakusalañhi akusalaṃ abyākataṃ vā, tañca sahajātapaccayaṃ katvā uppajjamāno kusalo nāma natthi, tasmā akusalābyākatavasena desanā katā. Tattha “akusalaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā”ti evaṃ nakusalaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca vissajjanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Abyākato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayāti ayaṃ pana pañho “vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpa”nti vissajjitova. Iti sabbapañhesu avissajjitassa atthānurūpaṃ vissajjitassa ca pāḷiāgatameva vissajjanaṃ. Ekekasmiñca tikaduke vārappabhedapaccayagaṇanavidhānaṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttanayānusāreneva veditabbaṃ.

1. Now, to demonstrate the Paccanīyānuloma Paṭṭhāna, which has acquired its name from the negative-positive method regarding states—that is, by rejecting the conditioning state in relation to wholesome and other states, but by not rejecting the wholesome and other nature of the conditioned state—it begins with the statement: 'An unwholesome state arises dependent on a not-wholesome state by way of root condition,' and so on. Herein, 'dependent on a not-wholesome state' denies that a wholesome state is a condition. 'An unwholesome state arises' permits the arising of an unwholesome state. For there is no wholesome state that arises by making an unwholesome or indeterminate state a co-nascence condition; therefore, the teaching is given in terms of the unwholesome and the indeterminate. Herein, regarding 'dependent on a not-wholesome state,' the answer should be understood thus: 'Dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise.' As for the question, 'An indeterminate state arises by way of root condition,' this has been answered thus: 'Dependent on one resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregate, the other three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise.' Thus, in all questions, for what is not answered, the answer conforms to the meaning, and for what is answered, the answer is just as it comes in the Pāli text. And for each triad and dyad, the classification of turns, the grouping of conditions, and the method of calculation should all be understood entirely in accordance with the method explained above.

Ettāvatā ca –

Thus far—

Tikañca paṭṭhānavaraṃ dukuttamaṃ,

Dukaṃ tikañceva tikaṃ dukañca;

Tikaṃ [V 0.0491] tikañceva dukaṃ dukañca,

Cha paccanīyānulomamhi nayā sugambhīrāti. –

The Triad and the supreme Paṭṭhāna, the excellent Dyad; the Dyad and the Triad, and the Triad and the Dyad; the Triad and the Triad, and the Dyad and the Dyad—these six methods in the Negative-Positive are truly profound.

Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttagāthāya dīpitā. Dhammapaccanīyānulomapaṭṭhāne cha nayā niddiṭṭhā honti. Paccayavasena panettha ekekasmiṃ paṭṭhāne anulomādayo cattāro cattāro nayāti ekena pariyāyena catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ paccanīyānulomapaṭṭhānaññeva veditabbaṃ.

This is illustrated by the verse stated in the commentary. In the Dhamma-Negative-Positive Paṭṭhāna, six methods are indicated. Moreover, by way of conditions, here in each Paṭṭhāna there are four methods each—the Positive, and so on; thus, in one way, the Paccanīyānuloma Paṭṭhāna itself should be understood as being adorned with twenty-four methods.

Paccanīyānulomapaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā.

The Explanation of the Negative-Positive Paṭṭhāna.

Evaṃ [M 0.0497] dhammānulomādivasena catūsu vāresu ekekasmiṃ catuvīsatiyā catuvīsatiyā nayānaṃ vasena channavuti nayā honti. Tattha paccayanaye aggahetvā ekekasmiṃ paṭṭhāne tikadukādīnaññeva channaṃ channaṃ nayānaṃ vasenetaṃ catuvīsatinayapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ samantapaṭṭhānamahāpakaraṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Keci pana “kusalārammaṇo dhammo akusalārammaṇo dhammo”tiādinā nayena ārammaṇamātikaṃ nāma ṭhapetvā “kusalārammaṇo dhammo kusalārammaṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo”tiādinā nayena ārammaṇapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma dassetvā aparampi phassādīnaṃ vasenapi phassapaṭṭhānaṃ nāma uddharitvā dassenti. Taṃ neva pāḷiyaṃ na aṭṭhakathāsu sandissatīti idha na vicāritaṃ. Saṅgītiāruḷhapāḷivaseneva panettha vaṇṇanā katāti veditabbā.

Thus, by way of the Dhamma-Positive and so on, in the four turns, there are ninety-six methods, by way of twenty-four methods in each. Herein, without taking the condition-method, this great treatise, the Samantapaṭṭhāna, should be understood as adorned with twenty-four methods, by way of six methods each for the triads, dyads, and so on, in each Paṭṭhāna. However, some, having established a matrix of objects named 'a state with a wholesome object, a state with an unwholesome object,' and so on, then present a Paṭṭhāna of objects, such as 'a state with a wholesome object is a condition for a state with a wholesome object by way of root condition,' and so on; and further, by way of contact and so on, they extract and present a Paṭṭhāna of contact. Since this is found neither in the Pāli Canon nor in the commentaries, it is not discussed here. It should be understood that the explanation here is made solely in accordance with the Pāli text established at the Council.

Ettāvatā ca –

Thus far—

Sammūḷhā yattha pajā, tantākulādibhāvamāpannā;

Nekavidhadukkhagahanaṃ, saṃsāraṃ nātivattanti.

Where beings are deluded, having fallen into a state like a tangled skein, they do not transcend saṃsāra, the thicket of manifold suffering.

Paccayabhede kusalo, loke garutampi paccayākāraṃ;

Atinippuṇagambhīraṃ, javanabbhūmiṃ buddhañāṇassa.

Skilled in the analysis of conditions, (he understands) the conditional mode, weighty in the world; exceedingly subtle and profound, the swift realm of the Buddha's knowledge.

Kusalādidhammabhedaṃ, nissāya nayehi vividhagaṇanehi;

Vitthārento sattama-mabhidhammappakaraṇaṃ satthā.

Elaborating on the classification of wholesome and other states, relying on various methods and diverse enumerations, the Teacher expounded the seventh Abhidhamma treatise.

Suvihitasanniṭṭhāno[V 0.0492], paṭṭhānaṃ nāma yaṃ pakāsesi;

Saddhāya samāraddhā, yā aṭṭhakathā mayā tassa.

That Paṭṭhāna, which he expounded, with its well-established conclusion; this commentary for it was undertaken by me with faith.

Ācariyānaṃ vādaṃ, avihāya vibhajjavādisissānaṃ;

Atibahuvidhantarāye, lokamhi anantarāyena.

Without abandoning the doctrine of the teachers, for the disciples of the Analysts, in a world with very many kinds of obstacles, it was completed without hindrance.

Sā evaṃ ajja katā, cuddasamattehi bhāṇavārehi;

Atthaṃ pakāsayantī, paṭṭhānavarassa sakalassa.

Thus it was completed today, with about fourteen recitation sections, revealing the meaning of the entire supreme Paṭṭhāna.

Sanniṭṭhānaṃ pattā yatheva niṭṭhaṃ tathā bahujanassa;

Sampāpuṇantu sīghaṃ, kalyāṇā sabbasaṅkappā.

Just as this work has reached its conclusion, so may all the wholesome aspirations of the multitude quickly be fulfilled.

Ettāvatā [M 0.0498] –

Thus far—

Sattappakaraṇaṃ nātho, abhidhammamadesayi;

Devātidevo devānaṃ, devalokamhi yaṃ pure.

The Lord, the God beyond gods, expounded the seven treatises of the Abhidhamma, which he formerly taught to the devas in the deva-world.

Tassa aṭṭhakathā esā, sakalassāpi niṭṭhitā;

Ciraṭṭhitatthaṃ dhammassa, niṭṭhapentena taṃ mayā.

This commentary for all of it has been completed by me, who finished it for the long endurance of the Dhamma.

Yaṃ pattaṃ kusalaṃ tassa, ānubhāvena pāṇino;

Sabbe saddhammarājassa, ñatvā dhammaṃ sukhāvahaṃ.

By the power of whatever merit has been attained by this, may all beings, having known the happiness-bringing Dhamma of the King of the True Dhamma,

Pāpuṇantu visuddhāya, sukhāya paṭipattiyā;

Asokamanupāyāsaṃ, nibbānasukhamuttamaṃ.

attain, by means of the pure and happy practice, the supreme bliss of Nibbāna, free from sorrow and distress.

Ciraṃ tiṭṭhatu saddhammo, dhamme hontu sagāravā;

Sabbepi sattā kālena, sammā devo pavassatu.

May the True Dhamma long endure; may all beings be respectful towards the Dhamma; may the deva rightly send rain in due season.

Yathā [V 0.0493] rakkhiṃsu porāṇā, surājāno tathevimaṃ;

Rājā rakkhatu dhammena, attanova pajaṃ pajanti.

Just as the good kings of old protected, so may this king protect the populace with Dhamma, as if they were his own children.

Paṭṭhānappakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Paṭṭhāna Treatise is concluded.

Niṭṭhitā ca pañcapakaraṇaṭṭhakathāti.

And thus the Commentary on the Five Treatises is completed.

Nigamanakathā

Concluding Discourse

Paramavisuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyapaṭimaṇḍitena [M 0.0499] sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇasamudayasamuditena sakasamayasamayantaragahanajjhogāhaṇasamatthena paññāveyyattiyasamannāgatena tipiṭakapariyattippabhede sāṭṭhakathe satthusāsane appaṭihatañāṇappabhāvena mahāveyyākaraṇena karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacanalāvaṇṇayuttena yuttamuttavādinā vādīvarena mahākavinā pabhinnapaṭisambhidāparivāre chaḷabhiññādippabhedaguṇapaṭimaṇḍite uttarimanussadhamme suppatiṭṭhitabuddhīnaṃ theravaṃsappadīpānaṃ therānaṃ mahāvihāravāsīnaṃ vaṃsālaṅkārabhūtena vipulavisuddhabuddhinā buddhaghosoti garūhi gahitanāmadheyyena therena katā ayaṃ sakalassapi abhidhammapiṭakassa aṭṭhakathā –

Adorned with supreme purity of faith, intellect, and energy; endowed with the accumulation of virtues such as morality, conduct, honesty, and gentleness; skilled in deeply penetrating his own and other schools of thought; possessing wisdom and discernment, with unhindered knowledge of the Teacher’s Dispensation, which is differentiated into the three Piṭakas along with their commentaries; a great grammarian, whose sweet and noble speech, issuing from the bliss born of accomplished action, is endowed with charm; a speaker of reasoned discourse, a pre-eminent debater, and a great poet; possessed of the analytical knowledges; an ornament to the lineage of the elders dwelling in the Great Monastery—who are lamps of the Theravada lineage, their intellects well-established in the superhuman state adorned with qualities such as the six supernormal knowledges; with vast and purified intellect, given the name Buddhaghosa by his preceptors; by that elder, this commentary on the entire Abhidhamma Piṭaka has been composed.

Tāva tiṭṭhatu lokasmiṃ, lokanittharaṇesinaṃ;

Dassentī kulaputtānaṃ, nayaṃ paññāvisuddhiyā.

May it long endure in the world for those who seek to cross over, showing to noble sons the way to the purity of wisdom.

Yāva buddhoti nāmampi, suddhacittassa tādino;

Lokamhi lokajeṭṭhassa, pavattati mahesinoti.

As long as the very name “Buddha”—of the pure-minded one, the steadfast one, the foremost in the world, the great sage—endures in the world.

Abhidhammapiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Abhidhamma Piṭaka is concluded.
